The header of [`patch/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py#L17-L27) states exactly this contract: platform patches are applied by `NPUPlatform.pre_register_and_update`, worker patches by each worker's `__init__`.

| Caller | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NPUPlatform.pre_register_and_update` ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L285-L299)) | platform (`is_global_patch=True`) | Runs before quantization configs are imported and before the DeepSeek-V4 config convertor is registered, so the patch package finishes importing first |
| `_ensure_global_patch()` ([`vllm_ascend/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/__init__.py#L51-L65)) | platform | Idempotent behind `_GLOBAL_PATCH_APPLIED`; invoked by `register_connector`, `register_model_loader`, `register_service_profiling` so **engine-core subprocesses** get the platform tier even when no CLI parse happened there |
| `NPUWorker.__init__` ([`worker/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L144-L152)) | worker (`adapt_patch()`) | Runs before `vllm_ascend.ops` registration, custom-op registration, and `init_ascend_config` |
| `tests/e2e/conftest.py` ([`conftest.py`](../../tests/e2e/conftest.py#L67-L73)), [`tests/ut/base.py`](../../tests/ut/base.py#L23-L30), [`tests/ut/conftest.py`](../../tests/ut/conftest.py#L239-L243) | both, explicitly | Pytest has no plugin entry point, so conftests call `adapt_patch(True)` **and** `adapt_patch()` by hand |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PLAT["NPUPlatform.pre_register_and_update"] --> AP["vllm_ascend.utils.adapt_patch"]
    GPL["_ensure_global_patch from general plugins"] --> AP
    TESTC["e2e and ut conftests"] --> AP
    AP -->|"is_global_patch=True"| PKGP["patch/platform/__init__.py"]
    AP -->|"default False"| PKGW["patch/worker/__init__.py"]
    WK["NPUWorker.__init__"] --> AP
    PKGP --> EAGER["eager module-level rebinds in main process"]
    PKGP --> WRAP["wrapped run_engine_core entry points"]
    PKGW --> SWAPS["class and function swaps inside the worker"]
```

*Both tiers funnel through one function; the caller decides which package is imported, and each package's import side effects do the patching.*

The separate general-plugin entry (`_ensure_global_patch`) exists because [`docs/source/developer_guide/Design_Documents/patch.md`](../../docs/source/developer_guide/Design_Documents/patch.md#L72-L75) records that engine-core code cannot be patched "by default". In practice the platform tier reaches an engine-core subprocess two ways: vLLM loads the general plugins there, and — in spawn mode — a child that unpickles a wrapped target such as `_balance_run_engine_core` imports its defining module, which imports the parent package and re-applies every platform patch. [`patch_profiling_chunk.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_profiling_chunk.py#L210-L229) is the explicit form of that idiom: it wraps `EngineCoreProc.run_engine_core` precisely so the child re-applies the `EngineCore.__init__` patch before any `EngineCore` exists.

## The catalog contract

[`patch/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py) is a documentation module: its body is a single comment block, so importing it has no runtime effect. It is the index. Each patch file gets a numbered section that must record:

- the **target symbol** on the first line — as specific as `vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler.Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split` or `torch.accelerator.memory_stats`, not just the module;
- **Why** — the concrete failure or capability the patch addresses, often naming the upstream PR that removed or never provided an extension point;
- **How** — the mechanism, including which argument or condition the replacement changes;
- **Related PR (if no, explain why)** — an upstream or vllm-ascend PR link, or an explicit justification for having none;
- **Future Plan** — the removal condition, usually "remove when upstream ships PR #NNNNN".

Optional fields appear where they matter: `Related issue`, `Related RFC`, and `Test`.

This is a **review-enforced contract, not a tested one**. No unit test parses the catalog; the requirement lives in [`docs/.../patch.md`](../../docs/source/developer_guide/Design_Documents/patch.md#L34-L70) (step 6 of "how to write a patch") and in [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md#L228-L250), which makes architectural review of every new patch mandatory and asks reviewers to confirm the patch hits the right upstream component, is minimal, has understood performance costs, and has a long-term upstream plan. The same doc states the strategy in one line each: *less is more*, *every patch must describe its future removal*, *cleaning patch code is always welcome*.

Three consequences for anyone reading or extending the tree:

1. **The catalog is two-level.** Items added later were documented in the sub-package header instead: [`patch/platform/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/__init__.py#L52-L101) carries additional entries for GLM-Next cache planning in `patch_kv_cache_utils`, the GLM-Next alignment variant of `patch_mamba_config`, and the sparse index-kpool variant of `patch_mamba_block_aligned_split`. Read both files.
2. **The catalog drifts; the import lists are authoritative.** Section 21 documents `platform/patch_tool_choice_none_content.py`, which no longer exists in the tree, while `worker/patch_distributed.py` (the HCCL process-group registry) is imported but has no catalog entry. When you need the current inventory, use the import statements in the two `__init__.py` markers; when you need the *reason*, use the catalog.
3. **Numbers are hand-assigned and non-unique** (`7a`, `10a`, `27a`, and two sections numbered 18 in the worker list). Treat the `** N. File: ... **` header as the anchor, not the ordinal.

## Ordering: the imports are the design

The catalog lists entries alphabetically by file name — it says so in its own header. The **import order in the package markers is deliberately not alphabetical**, because importing a patch module is what applies it, and several patches only work in a specific sequence.

The clearest case is the engine-core wrapper chain. `patch_balance_schedule` is imported before `patch_dyntra_lb_core` ([`patch/platform/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/__init__.py#L41-L42)) because DyntraLB captures whatever `EngineCoreProc.run_engine_core` currently is and wraps *it*:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    UP["upstream EngineCoreProc.run_engine_core"] --> BAL["_balance_run_engine_core installed by patch_balance_schedule"]
    BAL --> DYN["_dyntra_lb_run_engine_core installed by patch_dyntra_lb_core"]
    DYN -->|"DyntraLB disabled"| BAL
    DYN -->|"DyntraLB enabled"| DU["upstream body with DPEngineCoreProc swapped to DyntraLBDPEngineCoreProc"]
    BAL -->|"balance enabled"| BU["upstream body with DPEngineCoreProc swapped to BalanceDPEngineCoreProc"]
    BAL -->|"balance disabled"| BP["upstream body with the pristine DPEngineCoreProc"]
```

*DyntraLB is always the outer wrapper; it delegates inward to the balance wrapper when off and bypasses it when on.*

The worker marker shows the same discipline for 310P. `patch_v2.patch_eagle_speculator` installs `AutoRegressiveAclGraphManager` on the upstream speculator module; only **after** that does [`patch/worker/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/__init__.py#L61-L74) re-override `SpeculatorCudaGraphManager` with `AutoRegressiveAclGraphManager310` for non-standard hardware — the comment there states the reason outright ("patch_eagle_speculator above installs the 910 manager; re-override here"). `patch_v2/patch_spec_decode_310` is imported *earlier* (line 39) and deliberately does not touch the graph manager, delegating that to the late override so the 310P manager cannot be silently overwritten. Reordering these imports produces no error — it produces the wrong graph manager, which surfaces as a runtime graph-capture failure far from the patch tree.

Other ordering dependencies are structural rather than positional: `patch_dyntra_lb_core` imports `patch_balance_schedule` as a module to reuse its captured `_OriginalRunEngineCore`, and `_ensure_global_patch` guarantees the platform tier is imported exactly once per process regardless of which entry point fires first.

## Conditional activation

Three different gates decide whether a patch is applied at all. Knowing which gate a patch uses tells you whether a behaviour is missing because of hardware, environment, or configuration.

**Hardware capabilities.** The preferred gate is `get_current_hardware_profile().supports(HardwareCapability.X)` — never a device-type comparison. Capabilities introduced for patch selection specifically are `STANDARD_MAMBA_PATCH` and `STANDARD_WORKER_PATCHES`. Where a family needs a different implementation, the marker imports a *different module* rather than branching inside one:

- `STANDARD_MAMBA_PATCH` present → [`patch_mamba_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_mamba_config.py); absent (310P) → [`patch_mamba_config_310.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_mamba_config_310.py), which aligns both mamba and attention block sizes to the 128-token kernel alignment ([`patch/platform/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/__init__.py#L28-L31)).
- `STANDARD_WORKER_PATCHES` present → `patch_qwen3_5`, `patch_qwen3_dflash`, `patch_qwen3vl`; absent → `patch_idex_310` plus `patch_v2.patch_spec_decode_310` ([`patch/worker/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/__init__.py#L33-L39)).

Finer gates live inside individual modules, so the module is importable everywhere but self-disables: `DISTRIBUTED_COMMUNICATION_ADAPTATION` guards the 310P `all_reduce`/`broadcast` rewrites ([`patch_distributed.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_distributed.py#L88-L89)), `GDN_COMPATIBILITY` chooses the 310P GDN forward/state dtype ([`patch_qwen3_5.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_qwen3_5.py#L207-L214)), `FP8_ATTENTION` gates the A5 `MoonViT3dPretrainedModel.to` dtype filter ([`patch_kimi_k25.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_kimi_k25.py#L85-L95)).

**Environment.** The platform marker imports `patch_multiproc_executor` only when `DYNAMIC_EPLB` is truthy or `EXPERT_MAP_RECORD == "true"` ([`patch/platform/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/__init__.py#L38-L39)), because that patch exists to make worker processes non-daemonic so EPLB can spawn its own process. The worker marker wraps both Triton patch modules in `HAS_TRITON`, so a 310P or CPU unit-test environment simply never installs them ([`patch/worker/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/__init__.py#L18-L24)).

**Configuration.** A few patches are activated from the platform config path rather than from the package marker. `patch_profiling_chunk` is imported only when `scheduler_config.profiling_chunk_config.enabled`, at the same moment the profiled scheduler class is written into `vllm_config` ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L1256-L1261)); balance scheduling and DyntraLB redirect the engine-core class only when their own config is enabled (next section).

## Lazy installation and late rebinding

A patch module does not guarantee that its assignment is the last word. Three installation styles coexist, and mixing them up is a common source of "the patch is applied but has no effect".

**Eager, at import.** The simple majority: `ModelConfig.is_deepseek_mla = property(...)`, `Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split = _mamba_block_aligned_split`, `model_runner.BlockTables = AscendBlockTables`. The symbol is rebound the moment the module is imported, which is why the platform tier must be imported *before* the code that captures the symbol by name.

**Deferred to a wrapped entry point.** [`patch_balance_schedule.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_balance_schedule.py#L912-L940) rebinds `vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler.Scheduler` eagerly but swaps `vllm.v1.engine.core.DPEngineCoreProc` *inside* its `run_engine_core` wrapper, only when balance scheduling is enabled, and restores the original otherwise. [`patch_dyntra_lb_core.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_dyntra_lb_core.py#L523-L547) does the same with a `try/finally` restore. The reason is stated in the module docstring: an unconditional swap would inject balance machinery into configurations that do not use it, such as PD-disaggregated recompute with its own scheduler class.

The whole technique rests on a **load-bearing assumption**: upstream's `run_engine_core` resolves `DPEngineCoreProc` through the `vllm.v1.engine.core` module global *at call time*. If upstream ever bound it at import time or behind a factory, both patches would keep importing fine and silently stop taking effect. [`tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_balance_schedule.py`](../../tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_balance_schedule.py#L541-L590) pins exactly that assumption (it reads the upstream source and asserts `"DPEngineCoreProc(" in src`), along with the wrapper chain order and the "not swapped at import time" invariant.

**Deferred to a per-object install call.** Two worker patches cannot run as import side effects because they need per-model or per-config state: [`patch_eagle3_pp_aux.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_eagle3_pp_aux.py#L210) exposes `patch_eagle3_pp_aux_propagation(inner_model)`, called from the v1 model runner once the inner model is known ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4136-L4145)); [`patch_v2/patch_spec_pp.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_v2/patch_spec_pp.py#L11-L13) exposes `install_spec_pp_token_broadcast(pp_handler, req_states)`, called from the v2 model runner when spec-decode PP is active and the engine is on the release lane ([`worker/v2/model_runner.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py#L156-L162)). These are listed in the catalog like any other patch but are *not* imported by the worker marker — do not assume the marker's import list is the complete set of active worker patches.

One patch needs a fourth trick: [`patch/platform/patch_fused_moe.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_fused_moe.py#L212-L220) rebinds the factory on both the `fused_moe` package and its `layer` module, then sweeps `sys.modules` for already-imported `vllm.model_executor.models.*` modules and rewrites any `FusedMoEFactory` name still pointing at the original. That is necessary because models do `from ... import FusedMoEFactory`, capturing a local binding at import time.

## Idempotency and contract guards

The platform tier can be imported several times per process (package import, general plugin, spawn-time unpickle), and a worker may import a compatibility module whose logic already lives in the platform tier. Two patterns keep that safe:

- **Reuse by import.** [`worker/patch_fused_moe.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_fused_moe.py) and [`worker/patch_v2/patch_use_v2_model_runner.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_v2/patch_use_v2_model_runner.py) are two lines each: they import the platform module so one implementation serves both processes. The comments state the hazard explicitly — re-applying would wrap an already-patched factory, and EngineCore subprocesses only see the platform tier.
- **Markers and signature guards.** Wrappers tag themselves (`_PATCH_MARKER`, `_EPLB_ROUTER_ADAPTED`, `_profiling_patches_applied`, `_vllm_ascend_pp_mtp_patched`, `_GLOBAL_PATCH_APPLIED`) and short-circuit on re-entry. Where the upstream call signature is part of the contract, the module inspects it and raises a `RuntimeError` *before* installing anything rather than misbehaving later: `Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split`'s parameter tuple ([`patch_mamba_block_aligned_split.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_mamba_block_aligned_split.py#L91-L99)), the EPLB communicator factory's `group_coordinator` parameter and `_move_to_workspace`'s `model_state`/`ep_rank` parameters ([`patch_eplb.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_eplb.py#L66-L94)), and the MoE router's `_apply_eplb_mapping` signature ([`patch_fused_moe.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_fused_moe.py#L105-L111)).

Version lanes are a third axis. `vllm_version_is("0.28.0")` selects which upstream symbol set exists — [`patch_kv_cache_utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_utils.py#L612-L637) patches a different planner entry per lane, and [`patch_use_v2_model_runner.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_use_v2_model_runner.py#L58-L66) only installs the v1-unsupported-features hook where the symbol exists. Symbols that may be absent are imported under `try/except ImportError` so a lane that lacks them still imports the package ([`patch_balance_schedule.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_balance_schedule.py#L83-L89) for `KVConnectorBlockState`, [`patch_triton.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_triton.py#L66-L87) for the FLA KDA entry points).

## Failure modes worth recognising

| Symptom | Likely cause in the patch tree |
| --- | --- |
| Behaviour is correct in the main process but wrong in the scheduler | Patch belongs in the platform tier but was added to `worker/`, so the engine core never imports it |
| A patch module is imported, yet the symbol is unchanged | Something downstream rebound it later, or the patch was captured by an earlier `from X import Y` — see the `FusedMoEFactory` sweep |
| 310P captures the 910 spec-decode graph manager | `patch_eagle_speculator` re-imported after the 310P re-override, or the re-override block removed from `patch/worker/__init__.py` |
| Balance or DyntraLB silently never activates | Upstream stopped resolving `DPEngineCoreProc` by module-global name — guarded by `test_upstream_run_engine_core_instantiates_dp_proc_by_name` |
| A `RuntimeError` about an unexpected upstream signature at import time | A contract guard firing deliberately; the upstream function it wraps changed shape |
| A patch appears nowhere in the catalog | Catalog drift; cross-check the `__init__.py` import lists and add the missing entry |

## Adding a patch

The documented procedure ([`patch.md`](../../docs/source/developer_guide/Design_Documents/patch.md#L34-L70)) is short, and the two steps that are easy to forget are the ones this architecture depends on:

1. Decide the tier by asking **which process must observe the change**; if it is scheduler- or config-visible, it is platform.
2. Name the file `patch_{module_name}.py` in the chosen tier.
3. Import it in that tier's `__init__.py` — at a position consistent with the ordering dependencies above, and inside the relevant hardware-capability or environment gate.
4. Add the catalog section in [`patch/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py) with target symbol, Why, How, Related PR (or a reason there is none), and Future Plan.
5. Add unit and e2e coverage. If the patch wraps an upstream call, also add a guard for the upstream surface it depends on, in the style of `tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_balance_schedule.py`.

Related reading: [NPUPlatform and hardware capability profiles](platform-and-hardware-profiles.md) for the capability model the gates use, [Plugin registration and startup sequence](../workflows/plugin-bootstrap.md) for where in startup each tier fires, [Upstream vLLM integration surface](../integrations/upstream-vllm-interfaces.md) for the two version lanes, and [Scheduler variants](../workflows/scheduler-variants.md) for the balance/DyntraLB/profiling scheduler patches in context.

nodes.title: NPUPlatform and Hardware Capability Profiles
nodes.description: How vllm-ascend fixes the Ascend hardware family at build time, validates it against the runtime SoC, and turns identity into an immutable HardwareProfile whose families and HardwareCapability set drive attention backends, worker class, weight layout, MoE communication, CPU binding, and patch selection.
nodes.body:
# NPUPlatform and Hardware Capability Profiles

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../../vllm_ascend/device] file "../../vllm_ascend/device" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
Hardware identity in vllm-ascend is resolved exactly once per process and then never consulted directly by business code. Three modules under [`vllm_ascend/device/`](../../vllm_ascend/device) split the job: [`hardware.py`](../../vllm_ascend/device/hardware.py) turns SoC strings and numbers into an `AscendDeviceType`, [`device_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/device/device_config.py) reads the generated `_build_info` module into an immutable `DeviceConfig` and validates it against the live NPU, and [`hardware_profile.py`](../../vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py) maps that one enum value onto a frozen `HardwareProfile` — a table of implementation families plus a `frozenset[HardwareCapability]`.

Everything else in this page is a consumer of that third step. `NPUPlatform` answers vLLM's questions from the profile, the MoE layer picks its communication method from `moe_comm_policy`, `cpu_binding.py` picks its allocation strategy from `cpu_binding_mode` and two capabilities, and the patch packages decide which variant file to import from a capability. The rule the codebase is converging on, stated in `hardware.py`'s docstring and again as a comment above the compatibility helpers in `device_config.py`: **new business code asks the profile for a capability or family; it does not branch on device identity.**

## Identity is fixed at build time, checked at run time

The device family is a property of the installed wheel, not of the process. `setup.py` derives it during the build and writes it into a Python module; the runtime then asserts the wheel matches the machine it is running on.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ENV["SOC_VERSION env or npu-smi info"] --> CHIP["get_chip_type: Chip Name plus Chip Type or NPU Name"]
    CHIP --> SOC["envs.SOC_VERSION"]
    SOC --> MAP["device_type_from_soc_version in hardware.py"]
    MAP --> BI["_build_info.__device_type__ = A2 A3 A5 or _310P"]
    BI --> DC["get_device_config: DeviceConfig, lru_cached"]
    DC --> HP["get_hardware_profile: frozen HardwareProfile"]
    HP --> CUR["_CURRENT_HARDWARE_PROFILE resolved at import"]
    RT["torch_npu.npu.get_soc_version"] --> RTT["device_type_from_runtime_soc"]
    RTT --> CHK["check_ascend_device_type at NPUWorker init"]
    DC --> CHK
    CHK -->|mismatch| FAIL["RuntimeError: check your installation package"]
```

*The build writes a device-type string into the wheel; the worker validates it against the live `torch_npu` SoC version before constructing anything else.*

### Build-time path: `npu-smi` → `SOC_VERSION` → `_build_info`

`gen_build_info()` in [`setup.py`](../../setup.py) is invoked by the `build_py` and `develop` command subclasses, so an editable install regenerates it every time. It takes `envs.SOC_VERSION`, converts it through the *hardware module loaded directly from its file path* (`load_module_from_path`, because vllm-ascend is not installed yet at that point), and writes:

```python
# Auto-generated file
__device_type__ = 'A3'
```

Two details matter operationally. First, `vllm_ascend/_build_info.py` is gitignored — it exists only in a built tree, so a source checkout without an install fails at import with a plain `ImportError` rather than a confusing hardware guess. Second, if `SOC_VERSION` is unset, `get_chip_type()` shells out to `npu-smi info -l` and `npu-smi info -t board` (retrying with `-c 0` only when the board query has no `Chip Name`, as on A2/A3/310P), then normalizes the output into one of the keys of `_SOC_VERSION_TO_DEVICE_TYPE`: 310 names and 910B names become `chip_type + chip_name`, 910C and 950 names become `chip_name + "_" + npu_name`, and the HDK code name `a2g3` is hard-mapped to `ascend910b1`. On a CPU-only builder `npu-smi` is absent, `get_chip_type()` returns `""`, and `setup.py` raises with the exact `export SOC_VERSION=...` values per family. The installation guide and FAQ repeat those values (`ascend910b1`, `ascend910_9391`, `ascend310p1`, `ascend950dt_9582`), and the per-family Dockerfiles bake them in as `ARG SOC_VERSION`.

`hardware.py` is deliberately standard-library-only for this reason, and its docstring states the constraint as an invariant: device identity stays inside the device abstraction package, and `setup.py` must be able to import it before the package is installed.

The same `SOC_VERSION` string also drives the C++ build, independently of the Python enum: [`CMakeLists.txt`](../../CMakeLists.txt) skips `vllm_ascend_kernels` entirely for `ascend310p.*` and `ascend950`, removes the MLAPO and batch-matmul-transpose kernels for `ascend950`, and enables `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_SPARSE_KV_OFFLOAD` plus OpenMP only for `ascend910_93.*`. That is why the runtime mismatch check exists: the compiled `.so` and the Python profile come from the same string, and a wheel built for one family cannot be repaired by editing a config at runtime.

### Run-time path: `DeviceConfig` and the mismatch guard

`get_device_config()` is `lru_cache`d and reads `_build_info.__device_type__` by name (`AscendDeviceType[device_type]`), so the generated string must equal an enum member name verbatim — including the leading underscore of `_310P`. If the attribute is missing (a wheel built before the field existed), it falls back to `_build_info.__soc_version__`, defaulting to `ASCEND910B1`, and resolves it through the string table.

Import safety is an explicit design constraint: `device_config.py` never touches `torch_npu` while importing. The docstring says so, `tests/ut/device/test_device_config.py::test_import_time_config_does_not_probe_runtime` pins it by making `get_soc_version` raise, and the probe is deferred to `check_ascend_device_type()`:

- build-time family from `DeviceConfig`
- runtime family from `device_type_from_runtime_soc(torch_npu.npu.get_soc_version())`, which buckets the numeric SoC version: `220–225` → A2, `250–256` → A3, `200–205` → 310P, `260` → A5
- mismatch raises `RuntimeError("Current device type: ... does not match the installed version's device type: ... please check your installation package.")`

`NPUWorker.__init__` calls `check_ascend_device_type()` *before* `WorkerBase.__init__`, alongside `register_ascend_customop` and `init_ascend_config`. A wheel installed on the wrong silicon therefore fails at worker construction, before any kernel, weight layout, or graph decision is made on a false premise.

`device_config.py` still exports the identity-flavored compatibility API — `get_ascend_device_type()`, `is_310p()`, `is_950()` — but the comment above them marks them as compatibility surface. Real remaining users are a handful of sites: `lora/punica_npu.py` (single-slot LoRA fast path restricted to A2/A3), `quantization/methods/w8a8/fp8_block.py` (`is_950()` selecting the MXFP8 linear/MoE methods), the Minimax-M3 model files and `msa_m3` kernel dispatch, and three patch/runner sites using `is_310p()`. Everything newer goes through capabilities.

## The profile: a frozen record keyed by device type

`HardwareProfile` is a `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` whose fields are the private `_device_type`, the `default_worker_cls` dotted path, `capabilities: frozenset[HardwareCapability]`, and seven implementation-family enums: `attention_backend_family`, `cpu_binding_mode`, `device_adaptor_family`, `device_addressing_mode`, `weight_layout_policy`, `moe_comm_policy`, and `quantization_backend_family`. Its only method is `supports(capability) -> bool`.

The registry `_HARDWARE_PROFILES` is a `MappingProxyType` over all four enum members, so it cannot be mutated at runtime. `get_hardware_profile(device_type)` raises `RuntimeError(f"No hardware profile is registered for device type: ...")` for anything not in the map, and `tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py::test_every_device_type_has_a_profile` guarantees the mapping stays total as enum members are added.

`_CURRENT_HARDWARE_PROFILE = get_hardware_profile(get_device_config()._device_type)` runs at module import, and `get_current_hardware_profile()` just returns it. Two consequences:

1. It is a module-level constant, which is why `supports(...)` calls are safe inside `torch.compile`d code — `test_current_hardware_profile_is_dynamo_safe` compiles a function that branches on `HardwareCapability.RUNTIME_CUSTOM_OPS` with `fullgraph=True`.
2. A corrupt or unknown `_build_info` fails at import of `hardware_profile`, i.e. at plugin load, long before a worker exists.

### The four registered profiles

| | **A2** (`AscendDeviceType.A2`) | **A3** (`AscendDeviceType.A3`) | **310P** (`AscendDeviceType._310P`) | **A5** (`AscendDeviceType.A5`) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Typical SoC strings | `ascend910b1`, `ascend910b2/b3/b4`, `910b` | `ascend910_9391`, `910_9381/9372/9392/9382/9362/9363`, `910c` | `ascend310p1/p3/p5/p7`, `310p3vir01..08`, `310p` | anything containing `ascend950` |
| `attention_backend_family` | `STANDARD` | `STANDARD` | `COMPATIBILITY` → `vllm_ascend._310p.attention.attention_v1.AscendAttentionBackend310` | `STANDARD` |
| `device_adaptor_family` | `STANDARD` → `BaseDeviceAdaptor` | `STANDARD` → `BaseDeviceAdaptor` | `COMPATIBILITY` → `Ascend310PDeviceAdaptor` | `FP8_OPTIMIZED` → `A5DeviceAdaptor` |
| `quantization_backend_family` | `STANDARD` | `STANDARD` | `COMPATIBILITY` → `AscendModelSlimConfig310` | `STANDARD` |
| `weight_layout_policy` | `CONFIGURABLE` | `CONFIGURABLE` | `FORCE_NZ` | `CONFIGURABLE` |
| `moe_comm_policy` | `CAPACITY_AND_EXPERT_DENSITY` | `FUSED_OR_CAPACITY` | `ALLGATHER` | `CAPACITY_AND_WORLD_SIZE` |
| `cpu_binding_mode` | `TOPO_AFFINITY` | `GLOBAL_SLICE` | `TOPO_AFFINITY` | `TOPO_AFFINITY` (overridden by `CLUSTER_CPU_TOPOLOGY`) |
| `device_addressing_mode` | `DIRECT` | `DUAL_CHIP_CARD` | `DIRECT` | `DIRECT` |
| `default_worker_cls` | `vllm_ascend.worker.worker.NPUWorker` | same | `vllm_ascend._310p.worker_310p.NPUWorker310` | `vllm_ascend.worker.worker.NPUWorker` |
| Capability set | standard set + `NPU_TOP_K_TOP_P` | standard set + `MC2_FULLMESH_V2_COMM`, `CANN_MEGAMOE`, `MOE_DISPATCH_EXTRA_ARGS`, `NPU_TOP_K_TOP_P` | eight compatibility capabilities (no standard set) | 24-capability A5 set (no standard set) |

The "standard set" (`_STANDARD_CAPABILITIES`) is 17 capabilities shared by A2/A3; A3 adds one via `_A3_CAPABILITIES`. 310P and A5 are written as explicit frozensets rather than diffs, because their capability sets barely intersect the standard one. `tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py` restates all four tables and every capability set literally, so any profile edit fails a test until the expectation is updated — the profile is effectively schema-checked.

`AscendDeviceType` values are small integers (`A2=0, A3=1, _310P=2, A5=3`) and the leading underscore on `_310P` exists because the generated `_build_info` string is looked up as an enum member name.

## What each family's capability set actually decides

`HardwareCapability` declares 40 members and the four profiles between them reference every one; only `SWIGLU_OAI_MX_QUANT` (A5) currently has no consumer call site. The capability set is where the profile earns its keep, because a single field like `FP8_ATTENTION` is consulted from a dozen unrelated subsystems. Grouped by the decision a reader is trying to make:

**Attention backends.** `attention_backend_family` is the coarse switch inside `NPUPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls`. Before any family check, `_validate_fa3_backend` may return `vllm_ascend.attention.fa3_v1.AscendFABackend` when RL training-inference consistency is enabled and `flash_attn_npu_v3` is installed (GQA only; MLA/SFA raise). Otherwise, on `STANDARD` the platform chooses from the `(use_mla, use_sparse, use_compress)` key into `AscendMLABackend` / `AscendAttentionBackend` / `AscendSFABackend` / `AscendDSABackend`, with a separate PCP map that raises `NotImplementedError` for unmapped keys. On `COMPATIBILITY`, only the GQA non-sparse entry exists and every other key falls back to it, which is why `attention/indexer_kpool.py` raises `NotImplementedError("KPool sparse attention requires Ascend A2, A3 or A5.")` on the compatibility family. Finer behavior is capability-gated on top: `PAGED_ATTENTION` (A2/A3 only) gates `using_paged_attention()`; `FP8_ATTENTION` (A5 only) turns on FP8 KV/attention paths in MLA/DSA/SFA, the indexer, KV-c8 quantization, and `enable_fa_quant`; `CHUNKED_PREFILL_PHASE_SPLIT`, `MLA_DECODE_PROLOG_WITHOUT_ROPE`, `MLAPO_NATIVE_WEIGHTS`, `UNRESTRICTED_MLAPO`, `DSA_C128_STATE_SMALL_BLOCK_SIZES`, and `DSV4_COMPRESSED_CACHE` are all A5-only refinements. `SFA_DCP_REPLICATED_INDEXER` (in the standard set, so A2/A3 only) is validated in `_validate_parallel_config` and raises `NotImplementedError` when the user requests SFA DCP with a replicated indexer on a family that lacks it.

**MoE communication.** `moe_comm_policy` is not a direct answer — it selects a selector. `select_moe_comm_method()` in [`ascend_forward_context.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py) short-circuits to `ALLGATHER` when expert parallelism is off or EP world size is 1, forces `ALLTOALL` for LoRA + EP, short-circuits to `ALLGATHER` when the policy *is* `ALLGATHER` (310P), and otherwise indexes `_MOE_COMM_SELECTORS`:

| Policy | Families | Decision logic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CAPACITY_AND_EXPERT_DENSITY` | A2 | `MC2` when ≤24 experts/device, EP ≥ 16, and tokens ≤ MC2 capacity; else `ALLGATHER` |
| `FUSED_OR_CAPACITY` | A3 | `FUSED_MC2` when CANN MegaMoe applies or `enable_fused_mc2` with EP ≤ 32; else `MC2` under capacity; else `ALLTOALL` |
| `CAPACITY_AND_WORLD_SIZE` | A5 | `MC2` under capacity when world size > 1; `ALLGATHER` when world ≤ experts-per-token; else `ALLTOALL` |
| `ALLGATHER` | 310P | No selector; all-gather always |

The per-family capability set then changes the arguments: `MOE_DISPATCH_EXTRA_ARGS` (A3/A5) and `MOE_DISPATCH_SHARED_EXPERT_ARGS` (A5) make `TokenDispatcherWithMC2` pass extra and `expert_scales` arguments; `CANN_MEGAMOE` (A3) gates `use_cann_megamoe()`; `FUSED_MOE_COMPATIBILITY` (310P) swaps in `AscendGroupedTopKRouter310`; `MC2_HIERARCHY_COMM` (A2/A3 only) is required before `mc2_comm_alg = "hierarchy"` is accepted; `MC2_FULLMESH_V2_COMM` (A3 only) both validates `fullmesh_v2` and rewrites a plain `"fullmesh"` request to `"fullmesh_v1"` inside `get_mc2_comm_alg()`.

**Graph and compilation features.** `NPUGRAPH_EX` (A2/A3/A5, not 310P) is checked in `AscendCompilationConfig`'s after-validator, which forces `enable_npugraph_ex` off and cascades to `enable_static_kernel` and `enable_super_kernel`, warning separately for each field it clears. `GRAPH_NORM_QUANT_FUSION` and `GRAPH_MULS_ADD_FUSION` gate whether `GraphFusionPassManager` installs the norm-quant and muls-add fusion passes at all. `REDUCED_CUDAGRAPH_CAPTURE_SIZES` (A5 only) is consulted inside the piecewise-compilation branch of `_setup_compile_backend` and triggers `_prune_reduced_capture_sizes`, which downsamples a longer capture-size list to `MAX_REDUCED_CAPTURE_SIZES = 4` entries with an explicit "HDK incompatibility" warning and a dated removal TODO. `AUTO_ENABLE_CUSTOM_OPS` (A2/A3/A5) writes `custom_ops = ["all"]` into the compilation config, and `tests/ut/test_platform.py::test_check_and_update_config_310p_no_custom_ops` pins that 310P leaves it empty.

`AUTO_ENABLE_CUSTOM_OPS` and `RUNTIME_CUSTOM_OPS` are deliberately separate: A5 has the former but not the latter, so the compilation config is populated while `utils.enable_custom_op()` still returns `False` early — matching the in-code note that custom-op compilation and execution are only partially available on Ascend 950 and are temporarily disabled.

## `NPUPlatform` as the identity-mediated front door

[`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py) is the single `Platform` subclass vLLM resolves (`PlatformEnum.OOT`, `device_type = "npu"`, `dispatch_key = "PrivateUse1"`), and it is where most profile reads surface to upstream. Notably, `get_device_capability()` returns `None`: vLLM's usual upstream habit of branching on a numeric device capability has no analogue here, so capability questions have to be answered by the plugin's own profile instead. Its hardware-dependent answers are all mediated — `get_attn_backend_cls` and `pre_register_and_update` by family enums, `_setup_worker_and_scheduler` and `_setup_compile_backend` by worker/capability fields, `_validate_parallel_config` by capability checks that raise rather than silently degrade.

The platform also does the reverse job: it *removes* upstream options whose hardware assumption does not hold, via `_fix_incompatible_config` (cascade attention, `calculate_kv_scales`, `mm_encoder_attn_backend`, NVTX layerwise tracing, `max_num_partial_prefills`, speculative quantization, `kv_buffer_size`, `ray_workers_use_nsight`, `--numa-bind*`, `enable_dbo`, `ubatch_size`, and others), each with a warning naming the parameter and the reset value. Those corrections are not profile reads, but they belong to the same seam: everything that would otherwise be a scattered "does this box support X" test lands in the platform layer, and anything the platform cannot answer that way becomes a profile field or a capability.

## Consumers: who reads the profile, and when

Because the profile is resolved at import, consumers fall into three timing classes.

**Import-time / module-scope.** `device/device_op.py` binds `DeviceOperator = get_device_adaptor()` at import from `device_adaptor_family`, so every `DeviceOperator.xxx` call site is routed to `BaseDeviceAdaptor`, `A5DeviceAdaptor` (FP8-oriented fused-infer wrapper), or `Ascend310PDeviceAdaptor` (which emulates `index_fill` with a boolean mask because `index_fill_` is unavailable). `meta_registration.py` registers bgmv/sgmv expand meta kernels at import only when `BGMV_SGMV_META_REGISTRATION` holds. `patch/platform/__init__.py` imports `patch_mamba_config` or `patch_mamba_config_310` based on `STANDARD_MAMBA_PATCH`; `patch/platform/patch_distributed.py` applies the 310P all-reduce wrapper behind `DISTRIBUTED_COMMUNICATION_ADAPTATION`; `patch/worker/__init__.py` imports the Qwen3/Qwen3-VL patches or the 310P index/spec-decode patches based on `STANDARD_WORKER_PATCHES`, and re-overrides the draft ACL-graph manager for 310P after the standard one is installed. All of these run once per process, so the profile must already be correct at import.

**Config-time (`check_and_update_config` and `pre_register_and_update`).** `attention_backend_family` and `quantization_backend_family` branch imports and backend maps. `_setup_worker_and_scheduler` sets `parallel_config.worker_cls = hardware_profile.default_worker_cls` when the user left it as `"auto"` — but prefers `vllm_ascend.xlite.xlite_worker.XliteWorker` when `xlite_graph_config.enabled` *and* `STANDARD_WORKER_PATCHES` is supported, which is why Xlite is unavailable on 310P. The same function applies `AUTO_ENABLE_CUSTOM_OPS`. `_validate_parallel_config` enforces `SFA_DCP_REPLICATED_INDEXER`.

**Per-step.** `select_moe_comm_method` runs on every forward (and in `set_additional_forward_context` for the v2 runner). Attention code checks `FP8_ATTENTION`, `PAGED_ATTENTION`, `CHUNKED_PREFILL_PHASE_SPLIT`, `MLA_DECODE_PROLOG_WITHOUT_ROPE`, and `DSV4_COMPRESSED_CACHE` inside `forward`. `sample/sampler.py` binds `apply_top_k_top_p` at module scope to either the `npu_top_k_top_p` kernel or a sort-based PyTorch fallback, chosen by `NPU_TOP_K_TOP_P` — the in-code comment records that the NPU kernel degrades to 5–28 ms for large or mixed `k` while sort-and-mask stays near 1 ms. Weight loading checks `weight_layout_policy is FORCE_NZ` through `maybe_trans_nz`/`_should_keep_nd_for_compatibility_weight`, and `DYNAMIC_MX_QUANT_FUSION` in `linear.py`'s `weight_loader`. `worker/worker.py` checks `ATB_EXTENSIONS` in `__init__` before registering ATB kernels, `LOCAL_KV_COMM_RESOURCE` during device init, and `ATB_WARMUP` before calling `_warm_up_atb()`; 310P overrides `_warm_up_atb` to log and return.

### Weight layout

`WeightLayoutPolicy` has exactly two behaviors, both routed through [`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py)'s `_should_trans_nz`: `FORCE_NZ` (310P) converts any supported weight to `FRACTAL_NZ` regardless of configuration, while `CONFIGURABLE` defers to `additional_config.weight_nz_mode` (0 off, 1 for quantized only, 2 to include BF16/FP16). FP32 and meta tensors are never converted in either case. `ops/linear.py` adds a matching carve-out: under `FORCE_NZ`, weights whose last dimension is 1 stay `ND`, because the compatibility kernels cannot consume a degenerate NZ shape.

## CPU binding is profile-driven, including its failure modes

`bind_cpus(rank_id, npu_id)` is called from `NPUWorker` after the ATB warm-up and before the seed reset, but only when `additional_config.enable_cpu_binding` is true (default) and `platform.machine()` looks ARM. Exceptions are caught and downgraded to `Bind cpus failed ... Skip binding cpu.` — CPU binding is an optimization, never a correctness requirement. `NPUPlatform` additionally converts vLLM's unsupported `--numa-bind` into `{"enable_cpu_binding": true}` and drops `--numa-bind-nodes`/`--numa-bind-cpus` with an explanatory log.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START["CpuAlloc.run_all"] --> POOLS["build_cpu_pools"]
    POOLS --> CLUSTER{"supports CLUSTER_CPU_TOPOLOGY"}
    CLUSTER -->|yes, A5| A5["bind uvb_poll_window_threads then build cluster pools by NUMA"]
    CLUSTER -->|no| MODE{"cpu_binding_mode"}
    MODE -->|GLOBAL_SLICE, A3| SLICE["build_global_slice_cpu_pool: slice allowed_cpus by global NPU id"]
    MODE -->|TOPO_AFFINITY, A2 and 310P| TOPO["npu-smi topo affinity per NPU plus NUMA extension"]
    TOPO -->|no topo data| SLICE
    A5 --> ROLES["allocate: whole cluster to main thread"]
    SLICE --> ROLES2["allocate: main, acl and release split"]
    TOPO --> ROLES2
    ROLES --> BIND["bind_threads, then bind_memory, then bind_npu_irq"]
    ROLES2 --> BIND
```

*Three allocation strategies selected by one enum field plus one capability; A5 bypasses the mode field entirely.*

The three strategies and their guards:

- **`GLOBAL_SLICE`** (A3) divides the process's `Cpus_allowed_list` by the *global* logical NPU count rather than by the visible NPUs, so multiple DP groups sharing one cpuset never overlap. It rejects an NPU id ≥ `total_npus` and raises `RuntimeError("Insufficient CPUs for binding ...")` when the per-NPU slice would fall below the role minimum.
- **`TOPO_AFFINITY`** (A2, 310P) reads `npu-smi info -t topo`, extends the affinity set with the next NUMA node's allowed CPUs, and averages CPU groups shared by several NPUs. Non-visible NPUs that overlap this process's cpuset are included in the computation purely to avoid collisions, then dropped from the final pool. An empty topo map logs a warning and falls back to global-slice rather than failing.
- **`CLUSTER_CPU_TOPOLOGY`** (A5 only) takes priority over `cpu_binding_mode`. `build_ascend_950_cpu_pools()` derives a cluster size from `lscpu`'s threads-per-core (`8 * threads`), requires one thread per core value in `{1, 2}`, assigns one contiguous cluster per NPU per NUMA node, and binds the `uvb_poll_window_thread` threads (warning, with a `--pid=host` hint, when they are invisible). Every failure path here returns `False`, which makes `run_all()` skip allocation, printing, thread binding *and* IRQ binding — no fallback.

Role allocation depends on one more capability. `IRQ_CPU_RESERVATION` (A2/A3/310P) reserves `MIN_CPUS_PER_NPU = 5` CPUs per NPU — two IRQ CPUs at the head, then `main`, `acl`, and `release` — and `bind_npu_irq()` pins `sq_send_trigger_irq` and its successor to those first two CPUs after stopping `irqbalance`. Without it (A5), `_min_cpus_per_npu()` drops to 3, `bind_npu_irq()` logs and returns immediately, and A5 role allocation puts the whole cluster in the main thread with empty `acl`/`release` sets. The IRQ path also exercises `device_addressing_mode`: on `DUAL_CHIP_CARD` (A3) a logical NPU maps to `card = npu // 2`, `chip = npu % 2` when querying board PCIe info, while `DIRECT` uses the NPU id as the card id. A non-writable `/proc/irq` logs the `--privileged=true` hint and returns, and a missing `sq_send_trigger_irq`, absent `msi_irqs` directory, or CPU pool smaller than two all warn and skip rather than raise.

`310P` exposes `RC_DEVICE_DISCOVERY`, consumed by `utils.is_rc_device()`: it runs `lspci` once, caches the answer, and reports whether the part is a Root-Complex device (Atlas 200I Pro, host and NPU sharing memory) rather than a PCIe endpoint (Atlas 300I DUO). `NPUWorker310.determine_available_memory` uses it to switch its free-memory source from `torch.npu.mem_get_info()` to `psutil.virtual_memory()` and to halve the KV budget; `NPUModelRunner310` branches on it for several allocation paths; and `patch_idex_310` installs RC-only Qwen3-VL/GDN patches when it is true.

## Extension points and failure semantics

**Adding a SoC family.** Four coordinated edits: an `AscendDeviceType` member (its *name* becomes the `_build_info` value), entries in both `_SOC_VERSION_TO_DEVICE_TYPE` and `device_type_from_runtime_soc` (the numeric bucket is what the runtime guard checks), a `HardwareProfile` in `_HARDWARE_PROFILES`, and updated expectations in `tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py` plus `tests/ut/device/test_device_config.py`. Adding a family with an unregistered profile is not silently tolerated: `get_hardware_profile` raises, and `test_every_device_type_has_a_profile` fails first.

**Adding a hardware-conditional behavior.** Add a `HardwareCapability` member, set it on the profiles that have it, and gate the call site on `get_current_hardware_profile().supports(...)`. Do not add a `device_type == ...` branch — the surviving identity checks (`is_310p()` in three patch/v2-runner sites, `get_ascend_device_type()` in the Minimax-M3 files and the LoRA punica wrapper, `is_950()` in the FP8-block quantization method) are legacy surface, and the comment above the helpers marks the API as compatibility-only.

**Failure modes to expect, keyed to the layer that detects them:**

| Symptom | Raised by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Undefined soc_version: ... Please file an issue` | `device_type_from_soc_version` | `npu-smi` produced a chip name the string table does not know |
| `Could not determine chip type automatically via 'npu-smi'` | `setup.py` | no NPU visible at build time and `SOC_VERSION` unset |
| `Unsupported built-in device type: ...` | `_device_type_from_build_info` | `_build_info.__device_type__` from a newer/older wheel |
| `No hardware profile is registered for device type: ...` | `get_hardware_profile` | enum member added without a profile; fails at plugin import |
| `Cannot support runtime soc_version: ...` | `device_type_from_runtime_soc` | new silicon with no numeric bucket |
| `Current device type: X does not match the installed version's device type: Y` | `check_ascend_device_type` (worker init) | wrong wheel for this machine — rebuild with the right `SOC_VERSION` |
| `... is not supported by the current hardware profile` | `AscendConfig` validators, `_validate_parallel_config`, `ascend_config._validate_mc2_comm_alg` | user requested a feature this family lacks (`fullmesh_v2`, `hierarchy`, SFA DCP replicated indexer) |

## Focused tests

- [`tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py`](../../tests/ut/device/test_hardware_profile.py) — the implementation matrix (all nine non-capability fields for all four families), the exact capability set per family with a per-capability `supports()` cross-check, `get_current_hardware_profile() is get_hardware_profile(get_device_config()._device_type)`, dynamo safety under `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)`, rejection of unregistered types, and totality over `AscendDeviceType`.
- [`tests/ut/device/test_device_config.py`](../../tests/ut/device/test_device_config.py) — string and numeric SoC mappings, build-info precedence, the legacy `__soc_version__` fallback, the no-runtime-probe-on-import guarantee, and both directions of the mismatch check.
- [`tests/ut/device_allocator/test_cpu_binding.py`](../../tests/ut/device_allocator/test_cpu_binding.py) — patches `vllm_ascend.cpu_binding.get_current_hardware_profile` with each profile to exercise slice arithmetic, A5 cluster assignment with hidden global NPUs, A5 IRQ skip, A3 dual-chip-card IRQ addressing, and the insufficient-CPU errors.
- [`tests/ut/test_platform.py`](../../tests/ut/test_platform.py) — `worker_cls` resolution (default vs Xlite), 310P leaving `custom_ops` empty, and profile-patched config-time behaviour.
- [`tests/ut/conftest.py`](../../tests/ut/conftest.py) injects a fake `vllm_ascend._build_info` module with `__device_type__ = "A2"`, which is how the whole CPU test suite runs without a built wheel.

## Related pages

- [System architecture overview](overview.md) — where the profile sits among the plugin's domains.
- [Patching architecture](patching-architecture.md) — how capability-gated patch selection fits the catalog contract.
- [Attention backend selection](../concepts/attention-backends.md) — the backend map behind `attention_backend_family`.
- [Performance tuning](../operations/performance-tuning.md) — `enable_cpu_binding`, `mc2_comm_alg`, `weight_nz_mode`, and the other knobs whose validity depends on the profile.

nodes.title: Attention Backend Selection and Implementations
nodes.description: How vLLM-Ascend maps a model's attention shape (GQA, MLA, sparse SFA, compressed DSA, FA3) onto a concrete NPU attention backend, and how each backend's metadata builder, KV-layout contract, and AscendC operator path fit together - including the couples that make metadata builders part of the ACL graph contract.
nodes.body:
# Attention Backend Selection and Implementations

Attention on Ascend is not a single kernel with a flag; it is a small family of backends, each of which ships three things: a **backend class** that owns the KV-cache layout and block-size contract, a **metadata builder** that turns the batch into per-layer tensors, and an **implementation class** that issues one specific AscendC operator (FIA, paged attention, sparse flash attention, lightning indexer). `NPUPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls` picks the family member once, from the model/attention shape; everything after that is per-backend.

The page assumes the hardware-family machinery described in [NPUPlatform and Hardware Capability Profiles](../architecture/platform-and-hardware-profiles.md), and the graph mechanics described in [Graph Mode and Compilation](graph-mode-and-compilation.md).

## `get_attn_backend_cls`: the single decision point

[`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L226-L267) is the only place that decides which backend a model runs on. It builds a three-element key from the selector config and then consults three different maps, in a fixed order:

```python
use_compress = getattr(attn_selector_config, "use_compress", False)
use_mla = attn_selector_config.use_mla
use_sparse = attn_selector_config.use_sparse
key = (use_mla, use_sparse)
backend_key = (*key, use_compress)
```

`use_compress` is read with `getattr(..., False)` so a selector config that predates the field (or a test double that only sets `use_mla`/`use_sparse`/`use_pcp`) still resolves.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SEL["AttentionSelectorConfig: use_mla, use_sparse, use_compress, use_pcp"] --> KEY["key = use_mla, use_sparse, use_compress"]
    KEY --> FA{"use_pcp false and FA3 validation passes"}
    FA -->|"yes"| FA3["fa3_v1.AscendFABackend"]
    FA -->|"no"| FAM{"attention_backend_family"}
    FAM -->|"COMPATIBILITY"| COMP["compatibility map on 2-tuple key, always yields AscendAttentionBackend310"]
    FAM -->|"STANDARD"| PCP{"use_pcp"}
    PCP -->|"yes"| PMAP["pcp_backend_map on 3-tuple"]
    PMAP -->|"unmapped key"| ERR["NotImplementedError: Ascend MRV2 PCP does not support this backend"]
    PMAP -->|"hit"| BACK["mla_v1 / attention_v1 / sfa_v1 / dsa_v1 backend class"]
    PCP -->|"no"| MAP["backend_map on 3-tuple"]
    MAP --> BACK
```

*Selection order: FA3 override, then the 310P compatibility family, then the PCP map, then the standard map.*

The three maps differ in more than their contents:

| Map | Key | Behavior on an unknown key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend_map` | 3-tuple | plain `KeyError` — `(False, True, *)` and `(False, False, True)` are simply absent |
| `pcp_backend_map` | 3-tuple | raises `NotImplementedError("Ascend MRV2 PCP does not support attention backend ...")` |
| `compatibility_backend_map` | 2-tuple (`use_mla`, `use_sparse`) | falls back to `(False, False)` — the only entry that exists |

The standard and PCP maps currently contain the same four entries, so a model's backend is unchanged by PCP; what PCP changes is *which implementation and builder* the class resolves (see "The triple" below) plus the slot-mapping expansion the builder performs. The compatibility map carries the TODO comments for hypothetical `AscendMLABackend310`/`AscendSFABackend310` entries and today maps every key to the 310P GQA backend. `AttentionBackendFamily` is `COMPATIBILITY` only for the `_310P` profile, so the fallback is effectively "310P always runs the compatibility GQA backend".

### The FA3 override

Before any map is consulted — and before the hardware family is checked — `_validate_fa3_backend(key, attn_selector_config)` in [`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L1349-L1374) can return `vllm_ascend.attention.fa3_v1.AscendFABackend`. It is gated on RL training-inference consistency, not on a user backend choice:

- `ascend_config.rl_config.enabled` and `rl_config.enable_training_consistency` must both be true, otherwise it logs and returns `False` (the note in the log says Ascend will use its registered plugin backend);
- the key must be `(False, False)` — `raise ValueError("FA3 backend does not support MLA and SFA.")`;
- `flash_attn_npu_v3` must be importable (`util.find_spec`) and must expose `flash_attn_with_kvcache`, else `ValueError` with an install/upgrade hint.

The user-facing `att_config.backend` field is deliberately reset to `None` during config validation with a log line saying Ascend uses its registered plugin backend, precisely because FA3 is selected here rather than through that field ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L759-L768)).

## The triple: backend class, metadata builder, implementation

Every backend class is a thin contract object registered with vLLM. `AscendAttentionBackend` is registered as `AttentionBackendEnum.CUSTOM` / `"ASCEND"` ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L78-L149)); the 310P variant re-registers under the same name in its own module. What matters for this page is that all three pieces are produced by static factory methods on the backend class, so *which* backend you selected determines the whole pipeline.

| Backend class | `get_name()` | KV cache shape (kernel view) | Kernel block sizes | Builder / impl selection |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AscendAttentionBackend` (GQA) | `CUSTOM` | `(2, num_blocks, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size)` | `[128]` | `AscendAttentionMetadataBuilder` / `AscendAttentionBackendImpl`, swapped for the DCP pair when `decode_context_parallel_size > 1` |
| `AscendMLABackend` | `ASCEND_MLA` | `(num_blocks, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size)` | `[128]` | `AscendMLAMetadataBuilder` / `AscendMLAImpl`, DCP pair when DCP is on |
| `AscendSFABackend` | `ASCEND_SFA` | `(num_blocks, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size)` | `[128]` | `resolve_sfa_metadata_builder` / `resolve_sfa_impl`, or the sparse-KV-offload pair |
| `AscendDSABackend` (+ C4 / C128 / SWA / state subclasses) | `ASCEND_DSA`, `ASCEND_DSA_C4`, ... | `(num_blocks, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size)` | `[2..128]`, and per-subclass contracts below | `AscendDSAMetadataBuilder` / `AscendDSAImpl`, DSACP or PCP pair |
| `AscendFABackend` (FA3) | `CUSTOM` | same 5-D GQA shape | `[128]` | reuses `AscendAttentionMetadataBuilder`, with `AscendFAImpl` |
| `_310p` `AscendAttentionBackend310` | `CUSTOM` | `(2, num_blocks, (num_kv_heads * head_size) // 16, block_size, 16)` | `[128, 64]` | `AscendAttentionMetadataBuilder310` / `AscendAttentionBackendImpl310` |

Two invariants fall out of the table and matter when you change a backend:

1. **The KV shape is a kernel contract, not a storage detail.** 310P splits the head dimension into `(kv_heads * head_size) // 16` and a 16-wide tail so pages stay aligned; MLA-shaped backends drop the leading `2` because latent KV is one fused tensor. Changing `get_kv_cache_shape` invalidates every cached slot mapping and every block table built against it — see [KV Cache and Block Layout](kv-cache-and-block-layout.md).
2. **Block sizes feed `select_common_block_size`.** Builders for SFA and the SFA indexer call `select_common_block_size(kv_cache_spec.block_size, [backend])` and use the result as `kernel_block_size` ([`sfa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py#L396-L397), [`indexer.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/indexer.py#L480-L481)), and the model runner does the same when it derives `kernel_block_sizes` ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5442-L5452)). A backend that advertises a size the KV planner cannot satisfy silently changes per-layer page geometry.

`AscendAttentionBackend.supports_pcp()` is an identity check (`cls.get_impl_cls() is AscendAttentionBackendImpl`) rather than an inheritance check, so the 310P subclass and the DCP/FA3 impls do not inherit a PCP capability they do not implement ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L102-L107), pinned by `test_supports_pcp_only_for_main_implementation`).

## Metadata builders: what they produce and what they must not do

A builder is fed vLLM's `AscendCommonAttentionMetadata` (a `CommonAttentionMetadata` subclass carrying CPU mirrors `seq_lens_cpu`, `_seq_lens_cpu`, `num_computed_tokens_cpu`, positions, `attn_state`, `graph_pad_size`, `num_input_tokens`, DCP metadata, and the offload request/token tensors — [`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py#L279-L326)) and emits a per-layer metadata dataclass. The builders share a common skeleton even though their dataclasses differ:

- **Phase split.** `split_decodes_and_prefills` classifies the batch assuming the decode → short-extend → long-extend → prefill order and returns `(num_decodes, num_prefills, num_decode_tokens, num_prefill_tokens)` ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py#L412-L500)). `decode_threshold` is `1` plus `num_speculative_tokens`, and every builder asserts `decode_threshold <= 16` with the message that this is the FIA TND layout limit ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L248-L259), same assert in `mla_v1.py`, `dsa_v1.py`, `sfa_v1.py`).
- **CPU sequence lengths, not GPU round-trips.** Builders prefer `_seq_lens_cpu` (populated in async speculative decoding) over `seq_lens_cpu`, and only fall back to a device→host copy. SFA's NoPE path skips the CPU copy entirely because its operators take device lengths.
- **Masks and rope tables.** Masks come from the singleton `AttentionMaskBuilder`: causal batches get the splitfuse mask, non-causal batches get `None` because FIA would treat a provided mask as a `defaultMask`, and pooling runners get a boolean causal mask ([`attention_mask.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_mask.py#L33-L70)). MLA/SFA/DSA builders materialize `cos`/`sin` themselves, since RoPE runs *inside* the attention impl.
- **FIA shape padding.** The GQA builder pads `seq_lens_list`, the `seq_lens` tensor, and the block table up to the query-derived FIA batch size, because the model runner inserts a dummy padding request to satisfy the TND constraint (`sum(q_lens) == hidden_states.shape[0]`) and the seq/block buffers are only `max_num_reqs` wide; otherwise FIA fails with error `561002` ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L350-L382)).
- **PCP finalization.** With PCP enabled, `_finalize_pcp_metadata` validates that the expanded slot mapping divides evenly by the PCP world size, stores `pcp_local_num_input_tokens` (and, for MLA, rank-local prefill start/end), and forces `ChunkedPrefill` whenever the batch contains prefill work so it takes the chunked path instead of the decode graph path ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L416-L437), [`mla_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/mla_v1.py#L525-L558)).

### Graph-capture entry points are part of the builder API

Each builder exposes a capture-time variant in addition to `build`:

- `build_for_graph_capture(...)`: GQA accepts `DecodeOnly`, `ChunkedPrefill` and `SpecDecoding` and raises `NotImplementedError` for anything else; MLA, SFA and DSA accept only `DecodeOnly`/`SpecDecoding` ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L439-L459), [`mla_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/mla_v1.py#L743-L759), [`sfa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py#L604-L618), [`dsa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v1.py#L1442-L1461)).
- `build_for_cudagraph_capture(...)`: SFA and DSA forward straight to `build`; the runner prefers it when capturing but routes DSA/DSA-CP/SFA-DCP builders through plain `build` with extra arguments (`num_actual_reqs`, `common_ratio_to_sas_metadata`, `full_graph_mode`) ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3522-L3542)).
- `get_cudagraph_support(...)` declares the capture contract: GQA returns `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`; MLA, SFA, DSA and the SFA indexer return `UNIFORM_BATCH` ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L265-L273), [`mla_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/mla_v1.py#L321-L329), [`sfa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py#L445-L453), [`dsa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v1.py#L724-L732)).

### Why a builder change can invalidate captured graphs

Metadata tensors are not consumed once and thrown away: the captured op is *patched* on every replay with the current step's metadata. `AscendAttentionBackendImpl.update_graph_params` walks `forward_context.attn_metadata`, reads each layer's `seq_lens`, `block_tables`, and (for MLA) `decode.block_table` / `decode.actual_seq_lengths_q`, and re-issues the operator inside `torch.npu.graph_task_update_begin/end` ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L521-L620), [`mla_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/mla_v1.py#L854-L970)). `acl_graph.update_full_graph_params` is the entry point that resolves the impl class under `set_current_vllm_config` and calls it ([`acl_graph.py`](../../vllm_ascend/compilation/acl_graph.py#L304-L336)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Runner as NPUModelRunner
    participant Builder as MetadataBuilder
    participant Impl as BackendImpl
    participant Graph as ACLGraphWrapper
    Runner->>Builder: build_for_graph_capture or build_for_cudagraph_capture
    Builder-->>Runner: metadata tensors, buffers sized for the capture grid
    Runner->>Impl: forward under capture, appends attn_params, handle, event
    Graph->>Graph: capture NPUGraph per batch descriptor
    Runner->>Impl: update_graph_params before each replay
    Impl->>Impl: graph_task_update_begin, re-issue op from live metadata, end
    Graph->>Graph: replay
```

*Metadata tensors built at capture time are re-read on every replay, so builder output shapes, dtypes, and buffer identity are part of the graph contract.*

This produces concrete, checkable invariants for anyone editing a builder:

- **Stable addresses.** Buffers whose pointer is captured must not be reallocated per step. DSA preallocates `sas_metadata_buffer`, `qli_metadata_buffer`, `qli_seqused_k`, `dspark_swa_indices_buffer` and sizes per-request buffers for `max(max_num_seqs, max_cudagraph_capture_size) + 1` so graph-mode padding and the FIA dummy request fit ([`dsa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v1.py#L672-L701)). `build_dspark_swa_indices` documents the same requirement: writing into a supplied buffer keeps the `ori_sparse_indices` pointer stable across async replays ([`dsa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v1.py#L416-L437)).
- **Fixed shapes.** `scatter_paged_cache` and the DSA slot-mapping formatter keep static shapes and write padding rows to a sentinel so a captured scatter stays valid ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py#L83-L111), [`dsa_attn_kv_plan.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_attn_kv_plan.py#L102-L123)).
- **No host synchronization inside `build`.** SFA's NoPE metadata deliberately passes scheduler CPU scalars (`max_query_len`, `max_seq_len`) instead of device `max()` results to avoid a per-build sync ([`sfa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py#L75-L104)).
- **Dtype/shape changes are breaking.** The captured op's parameter tuple (recorded in `graph_params.attn_params[num_tokens]`) is unpacked positionally by `update_graph_params`; adding a field in the middle shifts every later argument.

## Operator paths inside the implementations

### GQA: paged attention or FIA

`AscendAttentionBackendImpl.forward_impl` chooses between two operators per step: paged attention when the batch is `DecodeOnly`, has no sliding window, and `using_paged_attention(...)` returns true; otherwise fused infer attention ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L1716-L1737)).

`using_paged_attention` is itself a capability gate ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py#L237-L253)): speculative decoding disables it, the hardware profile must expose `PAGED_ATTENTION` (A2/A3 only), `cudagraph_mode` must be `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, and the runtime shape must be listed in `ascend_config.pa_shape_list`. A 512-dim head (`FIA_TND_LARGE_HEAD_FALLBACK_HEAD_SIZE`) short-circuits to PA because prefill is handled by the device adaptor instead.

The FIA path issues `npu_fused_infer_attention_score` (or `_v2` when learnable sinks are present) in TND layout, selecting `sparse_mode` from causality and sliding window: `0` for non-causal, `4` with `pre_tokens=sliding_window` for SWA, `3` for the default causal case ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L1386-L1492)). On A5 — or whenever `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is set — a mixed `ChunkedPrefill` batch is split into one decode FIA call and one prefill FIA call so prefill and decode never share a kernel invocation ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L1447-L1489), [`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L1494-L1530)). During capture, `forward_fused_infer_attention` diverts to `full_graph_fia` / `full_graph_fia_v2`, which allocate or reuse a per-`num_tokens` workspace (max-workspace caching when layers have mixed shapes) and append the op parameters to `GraphParams` ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L1100-L1215), [`acl_graph.py`](../../vllm_ascend/compilation/acl_graph.py#L330-L360)).

Late-bound hooks let quantization change the implementation without changing the backend: `AscendC8KVCacheAttentionMethod.create_weights` performs class surgery on the per-layer impl (`layer.impl.__class__ = AscendC8AttentionBackendImpl`) so C8/INT8 KV layers automatically take the INT8 forward path ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L1811-L1818), [`kv_c8.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/kv_cache/kv_c8.py#L119-L131)).

### MLA: preprocess, split, one FIA v2 per phase

`AscendMLAImpl.forward` runs the whole MLA pipeline: optional fused preprocess (`prolog_v3` or MLAPO) or native projection, then decode and/or prefill attention, then `o_proj` ([`mla_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/mla_v1.py#L2036-L2122)). Decode uses `npu_fused_infer_attention_score_v2` with `query_rope`/`key_rope` operands and a paged latent cache; prefill (`_forward_prefill`) and chunked context (`ChunkedContextMetadata`) handle the uncached suffix with a workspace sized by `ascend_chunked_prefill_workspace_size`. `forward_mha`/`forward_mqa` raise, because MLA does not use the upstream MHA/MQA entry points.

Upstream's `MLAPrefillBackend` would assert `flash_attn_varlen_func` availability on Ascend; [`patch_mla_prefill_backend.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_mla_prefill_backend.py) installs a no-op `AscendMLAPrefillBackend` so `MLAAttention.__init__` completes while the real prefill stays in `impl.forward()`.

### SFA: indexer top-k, then sparse flash attention

`AscendSFABackend` resolves its builder and impl through helpers rather than a fixed class, because CP layouts compose independently ([`sfa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py#L264-L303), [`sfa_cp.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/context_parallel/sfa_cp.py#L1518-L1551)):

- sparse KV offload enabled → `AscendSFAKVOffloadMetadataBuilder` / `AscendSFAKVOffloadImpl`, which add the decode split and per-request identity for the resident LRU ([`sfa_kv_offload.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_kv_offload.py#L89-L160));
- otherwise `resolve_sfa_metadata_builder` / `resolve_sfa_impl` combine DSA-CP, SFA-DCP (replicated indexer) and PCP into four composite classes, falling back to `AscendSFAMetadataBuilder` / `AscendSFAImpl`.

The forward is one shared template with overridable hooks (`_prepare_parallel_metadata`, `_prepare_kv_for_parallel`, `_store_parallel_kv`, `_get_parallel_forward_context`, `_finalize_o_proj`) that the CP variants override ([`sfa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py#L1412-L1445)). The stages are: preprocess (fused `prolog_v3`/MLAPO for decode-sized batches, native otherwise) → main KV store → indexer k-path, cache write and top-k selection → sparse attention → `v_up_proj`/gate → `o_proj` ([`sfa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py#L1546-L1766)).

The operator choice is data-driven, not flag-driven:

- `_execute_sparse_flash_attention_process` returns `sparse_mla(...)` for NoPE layers (`qk_rope_head_dim == 0`); otherwise `DeviceOperator.execute_sparse_flash_attention_process` picks `npu_kv_quant_sparse_flash_attention` when the KV cache dtype is `int8`/`float8_e4m3fn`/`float8_e5m2`, and plain `npu_sparse_flash_attention` for BF16/FP16 ([`sfa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py#L1323-L1346), [`device_op.py`](../../vllm_ascend/device/device_op.py#L389-L494)). The dispatch is on the actual tensor dtype so fallback and test paths that pass a non-quantized cache still work.
- `sparse_mla` has two implementations of its own: A5 uses the CANN `SparseFlashMla` pair via the adapter in [`sparse_flash_mla.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sparse_flash_mla.py#L36-L62) with a persistent metadata buffer, and A2/A3 use `npu_sparse_flash_attention`, re-viewing over-large hybrid pages into C128 pages and masking unwritten graph rows to zero ([`sfa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py#L106-L162)).

The indexer is a *separate attention layer*, not an inline helper: `AscendSFAIndexerBackend` is both an `AttentionBackend` (engine side: builder selection, cache shape `(num_blocks, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size)`, kernel block size `[128]`) and an `nn.Module` (model side: k path, cache persistence, top-k) ([`indexer.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/indexer.py#L79-L150)). Its builder emits its own metadata and the SFA impl composes the main and indexer cache tuples at forward time ([`indexer.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/indexer.py#L459-L534), [`sfa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py#L1447-L1516)). Two consequences: layers that share another layer's top-k (`skip_topk`, `use_index_cache`, `indexer_types: shared`) still run the k path and cache write with `compute_topk=False`, and a missing indexer metadata for the expected prefix raises rather than silently degrading.

### DSA: compressed KV, SWA and a planner

DSA is the DeepSeek-V4 family. Its builder/impl selection is driven by *parallel mode*, and its cache geometry by *compress ratio*:

- `AscendDSABackend.get_builder_cls` / `get_impl_cls` raise when legacy DSACP and PCP are both on, otherwise return the DSACP, PCP, or plain trio ([`dsa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v1.py#L217-L265)).
- The concrete backend class is chosen by the attention layer itself, not by `get_attn_backend_cls`: `DSAAttention.__init__` assigns `AscendDSAC4Backend` for `compress_ratio == 4`, `AscendDSAC128Backend` for `128`, and `AscendDSASWABackend` otherwise; the compressor-state layers use `AscendDSAC4StateBackend`/`AscendDSAC128StateBackend` ([`layer.py`](../../vllm_ascend/models/layer/attention/layer.py#L127-L132), [`dsa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v1.py#L272-L325)). Subclasses only override `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`, expressing Ascend's physical page in scheduler ("raw token") units: C4 pages of 32/64/128 represent 128/256/512 tokens, C128 pages represent 4096/8192/16384, SWA stays `[32, 64, 128]`, and the state backends use `[2, 4, 8]` or hardware-dependent `[4, 8, 16]`/`[8, 16, 32]`.
- The operator plan lives in [`dsa_attn_kv_plan.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_attn_kv_plan.py#L138-L182): non-A5 gets `PA_ND` with `npu_sparse_attn_sharedkv` and block-offset slot mapping; A5 BF16 KV gets `PA_BBND` with the `SparseFlashMla` adapter; A5 FP8 KV gets `PA_ND` with `npu_kv_quant_sparse_attn_sharedkv` (`kv_quant_mode=1`, `tile_size=64`, `rope_head_dim=64`) and the `kv_compress_epilog` scatter.
- Metadata is per cache group, not per layer: the builder memoizes compressor metadata on the forward context under `cache_group_key` so `compressor_metadata` runs once per group per substep ([`dsa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v1.py#L92-L144)), and the impl resolves each layer's attention/SWA/compressor/indexer metadata from the shared dict ([`dsa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v1.py#L1532-L1566)).

### FA3

`AscendFABackend` exists only for the RL training-consistency case. It reuses `AscendAttentionMetadataBuilder` and the GQA 5-D cache shape, and `AscendFAImpl.forward_impl` splits the batch into decode and prefill calls to `flash_attn_with_kvcache` ([`fa3_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/fa3_v1.py#L42-L144)). Its constructor rejects two configurations loudly: sliding-window attention, and ACL graph capture with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` while `enforce_eager` is false.

## 310P: the compatibility family

On the `_310P` profile, `attention_backend_family` is `COMPATIBILITY` and `get_attn_backend_cls` returns `vllm_ascend._310p.attention.attention_v1.AscendAttentionBackend310` for every key. That backend is a genuine sibling implementation, not a shim:

- a different `get_kv_cache_shape` (16-aligned pages) and block sizes `[128, 64]` ([`_310p/attention/attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/_310p/attention/attention_v1.py#L47-L99));
- a 310P mask builder (`FRACTAL_NZ`, compressed `[2048, 2048]` variants) installed over the base one, plus pinned host `query_lens_cpu` for ATB splitfuse and device-side `seq_lens` binding before graph capture ([`_310p/attention/metadata_builder.py`](../../vllm_ascend/_310p/attention/metadata_builder.py#L51-L148));
- a state-machine `forward_impl`: `PrefillNoCache` → `_npu_flash_attention`/`_npu_flash_attention_v3`, `DecodeOnly` → `_npu_paged_attention`, `ChunkedPrefill`/`PrefillCacheHit`/`SpecDecoding` → `_npu_paged_attention_splitfuse` or the `_v2` compressed-mask variant, and any other state raises `NotImplementedError` ([`_310p/attention/attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/_310p/attention/attention_v1.py#L112-L353)).

Because those paths require metadata already on device, both paged attention and splitfuse explicitly raise if `seq_lens` is still on host *during* capture ("move it outside `torch.npu.graph()`") rather than performing a pageable H2D inside a captured graph. The runner is the enforcement point for what 310P cannot do at all: `_allocate_kv_cache_tensors` rejects KV transfer, sparse attention, and MLA with distinct errors ([`_310p/model_runner_310p.py`](../../vllm_ascend/_310p/model_runner_310p.py#L700-L709)), and the KPool indexer additionally rejects the compatibility family and PCP/DCP ([`indexer_kpool.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/indexer_kpool.py#L344-L356)).

## Extension points and failure modes

To add or change a backend, the touch points are:

1. **Selection.** Extend `backend_map`/`pcp_backend_map` (and, if it should exist on 310P, `compatibility_backend_map`) in `get_attn_backend_cls`. Remember the 3-tuple key: a new `use_compress`-style dimension must be threaded into every map at once.
2. **The class contract.** Implement `get_name`, `get_kv_cache_shape`, `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`, `get_builder_cls`, `get_impl_cls`; use `@register_backend(AttentionBackendEnum.CUSTOM, "ASCEND")` if the backend must satisfy lookups by the plugin name. `supports_pcp` must be an identity or explicit check.
3. **The builder.** Implement `build`, `build_for_graph_capture` (and `build_for_cudagraph_capture` if the runner should use it), `reorder_batch`, `get_cudagraph_support`, and keep any captured-buffer allocation at construction time with graph-grid sizing.
4. **The impl.** Add a `update_graph_params` classmethod if the operator participates in ACL graph replay, mirroring `AscendSFABackend.update_graph_params` which is a deliberate no-op because SFA needs no parameter patching ([`sfa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py#L742-L752)).

Common failure signatures, and what they mean:

| Symptom | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `NotImplementedError: Ascend MRV2 PCP does not support attention backend ...` | PCP enabled with a key absent from `pcp_backend_map` (e.g. GQA + sparse) |
| `KeyError` out of `backend_map` | selector produced a key the standard path never implemented |
| `ValueError: FA3 backend does not support MLA and SFA.` / "flash_attn_npu_v3 is not installed" | RL consistency enabled but the model or the environment cannot use FA3 |
| FIA error `561002` about `actualSeqLengthsKv`/block-table rows | builder did not pad seq_lens/block table to the FIA batch size |
| "seq_lens must already be on-device before ACLGraph capture" | 310P path given host metadata inside `torch.npu.graph()` |
| "PCP slot mapping size must be divisible by the PCP world size" | expanded slot mapping inconsistent with `prefill_context_parallel_size` |
| graph replay sees different input addresses (debug assertion in `ACLGraphWrapper`) | a builder reallocated a captured buffer |

## Focused tests

- [`tests/ut/test_platform.py`](../../tests/ut/test_platform.py#L1741-L1914) pins `get_attn_backend_cls` end to end: MLA → `mla_v1`, GQA → `attention_v1`, the four PCP cases, legacy selectors without `use_dcp`, SFA selection including PCP, `NotImplementedError` for unsupported PCP keys, and both FA3 branches (enabled with `flash_attn_npu_v3`, disabled without training consistency, where an explicit `FLASH_ATTN` request still collapses to `AscendAttentionBackend`).
- [`tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_sfa_routing.py`](../../tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_sfa_routing.py#L16-L60) checks that both plain-`index_topk` and kpool sparse models route to `AscendSFABackend`, and that kpool indexing fails explicitly on the compatibility family and under PCP/DCP.
- [`tests/ut/attention/test_attention_v1.py`](../../tests/ut/attention/test_attention_v1.py#L36-L105) covers the GQA contract details: workspace caching policies, the large-head PA fallback on A2, `supports_pcp` identity, DCP builder/impl swap, reorder policy, PCP slot-mapping retention, and PCP short-extend classification.
- [`tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_nope_metadata.py`](../../tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_nope_metadata.py#L89-L239) and `test_sfa_v1.py` exercise NoPE metadata paging, A3 storage-address preservation, and A5 `SparseFlashMla` sorted indices with a stable metadata buffer — the graph-safety invariants above.
