- [`tests/ut/attention/test_attention_fa3.py`](../../tests/ut/attention/test_attention_fa3.py#L1-L80) compares FA3 against `npu_fused_infer_attention_score` and is skipped when `flash_attn_npu_v3` is absent.

nodes.title: Graph Mode, Compilation, and Fusion Passes
nodes.description: How Ascend turns a model forward into replayable NPU graphs - the ACLGraphWrapper batch-descriptor cache and FULL/PIECEWISE contract, capture-time hazards and their mitigations, the npugraph_ex/static-kernel/super-kernel compiler interface, and the graph fusion pass manager.
nodes.body:
# Graph Mode, Compilation, and Fusion Passes

Graph execution on Ascend is two independent stages that are easy to conflate:

- **Compile time.** vLLM's `torch.compile` path hands an FX graph to an out-of-tree compiler
  (`AscendCompiler`), which either runs only the FX pattern-fusion passes or forwards the graph to
  `npugraph_ex` for further operator fusion plus optional static-kernel and super-kernel
  compilation.
- **Runtime.** A captured-and-replayed `torch.npu.NPUGraph` wraps a callable — the whole model in
  `FULL` mode, or per-segment callables in `PIECEWISE` mode. `ACLGraphWrapper` owns that capture
  cache.

The two stages are coupled by mode: which compiler runs, and whether it runs at all, is decided from
the effective `cudagraph_mode`. This page covers the mode derivation, the wrapper's dispatch
contract, the capture-time hazards the wrapper works around, the compiler interface, and — briefly —
the fusion passes. Upstream vLLM remains the canonical reference for generic graph concepts
(bucketing, dispatch, the meaning of `FULL` vs `PIECEWISE`); what follows is the Ascend-specific
layer.

## Where the effective modes come from

`NPUPlatform.check_and_update_config` runs two steps back to back that together decide everything
downstream: step 6 `_update_compilation_modes` (ascend config → `vllm_config`) and step 7
`_setup_compile_backend` (recompute sizes, install the compile backend).

`_update_compilation_modes` first *syncs* the validated `ascend_compilation_config` back into
`additional_config` so worker processes observe the same values, then applies these overrides in
order:

| Trigger | Effect | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model_config.enforce_eager` | `compilation_config.mode = NONE`; `splitting_ops` defaults to `[]` | Eager mode excludes compilation entirely |
| `mode` not in `{NONE, VLLM_COMPILE}` | forced to `NONE` with a warning | NPU only supports those two compilation modes |
| `xlite_graph_config.enabled` and `full_mode` and no `speculative_config` | `enforce_eager = True` on `model_config`, `cudagraph_mode = NONE` | Xlite drives the whole forward itself, so ACLGraph capture is redundant |
| `xlite_graph_config.enabled` (otherwise) | `cudagraph_mode = FULL_DECODE_ONLY` | Xlite owns decode; prefill falls back to ACLGraph |
| encoder-decoder model whose mode is not already `NONE`/`PIECEWISE` | `PIECEWISE` when `mode == VLLM_COMPILE`, else `NONE` | Encoder-decoder only supports piecewise graph mode |

Note the write-back discipline: the xlite/eager branch mutates `model_config.enforce_eager`, not just
a local variable, precisely so workers see it.

`_setup_compile_backend` then normalizes the *compile* side relative to the final cudagraph mode:

- `cudagraph_num_of_warmups = 1`, then `vllm_config._set_cudagraph_sizes()` recomputes capture sizes
  after the mode edits.
- Sequence-parallel token alignment is applied only when TP > 1, graph mode is on, the model is not
  eager, and SP / shared-expert-DP / DSA-CP is active — and any resulting size list must be
  non-empty, otherwise startup fails with the list and the TP size in the message.
- `compilation_config.oot_compiler` is set to the platform's compile backend and `use_inductor` is
  forced `False`.
- The three Ascend compilation flags (`enable_npugraph_ex`, `enable_static_kernel`,
  `enable_super_kernel`) are written back as `False` into `additional_config` whenever
  `cudagraph_mode` is `NONE`, requires piecewise compilation, or is an unsupported mode that falls
  back to `NONE`. So npugraph_ex is only alive on full-graph paths.
- `requires_piecewise_compilation()` additionally asserts `mode == VLLM_COMPILE` — but tolerates
  `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` as the escape hatch, because `is_cuda_alike` is `False` on NPU so
  upstream's assertion cannot be reused. It calls `set_splitting_ops_for_v1`, appends
  `vllm::mla_forward` and `vllm::dsa_forward` to `splitting_ops`, and may prune capture sizes on
  hardware advertising `REDUCED_CUDAGRAPH_CAPTURE_SIZES`.
- `has_full_cudagraphs()` empties `splitting_ops` — splitting the FX graph would make static-kernel
  compilation run once per segment.

Two more pieces of sizing policy live outside those functions: `apply_config_platform_defaults`
injects a default `max_cudagraph_capture_size = min(max_num_seqs * decode_query_len, 512)` (upstream's
CUDA-oriented trailing `* 2` is deliberately dropped), and `_prune_reduced_capture_sizes` evenly
subsamples the size list down to `MAX_REDUCED_CAPTURE_SIZES = 4` on affected hardware,
warning that the reduction is temporary.

Finally, `ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` is rejected with a `ValueError` whenever `cudagraph_mode` is not
`NONE`, pointing at plog files as the debugging alternative.

The result is a single coupling between the two stages — the effective cudagraph mode picks the
compile-time path, and the same mode picks what the runtime wrapper captures:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    MODE["effective cudagraph_mode"] --> NONE{"NONE"}
    NONE -->|"yes"| EAGER["CompilationMode.NONE, all three Ascend flags forced off, eager runtime"]
    NONE -->|"no"| PIPE{"requires_piecewise_compilation"}
    PIPE -->|"yes"| PIECE["splitting_ops for v1 plus mla_forward and dsa_forward, npugraph_ex off, fusion_pass_compile, ACLGraph per segment"]
    PIPE -->|"no"| FULL{"has_full_cudagraphs"}
    FULL -->|"yes"| FULLP["splitting_ops emptied, npugraph_ex and static and super kernel as configured, ACLGraphWrapper runtime_mode FULL"]
    FULL -->|"no"| FALL["warn and fall back to NONE"]
```

*One mode drives both stages; only full-graph paths keep npugraph_ex alive.*

## The runtime contract: runtime mode plus `BatchDescriptor`

[`ACLGraphWrapper`](../../vllm_ascend/compilation/acl_graph.py#L74-L292) is what
`NPUPlatform.get_static_graph_wrapper_cls()` returns, so vLLM constructs it whenever static graph
mode is active. It is deliberately dumb about policy: on every `__call__` it reads
`forward_context.cudagraph_runtime_mode` and `forward_context.batch_descriptor`, then *trusts* them.

- The wrapper is constructed with one `runtime_mode` (`FULL` for the main model installed by
  `model_runner_v1.load_model`; `FULL` also for the EAGLE draft runnable). `runtime_mode=NONE`
  asserts at construction, since graph state would be meaningless. It also captures the platform-wide
  `current_platform.get_global_graph_pool()` at construction and passes it as `pool=` to every
  `torch.npu.graph`, so all captured graphs of a process share one memory pool.
- If the forward context's runtime mode is `NONE` **or differs from the wrapper's mode**, the
  wrapper calls the runnable eagerly. This is what makes nested wrappers of different modes
  dispatch correctly: the inner wrapper simply declines.
- Otherwise the pair `(batch_descriptor)` is the dispatch key into
  `concrete_aclgraph_entries: dict[BatchDescriptor, ACLGraphEntry]`. A missing entry is created, and
  a missing `entry.aclgraph` means capture; a present one means replay.
- `BatchDescriptor` is produced upstream by `CudagraphDispatcher`, with
  [`_create_padded_batch_descriptor` patched](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_cudagraph.py#L6-L38)
  so that, for full-graph modes other than plain `FULL`, `num_reqs` is derived from
  `num_tokens_padded // uniform_decode_query_len` and `uniform` stays true; plain `FULL` forces
  `uniform = False` and `num_reqs = min(num_tokens_padded, max_num_seqs)`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CALL["ACLGraphWrapper.__call__"] --> CTX["read forward_context.cudagraph_runtime_mode and batch_descriptor"]
    CTX --> MATCH{"runtime mode matches wrapper mode and is not NONE"}
    MATCH -->|"no"| EAGER["call runnable eagerly - no capture, no replay"]
    MATCH -->|"yes"| ENTRY["lookup concrete_aclgraph_entries by batch_descriptor"]
    ENTRY --> HAS{"entry.aclgraph set"}
    HAS -->|"no"| CAP["validate capture is legal, record input addresses, capture NPUGraph"]
    CAP --> WEAK["weak-ref workspaces and output, bump compilation_counter"]
    WEAK --> RET1["return the live output"]
    HAS -->|"yes"| ADDR{"debugging mode and addresses changed"}
    ADDR -->|"mismatch"| FAIL["assert: input addresses differ from capture"]
    ADDR -->|"ok or not debugging"| SYNC["optionally synchronize current stream"]
    SYNC --> REPLAY["entry.aclgraph.replay, return cached output"]
```

*The wrapper never chooses a mode; it only obeys the runtime mode and batch descriptor it is handed.*

A stated invariant accompanies this design: the wrapper keeps **no** persistent input buffers and
copies **no** runtime inputs; it makes no assumption about dynamic batch shape, because doing so
would couple it to compilation. Buffer management for replay is the caller's job. `__getattr__`
proxies unknown attributes to the runnable (with a `DEBUG`-only hint in the error) and `unwrap()`
returns it — `AscendSpecDecodeBaseProposer.get_model` relies on that to hand out the raw model.

## Capture-time hazards and their mitigations

Capture is the fragile part of the design, and most of the wrapper's body is mitigation.

| Hazard | Mitigation |
| --- | --- |
| Retaining capture-time tensors that only the wrapper needs leaks device memory | `weak_ref_tensors` / `weak_ref_workspaces` convert captured outputs, attention workspaces, and graph-task params to weak refs, keeping the buffer pointer without owning the tensor. The wrapper *returns* the live output of a capture, not the weak ref, so PyTorch can still manage memory during capture. |
| Per-layer GC and allocator cache flushes make piecewise capture crawl | `aclgraph_options.gc_disable` patches `gc.collect` and `torch.npu.empty_cache` to no-ops for all but the first graph. |
| `weak_ref_output` is only safe on the last subgraph | The option is honored only where the caller sets it (piecewise last graph), because earlier subgraph outputs are consumed by later ones. |
| The offloader's copy stream is forked during forward, and joining is deferred to the next iteration | Capture calls `get_offloader().sync_prev_onload()` before `torch.npu.graph(...)` and `get_offloader().join_after_forward()` inside the graph scope, avoiding an unjoined-stream error. |
| An old HDK/CANN stack fails capture with `Alloc sq cq fail` | `_is_old_hdk_capture_error` re-raises a `RuntimeError` telling the user to upgrade to HDK 25.5.1 or later with a matching CANN stack. |
| The selected graph sizes exceed runtime stream capacity (most likely in piecewise mode) | `_is_stream_resource_capture_error` matches error code `207008` together with a stream-resource phrase, or the explicit `insufficient_stream_resources` markers, and re-raises with mitigation guidance: reduce `cudagraph_capture_sizes`, lower `max_cudagraph_capture_size`, prefer `FULL`/`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` for uniform decode, or disable graph mode to confirm. |
| Replay silently reuses a graph captured for different buffers | In `DEBUG` logging mode the wrapper records `input_addresses` at capture and asserts they are identical at replay, naming both lists on failure. |
| Host-side attention parameter updates can race graph replay | See the ordering section below. |
| Super-kernel scopes must enclose exactly one full-model capture | `_super_kernel_scope("full_model", enabled)` brackets the runnable inside the graph and always emits the matching `super_kernel_scope_end` in a `finally`; after capture, `aclgraph.super_kernel_optimize({"dcci_after_kernel_end": [".*"]})` is applied when enabled. |

Note that capture breadth is *not* trimmed by an Ascend-local heuristic any more: upstream sizing and
dispatch are preserved, and only the confirmed stream-resource failure is rewritten at runtime.

### Replay ordering

FULL-mode attention needs `update_graph_params()` to rebind operator arguments on an update stream
between iterations. If the CPU's event record for iteration *i* completes before the replay of
iteration *i-1*, a graph can consume another iteration's metadata — wrong results, precision
problems, or hangs. `ACLGraphWrapper.__call__` therefore synchronizes the current stream before
replay when `runtime_mode == FULL` and the runnable is not a merged EAGLE draft. Two escapes exist:
`enable_enpu` (the model runner orders update vs. replay itself, calling
`_update_full_graph_params_if_needed` *before* `run_model()` and synchronizing there), and the
FULL + EAGLE draft merge path. `BreakableACLGraphWrapper` reproduces the same sync so both wrappers
behave identically.

### Per-graph bookkeeping

The parameters that must survive capture are held in module-level
[`GraphParams`](../../vllm_ascend/compilation/acl_graph.py#L330-L410) instances keyed by captured
token count: `events` (`torch.npu.ExternalEvent`), `workspaces`, `handles` (graph-task group
handles), and `attn_params` (per-layer argument tuples). There are three of them — main model, draft
model, draft prefill — each requiring an explicit `set_*_graph_params(capture_sizes)` before capture;
setting one twice raises `ValueError`. They are keyed by the *actual* capture descriptors, not raw
config sizes: with speculative decoding under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, each configured size is rounded up
to a multiple of `decode_query_len`, so Model Runner V2 derives the keys with
`collect_sorted_captured_token_sizes` and V1 inlines the same `sorted({desc.num_tokens ...})`
comprehension. `update_full_graph_params` wraps the backend dispatch in
`set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config)` because newer vLLM raises outside that scope and SFA backend
resolution needs it; Model Runner V1 reaches it through `_update_full_graph_params_if_needed`, which
fires only for `FULL` replays that are neither capturing nor using sparse/compressed attention.

Sleep mode reuses this same state: `AclGraphSleepWakeupManager.sleep()` nulls every workspace (keeping
the size keys), clears the list-valued fields, empties every registered wrapper's
`concrete_aclgraph_entries` through the `_acl_graph_wrappers` `WeakSet`, resets `first_run_finished`,
and drops the manager's graphs; wakeup re-runs `capture_model()` only once the KV cache tag is
present.

The encoder path has a parallel structure: `EncoderGraphParams` keyed by *token budget* instead of
token count, `update_encoder_graph_params` re-issuing FIA with freshly computed host
`actual_seq_lengths`, and `EncoderAclGraphManager` overriding `_capture_budget_graph` /
`_run_budget_graph` while reusing the same `graph_task_update_{begin,end}` + `ExternalEvent` pattern.
Its bookkeeping is single-path — the code notes dual-path encoder graphs would need
`(path, token_budget)` keys.

### Host-side parameter refresh

Full-graph replay is only correct because each attention backend records, at capture time, a graph-task
handle, an `torch.npu.ExternalEvent`, a workspace, and a tuple of the tensors/arguments to rebind.
`update_full_graph_params` then delegates to the backend's static `update_graph_params`, which switches
to the update stream, brackets the underlying attention operator launch in
`torch.npu.graph_task_update_begin(stream, handle)` / `graph_task_update_end(stream)`, and records the
event so the replay stream can be ordered after it. Without a backend-side `update_graph_params`
implementation, capturing a FULL graph is not enough to replay correct attention state — which is the
concrete reason backend graph support (`AttentionCGSupport`) is coupled to mode selection.

Two workspace policies coexist in `attention_v1`: a plain per-size cache in
`graph_params.workspaces[num_tokens]`, and a "max workspace" mode used when layer-aware replay is
needed, where capture keeps the *largest* workspace required by any layer shape sharing that graph
size (mixed-shape models would otherwise replay with an undersized buffer). The paged-attention path
additionally reuses one workspace query across all layers of a single update pass, re-querying only when
a size-relevant input (shapes, dtypes, seq_lens pointer, head counts, scale) changes.

## FULL vs PIECEWISE in practice

`PIECEWISE` is the conservative path: vLLM splits the FX graph at `splitting_ops` and ACLGraph
captures the non-attention segments, so the number of captured graphs scales with model depth —
which is exactly why it is the mode most exposed to stream exhaustion. `FULL` / `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`
rely on the attention backend supporting runtime parameter patching through `update_graph_params()`
and on capture-time workspace/handle recording.

Whether a wrapper is even installed depends on the effective mode and on which flag combination
holds:

- `_use_aclgraph()` requires `cudagraph_mode != NONE`, and either `mode == VLLM_COMPILE` or breakable
  cudagraph being enabled, and not `enforce_eager`.
- Breakable CUDAGraph is opt-in on Ascend: `platform.py` sets `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` to `"0"`
  by default so upstream's architecture-based auto-enable cannot kick in. When enabled, the model (and
  drafter) are wrapped in `BreakableACLGraphWrapper` instead of `ACLGraphWrapper`; the subclass only
  sets `forward_context.capturing` for FULL capture, weak-refs the three `GraphParams` workspace maps,
  and reproduces the replay sync — the break/segment logic itself is upstream's.
- In Model Runner V2 the main graph manager is `ModelAclGraphManager`, which subclasses vLLM's
  `ModelCudaGraphManager`, calls `set_graph_params(self.capture_sizes)` when capture is needed, and
  overrides `run_fullgraph` to append its own parameter update after the upstream replay. Its
  `capture` wraps the model in `ModelWithContext`, which sets `_EXTRA_CTX.capturing` (true only while
  the stream is capturing and the runtime mode is not `PIECEWISE`) and marks draft / draft-prefill
  models. Only the breakable path installs a `BreakableACLGraphWrapper`
  (`init_breakable_cg_runner`); otherwise capture goes through the upstream manager's own wrapping.

Effective mode can also be *narrowed* by attention-backend capability
(`AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` vs `UNIFORM_BATCH`), because
`_check_and_update_cudagraph_mode` takes the minimum support across all attention backends and
KV-cache groups before calling `resolve_cudagraph_mode_and_sizes`; the resulting mode is what
`initialize_cudagraph_keys` and `set_graph_params` see. See
[Attention Backend Selection](attention-backends.md) for which backend declares what.

## The compile stage: `AscendCompiler`

`NPUPlatform.get_compile_backend()` returns `vllm_ascend.compilation.compiler_interface.AscendCompiler`,
which vLLM installs as `compilation_config.oot_compiler`. Its contract:

- **`compute_hash`** folds `torch_npu.__version__` plus the three `ascend_compilation_config` flags
  into a 10-character SHA-256 prefix, so changing any of them invalidates the cache.
- **`compile`** deep-copies the FX graph (inductor mutates in place), rewraps FakeTensor inputs under
  the current fake mode, then dispatches: `enable_npugraph_ex` → `npugraph_ex_compile`, otherwise
  `fusion_pass_compile` (decompositions from `select_decomp_table`, the pass manager invoked as the
  inner compiler via `compiler_config[COMPILATION_PASS_KEY]`).
- **`npugraph_ex_compile`** prefers importing `npugraph_ex`, falling back to `torchair` for older
  stacks. In both cases it calls `torch.npu.set_compile_mode(jit_compile=False)` and configures the
  backend, then wraps non-tuple-returning graphs with `make_graph_return_tuple` because
  `torch.compile` requires tuple output.
- Backend configuration differs by stack. For npugraph_ex the options dict is
  `force_eager=True`, `inplace_pass=False` (avoiding a GELU fallback to CPU), `clone_input=False`,
  `clone_output=False`; for the torchair fallback the equivalent is `mode="reduce-overhead"`,
  `debug.run_eagerly=True`, and `disable_reinplace_inplaceable_ops_pass=True`.
- **Static kernel** adds `static_kernel_compile=True` (or `_aclnn_static_shape_kernel` on torchair)
  and restricts compilation to the decode capture sizes, computed by
  `_compute_decode_cudagraph_batch_sizes` as those configured sizes between
  `uniform_decode_query_len` and `max_num_seqs * uniform_decode_query_len`. It also synthesizes
  `LOCAL_WORLD_SIZE = local_world_size * data_parallel_size_local` when unset, because npugraph_ex
  builds per-node Gloo groups from it.
- **Super kernel** piggybacks on static kernel: `super_kernel_optimize=True` with
  `{"dcci_after_kernel_end": [".*"]}`, matching what the runtime wrapper applies post-capture.
- **Caching** patches `_NpuFxCompiler._get_compiled_gm` to dump the compiled graph's Python code to
  `cache_dir/key`, and *skips* the dump when the code contains `triton_kernel_wrapper`, because Triton
  kernel side-table indices are process-local. `load` therefore treats a missing file as a cache miss
  and recompiles; on a hit it rebuilds `_CompiledFxGraph` from the py_code and re-adds an unflattening
  wrapper for graphs that originally returned a non-tuple.

The three flags themselves are a strict dependency chain in
[`AscendCompilationConfig`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py#L95-L152): `enable_super_kernel`
defaults from `enable_static_kernel` when omitted, static kernel asserts npugraph_ex, super kernel
asserts static kernel, and a hardware profile lacking `HardwareCapability.NPUGRAPH_EX` (310P) disables
all three with one warning each. See
[NPUPlatform and Hardware Capability Profiles](../architecture/platform-and-hardware-profiles.md).

## Fusion passes, briefly

`NPUPlatform.get_pass_manager_cls()` returns `GraphFusionPassManager`, registered under
`NPUPlatform.pass_key` — `COMPILATION_PASS_KEY = "graph_fusion_manager"` — which is also the key the
compiler interface uses to find the manager inside `compiler_config`. It exists because `torch_npu`
has no Triton support, so vLLM's `PostGradPassManager` cannot be reused.

`GraphFusionPassManager.__call__` reads `get_pass_context().compile_range`, runs each pass whose
`is_applicable_for_range(compile_range)` returns true, then calls `graph.recompile()`.
`configure(config)` appends passes from the validated `ascend_compilation_config` (not the raw
`additional_config` dict, so `"false"` is not truthy):

| Pass | Flag | Extra gate | Fuses |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AddRMSNormQuantFusionPass` | `fuse_norm_quant` | `HardwareCapability.GRAPH_NORM_QUANT_FUSION` | `npu_add_rms_norm_bias` + `vllm.quantize` → `npu_add_rms_norm_quant` |
| `QKNormRopeFusionPass` | `fuse_qknorm_rope` | none (self-gates on bf16 and `head_size == 128`) | QKV split + per-head RMSNorm + bias + rotary embedding → one fused `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope` op |
| `MulsAddFusionPass` | `fuse_muls_add` | `HardwareCapability.GRAPH_MULS_ADD_FUSION` | `x * scale + y` → `vllm.muls_add`, with `scale` taken from the model's `routed_scaling_factor` |

Patterns are declared through `BasePattern`, which registers each replacement twice: once with
inductor's `PatternMatcherPass` and once with `npugraph_ex.register_replacement`. The npugraph_ex
registration also carries `extra_stream_scope_check` as its `extra_check`, so a match spanning two
`stream_label`s (or mixing the default stream with a labelled one) is never fused. Registrations are
deduplicated by `ClassName_eps`. Two further passes exist in the package that `configure()` does not
currently append: `AllGatherChunkNoOpCleanupPass` (folds `all_gather` +
`sequence_parallel_chunk_impl` into identity) and `NoOpEliminationPass` (drops `view`/`reshape` nodes
whose shapes are statically identical).

## Operating it

- Enable verification the boring way: `--cudagraph-metrics` plus logs left on (`disable_log_stats=False`
  in Python). Profiling and temporary prints are secondary evidence.
- The primary levers when capture fails are `cudagraph_capture_sizes` and
  `max_cudagraph_capture_size`. `update_cudagraph_capture_sizes` enforces consistency between them: an
  explicit `max_cudagraph_capture_size` that disagrees with the list's last element raises if the list
  was also user-specified, and otherwise truncates with a warning.
- `enforce_eager=True` is the escape hatch to confirm a failure is graph-related.
- `enable_super_kernel` without `enable_static_kernel` fails validation; static kernel compilation adds
  minutes to tens of minutes of startup time and is verified via `op_statistic.csv` entries containing
  `static_kernel`.
- `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` turns on the input-address replay assertion and per-capture debug logs;
  keep it off in production, where the check costs a `data_ptr()` sweep per call.

## Tests that pin this behavior

- `tests/ut/compilation/test_acl_graph.py` covers the wrapper end to end with mocks: NONE and
  mismatched modes falling through to the runnable, first-call capture vs. second-call replay (the
  runnable must not run on replay), the super-kernel scope and `super_kernel_optimize` call for both
  flag states, `gc_disable`, `weak_ref_output`, debug-log gating, the input-address assertion's
  success and failure paths, `__getattr__`/`unwrap`, the `WeakSet` registration, `GraphParams`
  sleep-mode clearing, and the DCP/MLA `update_graph_params` paths.
- `tests/ut/compilation/test_graph_fusion_pass_manager.py` asserts `configure()` consumes the
  validated config (`"false"` disables a pass) and appends nothing when all three flags are off.
- `tests/ut/test_platform.py` covers the default capture-size injection (including respect for an
  explicit max or size list), the SP/shared-expert-DP/DSA-CP alignment gate, and the eager and
  unsupported-compilation-level fallbacks to `NONE`. The dedicated
  `test_check_and_update_config_unsupported_cudagraph_mode` case is currently `skip`ped with the note
  "Revert me when vllm support setting cudagraph_mode on oot platform".
- `tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py` covers the static-kernel → super-kernel defaulting, the explicit
  `enable_super_kernel: false` override, and the rejection of super kernel without static kernel.

## Related pages

- [Configuration System](../architecture/configuration-system.md) — how `ascend_compilation_config`
  and `xlite_graph_config` are validated before these modes are derived.
- [NPUPlatform and Hardware Capability Profiles](../architecture/platform-and-hardware-profiles.md) —
  the capability gates reused by the compiler and the fusion passes.
- [Attention Backend Selection](attention-backends.md) — which backends declare graph support and
  implement `update_graph_params()`.
- [Custom Ops and Kernels](../architecture/custom-ops-and-kernels.md) — the fused operators the passes
  target.

# Files

- [Attention Backend Selection and Implementations](attention-backends.md) - How vLLM-Ascend maps a model's attention shape (GQA, MLA, sparse SFA, compressed DSA, FA3) onto a concrete NPU attention backend, and how each backend's metadata builder, KV-layout contract, and AscendC operator path fit together - including the couples that make metadata builders part of the ACL graph contract.
- [Graph Mode, Compilation, and Fusion Passes](graph-mode-and-compilation.md) - How Ascend turns a model forward into replayable NPU graphs - the ACLGraphWrapper batch-descriptor cache and FULL/PIECEWISE contract, capture-time hazards and their mitigations, the npugraph_ex/static-kernel/super-kernel compiler interface, and the graph fusion pass manager.
- [KV Cache Specs, Block Layout, and Placement](kv-cache-and-block-layout.md) - The Ascend KV-cache data model - separate K/V (and state) tensors instead of upstream packed pages, the Ascend cache-spec family, storage block size vs scheduler block, padded page and block-stride addressing for mixed attention/Mamba pools, block tables and slot mapping, NZ reshaping on the transfer path, and KV layer parallelism (KVPP) placement.
- [MoE Execution: Router, Dispatch, Comm Methods, and EPLB](moe-execution.md) - The end-to-end Ascend Mixture-of-Experts path — expert routing through the Ascend router factory, the token dispatcher and prepare/finalize variants, how select_moe_comm_method picks ALLGATHER/ALLTOALL/MC2/FUSED-MC2 per forward from the hardware MoECommPolicy, shared-expert overlap, and the dynamic versus force EPLB flavours.
- [Quantization Methods and Schemes](quantization.md) - The Ascend quantization stack - how a checkpoint's quant config is recognized and auto-detected, the scheme registry keyed by (quant_type, layer_type) and its linear/MoE/attention base classes, the weight-loading invariants at TP boundaries (MX group phase, block-scale rounding), KV-cache quantization, and the 310P compatibility variant.
- [Speculative Decoding and Draft Proposers](speculative-decoding.md) - How speculative decoding is wired on Ascend - the method-to-proposer dispatch table, the shared LLM proposer base and its ACL-graph draft runnable, the draft-token handoff from sample_tokens to the scheduler, and the Ascend rejection sampler that verifies drafts.

# KV Cache Specs, Block Layout, and Placement

Ascend stores KV cache differently from upstream vLLM. Upstream hands every attention backend a packed `[blocks, heads, block_tokens, head_dim]` page and lets the backend reshape it; vllm-ascend splits each attention layer into **separate K and V allocations**, allocates recurrent state as its own tensor list, aligns every raw allocation to 2 MiB when a KV-transfer connector is active, and rebuilds the tensor views itself with explicit page strides. That is why two functions that exist upstream have no direct Ascend counterpart: allocation (`_allocate_kv_cache_tensors`) and reshaping (`_reshape_kv_cache_tensors` / `_reshape_kv_cache_v2`) are owned by the plugin.

The Model Runner V2 README tracks exactly this deviation as a known gap: "KV cache requires continuous space (thus divided as K cache and V cache separately) and PD disaggregation requires 2M-aligned tensors for KV cache, so custom KV cache initialization is needed" ([`README.md`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/README.md#L16-L20)). Everything else on this page follows from those two constraints, plus hybrid attention+Mamba pools where one scheduler block owns pages in two different caches.

See also [Attention Backend Selection and Implementations](attention-backends.md) for what each backend does with the views produced here, and [KV Cache Initialization](../workflows/kv-cache-initialization.md) for the engine-side ordering.

## Vocabulary: four different things called "block size"

The single most common source of bugs in this area is conflating these. They are distinct numbers and can differ by the compression ratio, by the kernel block size, or by page padding.

| Term | Owner | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scheduler block | `KVCacheSpec.block_size` | The unit the scheduler allocates, frees, hashes for prefix caching, and stores in the block table. Measured in **logical tokens**. |
| Storage block size | `get_storage_block_size(spec)` | How many **physical token rows** one scheduler block occupies in the resident tensor. For a compressed spec this is `block_size // compression_ratio`. |
| Page | `KVCacheSpec.page_size_bytes` | Bytes one scheduler block occupies for one layer: `storage_block_size * num_kv_heads * per_head_bytes` (plus a scale tail when the cache is quantized per block). `num_blocks * page_size_bytes` is the per-layer allocation size. |
| Padded page | `page_size_padded` | The page rounded up to a pool-wide common size so that one scheduler block id can own the same physical page in an attention cache *and* a recurrent-state cache. |
| Block stride | `indexes_kv_by_block_stride`, `KVCacheTensor.block_stride`, `tensor.stride(0)` | The step between consecutive scheduler blocks inside the resident tensor. Equals `page_size_bytes` for a compact layout; larger when pages are padded, and then kernels must be told about it. |

### `get_storage_block_size` and the version lane

[`kv_cache_interface.py`](../../vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_interface.py#L27-L48) is the one place that answers "how many physical rows is a scheduler block", and it has to bridge two upstream API shapes:

```python
def get_kv_cache_compression_ratio(kv_cache_spec: KVCacheSpec) -> int:
    if vllm_version_is("0.28.0"):
        return kv_cache_spec.compress_ratio
    return kv_cache_spec.tokens_per_state
```

* On the `0.28.0` lane the field is `compress_ratio`, and `AscendMLAAttentionSpec` exposes a read-only `storage_block_size` property (`block_size // compress_ratio`) that the generic `getattr` fallback in `get_storage_block_size` picks up.
* On `main` the field is `tokens_per_state` (vLLM #53906 renamed it), and `AscendMLAAttentionSpec` deliberately has **no** `storage_block_size` property because main initializes a dataclass field of that name and a read-only property would reject the constructor assignment. `get_storage_block_size` therefore derives the number itself: `block_size // tokens_per_state` for `AscendMLAAttentionSpec`, and for a plain `MLAAttentionSpec` it prefers main's explicit view override, falling back to `block_size`.
* For a `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` group the helper asserts that every inner spec resolves to the **same** storage block size, because one block table row addresses the whole group.

Both callers that matter treat the storage block size as the tensor geometry: the reshape builds backend shapes with `get_storage_block_size(spec)` rather than `spec.block_size` ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5011-L5021), [`attn_utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/attn_utils.py#L447-L465)), and the DSA compressor op is handed a `storage_block_size` argument ([`dsa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v1.py#L131-L142)). `tests/ut/test_compressed_prefix_cache.py` pins the split for ratios 4 and 128: `spec.block_size` stays the logical size while `get_storage_block_size(spec) == physical_block_size`.

## The Ascend cache-spec family

`vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_interface.py` defines four specs and registers them with the upstream spec registry so the scheduler picks the right block manager for each.

| Spec | Extends | Cache role | Manager registered |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AscendMLAAttentionSpec` | `MLAAttentionSpec` | Main MLA latent cache, and the GLM-Next compressed indexer K cache (`model_version="glm5_next"`, `tokens_per_state > 1`) | `FullAttentionManager` |
| `AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec` | `MLAAttentionSpec` | SFA indexer K plus its quantization scale, allocated as an **independent physical tensor** even though it shares scheduler block ids with the MLA cache | `FullAttentionManager` |
| `AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec` | `SlidingWindowMLASpec` | Sliding-window / compressed MLA | `SlidingWindowManager` |
| `AscendIndexerKPoolStateSpec` | `AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec` | Paged FP32 `[K, gate]` compressor state for an incomplete pool; `cache_role="indexer_state"` | `SlidingWindowManager` |

`register_ascend_kv_cache_specs()` is called from `NPUPlatform.register_custom_kv_cache_specs` ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L161-L165)), so the registry is populated before any group is built.

The Ascend-specific fields on `AscendMLAAttentionSpec` are all layout metadata rather than attention semantics:

- `scale_dim` / `scale_dtype` - the per-block quantization scale tail folded into the page, and its dtype (FP32 or FP16 depending on hardware capability).
- `cache_sparse_sfa_c8` - the sparse C8 main cache becomes **one packed byte tensor**; the indexer-specific C8 flags live on `AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec` instead.
- `store_on_host` - set when sparse KV offload keeps the cache off device.
- `indexes_kv_by_block_stride` - the cache is addressed by an explicit physical block stride (see [padded pages](#padded-pages-and-requires_padded_page_layout)). vLLM main removed this field from `AttentionSpec`; it remains part of the Ascend runner/backend contract.
- `non_causal_multi_token_decode` - `merge` rejects a mixed set, forcing causal target layers and non-causal multi-token draft layers into **separate** KV cache groups.
- `alignment` (on the sliding-window spec) - optional page padding for DeepSeekV4.

`merge` is therefore an invariant checker as much as a fold: two layers may only share one group if their scale layout, sparse-C8 flag, host-storage flag, alignment, compression ratio and block-stride flag all agree, and the assertion messages say so. `AscendIndexerKPoolStateSpec` goes further and requires FP32 plus `block_size == sliding_window`, and its `max_memory_usage_bytes` returns exactly one page, because the state group keeps only the current incomplete pool.

## Why the custom allocate/reshape path exists

Three requirements force it:

1. **Continuous K and V.** The attention implementations consume `(k_cache, v_cache)` tuples (or a one-element tuple for the packed C8 layout and a `(k, scale)` tuple for the indexer), not a packed page with a leading `2` dimension. `_get_attention_kv_cache_dims` resolves the split point per layer - `kv_lora_rank` / `qk_rope_head_dim` for an MLA layer, `spec.head_size` twice for a `CacheOnlyAttentionLayer`, otherwise `head_size` / `head_size_v` - and the allocator splits one logical page into two allocations using `calc_split_factor` (or the quant method's `get_kv_quant_split_factor` when FA quantization is on) ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4388-L4407), [`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L1468-L1470)).
2. **PD alignment.** Prefill/decode disaggregation requires the K and V allocations of a layer to start on 2 MiB boundaries ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4491-L4506)). `_allocate_int8_cache_tensor` allocates `numel + alignment` bytes and trims to an aligned slice **only** when `vllm_config.kv_transfer_config` is set, so a non-transfer deployment pays nothing. `_align_kv_ptrs` in the KV-store worker re-derives registered region starts by rounding *down* to 2 MiB, asserting that a raw tensor pointer is already aligned.
3. **Two runner generations.** V1 (`worker/model_runner_v1.py`) and V2 (`worker/v2/attn_utils.py`) each carry their own copy of the allocate/reshape pair, with the V2 copy additionally exposing `allocate_kv_cache_main` as the adapter for main's #51718 `allocate_kv_cache` entry point.

## Allocation: `_allocate_kv_cache_tensors`

[`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4491-L4946) is the authoritative flow. It first builds `layer_kv_cache_spec` (unwrapping `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` per layer and refreshing SFA indexer specs from the live attention module), then picks a **pool strategy** before any allocation happens:

| Condition | Strategy |
| --- | --- |
| `kvpp_config.size > 1` | `allocate_kvpp_cache` owns the whole pool (see [KVPP](#kv-layer-parallelism-kvpp)) and hybrid mode is forced off. |
| `requires_padded_page_layout(...)` | GLM-Next shared-slot layout: **one backing per descriptor**, shared by every layer the descriptor lists, after validating `offset == 0`, `layer_stride == 0`, `block_stride == page_size_bytes`, `size == num_blocks * block_stride`. |
| main lane and any `model_version == "deepseek_v4"` | All descriptors must declare the same `size`; that one backing is allocated once and sliced into contiguous per-layer regions, each `block_stride` checked against the layer's `page_size_bytes`. |
| main lane, hybrid attention+Mamba, layer/block-compact layout, compatible transfer connector | One backing allocated once and sliced per layer, preserving #51718 overlay semantics without duplicating the pool. |

The per-descriptor loop then allocates:

- a single tensor shared by all listed layers when the group is Mamba / hybrid / `cache_only_layers` / `HiddenStateCacheSpec`, with an extra safeguard: if one descriptor mixes `MambaSpec` and `HiddenStateCacheSpec` layers they get **separate** buffers, because float32 `ssm_state` writes into a bfloat16 hidden-state region would corrupt it;
- one tensor per layer for a page-strided (`_uses_page_strided_kv_layout`) group;
- a `(k, scale)` view pair from one raw allocation for `AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec`, with the scale view offset rounded up to the scale dtype size, which lets HCCL/Mooncake register a single memory range;
- `(k_tensor, v_tensor)` for ordinary attention layers, sized by the split factor, or a one-element tuple for sparse-C8.

The loop ends with `assert layer_names == set(kv_cache_raw_tensors.keys())`: every layer in every group must be materialized exactly once.

On main, `kv_cache_config.num_blocks` is the **per-layer** block count and descriptors describe a common backing; on `0.28.0` the legacy `shared_by` descriptor carries its own per-descriptor `size` and layers alias the same physical blocks. `get_kv_cache_tensor_layers` is the single bridge for that difference (`shared_by` vs `layers`) ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L642-L650)).

## Reshape: page-strided views

`_reshape_kv_cache_tensors` (V1) and `_reshape_kv_cache_v2` (V2) recompute `num_blocks` from the raw allocation (`numel // page_size_bytes`) and assert it is **at least** `kv_cache_config.num_blocks` - ranks may have different capacities, and the scheduler uses the minimum, so over-allocation on one rank is legal but under-allocation is not.

`_adjust_kv_layout` is the primitive that makes padded pages work ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4948-L4978)). It builds each view with `torch.as_strided`, overriding the **outermost** stride with `page_size_bytes // dtype_size`:

```python
stride = torch.empty(shape).stride()
target_stride = (num_element_per_page, *stride[1:])
tensor = torch.as_strided(raw_tensor.view(dtype), size=shape, stride=target_stride,
                          storage_offset=storage_offset_bytes // dtype_size)
storage_offset_bytes += stride[0] * dtype_size
```

Consequences worth knowing:

- A page-strided MLA cache still exposes its latent KV and RoPE halves as two logical tensors over one allocation (`(*prefix, k_dim)` and `(*prefix, v_dim)`), each advanced by the same page stride.
- A DSV4 compressed cache with `scale_dim != 0` and `HardwareCapability.DSV4_COMPRESSED_CACHE` gets a third, overlapping **full** view sized `head_size + scale_dim * scale_dtype_size`, and `_adjust_kv_layout` resets the storage offset for that third tensor so it aliases the page start.
- When a hybrid attention page is padded to a Mamba page, the trailing padding is trimmed off the attention views (`should_trim_page_padding`), from the front of a combined raw tensor when K and V share one allocation.
- For compressed specs the kernel block size *is* the storage block size: `kernel_block_size = group_storage_block_size if group_storage_block_size != group_spec.block_size else kernel_block_sizes[group_id]` ([`attn_utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/attn_utils.py#L978-L984)). `tests/ut/worker/test_attn_utils_v2.py` pins this (`storage == 32` while `prepare_kernel_block_sizes` still reports the logical 128).

## Padded pages and `requires_padded_page_layout`

`requires_padded_page_layout(kv_cache_specs)` answers a **pool-level** question, not a per-spec one ([`kv_cache_interface.py`](../../vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_interface.py#L51-L72)):

1. there must be at least one `MambaSpec` in the pool, and
2. at least one of those state specs must carry `page_size_padded`, and
3. at least one spec in the pool - attention or state - must set `indexes_kv_by_block_stride`.

Why a conjunction rather than "is anything padded": hybrid models already pad Mamba pages through `cache_config.mamba_page_size_padded` while keeping the *packed contiguous* state layout, so padding alone must not switch the layout. The distinguishing fact is that in a **pooled** layout one physical page is bound to both an attention cache and a recurrent state cache. The attention side of such a pool is addressed by an explicit physical block stride, so every view over the shared page - including the state views - must advance by that same padded page size. If a state view advanced by its compact size instead, a state update for scheduler block id `n` would land in pages owned by a different block id.

`_reshape_kv_cache_tensors` therefore builds state views with `_adjust_kv_layout(raw_tensor, [(num_blocks, *shape) ...], dtypes, page_size_bytes)` instead of the packed cursor walk used by ordinary hybrid models ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5361-L5407)). The packed path stays for the non-pooled case and is documented in-line with the buffer-overlay picture:

```
tensor1: [(kv_padding), conv           , ...]
tensor2: [k           , ssm            , ...]
tensor3: [v           , (mamba_padding), ...]
```

The lane difference matters: `worker/v2/attn_utils.get_kv_cache_spec` sets `indexes_kv_by_block_stride=True` only on `0.28.0`, because main removed the field and "`page_size_padded` alone carries the padding there" ([`attn_utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/attn_utils.py#L161-L183)). GLM-Next is the exception on both lanes: `Glm5NextIndexerCache` and `Glm5NextStateCache` set the flag explicitly in their specs ([`kv_cache.py`](../../vllm_ascend/models/glm5next/kv_cache.py#L84-L100)), and the V1 runner propagates it from either the spec or the attention module ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5710-L5729)).

`tests/ut/worker/test_glm5next_pooled_cache.py` is the behavioural contract: it asserts the flag is true for the pooled layout, false for a standalone MTP runner with the same attention specs but no state caches, and false for a packed hybrid pool whose `MambaSpec` has `page_size_padded` but no block-stride spec. A second test fills `latent[mla_id]`, `conv[state_id]` and `ssm[state_id]` for every permutation of block ids and verifies no view can reach another block's bytes.

## Block tables: scheduler ids to slots

[`worker/block_table.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/block_table.py) holds one `BlockTable` per KV cache group and a `MultiGroupBlockTable` over them, built by `NPUInputBatch`.

**Physical vs logical block size.** A group's `block_size` is the scheduler allocation unit (`physical_block_size`). If the attention backend advertises supported kernel block sizes (`[128]` for the GQA and MLA backends, `[128, 64]` on 310P, `[MultipleOf(1)]` for the GLM-Next indexer pool), the table picks the first kernel size that divides the physical block evenly and reports `blocks_per_phys_block = physical // logical`. If none divides, construction fails with `ValueError`. When the split is greater than one, `use_hybrid_blocks` is set and `append_row` expands each scheduler (physical) block id into `blocks_per_phys_block` consecutive logical ids ([`block_table.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/block_table.py#L52-L118), [`block_table.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/block_table.py#L286-L301)). DSV4 with `block_size == kernel_size` is pinned by `test_dsv4_logical_block_ids_are_not_expanded`: ids `[7, 11]` are stored verbatim.

**Slot mapping.** `compute_slot_mapping` launches `_compute_slot_mapping_kernel` over `(num_reqs + 1)` programs; the spare program pads the tail of `slot_mapping` up to `max_num_batched_tokens` with `PAD_SLOT_ID` for graph compatibility ([`compute_slot_mapping.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/triton/compute_slot_mapping.py#L11-L84)). Per token it computes `block_index = pos // block_size`, gathers the block id from the row, and writes `block_number * block_size + offset`. Under DCP the block is virtualized to `physical_block_size * cp_world_size`, an interleave mask decides which tokens this rank owns, non-owned tokens become `-1`, and the logical row index becomes `physical_block_idx * blocks_per_phys_block + local_offset // block_size` ([`block_table.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/block_table.py#L232-L277)).

**Capacity rules.** `max_num_blocks_per_req` comes from the spec, never from an expansion: for a Mamba group the state is *replicated* across DCP ranks rather than sharded, so the width must not be multiplied by `dcp_world_size` (`test_mamba_table_preserves_speculative_capacity_with_dcp` exercises a 354-wide Mamba row). When `max_num_blocks` is not supplied, `MultiGroupBlockTable` instead computes `cdiv(max_model_len, block_size * dcp_world_size)` per group, because each DCP rank only stores `1/dcp` of the tokens. Block-table rows are duplicated (`1 + num_speculative_tokens` copies) when DCP is on, and `slot_mapping` gets `max(num_speculative_tokens - 1, 0) * max_num_reqs` extra entries for MTP draft positions.

**Group fan-out.** `MultiGroupBlockTable` fuses slot-mapping computation across groups (`compute_slot_mapping_fused_groups`) when more than one non-Mamba group exists and every one has `dcp_world_size == 1`, passing per-group table pointers, row strides, block sizes and the minimum block size as one constexpr window. Mamba groups are skipped entirely - `if block_table.is_mamba_group: continue` - because no token-level slot mapping exists for recurrent state. The V2 runner instead subclasses upstream `BlockTables` as `AscendBlockTables`, mainly because Ascend's `reshape_and_cache` requires `int32` slot mappings ([`block_table.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/block_table.py#L76-L141)).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    IDS["Scheduler block ids from the shared BlockPool"]
    IDS --> BT0["BlockTable group 0: MLA plus SFA indexer"]
    IDS --> BT1["BlockTable group 1: compressor state"]
    IDS --> BT2["BlockTable group 2: Mamba states"]
    BT0 --> SM0["slot mapping int32: block id times kernel block size plus offset"]
    BT1 --> SM1["slot mapping int32"]
    BT2 --> NONE["is_mamba_group, skipped by slot mapping"]
    SM0 --> KV["k_cache and v_cache page-strided views"]
    SM1 --> STATE["state views advanced by the padded page"]
    KV --> PAGES["one physical page per layer per scheduler block id"]
    STATE --> PAGES
```

*Scheduler block ids are per-request rows; each cache group owns a block table, and only attention-like groups produce slot mappings into their own page-strided views.*

The GLM-Next layout shows why group identity and physical identity are separate: its scheduler groups allocate **disjoint ids from one global `BlockPool`**, so a request needs enough ids for every group, yet one physical tensor slot can be reused by layers from different groups ([`cache_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/models/glm5next/cache_config.py#L441-L458)). That is what makes `get_glm5_next_pool_bytes_per_block = main_slot_count * main_page_size + small_slot_count * small_page_size` the right divisor for a global block id.

## Scheduler-side ids, group formation, and block-size resolution

The scheduler never sees Ascend tensors, but three patched functions decide which ids mean what.

`_ascend_resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` replaces the upstream function (and the copy imported by `vllm.v1.engine.core`) ([`patch_kv_cache_utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_utils.py#L79-L112)). vLLM PR #40860 rejected hybrid groups with multiple block sizes under decode context parallelism; Ascend implements CP for MLA and SWA-MLA layers independently, so instead of raising it computes `scheduler_block_size = lcm(group_block_sizes) * dcp` and, when prefix caching is enabled, `hash_block_size = gcd(group_block_sizes)`. `tests/ut/patch/platform/test_prefix_cache_cp_patches.py` pins `lcm(16, 32) * 2 = 64` with `gcd = 16`.

`_ascend_get_kv_cache_config_from_groups` restores Ascend's DSV4 shared-tuple planner that vLLM #51718 replaced: on main it emits stride-aware descriptors (`offset`, `layer_stride`, `block_stride = page_size`) that all alias a single backing of `tuple_stride * num_tuple_slots` bytes, with MTP layers in trailing tuple slots ([`patch_kv_cache_utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_utils.py#L456-L518)). `_ascend_pool_bytes_per_block` and `_ascend_max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups` reuse the same divisor so a rank re-plan cannot change `num_blocks` and desynchronize ranks.

`_get_kimi_k3_dspark_mixed_kv_cache_groups` and `group_and_unify_kv_cache_specs` shape the groups themselves: target and causal draft full-attention layers are folded into one `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` group so they share a scheduler block table while keeping separate physical pages per layer, and recurrent layers are split into the fewest balanced groups not larger than the attention group ([`patch_kv_cache_utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_utils.py#L115-L205)). `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs.max_num_blocks_per_req` is patched too, to preserve the inner spec's block-table width rather than the base-class default.

## NZ layout on the KV path

Ascend KV cache is stored **ND-shaped with explicit page strides**; the fractal NZ format appears on the transfer side. `trans_nd_to_nz` converts the last two dimensions into NZ fractals - `(16, 32)` for `int8` and `(16, 16)` otherwise - by reshaping to `[..., ceil(b/b0), ceil(a/a0), a0, b0]` and permuting ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L1473-L1495)). The layerwise Mooncake connector is the only caller on the KV path: before sending, it views the resident tensor as `(-1, block_size, head_num * head_dim)`, applies `trans_nd_to_nz`, and reshapes back, with the comment that "due to the FIA operator constraints, the expected kv cache is ND format, NZ shape, while the `npu_format_cast` method only modifies the memory layout" ([`mooncake_layerwise_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_layerwise_connector.py#L2011-L2018)). Do not confuse this with `maybe_trans_nz`, which is the *weight* layout policy.

## DSA/DSA-compressed slot addressing

`attention/dsa_attn_kv_plan.py` centralizes a second, orthogonal layout decision: how a compressed sparse-attention cache is addressed. A `DsaAttnKvPlan` carries `layout_kv` (`"PA_ND"` or `"PA_BBND"`), the compressor slot-mapping format (`DSA_COMPRESSOR_SLOT_MAPPING_FLAT = 1` or `DSA_COMPRESSOR_SLOT_MAPPING_BLOCK_OFFSET = 2`), and whether block-offset slots are required ([`dsa_attn_kv_plan.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_attn_kv_plan.py#L60-L136)).

When `requires_block_offset_slots` is true, `format_dsa_slot_mapping` rewrites a flat slot tensor into `[num_tokens, 2]` of `(block_index, in-block offset)`; the scatter path then either feeds those two-column indices to `npu_scatter_nd_update_` (A5 BF16 `SparseFlashMla`, `PA_BBND`) or to `kv_compress_epilog` with `layout=1`. The flat format is used by the FP8 plan, which scatters with `npu_scatter_nd_update_sk`. Both `compressor_metadata` and `compressor_metadata_out` receive the storage block size and the format integer, so the metadata builder and the scatter op can never disagree about page addressing.

## KV layer parallelism (KVPP)

KVPP changes **where** cache lives, not what a block id means. `KVPPConfig.from_vllm_config` sets `size = tensor_parallel_size` when `additional_config.enable_kvpp` is true and validates eagerly-rejected combinations: no PCP, no DCP, no KV-transfer connector, `--enforce-eager` required, non-hybrid MLA only, and MTP-only speculation with a fixed token count ([`ascend_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py#L59-L92)).

[`core/kv_cache_placement.py`](../../vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_placement.py) builds a `KVPPPhysicalCachePlan` that keeps the upstream **logical** spec while budgeting the **physical** view:

- `map_kvpp_layers_to_owners` sorts PP-local layer indices and hands contiguous balanced partitions to KVPP ranks. MTP layers are excluded from ownership, so they stay fully allocated on every rank and can live on any pipeline stage.
- `build_layer_cache_bundles` groups all cache names sharing a layer index into one bundle (main MLA plus its indexer), sorting by `(layer_index, is_indexer, name)` so every rank derives identical bundle order regardless of dict/set iteration order.
- `build_kvpp_buffer_sizes` computes per-block byte sizes per component: indexer size from `sfa_dcp_replicated_indexer_size * block_size * num_kv_heads * head_size` plus an optional scale tail; a packed sparse-C8 main cache as the whole page; otherwise the page split by `calc_split_factor` or the quant split factor.
- `build_kvpp_layer_layout` lays the components of one bundle end-to-end with a running cursor, so each broadcast bundle is contiguous even though layers are not globally contiguous.
- `get_num_blocks(available_bytes)` divides by `persistent_bytes + KVPP_SCRATCH_BUFFER_COUNT * max_bundle_bytes` (scratch count is 2, one for the current layer and one for the prefetch).

`allocate_kvpp_cache` then allocates a private buffer for owned layers and aliases the two shared scratch buffers for the rest ([`kvpp_cache.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/kvpp_cache.py#L23-L52)). The worker converts the physical block count back into a logical budget - `num_blocks * sum(page_size_bytes)` - so the planner sees a consistent `num_blocks` ([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L553-L559)). `KVPPRuntime.create_from_kv_cache` re-derives each owned layer's contiguous byte span from the allocated views and installs the prefetch scheduler as each layer's `layerwise_kv_cache_hook` ([`kvpp.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/kvpp.py#L22-L63)).

`tests/ut/core/test_kvpp_cache_placement.py` pins the per-rank physical cost (e.g. TP=3 gives 404/392/328 bytes per block), that a budget floors to complete blocks, and that a stage holding only MTP caches has no scratch cost.

## Invariants and failure modes

- **Every group layer is materialized once.** `assert layer_names == set(kv_cache_raw_tensors.keys())` in both runner generations.
- **The worker may over-allocate but never under-allocate.** Every reshape compares `sum_page_size_bytes // page_size_bytes` against `kv_cache_config.num_blocks` and asserts `>=`.
- **A descriptor's geometry must match the layer it names.** GLM-Next requires `block_stride == page_size_bytes` for every shared layer; DSV4 requires contiguous per-layer pages (`block_stride == page_size_bytes`) and a single shared `size`. A mismatch raises `ValueError` naming the layer rather than silently aliasing pages.
- **Kernel block size must divide the physical block.** `BlockTable` raises if no advertised kernel size divides; the runner's `select_common_block_size` is the matching decision on the reshape side, so a backend that advertises an unsatisfiable size breaks either the table or the view geometry.
- **Padding without a block-stride spec is not the pooled layout.** An extra allocation is correct there; taking the padded path would alias unrelated scheduler blocks.
- **Mamba rows are not DCP-sharded.** Multiplying a Mamba group's width by `dcp_world_size` over-allocates and desynchronizes the table against the scheduler.
- **`page_size_padded` on the attention side alone does not shrink the allocation** - it only adds trailing padding that reshape must trim or stride over.

## Extension points and configuration

- **New cache kind**: subclass an upstream spec, add layout metadata, call `KVCacheSpecRegistry.register(kvcache_spec_cls=..., manager_class=..., uniform_type_base_spec=...)` from `register_ascend_kv_cache_specs`, and add a branch to both allocators and both reshapers. `manager_class` decides which upstream block manager allocates the scheduler's ids (full attention vs sliding window).
- **New view geometry**: implement `get_kv_cache_shape(num_blocks, storage_block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size)` on the backend. Because the runner feeds it the storage block size, a compressed spec needs no special case.
- **KVPP**: `additional_config.enable_kvpp` (default `false`); group size follows TP, `KVPP_SCRATCH_BUFFER_COUNT` is fixed at 2.
- **Transfer alignment**: any KV connector that registers cache memory is exposed to the 2 MiB alignment path via `_allocate_int8_cache_tensor`; `supports_shared_backing_with_kv_transfer` in the runner lists the connectors that are allowed to share one hybrid backing (`ExampleHiddenStatesConnector`, `MooncakeConnectorV2`, `MooncakePullConnector`); everything else falls back to per-layer buffers.

## Focused tests

| Test file | What it protects |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/ut/test_compressed_prefix_cache.py` | scheduler block vs storage block split, page size, `max_memory_usage_bytes`, logical-block hashing |
| `tests/ut/worker/test_glm5next_pooled_cache.py` | `requires_padded_page_layout` truth table and per-block-id isolation of pooled state views |
| `tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kv_cache.py` | spec publication from model cache modules, `get_storage_block_size == block_size // tokens_per_state` |
| `tests/ut/worker/test_block_table.py` | DCP slot mapping at several interleave sizes, MTP slot capacity, Mamba row width, no logical-block expansion for DSV4 |
| `tests/ut/worker/test_attn_utils_v2.py` | V2 allocation invariants, storage block size in views, SFA DCP replication size, hidden-state cache, KVPP view construction |
| `tests/ut/core/test_kvpp_cache_placement.py`, `tests/ut/worker/test_kvpp_cache.py` | owner partitioning, bundle layout, physical budget, scratch aliasing |
| `tests/ut/patch/platform/test_prefix_cache_cp_patches.py` | `lcm * dcp` / `gcd` scheduler and hash block sizes for hybrid groups |
| `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_compute_slot_mapping*.py` | the slot-mapping kernel against the DCP/interleave contract |

nodes.title: MoE Execution: Router, Dispatch, Comm Methods, and EPLB
nodes.description: The end-to-end Ascend Mixture-of-Experts path — expert routing through the Ascend router factory, the token dispatcher and prepare/finalize variants, how select_moe_comm_method picks ALLGATHER/ALLTOALL/MC2/FUSED-MC2 per forward from the hardware MoECommPolicy, shared-expert overlap, and the dynamic versus force EPLB flavours.
nodes.body:
# MoE Execution: Router, Dispatch, Comm Methods, and EPLB

An Ascend MoE layer is not one kernel call. It is a small distributed protocol: pad and shard the activations to a common batch shape, all-gather or all-to-all the tokens so every expert sees its work, run grouped matmuls locally, exchange the results back, reduce, and — in parallel on a second stream — execute the shared expert MLP. Which collectives that protocol uses is decided **fresh on every forward** from the token count, the expert-parallel (EP) world size, the quantization config and the hardware profile. That decision is the highest-leverage knob on this page: it changes which dispatcher runs, which padding rule applies, whether a `mc2_mask` exists, and whether a fused CANN operator replaces the whole dispatch/MLP/combine sequence.

Everything below hangs off three owner objects:

| Owner | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `AscendMoERunner` ([`fused_moe.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/fused_moe.py#L79-L145)) | Per-layer coordinator. Registers the comm methods, owns the shared-expert executor, chooses the forward entry point, and knows when outputs are already reduced. |
| `AscendRoutedExperts` ([`routed_experts.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/routed_experts.py#L334-L520)) | Owns expert weights, the quant method, EPLB placement maps, and `forward_impl` — prepare → route → fused experts → finalize. |
| `MoECommMethod` ([`moe_comm_method.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py#L79-L181)) | Holds one token dispatcher plus one prepare/finalize pair, and runs dispatch → MLP → combine. |

Related reading: [Custom Ops and Kernels](../architecture/custom-ops-and-kernels.md) for the grouped-matmul and routing kernels, [Quantization](quantization.md) for the per-quant-type MLP hooks the comm methods call, [Distributed and HCCL](../integrations/distributed-and-hccl.md) for the EP/MC2 process groups, and [Request Execution](../workflows/request-execution.md) for where the forward context is established.

## The per-forward communication decision

`select_moe_comm_method(num_tokens, vllm_config)` ([`ascend_forward_context.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py#L343-L382)) returns a `MoECommType` — `ALLGATHER`, `ALLTOALL`, `MC2`, or `FUSED_MC2` ([L26-L30](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py#L26-L30)). It runs inside `set_ascend_forward_context` and its Model Runner V2 equivalent, so the answer is baked into the forward context (`moe_comm_type` and the resolved `moe_comm_method`) before any MoE layer executes.

<!-- openwiki: mermaid parse failed and this diagram was converted to a text fence so it does not break rendering. Fix the diagram source and restore the mermaid fence. Parser error: Heuristic: an unescaped angle bracket inside a label breaks rendering; rephrase the label. -->
```text
flowchart TD
    A["select_moe_comm_method(num_tokens)"] --> B{"is_moe_model?"}
    B -->|no| N["None - no MoE path"]
    B -->|yes| C{"EP enabled and ep world size > 1?"}
    C -->|no| AG["ALLGATHER"]
    C -->|yes| D{"LoRA config present?"}
    D -->|yes| A2A["ALLTOALL"]
    D -->|no| E{"profile moe_comm_policy is ALLGATHER?"}
    E -->|yes| AG
    E -->|no| F["policy selector with num_tokens and mc2_tokens_capacity"]
    F --> G["CAPACITY_AND_EXPERT_DENSITY - A2"]
    F --> H["FUSED_OR_CAPACITY - A3"]
    F --> I["CAPACITY_AND_WORLD_SIZE - A5"]
    G --> G1{"experts per device <= 24 and ep >= 16 and tokens <= capacity?"}
    G1 -->|yes| MC2["MC2"]
    G1 -->|no| AG
    H --> H1{"CANN MegaMoe usable?"}
    H1 -->|yes| FM["FUSED_MC2"]
    H1 -->|no| H2{"enable_fused_mc2 == 1 and ep <= 32?"}
    H2 -->|yes| FM
    H2 -->|no| H3{"tokens <= capacity?"}
    H3 -->|yes| MC2
    H3 -->|no| A2A
    I --> I1{"world size <= top_k?"}
    I1 -->|yes| AG
    I1 -->|no| I2{"tokens <= capacity?"}
    I2 -->|yes| MC2
    I2 -->|no| A2A
```

*How `select_moe_comm_method` resolves to one of the four comm types; the policy enum comes from the frozen hardware profile.*

Three inputs deserve emphasis because they are easy to get wrong:

**The token count is a DP-maximum, not a local count.** Both call sites pass the largest per-rank batch (`max(num_tokens_across_dp)` in MRv1, `max_tokens_across_dp` in the MRv2 platform hook, [`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L588-L594)). Selecting from a local count would let different DP ranks choose different collectives and deadlock.

**`mc2_tokens_capacity` is a once-computed, per-rank capacity.** `set_mc2_tokens_capacity` ([L229-L260](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py#L229-L260)) derives a total batch budget — `max_num_batched_tokens` when prefill MC2 or non-decode-only MegaMoe is in play, else the largest ACLGraph capture size, else `max_num_reqs * uniform_decode_query_len` — then ceil-divides by TP size and clamps the *per-TP-rank* value to 4096 for CANN MegaMoe, 512 for `dispatch_ffn_combine`, or 512 for plain MC2. The clamp is what makes MC2 a small-batch method: above the cap the selector falls through to `ALLTOALL`.

**MegaMoe has its own gate.** `use_cann_megamoe` ([L87-L97](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py#L87-L97)) requires the `cann_ops_transformer` package to import, the profile to advertise `CANN_MEGAMOE` (A3 only), `enable_fused_mc2 == 1`, a MoE model, expert parallelism enabled, `1 < ep_world_size <= 64`, and no LoRA config. Note that `enable_fused_mc2=2` is downgraded to `1` during config validation while flipping `_MEGA_MOE_SUPPORTED` off unless the CANN op package is importable ([`ascend_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py#L535-L541)), so the integer is a *feature request*, not a guarantee.

The profile side is just an enum field: `moe_comm_policy` is `CAPACITY_AND_EXPERT_DENSITY` on A2, `FUSED_OR_CAPACITY` on A3, `ALLGATHER` on 310P, and `CAPACITY_AND_WORLD_SIZE` on A5 ([`hardware_profile.py`](../../vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py#L157-L251)). `_MOE_COMM_SELECTORS` maps each non-`ALLGATHER` policy to its selector function ([L336-L340](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py#L336-L340)). The consequence to remember when tuning: on A2 you can only reach `MC2` or `ALLGATHER`; on A3 `ALLTOALL` and `FUSED_MC2` are additionally reachable; on A5 the tie-breaker is `world_size <= top_k` → `ALLGATHER`.

The selected type is also consumed *outside* the forward: `should_skip_allreduce_across_dp_group` asks it twice — once at the potential decode batch size, once at `max_num_batched_tokens` — to decide whether DP all-reduce can be skipped, which in turn flips the MC2 dispatcher's `global_bs` between 0 (uniform, mask-driven) and a real value (per-rank ragged) ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L1160-L1217)). Both `profile_run` implementations also probe it to decide whether an extra dummy run at `mc2_tokens_capacity` is needed to reserve HCCL buffers ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4033-L4040), [`v2/model_runner.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py#L298-L316)).

## Registering the implementations

Comm types are mapped to live objects in a module-level dict, populated by `setup_moe_comm_method(moe_config)` ([L55-L62](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py#L55-L62)):

```python
def setup_moe_comm_method(moe_config):
    if moe_config.ep_size > 1:
        _MoECommMethods[MoECommType.ALLTOALL] = AlltoAllCommImpl(moe_config)
        _MoECommMethods[MoECommType.ALLGATHER] = AllGatherCommImpl(moe_config)
        _MoECommMethods[MoECommType.MC2] = MC2CommImpl(moe_config)
        _MoECommMethods[MoECommType.FUSED_MC2] = FusedMC2CommImpl(moe_config)
    else:
        _MoECommMethods[MoECommType.ALLGATHER] = AllGatherCommImpl(moe_config)
```

Only `AscendMoERunner.__init__` calls it ([L136-L145](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/fused_moe.py#L136-L145)), so the registry acquires entries lazily as the first MoE layer is constructed, and `get_moe_comm_method(None)` simply returns `None` for dense models. Constructing each impl eagerly (even the ones this step will never use) is what makes the per-forward lookup a dict read: instances build their dispatcher and prepare/finalize objects once, and `FusedMC2CommImpl.__init__` additionally imports the CANN MegaMoe ops and allocates `expert_token_nums` there. 310P keeps the same dict but overwrites the `ALLGATHER` entry with `AllGatherCommImpl310` ([`_310p/fused_moe/fused_moe.py`](../../vllm_ascend/_310p/fused_moe/fused_moe.py#L196)), whose dispatcher uses `npu_moe_init_routing_v2` and `cumsum`-mode `group_list`.

Registration is a *global* dict keyed only by comm type, while construction is per-layer — so the last layer constructed wins. That is safe because every layer of a model shares one `FusedMoEConfig`, and it is the reason the registry must not be treated as per-layer state.

### The patched factory

Upstream models never name `AscendMoERunner`. They call `FusedMoEFactory`, which `patch/platform/patch_fused_moe.py` rebinds to `_ascend_FusedMoE` in both `vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe` and `...fused_moe.layer`, plus every already-imported `vllm.model_executor.models.*` module that captured the original binding ([L212-L220](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_fused_moe.py#L212-L220)). Import order matters and is documented in the file header: the patch runs from `adapt_patch()` during worker init, before models load, so `deepseek_v2` and friends import the Ascend factory.

Inside the wrapper ([L114-L209](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_fused_moe.py#L114-L209)) four things happen that downstream code depends on:

1. **EPLB capacity is pushed upstream.** When `eplb_config.dynamic_eplb` or `expert_map_path` is set, the wrapper forces `enable_eplb=True` and injects its own `num_redundant_experts` (raising on a conflicting non-zero upstream value). This has to happen at factory time because `RoutedExperts` allocates its weight tensors before any runner exists. `AscendRoutedExperts.init_eplb` then re-checks that the allocated redundancy matches the placement plan and fails loudly on mismatch ([`routed_experts.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/routed_experts.py#L424-L464)).
2. **The router is built by `create_ascend_fused_moe_router`** unless the caller supplied one, with `global_num_experts=num_experts+num_redundant_experts` but `num_logical_experts=num_experts` so EPLB's logical/physical split stays coherent, and with an `AscendEplbLayerState` only when EPLB *and* the V2 model runner are both active.
3. **Routed-experts class adaptation.** An explicitly passed `routed_experts_cls` (upstream starts passing `GptOssRoutedExperts`) is composed into `type("Ascend"+name, (cls, AscendRoutedExperts))` so model-specific loading overrides keep MRO priority while Ascend owns init and device execution.
4. **The hash table is shared.** `hash_indices_table` is also forwarded as `routed_experts_args["tid2eid"]`, keeping the upstream router and the legacy `tid2eid` lookup path on one source of truth.

## One invocation, step by step

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Runner as AscendMoERunner
    participant RE as AscendRoutedExperts
    participant CM as MoECommMethod
    participant PF as PrepareAndFinalize
    participant RT as Router
    participant TD as TokenDispatcher
    participant SE as AscendSharedExperts
    Runner->>RE: prepare, route, finalize
    RE->>CM: prepare(hidden_states, router_logits, replace_allreduce, quant_type)
    CM->>PF: build padded or sharded views and mc2_mask
    RE->>RT: select logical experts
    RE->>CM: fused_experts(input, quant_method)
    CM->>TD: token_dispatch
    CM->>CM: apply_moe_mlp gmm1, activation, gmm2
    CM->>TD: token_combine
    RE->>CM: finalize with reduce_results from comm impl type
    Runner->>SE: shared expert forward on second stream
    SE-->>Runner: shared output
```

`AscendRoutedExperts.forward_impl` ([L617-L715](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/routed_experts.py#L617-L715)) is the spine. It calls `moe_comm_method.prepare` with `replace_allreduce=self.moe_config.is_sequence_parallel`, selects experts, calls `quant_method.apply(...)` — which forwards to `moe_comm_method.fused_experts` with the quant method itself as a hook provider — optionally accumulates EPLB load, and calls `finalize` with `reduce_results=isinstance(moe_comm_method, AllGatherCommImpl)`. That last expression is the reduction contract in one line: MC2/ALLTOALL/FUSED_MC2 finalize already ends in a reduce-scatter/all-reduce, while AllGather needs the explicit reduction in `FusedMoE`-level code.

`MoECommMethod.fused_experts` ([L117-L167](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py#L117-L167)) is the shared skeleton for the non-fused methods. It records `before_dispatch_evt`, builds a `MoETokenDispatchInput`, dispatches, builds a `MoEMlpComputeInput`, runs either `apply_moe_mlp` (quantized path) or the subclass `_apply_mlp` (legacy 310P path), records `before_combine_evt`, combines, and returns a `FusedExpertsResult` carrying `routed_out`, the three events, `group_list_type`, and `expert_tokens` (the per-expert token counts EPLB records). The `dataclass/` package is the contract boundary: `MoeRouterInput` carries `expert_map`, `mc2_mask`, `pertoken_scale`, `apply_router_weight_on_input`, and `log2phy`, so dispatch never reaches back into the layer for state.

## The four communication methods

| Comm type | Impl | Token dispatcher | Prepare / finalize | Typical selection |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ALLGATHER` | `AllGatherCommImpl` | `TokenDispatcherWithAllGather` | `PrepareAndFinalizeWithAllGather` | No effective EP, 310P, A2 sparse experts, A5 `world_size <= top_k` |
| `MC2` | `MC2CommImpl` | `TokenDispatcherWithMC2` | `PrepareAndFinalizeWithMC2` | Small batches within `mc2_tokens_capacity`, with EP |
| `ALLTOALL` | `AlltoAllCommImpl` | `TokenDispatcherWithAll2AllV` | `PrepareAndFinalizeWithAll2All` | Large batches, LoRA + EP |
| `FUSED_MC2` | `FusedMC2CommImpl` | `TokenDispatcherWithMC2` | `PrepareAndFinalizeWithMC2` | `enable_fused_mc2=1` on A3-eligible EP sizes, or CANN MegaMoe |

`MC2` and `FUSED_MC2` share a dispatcher and prepare/finalize; they differ only in `fused_experts`, which for `FUSED_MC2` bypasses the Python dispatch/MLP/combine sequence entirely.

### MC2: single fused dispatch/combine ops

`TokenDispatcherWithMC2` ([L109-L333](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py#L109-L333)) wraps `torch_npu.npu_moe_distribute_dispatch_v2` and `npu_moe_distribute_combine_v2` against the MC2 HCCL group, obtained by name from the process group backend. Its constructor resolves several flags from the hardware profile — `need_extra_args` (`MOE_DISPATCH_EXTRA_ARGS`), `need_shared_expert_args` (`MOE_DISPATCH_SHARED_EXPERT_ARGS`), `need_expert_scale` (shared-expert args or `mc2_comm_alg == "hierarchy"`) — and derives the batch contract:

* `max_num_tokens_per_rank = mc2_tokens_capacity // tp_size`, exposed so MegaMoe can size its symmetric buffer from a rank-invariant value.
* `global_bs = max_num_tokens_per_rank * ep_world_size` **only** when `should_skip_allreduce_across_dp_group` is true; otherwise `0`, meaning "uniform batch across ranks". When `global_bs == 0` the mask (`x_active_mask`) is passed and semantics are mask-driven; when it is non-zero the mask is *not* passed and per-rank token counts may differ. Hierarchy communication and MegaMoe both force `global_bs=0` because their operators do not support dynamic batch sizes.
* `expert_token_nums_type` is `count` for the W4A8 per-channel `grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2` path and `cumsum` otherwise, so downstream grouped matmul sees the layout it expects.
* `quant_mode` is chosen per call: an explicit `comm_quant_mode` wins, else 4 for A5 MXFP dispatch with quant, else 2 for legacy int communication quant, else 0. Combine additionally honors `additional_config.combine_quant_mode`, which overrides everything.

`MC2CommImpl` and `FusedMC2CommImpl` also expose `pad_and_split_input_ids` by delegation, because the router needs identically padded `input_ids` when a hash/vision route runs.

### ALLGATHER: local routing, EP-wide gather

`TokenDispatcherWithAllGather` ([L336-L439](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py#L336-L439)) does no token exchange. It masks out non-local experts through `expert_map`, restricts `npu_moe_init_routing` to this rank's contiguous expert range, and receives `group_list_type=1` (per-expert counts). `token_combine` is a single `npu_moe_token_unpermute` with the saved `expanded_row_idx` and routing weights. The output has arrived because `PrepareAndFinalizeWithAllGather` already all-gathered the tokens. Notable subtleties encoded here:

* Fused first-stage quantization is folded into init-routing when `dispatch_with_quant` is on but no `pertoken_scale` arrived (`quant_mode` 1/3/9 for plain/MXFP/MXFP4, else −1).
* W8A8FP and unquantized MXFP4-without-scales deliberately skip dispatch quantization and quantize inside the MLP instead.
* LoRA plus a quantized activation disables dispatch quantization entirely after validating the input, because the LoRA A matmul needs the original BF16/FP16 activations.

### ALLTOALL: permutation plus variable-split exchange

`TokenDispatcherWithAll2AllV` ([L442-L722](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py#L442-L722)) computes `input_splits` (tokens this rank sends to each EP rank) and `output_splits` (tokens it will receive) with two histograms and an EP all-gather of per-expert counts, permutes locally with `npu_moe_token_permute`, exchanges through `async_all_to_all` (an `all_to_all_single` on a dedicated `COMM_STREAM`, optionally event-gated so it can overlap other work), and re-sorts the received tokens by local expert with `npu_moe_init_routing_v2` when quantizing.
