Both exchange buffers are released with `untyped_storage().resize_(0)` immediately after their handle waits, and the per-expert quantization scale tensor is exchanged in a *second* all-to-all so the MLP can reuse it. `expert_ids_per_ep_rank` is precomputed at construction and registered as a non-persistent buffer on the runner, so graph capture sees it as a constant.

## Prepare and finalize: padding and reduction rules

Each prepare/finalize pair encodes a different alignment rule, and getting the rule wrong produces silent accuracy loss rather than an error.

**`PrepareAndFinalizeWithAll2All`** ([L113-L228](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/prepare_finalize.py#L113-L228)) pads to the next multiple of TP size *cyclically* (`pad_size = tp_size - num_tokens`), tensor-splits along the token dim, and in `finalize` allocates a fresh padded buffer, all-gathers into split views of it, and trims back to the original token count. The fresh allocation is deliberate: reusing the prepare-phase split could alias `hidden_states`, which the shared expert may still be reading, so an in-place all-gather would corrupt it.

**`PrepareAndFinalizeWithMC2`** ([L231-L348](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/prepare_finalize.py#L231-L348)) pads to `_EXTRA_CTX.padded_num_tokens` — the DP-wide, TP-aligned batch length reserved in the forward context — and splits both activations and `mc2_mask` per TP rank. In `replace_allreduce` mode (sequence-parallel MoE) the local shard is already token-sharded, so it slices the mask by `tp_rank` offset, pads only to `padded_num_tokens // tp_size`, and `finalize` returns the shard directly instead of running the collective.

**`PrepareAndFinalizeWithAllGather`** ([L351-L574](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/prepare_finalize.py#L351-L574)) has two paths selected by `moe_config.is_sequence_parallel`:

| Path | Prepare | Finalize | Communication sequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DP-group (no SP) | pad to `max_tokens_across_dp`, all-gather on DP group | reduce-scatter on DP group, trim | `Attn → TP AR → DP AG → MoE → DP RS → TP AR` |
| EP-group (SP) | `maybe_all_gather_and_maybe_unpad` (EP AG), optional fused quant first | `maybe_pad_and_reduce` (EP RS) | `TP AG → Attn → TP RS → EP AG → MoE → EP RS` |

The EP path is the optimization: it collapses TP all-gather with DP all-gather, and TP reduce-scatter with DP reduce-scatter, into EP-group collectives. `_use_ep_sequence_parallel` deliberately reads *only* `moe_config.is_sequence_parallel` — deriving it from any other flag would gather tokens a second time before routing. Note also that the DP path's `finalize` ignores `reduce_results`: with SP the reduce-scatter already replaces the TP all-reduce, which is why `AscendMoERunner._fused_output_is_reduced` reports `ALLGATHER`+SP as reduced ([L175-L187](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/fused_moe.py#L175-L187)).

PCP adds a third dimension: when `pcp_size > 1` both paths pad to `max_tokens_across_pcp`, all-gather on the PCP group before the MLP, and reduce-scatter plus trim afterwards.

## FUSED_MC2: `dispatch_ffn_combine` and CANN MegaMoe

`FusedMC2CommImpl` ([L258-L508](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py#L258-L508)) replaces the dispatch/MLP/combine sequence with a single fused CANN operator. It offers two operators, chosen per forward by `_EXTRA_CTX.use_mega_moe`:

* **`torch.ops._C_ascend.dispatch_ffn_combine`** — requires `w1_scale_bias`/`w2_scale_bias` (it asserts on them), takes `max_output_size = mega_moe_max_tokens`, an optional `swiglu_limit`, and a preallocated `expert_token_nums` buffer.
* **`cann_ops_transformer.ops.mega_moe`** — needs a symmetric buffer from `get_symm_buffer_for_mega_moe`, a collective handshake over the MC2 group.

The sym-buffer sizing ([L292-L370](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py#L292-L370)) is the most fragile invariant in this path and is documented as such in the code: every shape parameter must be **rank-invariant**, derived only from compile-time config, because ranks that compute different values allocate mismatched buffers or allocate at different points and HCCL aborts with *SUSPECT REMOTE ERROR 507057*. `num_max_tokens_per_rank` therefore comes from `global_bs // ep_world_size` when `global_bs > 0` and from the dispatcher's `max_num_tokens_per_rank` otherwise; `max_recv_token_num` is the absolute safe bound on decode-only nodes and `mega_moe_max_tokens` elsewhere, with a `warning_once` explaining that exceeding it on a P or PD-mixed node degrades precision rather than crashing. `_apply_cann_mega_moe` additionally rejects a forward whose token count exceeds `max_num_tokens_per_rank` and tells the operator the quantization layout via `_get_cann_mega_moe_quant_settings` — W8A8 and W4A8 INT for A2/A3, and only int8 + `FRACTAL_NZ` per-expert weight lists are acceptable, which is why `process_weights_after_loading` casts fused-MC2 weights to NZ and splits them into per-expert lists when MegaMoe or dynamic EPLB is active ([`routed_experts.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/routed_experts.py#L114-L128)).

`get_fused_mc2_weights` ([L163-L194](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/routed_experts.py#L163-L194)) is the weight adapter: it normalizes the layer's storage into `MoEWeights` and, on the MegaMoe path, hands over the int8-shaped per-expert lists untouched so the operator sees the packing it expects.

## Shared experts and the overlap schedule

`AscendSharedExperts` ([`shared_experts.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/shared_experts.py#L62-L432)) owns shared-expert execution and moves the split/overlap detail out of the runner while the original module stays registered for checkpoint compatibility. It resolves a `SharedExpertParallelMode` from the *physical* TP group rather than `moe_config.tp_size` — EP rewrites the latter to 1, but the shared-expert linears still span the TP group:

| Mode | Activations | Weights | Communication |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TENSOR_PARALLEL` | full | TP-sharded | none here; a TP all-reduce may be applied by the runner |
| `SHARED_EXPERT_DATA_PARALLEL_ONLY` | full | replicated | local token split, then TP all-gather |
| `SEQUENCE_PARALLEL_ONLY` | SP-sharded | TP-sharded | TP all-gather in, pad + reduce-scatter out |
| `SEQUENCE_PARALLEL_SEDP` | SP-sharded | replicated | none |

Overlap is driven by `additional_config.multistream_overlap_shared_expert` and a set of stream events carried in `FusedMoEEvents` (`before_routed_experts`, `after_routed_experts`, `before_dispatch`, `before_gmm2`, `before_combine`, `after_routed_finalize`). The schedule in `forward` is explicit: dynamic quantization waits only for the input, the gate-up projection waits for `before_dispatch` so it overlaps token dispatch, the activation waits for `before_gmm2` so it overlaps the routed down-projection, and the shared down-projection waits for `before_combine` so it overlaps the combine. The *output* collective is the operation that must wait for routed finalization, so it moves to the auxiliary stream after `after_routed_finalize`. When multistream is enabled the constructor also wraps the quant method's `process_weights_after_loading` to run `validate_consistency()` — a randomized comparison of integrated versus split computation that raises rather than silently degrade.

For sequence-parallel MoE with latent transforms, `AscendMoERunner` swaps its forward entry to the custom op `ascend_moe_forward_shared_sp`, which registers a fake implementation returning **SP-local** shared-output shape (the upstream fake used the gathered token count, [`fused_moe.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/fused_moe.py#L40-L76)). It also starts the shared-input all-gather before the routed latent down-projection (`apply_routed_input_transform`) and joins it after the routed up-projection (`apply_routed_output_transform`), guarded by `_can_overlap_sp_shared_with` so models without those transforms keep single-stream synchronization.

Reduction ownership is worth stating once: `_maybe_reduce_final_output` only falls back to a TP all-reduce when `_fused_output_is_reduced` is false *and* the model is not sequence-parallel — reducing SP token shards position-wise would corrupt them.

## Expert routing

`create_ascend_fused_moe_router` ([`router_factory.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/router/router_factory.py#L36-L118)) picks one of four routers:

| Condition | Router |
| --- | --- |
| `custom_routing_function` provided | upstream `CustomRoutingRouter` |
| profile supports `FUSED_MOE_COMPATIBILITY` (310P) | `AscendGroupedTopKRouter310` |
| `check_npu_moe_gating_top_k` passes | `AscendFusedTopKRouter` (NPU gating op) |
| otherwise | `AscendGroupedTopKRouter` (pure-torch grouped top-k) |

`check_npu_moe_gating_top_k` rejects sigmoid + `renormalize=False`, any custom routing function, unknown scoring funcs, `top_k < 1`, and `topk_group > num_expert_group`; accepted scoring funcs are `softmax`, `sigmoid`, and `sqrtsoftplus`. `AscendFusedTopKRouter` also re-checks a `is_fused_supported` divisibility condition at forward time and falls back to the torch path when it fails.

**Vision and hash checkpoints.** The factory threads two extra parameters that upstream does not have — `bias_vl` and `image_sentinel_lo` (default 129257) — through to `AscendFusedTopKRouter`. They exist for DeepSeek-V4-style vision checkpoints that borrow five consecutive in-vocabulary sentinel ids as `IMAGE_START..IMAGE_END`: text rows keep the deterministic `tid2eid` lookup, image rows use `bias_vl` with sqrt-softplus scores ([`fused_topk_router.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/router/fused_topk_router.py#L31-L76)). Because that route needs `input_ids` aligned with the local router rows, `_compute_routing` asks the *comm method* to align them: `prepare_finalize.all_gather_input_id_with_dp_group` on `ALLGATHER`, `pad_and_split_input_ids` on the others, plus a `sequence_parallel_chunk` only when the comm path has not already aligned them ([L164-L175](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/router/fused_topk_router.py#L164-L175)). This is the clearest example of a routing concern reaching into the comm layer, and the reason the `input_ids` argument is plumbed through `AscendRoutedExperts.forward_impl` at all.

`_select_experts` ([L562-L615](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/routed_experts.py#L562-L615)) then applies, in order: the router, the `log2phy` placement map (dynamic EPLB), optional `mix_placement` shared-expert id concatenation, and finally one of two load-balancing overrides — force EPLB's deterministic round-robin table, or the random permutation used during `_EXTRA_CTX.in_profile_run` dummy runs.

## EPLB: dynamic/async and force

Two load-balancing mechanisms reach into this path, and they are **mutually exclusive**: `AscendConfig.derive_and_validate` raises `ValueError("enable_force_eplb cannot be mixed with dynamic_eplb.")` for a MoE model with both set ([`ascend_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py#L549-L558)).

### Dynamic (asynchronous) EPLB — Model Runner V1

`eplb_config.dynamic_eplb` (guarded by `DYNAMIC_EPLB=true` or `EXPERT_MAP_RECORD=true`) turns on a full movement plane in the MRv1 runner ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L538-L562)):

* a `multiprocessing.Manager().dict` for `expert_map`/`moe_load`/`expert_maps`,
* an `EplbProcess` launched with `spawn` as a daemon subprocess running the policy worker,
* a `D2DExpertWeightLoader` and an `VllmEplbAdaptor` (registered per real MoE layer, so PP-missing layers never appear),
* an `EplbUpdator` that coordinates phases, and
* a dedicated `dynamic_eplb` HCCL process group created during model-parallel init ([`parallel_state.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/parallel_state.py#L102-L106)) used for the load all-gather and the D2D transfers.

`EplbUpdator` ([`eplb_updator.py`](../../vllm_ascend/eplb/eplb_updator.py#L32-L191)) runs a three-phase counter cycle rather than a stop-the-world pause:

| Phase | Counter range | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heat collection | `0 .. expert_heat_collection_interval-1` | `forward_end` all-gathers per-rank `moe_load` into `shared_dict`, then wakes the worker |
| Algorithm | next `algorithm_execution_interval` steps | `forward_before` blocks on `block_update_q` for the new placement and issues D2D transfer tasks |
| Weight update | next `num_moe_layers` steps | one layer per step: wait for P2P, then commit expert map, `log2phy` map and weights |

Per-step integration is a pair of hooks around the forward: `forward_before()` (fetch update info, `generate_expert_d2d_transfer_task`, launch async transfer) and `forward_end(eplb_heat_collection_status)` (gather load and/or commit weights). When `expert_heat_collection_status` is false the counter does not advance during the collection phase, which is how `eplb_heat_collection_stage = prefill|decode` restricts heat to one stage; `update_eplb_heat_collection_status` classifies an iteration by comparing padded token count against `max_num_reqs * uniform_decode_query_len`. `eplb_policy_type == 3` (FlashLB) additionally switches the per-layer load buffer to a time-series (`multi_stage`), which is why `moe_load` becomes `[interval, local_experts]` and `load_counter` is needed. The worker itself runs the selected `PolicyFactory` policy in the subprocess and packs per-layer update info back.

On the execution side, `AscendRoutedExperts.init_eplb` builds `global_expert_map`, `ascend_expert_map`, `log2phy`, and `global_redundant_expert_num`; `_select_experts` maps logical ids through `log2phy`; and after the MLP, `forward_impl` converts `expert_tokens` into per-expert counts (differencing the cumsum form) and accumulates them into `moe_load`. `log2phy`, `moe_load`, and `load_counter` are promoted to named buffers so level-2 sleep/wake restores them. Dynamic EPLB is incompatible with Ascend MoE LoRA and with a sizeable set of quantization layouts — `VllmEplbAdaptor` rejects unsupported combos and refuses `W4A8MXFP` outright ([`vllm_adaptor.py`](../../vllm_ascend/eplb/adaptor/vllm_adaptor.py#L135-L164)).

### Force EPLB

`additional_config.enable_force_eplb` is a debugging/validation mode, not a balancer: it *replaces* expert selection with a deterministic round-robin assignment so every rank has provably identical load. `_build_round_robin_topk` ([`force_eplb.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/force_eplb.py#L108-L142)) requires `num_logical_experts % ep_size == 0`, strides experts across ranks with an `ep_rank`-dependent offset, and caches tables on the comm-method instance keyed by `(num_tokens, top_k, num_logical_experts, ep_size, ep_rank, dtype, device)`. Because tables must exist before graph capture, `build_force_eplb_topk` pre-warms one table per capture size and for both int32 and int64 in `_dummy_run` when not capturing ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3968-L3970)). `get_force_eplb_topk` returns `None` when there is no MoE comm method, so the same code is inert on dense models.

### Model Runner V2 note

With `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` the legacy `dynamic_eplb` machinery is not used at all — quantization methods hard-set `dynamic_eplb = False` — and EPLB runs through the upstream control plane instead: `AscendEPLBController` with a per-batch `load_collection_phase` filter, `AscendEplbState`/`AscendEplbLayerState` holding a graph-stable `expert_replica_routing_table`, the `ascend_eplb_map_to_physical_and_record` custom op for map-plus-record, and `AscendGlooEplbCommunicator` for CPU-staged movement. The factory's `_adapt_eplb_router` (only when `enable_eplb and use_v2_model_runner`) rebinds `_apply_eplb_mapping` to that op. The design rationale lives in the repository docs: [`model_runner_v1_eplb.md`](../../docs/source/developer_guide/Design_Documents/model_runner_v1_eplb.md) and [`model_runner_v2_eplb.md`](../../docs/source/developer_guide/Design_Documents/model_runner_v2_eplb.md).

The replica routing table is the graph-safety trick: `build_expert_replica_routing_table` ([`eplb.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/eplb.py#L10-L34)) materializes a fixed `[1024, num_logical_experts]` int32 table whose rows cycle through replicas with an `ep_rank` offset, so routing for row *i* is a gather, and placement changes are copied into the existing tensor in place rather than replacing the object.

## Configuration and operations

| Knob | Effect on this path |
| --- | --- |
| `additional_config.enable_fused_mc2` (`0/1/2`) | Enables `FUSED_MC2` reachability; `2` requests MegaMoe and is normalized to `1`. |
| `additional_config.mega_moe_max_tokens` | `dispatch_ffn_combine` `max_output_size` **and** MegaMoe `max_recv_token_num` on P/PD nodes. A reference value: exceeding actual received tokens degrades precision. |
| `additional_config.mc2_comm_alg` (`fullmesh`/`hierarchy`/`fullmesh_v2`) | Passed as `comm_alg` to the MC2 ops; `hierarchy` forces `global_bs=0` and enables `expert_scales`. |
| `additional_config.combine_quant_mode` | Forces the combine-side `comm_quant_mode` regardless of quant type. |
| `additional_config.multistream_overlap_shared_expert` | Turns on the shared-expert overlap schedule. |
| `additional_config.enable_shared_expert_dp` | Selects replicated shared-expert weights (SEDP modes); downgraded to false without EP and `tp_size > 1`. |
| `additional_config.mix_placement` | Concatenates shared-expert ids into `topk_ids` instead of running a separate shared branch. |
| `enable_prefill_mc2` | Makes `mc2_tokens_capacity` follow `max_num_batched_tokens` instead of the decode estimate. |
| `eplb_config.*` (MRv1) | `dynamic_eplb`, `expert_heat_collection_interval`, `algorithm_execution_interval`, `eplb_policy_type`, `num_redundant_experts`, `expert_map_path`/`expert_map_record_path`, `eplb_heat_collection_stage`. |
| `enable_force_eplb` | Round-robin routing; mutually exclusive with `dynamic_eplb`. |
| `eplb_config.load_collection_phase` (MRv2 only) | The only Ascend-specific MRv2 EPLB field; rejected on MRv1. |

Failure modes worth recognizing on sight: `ValueError("Wrong value of self.enable_fused_mc2=…")` means `FUSED_MC2` was selected but the flag is not exactly 1; an assertion on `w1_scale_bias`/`w2_scale_bias` means a quant method reached the `dispatch_ffn_combine` path without the biases the op requires; an HCCL *SUSPECT REMOTE ERROR 507057* during MegaMoe means the symmetric buffer shape parameters diverged across EP ranks; and a `ValueError` about MegaMoe receiving more tokens than its buffer was sized for means `max_num_batched_tokens` must grow or fused MC2 must be disabled.

## Focused tests

* [`tests/ut/test_ascend_forward_context.py`](../../tests/ut/test_ascend_forward_context.py) pins the whole selection matrix per device profile — `(128, 129)` against capacity to prove the `<=` boundary, A3 with and without `enable_fused_mc2`, A5's `world_size`/`top_k` tie-break, 310P always `ALLGATHER`, LoRA and EP-disabled short-circuits, plus `set_mc2_tokens_capacity` ceiling division and the decode-only-node classification.
* [`tests/ut/ops/test_moe_comm_method.py`](../../tests/ut/ops/test_moe_comm_method.py) checks that each impl wires the right prepare/finalize and dispatcher, that `fused_experts` calls dispatch → MLP → combine with the expected payloads, and the MegaMoe sym-buffer sizing on decode-only versus P nodes.
* [`tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py`](../../tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py) covers MC2 mask slicing under SP, TP split/all-gather round-trips, and AllGather DP-group prepare/finalize.
* [`tests/ut/ops/test_eplb.py`](../../tests/ut/ops/test_eplb.py) pins the rank-offset replica table, periodic row wrap, and the load-recording gate.
* [`tests/ut/ops/test_force_eplb.py`](../../tests/ut/ops/test_force_eplb.py) checks round-robin ids, shape validation, and table caching identity.
* [`tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_fused_moe.py`](../../tests/ut/patch/platform/test_patch_fused_moe.py) verifies the factory propagates EPLB redundancy, keeps V1 EPLB on the legacy routing path, shares the hash table, and keeps `bias_vl` in the Ascend router only.
* [`tests/ut/ops/test_fused_moe.py`](../../tests/ut/ops/test_fused_moe.py) is the broadest: runner reduction contract, shared-expert parallel modes, SP multistream overlap ordering, and the hash/vision router `input_ids` alignment paths.

nodes.title: Quantization Methods and Schemes
nodes.description: The Ascend quantization stack - how a checkpoint's quant config is recognized and auto-detected, the scheme registry keyed by (quant_type, layer_type) and its linear/MoE/attention base classes, the weight-loading invariants at TP boundaries (MX group phase, block-scale rounding), KV-cache quantization, and the 310P compatibility variant.
nodes.body:
# Quantization Methods and Schemes

Quantization in vllm-ascend is a three-layer stack. The **top** layer is a set of `QuantizationConfig` subclasses registered with vLLM's own `@register_quantization_config` registry, one per checkpoint format the plugin can serve (`ascend`, `compressed-tensors`, `fp8`, `deepseek_v4_fp8`, `mxfp8`/`modelopt_mxfp8`). The **middle** layer is the plugin's own scheme registry, keyed by `(quant_type, layer_type)`, which maps a checkpoint's algorithm string plus the kind of layer being built to a concrete algorithm implementation. The **bottom** layer is thin vLLM-facing adapters (`AscendLinearMethod`, `AscendFusedMoEMethod`, `AscendKVCacheMethod`, `AscendEmbeddingMethod`) that translate vLLM's `LinearMethodBase` / `FusedMoEMethodBase` / `BaseKVCacheMethod` contracts into those schemes.

Everything else on this page follows from that split: a *config* class decides *whether* a layer is quantized and *which* algorithm string it carries; a *scheme* class owns weight-shape declarations, post-load transformation, and the forward kernel; an *adapter* owns parameter registration and the weight-loading contract with vLLM's loaders. See [Platform and Hardware Profiles](../architecture/platform-and-hardware-profiles.md) for how the active profile chooses between the standard and 310P stacks, [MoE Execution](moe-execution.md) for what MoE schemes feed, and [KV Cache Specs, Block Layout, and Placement](kv-cache-and-block-layout.md) for how KV quantization changes cache geometry.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CLI["vllm serve --quantization X"] --> Platform["NPUPlatform.pre_register_and_update"]
    Platform --> Auto["maybe_auto_detect_quantization"]
    Auto --> Cfg["registered QuantizationConfig subclass"]
    Cfg --> GQM["config.get_quant_method layer, prefix"]
    GQM --> QT["quant_type string for this prefix"]
    QT --> Reg["get_scheme_class quant_type, layer_type"]
    Reg --> Scheme["scheme instance"]
    Scheme --> Adapter["AscendLinearMethod / AscendFusedMoEMethod / AscendKVCacheMethod"]
    Adapter --> Weights["create_weights registers parameters"]
    Weights --> Post["process_weights_after_loading"]
    Post --> Fwd["apply"]
```

The full path from `--quantization` to a forward call, with the two registries in the middle.

## Platform pre-registration and the `--quantization` choices

`NPUPlatform.pre_register_and_update` is where the plugin makes its quantization backends visible to vLLM. It does three things in order ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L285-L320)):

1. It appends `"ascend"` to the `--quantization` `choices` list on the live argument parser if it is not already there. Upstream vLLM has no `ascend` method, so without this mutation `--quantization ascend` is rejected during argument parsing and the error message never mentions the plugin.
2. It imports **one** family of config classes, selected by `get_current_hardware_profile().quantization_backend_family`. On `STANDARD` profiles (A2/A3/A5) it imports `AscendCompressedTensorsConfig`, `AscendFp8Config`, `AscendModelOptMxFp8Config`, `AscendModelSlimConfig`; on `COMPATIBILITY` (310P) it imports only `AscendModelSlimConfig310`. Each class carries a `@register_quantization_config(<method name>)` decorator, so the import *is* the registration. Note that `AscendModelSlimConfig` and `AscendModelSlimConfig310` are both registered under the single name `ascend`, so the two branches must be mutually exclusive: exactly one family is imported per process.
3. It runs the config imports inside this hook rather than at module scope, after `adapt_patch(is_global_patch=True)`, because these modules reach into patched vLLM internals. The adjacent `register_deepseek_v4_vision_config_convertor()` call documents the same deferral as a multiprocessing-spawn safety measure.

`NPUPlatform.supported_quantization` also declares the served method names up front: `ascend`, `compressed-tensors`, `fp8`, `deepseek_v4_fp8`, `modelopt_mxfp8`, `mxfp8` ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L92-L99)).

The `vllm_ascend/quantization/__init__.py` package deliberately does **not** eagerly import its configs. `AscendModelSlimConfig`, `AscendCompressedTensorsConfig`, `AscendFp8Config` and `AscendModelOptMxFp8Config` are exposed through a module-level `__getattr__` so that importing a lightweight sibling such as `quant_type` does not drag in `torch_npu`, `compressed_tensors`, or the registration side effects ([`__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/__init__.py#L17-L57)). The same reasoning shapes `quant_type.py`, which is a bare enum module with no imports beyond `enum`.

## Auto-detection: `detect_quantization_method` and `maybe_auto_detect_quantization`

A checkpoint's format can be inferred from its files alone, and the plugin does so before anything heavy is loaded. `detect_quantization_method` inspects only JSON — never `.safetensors` or `.bin` — and resolves through `get_model_file`, which accepts either a local directory or a HuggingFace/ModelScope repo id and downloads `config.json` / `quant_model_description.json` into the hub cache when needed ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/utils.py#L83-L188)). The priority order is deliberate:

1. `quant_model_description.json` present → `"ascend"` (ModelSlim). This wins even when `config.json` also declares `compressed-tensors`, because a ModelSlim export is the more specific artifact.
2. `config.json` → `quantization_config.quant_method == "compressed-tensors"` → `"compressed-tensors"`.
3. Same field `== "fp8"` → `"fp8"`.
4. Otherwise `None`, meaning "load as float".

`maybe_auto_detect_quantization` is the policy layer around it ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/utils.py#L191-L264)). It is called from `NPUPlatform.check_and_update_config` as step 3, i.e. after `VllmConfig` exists but before weights are touched ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L442-L471)). Its rules:

- Detection returns `None` → an INFO log explains the model will load as float and suggests `--quantization`, and nothing is mutated.
- The user set `--quantization` → it is respected unconditionally; a mismatch against the detected value produces a WARNING that also names the detected method as the recommended alternative.
- No user value → `model_config.quantization` is set and an INFO log records the choice.

The last step is the non-obvious part. `VllmConfig.__post_init__` already ran `_get_quantization_config` while `model_config.quantization` was still `None`, so `vllm_config.quant_config` is `None` at this point. The function therefore recreates it by calling `VllmConfig._get_quantization_config(model_config, vllm_config.load_config)` after mutating `model_config.quantization` — otherwise the whole `get_quant_config` → `QuantizationConfig` → `get_quant_method` pipeline never starts.

`AscendModelSlimConfig.override_quantization_method` covers the complementary case: a checkpoint whose `quantization_config` exists but has no `quant_method`, on an available NPU, is claimed as `"ascend"` ([`modelslim_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelslim_config.py#L350-L356)).

## The scheme registry contract

`vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/registry.py` is a 40-line module holding a single dict, `_SCHEME_REGISTRY: dict[tuple[str, str], type]`, plus `register_scheme(quant_type, layer_type)` and `get_scheme_class(quant_type, layer_type)` ([`registry.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/registry.py#L20-L62)).

`register_scheme` is a class decorator. Its contract:

- The key is the exact `(quant_type, layer_type)` pair. `quant_type` is the algorithm string as spelled in the checkpoint (for example `W8A8_DYNAMIC`, `W4A4_MXFP4`, `FAKQuant`, or the method name `fp8`), and `layer_type` is one of `"linear"`, `"moe"`, `"attention"`, plus the two FP8-only pseudo-layer types `"ds_linear"` and `"ds_w4a8_moe"` used by the DeepSeek-V4 FP8 config.
- **A duplicate key raises `ValueError`** naming the already-registered class. Registration is therefore a global, once-per-process invariant, not a last-writer-wins lookup. This is what makes the "import exactly one config family" rule in `pre_register_and_update` load-bearing, and it is why adding a second implementation for an existing `(quant_type, layer_type)` requires removing the first rather than overriding it.
- `get_scheme_class` returns `None` for an unknown key. Callers differ on what they do with that: the ModelSlim and compressed-tensors paths raise `NotImplementedError` with a user-facing "unsupported quant_type" message, while the FP8 path `assert scheme_class is not None` because the pairing is structural.

Registration happens as an import side effect of `vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/__init__.py`, which imports the `w4a4`, `w4a8`, `w8a8`, `wna16` and `kv_cache` subpackages. The unit tests pin both halves of the contract: an unknown key yields `None`, a re-registration of `("W8A8_DYNAMIC", "linear")` raises, every `"linear"` entry subclasses `AscendLinearScheme`, and every `"moe"` entry subclasses `AscendMoEScheme` ([`test_registry.py`](../../tests/ut/quantization/methods/test_registry.py#L13-L70)). That second assertion is worth preserving when adding a scheme — the adapters rely on it.

The current registry contents, by layer type:

| `layer_type` | Registered `quant_type` values |
| --- | --- |
| `linear` | `W8A8`, `W8A8_DYNAMIC`, `W8A8FP8_DYNAMIC`, `W8A8_MXFP8`, `W8A8_MIX`, `W8A16`, `W4A4_DYNAMIC`, `W4A4_FLATQUANT_DYNAMIC`, `W4A4_MXFP4`, `W4A4_MXFP4_FLATQUANT`, `W4A8_MXFP`, `fp8` (block-wise, plus the `ds_linear` pseudo-type) |
| `moe` | `W8A8_DYNAMIC`, `W8A8FP8_DYNAMIC`, `W8A8_MXFP8`, `W4A8_DYNAMIC`, `W4A8_MXFP`, `W4A4_MXFP4`, `W4A16`, `W4A16_MXFP4`, `fp8`, plus the `ds_w4a8_moe` pseudo-type |
| `attention` | `FAKQuant`, `INT8_DYNAMIC` |

### Base classes and what subclasses must and may implement

`vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/base.py` defines the three abstract bases ([`base.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/base.py#L74-L388)).

`AscendLinearScheme` extends `WeightSwitchMixin` (see below) and requires `get_weight(input_size, output_size, params_dtype)` and `apply(layer, x, bias, tp_rank)`. It offers three optional parameter-declaration hooks that the adapter calls in a fixed order — `get_pertensor_param(params_dtype, layer_type=...)`, `get_perchannel_param(output_size, params_dtype)`, `get_pergroup_param(input_size, output_size, params_dtype, layer_type=...)` — plus an optional `process_weights_after_loading`. All default to empty/no-op.

`AscendMoEScheme` requires `get_weight(num_experts, intermediate_size_per_partition, hidden_sizes, params_dtype)`, `get_dynamic_quant_param(...)` with the same signature, and `apply(layer, x, topk_weights, topk_ids, shared_experts, shared_experts_input)`. On top of that it declares three class attributes that the MoE MLP dispatcher reads: `quant_type: QuantType`, `act_quant_type: torch.dtype | None`, and `fused_activations: frozenset[str]`, with `supports_fused_activation(activation)` comparing an `MoEActivation` member's `.value` against that set. `vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_mlp.py` branches on it: a supported activation calls `apply_gmm1_act_quant` (fused gate/up + activation + requantize), anything else falls back to `apply_gmm1` → generic activation → `apply_act_quant` ([`moe_mlp.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_mlp.py#L27-L57)). Declaring an activation in `fused_activations` without implementing `apply_gmm1_act_quant` is a `NotImplementedError` at forward time, not at registration time.

The MoE base also provides `_quant_hidden_states`, the shared activation-quantization helper. The A16 types (`W4A16`, `W4A16MXFP`) are checked first and short-circuit, because no activation quantization happens there at all; after that, the four MX types dispatch to `torch_npu.npu_dynamic_mx_quant` and everything else to `torch_npu.npu_dynamic_quant`. On the already-quantized-input branch it reuses the supplied scale instead of re-quantizing. MX per-token scales are normalized through `maybe_normalize_mxfp_scale_layout`, which reshapes a 2D scale to `(rows, cols // 2, 2)` for the A5 fused gmm ops and raises on an odd column count ([`base.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/base.py#L306-L335)). The MX type set is also exposed as `is_mx_quant_type()` for callers that only need the classification ([`methods/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/__init__.py#L77-L88)).

`AscendAttentionScheme` requires only `apply(layer, query, key, value, kv_cache, attn_metadata, attn_type, scale, output)`, with `create_weights` and `process_weights_after_loading` optional. Note the adapter comment: vLLM performs no weight processing or slicing for attention, so the entire create-weights step is hidden inside the scheme.

### `QuantType` versus the registry's string keys

`QuantType` ([`quant_type.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/quant_type.py#L26-L37)) is a plain `Enum` whose members carry integer values and name algorithm families (`NONE`, `W8A8`, `W4A8`, `W8A8MXFP`, `W4A16`, `W4A4MXFP`, `W4A8MXFP`, `W8A8FP`, `W4A16MXFP`). It is **not** the registry key. The registry is keyed by the checkpoint's string (`"W8A8_MXFP8"`, `"W8A8_DYNAMIC"`, …), and a scheme class sets its `quant_type` class attribute to a `QuantType` member so shared helpers such as `_quant_hidden_states` can branch without string compares. Both vocabularies must be kept in sync by hand when an algorithm is added: the string goes in the `@register_scheme` decorator and in the config's detection logic, the enum member goes on the scheme class. The module itself imports nothing beyond `enum`, so runtime modules can import `QuantType` without pulling in `torch_npu` or the registration side effects.

`vllm_ascend/quantization/quant_parser.py` holds a third, narrower vocabulary: `QuantTypeMapping` maps four *rollback* type strings (`W8A8_MXFP8`, `W4A4_MXFP4`, `W4A8_MXFP`, `W4A16_MXFP4`) to their activation/weight/scale/per-token-scale dtypes plus a rounding mode, and `parse_quant_moe_down_proj_params` restricts `round_mode` to the checkpoint's value only for `W4A4_MXFP4`, forcing `rint` everywhere else ([`quant_parser.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/quant_parser.py#L5-L68)).

## Config classes: from a checkpoint format to a `quant_type`

### `AscendModelSlimConfig` — the `ascend` method

This is the primary path and by far the most involved. Its lifecycle is unusual in two ways.

**It refuses to let vLLM find its own config file.** `get_config_filenames()` returns `[]`, so upstream `get_quant_config()` skips its file lookup; the actual load happens later in `maybe_update_config`, which can emit a friendly diagnostic. When `quant_model_description.json` is missing, that method raises a boxed message listing the model path, the JSON files actually found, and two remedies (drop `--quantization ascend`, or quantize with ModelSlim) ([`modelslim_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelslim_config.py#L337-L348), [`maybe_update_config`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelslim_config.py#L706-L804)).

**It rewrites its own key space repeatedly.** Three layers of remapping happen before any lookup:

- `_apply_extra_quant_adaptations` normalizes legacy naming in the loaded description at construction time — the `hc_head_fn` rewrite (`model.` prefixes, `.attn.`→`.self_attn.`, `ffn`→`mlp`, `.w1/.w2/.w3`→`gate_proj/down_proj/up_proj`, `head`→`lm_head`, `embed`→`embed_tokens`) and the unconditional `.shared_head.` / `transformer.shared_head.output.` / `weight_packed` rewrites ([`modelslim_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelslim_config.py#L806-L878)).
- `apply_vllm_mapper` applies vLLM's model-specific `WeightsMapper` to the description keys, deliberately preserving the `optional` sub-dictionary because checkpoint-level metadata (for example the `quarot` rotation map read by `get_rotation_path`) does not name parameters and must keep its schema ([`modelslim_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelslim_config.py#L358-L386)).
- `quant_prefix_mapper` applies per-model prefix and substring maps, then a set of prefix-alias probes: `QUANT_MODEL_PREFIX_MAPPINGS` / `QUANT_MODEL_SUBSTR_MAPPINGS` for `deepseek_v4`, `step3p5_mtp`, `glm5_next_mtp`, `gemma4`/`gemma4_text`, plus ad-hoc candidate probing for `glm5_next`/`glm5_next_text` and `step3p5_mtp`. Every probe is guarded by `_has_quant_weight`, so an alias is adopted only when the direct name has no entry and the candidate does.

`_update_packed_modules_mapping` then fills the fused-module map that `get_quant_type_for_layer` needs: the per-model deltas in `UPDATED_PACKED_MODULES_MAPPING`, the split Kimi K3 KDA projections, and — notably — auto-discovery of `experts` shard names by scanning the description for `\.experts\.\d+\.(\w+)\.weight$`. Auto-discovery is what generalizes the "all shards of a fused layer must share one quant type" check to `w1/w2/w3`-style expert naming without listing every model ([`modelslim_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelslim_config.py#L517-L557)).

`get_quant_type_for_layer` is the resolver. For a fused layer it expands the packed name into its shard prefixes, reads each shard's entry, and **raises `ValueError` if shards disagree** — a packed linear cannot be served by one scheme if its parts were quantized differently. One documented exception exists: a missing `.v_proj.weight` is tolerated when both `q_proj` and `k_proj` are present, because Gemma4's `k_eq_v` layers replicate `v_proj` from `k_proj` at load time. `"FLOAT"` is normalized to `None`, which means "use the unquantized method" ([`modelslim_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelslim_config.py#L203-L263)).

Kimi K3's mixed-precision KDA projection is resolved *before* that check: `uses_kimi_k3_mixed_kda_projection` recognizes the one layout where q/k/v are W8A8 and `g_proj`/`f_a_proj`/`b_proj` are FLOAT, returns `quant_type = None`, and lets the model adapter split the packed layer. Any other mixed packing still hits the consistency error ([`modelslim_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelslim_config.py#L426-L443), [dispatch](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelslim_config.py#L588-L593)).

`get_quant_method` then dispatches on the layer class: `LinearBase` → `AscendLinearMethod` (or `AscendUnquantizedLinearMethod` when `quant_type is None`); `AttentionLayerBase` → `AscendKVCacheMethod` with an FA/indexer/C8 scheme, or `None` for an unquantized attention layer; a fused MoE layer → `AscendFusedMoEMethod` (or `AscendUnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`); `VocabParallelEmbedding` → `AscendEmbeddingMethod`, and a quantized embedding requires a scheme registered under `layer_type="linear"`. Two model-specific prefix normalizations run first: `minimax`/`minimax_m2` rewrite `mlp`→`block_sparse_moe` and truncate to the `experts` component, and `bailing_hybrid` rewrites `linear_attn`/`self_attn`→`attention` ([`modelslim_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelslim_config.py#L559-L650)).

The MoE branch also **installs a wrapped weight loader on the layer before creating the scheme** (`layer.weight_loader = _make_modelslim_moe_weight_loader(layer.weight_loader)`), because `RoutedExperts` resolves its quant method before registering parameters. The wrapper only renames checkpoint-side scale-bias keys to the upstream scale path — `w13_scale_bias` → `w13_scale`, `w2_scale_bias` → `w2_scale` — preserving the rest of the signature including `return_success` ([`modelslim_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelslim_config.py#L52-L84)).

### `AscendCompressedTensorsConfig` — the `compressed-tensors` method

This path derives a `quant_type` from llm-compressor's `QuantizationArgs` rather than from a per-tensor description. `target_scheme_map` is built from `config_groups`, `should_ignore_layer` honours the `ignore` list (fused-aware), and `find_matched_target` picks the group for a layer name. `_add_fused_moe_to_target_scheme_map` copies the `Linear` target onto `RoutedExperts` because linear layers get fused into MoE modules ([`compressed_tensors_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/compressed_tensors_config.py#L82-L104)).

`_detect_quant_type` is the decision table, and each branch is a conjunction of `num_bits`, `strategy`, `dynamic`, `symmetric`, and `type` predicates:

| Detected condition | `quant_type` |
| --- | --- |
| `format == mxfp8_quantized` and dynamic group-wise MX on 8 bits, group size 32 | `W8A8_MXFP8` |
| `format == mxfp4_pack_quantized` and the same shape on 4 bits | `W4A4_MXFP4` |
| 8-bit channel weights + static tensor activations, symmetric | `W8A8` |
| 8-bit channel weights + dynamic token activations, symmetric, FLOAT type | `W8A8FP8_DYNAMIC` |
| 8-bit channel weights + dynamic token activations, symmetric, non-FLOAT | `W8A8_DYNAMIC` |
| 4-bit channel weights + 8-bit dynamic token activations, symmetric | `W4A8_DYNAMIC` |
| 4-bit INT group weights, static, no activation quantization | `W4A16` |

Anything else raises `NotImplementedError`. For both MX branches the detector writes `group_size` (defaulting to 32) back into `quant_description`, which is how MX schemes later read their group size from the config object rather than from the scheme. The dynamic predicates are asymmetric by design: in every dynamic branch the *weights* must be non-dynamic and the *activations* must be dynamic.

### `AscendFp8Config` — native block-wise FP8

Registered as `fp8`, this serves checkpoints published in FP8 with `weight_block_size` present. It refuses anything else explicitly: `_verify_block_quantization` raises with a message naming `weight_block_size` when scales are per-tensor or per-channel, and rejects a non-`dynamic` `activation_scheme` ([`fp8_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/fp8_config.py#L45-L59)). Layers in `ignored_layers` / `modules_to_not_convert` go to `AscendUnquantizedLinearMethod` / `AscendUnquantizedFusedMoEMethod`; `is_layer_skipped` is called with `match_mode` only when the installed vLLM's signature supports it, detected once via `inspect.signature`. Linear and MoE layers get the scheme registered under `(fp8, "linear")` / `(fp8, "moe")`, constructed with `weight_block_size`.

The execution strategy differs by hardware and lives in the scheme: `AscendFp8BlockLinearMethod.__init__` creates an `AscendW8A8MXFP8DynamicLinearMethod` only when `is_950()`, so on Ascend 950 the block scales are resolved and then re-quantized to MXFP8 while other generations resolve to the model dtype and use the BF16 matmul. If the reduction dim is not a multiple of the MX group size the scheme logs once and permanently drops to the model dtype for that layer ([`fp8_block.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/w8a8/fp8_block.py#L177-L249)).

### The `deepseek_v4_fp8` special case

`AscendDeepseekV4FP8Config` extends the upstream `DeepseekV4FP8Config` and is registered under its own method name, which is also listed in `supported_quantization`. It does not use the ordinary layer types: linear layers resolve `get_scheme_class(FP8_METHOD, "ds_linear")` (reached through `AscendLinearMethod`, constructed with `weight_block_size`), and fused MoE layers resolve `get_scheme_class(FP8_METHOD, "ds_w4a8_moe")` **only if `expert_dtype == "fp4"`** — any other expert dtype is an unconditional `NotImplementedError` ([`fp8_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/fp8_config.py#L114-L144)). The MTP draft loader keys off the method name too: when `quant_config.get_name() == "deepseek_v4_fp8"` it renames `embed.weight` and `head.weight` into the `mtp.0.emb.tok_emb` / `mtp.0.head` namespace before the usual speculative-layer rewriting ([`deepseek_v4/mtp.py`](../../vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v4/mtp.py#L319-L330)). The two `ds_*` scheme classes are variants of the MXFP8/MXFP4 pairs: `AscendW8A8MXFP8DSDynamicLinearMethod` stores a `block_size × block_size` scale (`_packed_dim=0`, `_packed_factor=block_size`) and expands it into 32×1 MX blocks in `process_weights_after_loading`, with an extra `wo_a` regroup for the o-projection ([`w8a8_mxfp8.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/w8a8/w8a8_mxfp8.py#L510-L570)); `AscendW4A8MXFPDSDynamicFusedMoEMethod` subclasses `AscendW4A8MXFPDynamicFusedMoEMethod` and only changes the per-expert scale parameter shapes ([`w4a8_mxfp4.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/w4a8/w4a8_mxfp4.py#L310-L323)).

### `AscendModelOptMxFp8Config` — `mxfp8` and `modelopt_mxfp8`

Registered under both names in one class decorator stack. It excludes layers via `is_layer_excluded`, additionally treats `vision_tower`, `vision_model` and `vit_large_projector` prefixes as unquantized for older ModelOpt checkpoints whose exclude list predates them, and otherwise hard-wires `AscendW8A8MXFP8DynamicLinearMethod` for `LinearBase`/`ParallelLMHead` and `AscendW8A8MXFP8DynamicFusedMoEMethod` for MoE ([`modelopt_mxfp8_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelopt_mxfp8_config.py#L32-L88)). It bypasses the registry rather than looking up a `quant_type`, so it is the one config that does not depend on `get_scheme_class` at all — but the schemes it instantiates are still the registry-registered ones.

## Weight loading: layout declarations and TP-boundary invariants

`AscendLinearMethod.create_weights` is the single place where a scheme's abstract parameter declarations become registered `torch.nn.Parameter` objects with vLLM-compatible sharding metadata ([`method_adapters.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/method_adapters.py#L86-L190)). The order is fixed and matters:

1. **Weights** from `get_weight`. Each is tagged `input_dim=1, output_dim=0`. Two pseudo-keys may be popped from the returned dict: `_packed_dim` / `_packed_factor`, which are replayed onto the parameter so vLLM's loader knows the tensor is bit-packed along that dim.
2. **Per-tensor params** from `get_pertensor_param`, registered as `PerTensorScaleParameter` with `ignore_warning` set and with the loader re-attached afterwards. `layer_type` is passed as `"row"` for a `RowParallelLinear` and `"others"` otherwise, because flat-quant shapes depend on it.
3. **Per-channel params** from `get_perchannel_param`, tagged `output_dim=0`.
4. **Per-group params** from `get_pergroup_param`, the most delicate step. Four pseudo-keys are popped before registration: `_packed_dim`/`_packed_factor`, `_input_dim`, and `_block_quant_scale`.

The `_block_quant_scale` branch exists for a specific correctness reason recorded in the code: block-wise scales must **not** reuse the `packed_dim`/`packed_factor` mechanism. That mechanism assumes a shard is a whole number of packs, so it converts shard bounds by plain division; block sizes carry no such guarantee and truncation there would drop the scale tile covering a shard's tail. Instead `layer.weight_block_size` is set and the parameter is built as a `BlockQuantScaleParameter`, which vLLM's loaders round up to whole blocks. `_VLLM_PARAMETER_CTOR_ATTRS` filters `weight_loader`/`output_dim`/`input_dim` out of the replayed attribute dict because those typed parameters expose them as read-only properties and replaying them raises.

Ordinary per-group params are plain `Parameter`s tagged `output_dim=0`, with `input_dim` resolved by three ordered heuristics: an explicit `_input_dim` from the scheme, else `1` when the name contains `weight_scale_second`/`weight_offset_second` or when `is_mx_quant_type(scheme)`, else left unset. The unit test pins the consequence — `weight_scale_pergroup` has no `input_dim` while `weight_scale_second`/`weight_offset_second` have `input_dim == 1` ([`test_method_adapters.py`](../../tests/ut/quantization/test_method_adapters.py#L54-L114)).

### MX group phase at TP boundaries

The non-obvious invariant: a row-parallel shard's start offset need not be a multiple of the MX group size, so the scale entries for that shard are **not** an even chunk of the global scale tensor. A shard that begins midway through a global group shares that boundary group's scale with the neighbouring rank.

`_make_mx_scale_weight_loader` encodes the fix ([`method_adapters.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/method_adapters.py#L42-L70)). It is installed only for `RowParallelLinear` layers whose scheme sets `supports_unaligned_tp_groups` (currently the W8A8_MXFP8 and W4A4_MXFP4 linear schemes). It then:

1. Accepts a `loaded_weight` whose shape already equals `param.shape` verbatim and copies it, returning `None`. This handles checkpoint loaders that ship a pre-sharded scale; applying the global offset on top would slice the same shard twice.
2. If the parameter has an `input_dim` and `input_size_per_partition % group_size != 0`, computes `scale_start = (tp_rank * input_size_per_partition) // group_size` and narrows along `input_dim` to `param.shape[input_dim]` entries. The floor division is exactly the "start from the shared boundary group" rule.
3. Otherwise delegates to the upstream loader unchanged.

The test `test_mx_scale_weight_loader_preserves_group_phase` pins rank 3 with `input_size_per_partition=528`, `group_size=32`: `528 % 32 == 16`, so `scale_start = (3 * 528) // 32 = 49`, and a 66-entry scale narrows to entries `49:66` — 17 entries, not the naive 16.5-rounded value ([`test_method_adapters.py`](../../tests/ut/quantization/test_method_adapters.py#L18-L51)).

The same phase problem shows up in the **weight** tensor, and MXFP8 handles it in `process_weights_after_loading` instead of the loader: for a `RowParallelLinear` it computes `prefix_padding = (tp_rank * input_size_per_partition) % group_size` and `suffix_padding` to close the group, stores the pair on `layer.mxfp8_tp_padding`, and pads the weight with zeros. `apply` reads the same pair and pads the activation identically — the two must agree or the matmul sees mismatched group boundaries. The transformed weight and scale are cached in persistent buffers (`_mxfp8_weight_buf`, `_mxfp8_scale_buf`) and copied in place on later calls so the data pointer stays stable across ACL-graph capture and RL weight reloads; `restore_weights_for_rl_loading` reverses both transformations and is required before `load_weights()` in an RL loop ([`w8a8_mxfp8.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/w8a8/w8a8_mxfp8.py#L130-L244)).

### MoE parameter registration and scale tagging

`AscendFusedMoEMethod.create_weights` registers `get_weight` outputs, then tags scale parameters with vLLM's `FusedMoeWeightScaleSupported` so the upstream loader knows how to narrow them ([`method_adapters.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/method_adapters.py#L286-L318)). Everything registered through `get_dynamic_quant_param` starts at `CHANNEL`; any parameter whose name contains `weight_scale_second`, `weight_offset_second`, or `scale_bias` is re-tagged `GROUP`, and so are `weight_scale`/`weight_offset` **but only when the scheme reports `group_size > 0`**. That is why `AscendFp8BlockFusedMoEMethod` sets `self.group_size = self.block_k` — it reports a group size purely so the loader narrows `*_weight_scale_inv` per expert shard.

`AscendFusedMoEMethod` also declines to participate in upstream's modular-kernel path: `maybe_make_prepare_finalize` returns `None` and `is_monolithic` is `False`, because Ascend uses its own MoE communication and forward path. `supports_eplb` is read off the scheme as a plain attribute, and `get_eplb_weight_views` delegates — the MoE-side consequences belong to [MoE Execution](moe-execution.md).

### TP rank selection at forward time

`AscendLinearMethod.apply` resolves `tp_rank` per call rather than per layer: an `o_proj` under `oproj_tp_enable()` takes the rank of `get_otp_group()`, a `down_proj` under `mlp_tp_enable()` takes the rank of `get_mlp_tp_group()`, other `RowParallelLinear`s use `get_tensor_model_parallel_rank()`, and everything else gets `0` ([`method_adapters.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/method_adapters.py#L208-L223)). Schemes therefore receive a rank that may belong to a *sub*-TP group, which is what allows those two projections to be sharded differently from the rest of the model.

### Weight switching

`AscendLinearScheme` inherits `WeightSwitchMixin`, which declares the layer attributes that must be all-gathered or locally repeated when a full (unsharded) weight copy is needed for a forward pass — the SFA and DSA context-parallel paths. A scheme opts in with `supports_weight_switch = True` **after** validating every declared layout, and declares separate input-sharded (`weight_switch_gather_specs`) and output-sharded (`weight_switch_output_gather_specs`) spec tuples; `gather_dim` must name the exact sharded dimension *after* post-processing, including transposes and packed layouts ([`weight_switch/linear.py`](../../vllm_ascend/weight_switch/linear.py#L124-L180)). Getting that wrong is silent corruption rather than an error, which is why the mixin docstring demands the post-processing layout be documented next to the spec declaration.

## KV-cache quantization

KV-cache quantization is configured through the same `quant_model_description.json` but is *not* resolved through the `(quant_type, layer_type)` registry in the same way. `AscendModelSlimConfig._add_kvcache_quant_metadata` reads three top-level keys once and then discovers which layer ids are affected by regexing `\.(\d+)\.` out of every description key ([`modelslim_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelslim_config.py#L880-L898)):

| Description key | Attribute | Per-layer discovery trigger |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fa_quant_type` | `enable_fa_quant`, `kvcache_quant_layers` | a key containing `fa_k.scale` |
| `indexer_quant_type` | `enable_indexer_quant`, `indexer_quant_layers` | a key containing `indexer.quant_type` |
| `kv_cache_type == "C8"` | `enable_c8_quant`, `c8_quant_layers` | a key containing `k_proj.kv_cache_scale` |

Dispatch in `get_quant_method` for an `AttentionLayerBase` checks these in order — FA, then indexer, then C8 — and falls back to `None` (no quant method) otherwise. FA and indexer go through `create_scheme_for_layer` and therefore the registry, under `layer_type="attention"`: `AscendFAQuantAttentionMethod` is registered as `FAKQuant` and `AscendSFAQuantAttentionMethod` as `INT8_DYNAMIC`. The indexer path also supports per-layer rollback, preferring `{prefix}.indexer.quant_type` over the global `indexer_quant_type`. C8 is constructed **directly** rather than looked up, because it needs the description and prefix at construction.

`vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/kv_cache/kv_c8.py` holds all three schemes:

- `AscendFAQuantAttentionMethod` creates `fa_q`/`fa_k`/`fa_v` submodules with per-head `scale` and int8 `offset` parameters, loaded by `_fa_quant_weight_loader` (a single-element tensor is broadcast; otherwise the first dim is TP-sharded with an explicit shape assertion). Post-loading it derives `fak_descale`, its reciprocal (float or int8 depending on `FP8_ATTENTION` hardware support), `fak_offset`, and a `quant_kscale` repeated to `kv_lora_rank` ([`kv_c8.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/kv_cache/kv_c8.py#L30-L72)).
- `AscendSFAQuantAttentionMethod` creates an `indexer` submodule with `q_rot`/`k_rot` float32 rotation matrices sized by `index_head_dim`, and does nothing post-loading.
- `AscendC8KVCacheAttentionMethod` is the dense-attention INT8 KV path. Its `create_weights` does two things beyond registering `k_cache_scale`/`k_cache_offset`/`v_cache_scale`/`v_cache_offset`: it sets `layer.kv_cache_torch_dtype = torch.int8` **only when the node is not a KV producer**, and it rewrites the layer's impl class in place to `AscendC8AttentionBackendImpl` so the C8 forward path is always taken. Its `apply` deliberately raises — quantization is handled inside the attention backend, not through this method ([`kv_c8.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/methods/kv_cache/kv_c8.py#L108-L164)).

Three hooks on `AscendModelSlimConfig` propagate KV quantization outward: `get_cache_scale_mapper` (checkpoint names → `.attn.k_cache_scale` etc.; FA and indexer names use negative-lookbehind regexes so a second `AutoWeightsLoader` pass over the nested `mla_attn.mla_attn.*` module does not double-map), `get_kv_quant_dtype` (returns the quant/original dtype pair, and for MLA quantizes **only K** so V stays in the original dtype), and `get_kv_quant_split_factor` (leaves the K head dim and doubles the V head dim before handing the pair to `calc_split_factor`). `enable_fa_quant` in `quantization/utils.py` is the gate the attention backends and KV placement consult; it requires either a KV-consumer role or hardware `FP8_ATTENTION` support before it will look at the config flag, and with a `layer_name` it defers to `AscendModelSlimConfig.enabling_fa_quant`, which additionally requires the node to be a decode instance (KV consumer but not producer) on hardware without `FP8_ATTENTION` ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/utils.py#L267-L276), [`enabling_fa_quant`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/configs/modelslim_config.py#L659-L668)). How those answers change page sizes is covered in [KV Cache Specs, Block Layout, and Placement](kv-cache-and-block-layout.md).

## The 310P compatibility variant

310P hardware runs a **parallel implementation** of the quantization stack rather than a set of patches on the standard one. `AscendModelSlimConfig310` subclasses `AscendModelSlimConfig` and overrides exactly one method, `get_quant_method`, to resolve schemes through `vllm_ascend/_310p/quantization/methods/registry.py` — a second, entirely separate `_SCHEME_REGISTRY` with the same decorator contract and the same duplicate-key `ValueError` ([`_310p/modelslim_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/_310p/quantization/modelslim_config.py#L75-L133), [`_310p registry`](../../vllm_ascend/_310p/quantization/methods/registry.py#L20-L41)).

The two registries are separate by design, and the class docstring states why the shared parts must stay aligned: `packed_modules_mapping` handling **must** match the base, or fused `qkv_proj`/`gate_up_proj` modules miss the 310P lookup, fall through to the base implementation, and produce NZ/transpose errors. Its supported surface is deliberately narrow — `W8A8` (static), `W8A8_DYNAMIC`, `W8A8S` (sparse), and `W8A8SC` (compressed weights with a separate `index` and `info` tensor) for `linear`, plus `W8A8_DYNAMIC` for `moe`. A quantized `VocabParallelEmbedding` raises `NotImplementedError` on 310P instead of being served.

The scheme *classes* are also separate, so a 310P scheme can carry different kernels without touching standard-path behaviour. `AscendW8A8Linear310pScheme` is the shared base declaring `input_scale`/`input_offset` per-tensor and `quant_bias`/`deq_scale` per-channel parameters, and the subclasses differ in how they quantize and which `torch_npu` kernel they call. Three 310P-specific behaviours matter operationally:

- Every linear scheme leaves the weight in NZ-transposed form (`maybe_trans_nz`, then a dim-0/1 transpose either in `process_weights_after_loading` or in `apply`) before handing it to `npu_quant_matmul`. [`w8a8_static.py`](../../vllm_ascend/_310p/quantization/methods/w8a8_static.py#L62-L74) records this as a temporary workaround: the planned replacement op will accept the canonical non-transposed layout, at which point the explicit transpose goes away.
- `AscendW8A8DynamicLinearMethod310` supports **symmetric quantization only** on 310P and carries a NOTE that its accuracy issue is deferred rather than worked around by falling back to load-time fp16 dequant plus `F.linear` ([`w8a8_dynamic.py`](../../vllm_ascend/_310p/quantization/methods/w8a8_dynamic.py#L186-L236)).
- `AscendW8A8SLinearMethod310` passes `quant_bias` only on TP rank 0 and `None` elsewhere, while `AscendW8A8SCLinearMethod310` cannot pass `None` to `npu_matmul_compress_dequant` at all and so substitutes a zeroed bias on non-zero ranks of a row-parallel linear.

The MoE scheme likewise declares `fused_activations = frozenset({"silu"})` because 310P fuses gmm1+swiglu+quant inside `npu_quant_grouped_matmul_dequant` plus `npu_swiglu` ([`w8a8_dynamic.py`](../../vllm_ascend/_310p/quantization/methods/w8a8_dynamic.py#L36-L183)).

Which stack is live is decided in one place: `HardwareProfile.quantization_backend_family`, set to `COMPATIBILITY` for `AscendDeviceType._310P` and `STANDARD` for A2/A3/A5 ([`hardware_profile.py`](../../vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py#L99-L125), [profiles](../../vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py#L155-L250)). See [Platform and Hardware Profiles](../architecture/platform-and-hardware-profiles.md) for the rest of that profile's contents.

## Tests that pin this page's invariants

| Behaviour | Test |
| --- | --- |
| Duplicate `(quant_type, layer_type)` raises; unknown key returns `None`; every registered linear/moe scheme subclasses its base | [`test_registry.py`](../../tests/ut/quantization/methods/test_registry.py#L13-L70) |
| MX scale loader preserves group phase and accepts pre-sharded scales | [`test_method_adapters.py`](../../tests/ut/quantization/test_method_adapters.py#L18-L51) |
| Block-wise FP8 scales become a `BlockQuantScaleParameter` and set `layer.weight_block_size` | [`test_method_adapters.py`](../../tests/ut/quantization/test_method_adapters.py#L116-L149) |
| MoE scale tagging flips from `CHANNEL` to `GROUP` when `group_size > 0` | [`test_method_adapters.py`](../../tests/ut/quantization/test_method_adapters.py#L216-L243) |
| ModelSlim wins over compressed-tensors; auto-detect respects user choice and rebuilds `quant_config` | [`test_utils.py`](../../tests/ut/quantization/test_utils.py#L94-L239) |
| Gemma4 `k_eq_v` tolerates a missing `v_proj` shard but other missing shards still raise | [`test_modelslim_config.py`](../../tests/ut/quantization/configs/test_modelslim_config.py#L251-L271) |
| ModelSlim MoE loader maps `w13_scale_bias`/`w2_scale_bias` and is installed before the scheme is created | [`test_modelslim_config.py`](../../tests/ut/quantization/configs/test_modelslim_config.py#L142-L215) |
| C8 KV cache selects `AscendC8KVCacheAttentionMethod` from `kv_cache_type: C8` | [`test_modelslim_config.py`](../../tests/ut/quantization/configs/test_modelslim_config.py#L217-L249) |
| `deepseek_v4_fp8` requires `expert_dtype == "fp4"` and uses the `ds_linear` scheme | [`test_fp8_config.py`](../../tests/ut/quantization/configs/test_fp8_config.py#L14-L111) |
| ModelOpt MXFP8 registers under both names and leaves KV cache/embeddings native | [`test_modelopt_mxfp8_config.py`](../../tests/ut/quantization/configs/test_modelopt_mxfp8_config.py#L28-L142) |
| 310P resolves through its own registry and falls back to base for unmatched layers | [`test_modelslim_config_310.py`](../../tests/ut/_310p/quantization/test_modelslim_config_310.py#L43-L116) |

## Extension checklist

Adding an algorithm normally means touching four places, and the failure modes differ for each:

1. **A scheme class** with the right base class, `@register_scheme(quant_type, layer_type)`, and the `quant_type`/`act_quant_type`/`fused_activations` class attributes if it is a MoE scheme. Import it from the matching `methods/<family>/__init__.py` so registration runs.
2. **A `quant_type` producer** in whichever config can emit it — a new branch in `AscendCompressedTensorsConfig._detect_quant_type`, or a new value in a ModelSlim description. A `quant_type` string that no config can produce is dead code; a `quant_type` string a config produces but nothing registers becomes a runtime `NotImplementedError` naming the method and layer type.
3. **`is_mx_quant_type`** if the algorithm is microscaling, because the adapter's `input_dim` heuristic and the MX TP loader gate both consult it.
4. **Weight-loading metadata** — `_input_dim`, `_block_quant_scale`, `_packed_dim`/`_packed_factor`, and `supports_unaligned_tp_groups` — if the parameter sharding differs from per-channel. Choosing the wrong one is not caught at registration.

nodes.title: Speculative Decoding and Draft Proposers
nodes.description: How speculative decoding is wired on Ascend - the method-to-proposer dispatch table, the shared LLM proposer base and its ACL-graph draft runnable, the draft-token handoff from sample_tokens to the scheduler, and the Ascend rejection sampler that verifies drafts.
nodes.body:
# Speculative Decoding and Draft Proposers

Speculative decoding splits a decode step into two cooperating programs: a **proposer**
that cheaply guesses the next `K` tokens (`num_speculative_tokens`), and a
**rejection sampler** that verifies those guesses against the target model's logits.
On Ascend the proposer half lives almost entirely in `vllm_ascend/spec_decode/`, and
the verifier half in `vllm_ascend/sample/rejection_sampler.py`.

The single most important structural fact is that Ascend does **not** re-implement the
drafting algorithms. The model-backed proposers are multiple-inheritance mixins: an
upstream vLLM class (`EagleProposer`, `DraftModelProposer`, `Gemma4Proposer`, …) supplies
the algorithm and weight layout, while `AscendSpecDecodeBaseProposer` supplies the NPU
execution shell — buffer sizes, attention-group discovery, `ACLGraphWrapper` capture, and
the `_propose()` call contract. A proposer that drops the Ascend half will still import,
but it will run the upstream CUDA-shaped execution path. The model-free and
hidden-state-extraction proposers (`AscendNgramProposer`, `AscendNgramProposerNPU`,
`AscendSuffixDecodingProposer`, `AscendMedusaProposer`,
`AscendExtractHiddenStatesProposer`) do not mix in the base at all — they subclass the
upstream class directly and override only what needs to be NPU-aware.

Two entry points consume that machinery, and they are not the same code:

| Model runner | Entry point | Proposer base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V1 (`worker/model_runner_v1.py`) | `get_spec_decode_method()` in `spec_decode/__init__.py` | `AscendSpecDecodeBaseProposer` + upstream class |
| V2 (`worker/v2/model_runner.py`) | `init_speculator()` in `worker/v2/spec_decode/__init__.py` | `AscendAutoRegressiveSpeculator` + upstream speculator |

This page covers the V1 path in depth (it owns the dispatch table, the draft-token
bookkeeping and the rejection sampler), then documents the V2 landing zone separately,
because on V2 the proposer contract is an inherited *speculator* object rather than
`propose_draft_token_ids`.

## Method-to-proposer dispatch

`get_spec_decode_method(method, vllm_config, device, runner)` is a flat
`if`/`elif` ladder over `speculative_config.method`. It is called once per worker from
`NPUModelRunner._get_drafter()`, itself called from `_set_up_drafter()`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    M["speculative_config.method"] --> N{"match"}
    N -->|"ngram"| NG["AscendNgramProposer"]
    N -->|"ngram_gpu"| NGPU["AscendNgramProposerNPU"]
    N -->|"suffix"| SFX["AscendSuffixDecodingProposer"]
    N -->|"medusa"| MED["AscendMedusaProposer"]
    N -->|"dspark"| DSP["AscendDSparkProposer"]
    N -->|"mtp + use_gemma4_mtp"| G4["AscendGemma4Proposer"]
    N -->|"eagle / eagle3 / mtp"| STEP{"use_step3p5_mtp"}
    STEP -->|"yes"| S35["AscendStep3p5MTPProposer"]
    STEP -->|"no"| EAG["AscendEagleProposer"]
    N -->|"dflash"| DF2{"is_dflash2_draft"}
    DF2 -->|"yes"| D2["AscendDflash2Proposer"]
    DF2 -->|"no"| DF1["AscendDflashProposer"]
    N -->|"draft_model"| DM["AscendDraftModelProposer"]
    N -->|"extract_hidden_states"| EHS["AscendExtractHiddenStatesProposer"]
    N -->|"anything else"| ERR["ValueError: Unknown speculative decoding method"]
```

Dispatch ladder in `get_spec_decode_method()`, including the architecture- and config-dependent splits inside the `mtp`, `eagle` and `dflash` branches.

Three dispatch decisions are *not* keyed on the method name alone, so the config has to
agree with the draft checkpoint:

- `mtp` with `use_gemma4_mtp()` is routed to `AscendGemma4Proposer` before the general
  `mtp` branch, and `eagle`/`eagle3`/`mtp` with `use_step3p5_mtp()` to
  `AscendStep3p5MTPProposer`. Both checks run *inside* the method branch, so a config
  that changes draft architecture at runtime must also agree with the method string.
- `dflash` splits on `is_dflash2_draft()`, which is a pure architecture sniff:
  `"DFlash2DraftModel" in draft_model_config.architectures`. DFlash2 replaces argmax
  drafting with a top-k selector walk, so it is a different proposer class rather than
  a flag on `AscendDflashProposer`.
- `dspark` has its own method string and `AscendDSparkProposer` subclasses
  `AscendDflashProposer` (not the eagle proposer), so a DSpark config must say
  `"method": "dspark"` to reach the DSpark-specific `set_inputs_first_pass()` and
  Markov-head drafting logic.

Because the ladder raises on the final `else`, an unsupported method fails at
`_set_up_drafter()` time rather than at the first decode step — and
`propose_draft_token_ids` carries a second, defensive `ValueError` for the same case.

### What setup derives from the dispatch result

`_set_up_drafter()` assigns `decode_token_per_req = 1 + num_speculative_tokens` on
**every** rank (it sizes the target model's decode query block everywhere downstream),
then builds the proposer and sampler only when `get_pp_group().is_last_rank`. Its side
effects are as important as the proposer it builds:

- `use_aux_hidden_state_outputs` is turned on for `eagle3` (delegated to
  `self.drafter.eagle3_use_aux_hidden_state`), for `extract_hidden_states`, and for
  `use_dspark()`. This flag changes the *target* model's forward return shape — it makes
  `_model_forward` yield `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)` — so it must be decided
  before the model is loaded.
- `AscendRejectionSampler(self.sampler, self.speculative_config, self.device)` is
  constructed for every method, including the ones (ngram, suffix) whose drafts carry
  no probabilities.

Non-last ranks keep `drafter = None`, run the target model shard, and pass
`IntermediateTensors` forward.

## The shared LLM proposer base

`AscendSpecDecodeBaseProposer` (`spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py`) is the largest
piece of the subsystem and the one worth reading before touching any proposer. It
subclasses upstream `SpecDecodeBaseProposer` and is mixed with a concrete upstream
proposer via `class AscendX(UpstreamX, AscendSpecDecodeBaseProposer)`. Subclasses call
`AscendSpecDecodeBaseProposer.__init__` **explicitly** rather than chaining through
`super()`, passing `pass_hidden_states_to_model` for the method
(`AscendDraftModelProposer` passes `False`, `AscendEagleProposer` passes `True`). Because
the explicit call makes the cooperative `super()` inside the base resolve past the
concrete upstream proposer, `EagleProposer.__init__` never runs — only
`SpecDecodeBaseProposer.__init__` does, and every Ascend-side buffer is then allocated in
the base body.

### Construction: the runner is the source of truth for sizes

The base takes a `runner` reference and derives nearly everything from it rather than
from `vllm_config`:

- `query_start_loc` is a `runner._make_buffer(max_num_reqs + 2)`;
- `dcp_size` / `dcp_rank` come from the runner's DCP state;
- `slot_mapping_group`, `seq_lens_group` and `query_start_loc_group` each hold
  `num_speculative_tokens` pinned copies (sized
  `max_num_tokens + 2 * max_num_reqs`), because each draft step's attention metadata
  rewrites those tensors in place and must not alias the previous step's;
  `token_indices_to_sample` is a single `max_num_batched_tokens`-sized buffer copied per
  `_propose()`;
- `use_cuda_graph = runner._use_aclgraph() and not speculative_config.enforce_eager`.
- `_runnable = _run_merged_draft`, replaced later by an `ACLGraphWrapper` in `load_model()`;
  M-RoPE drafts allocate a `(3, max_num_tokens + 1)` positions buffer instead of the flat
  one.

Two behaviours in `__init__` are policy, not plumbing:

- **Draft tensor parallelism is faked.** If `tensor_parallel_size !=
  draft_tensor_parallel_size`, the proposer builds a one-rank TP group and installs it
  through `patch_tensor_parallel_group()`, so the draft model runs with TP=1 while the
  target keeps its real TP. The comment is explicit that only the "1 or equal to
  target" cases are supported.
- **GLM target models force the draft to eager.** `_is_glm_model()` matches any
  `model_type` containing `glm`; the proposer then clears `use_cuda_graph` with a
  warning, leaving the target's graph mode untouched.

`_raise_if_padded_drafter_batch_disabled_and_full_graph_enabled()` then rejects the
combination `disable_padded_drafter_batch=True` + ACL graph + any full-cudagraph mode:
the unpadded drafter path only exists for eager and piecewise execution.

### Loading: discovery of the draft's attention layers

`load_model()` is where Ascend diverges most visibly from upstream. It asserts
`get_pp_group().is_last_rank`, builds the model inside `self.maybe_eager_context` — a
`CompilationMode.NONE` view of `compilation_config` (installed only for eager drafts with
sequence parallelism enabled, i.e. `not use_cuda_graph and enable_sp`, and a `nullcontext`
otherwise) that is retained specifically because FX-graph capture breaks draft
construction — and then **infers the draft's attention
layers by set difference**: every `AttentionLayerBase` registered in the static forward
context that is *not* a target layer and *does* return a non-`None` KV-cache spec, minus
`DeepseekV32IndexerCache` layers, is a draft layer. The sorted names become
`attn_layer_names` (the keys `_get_attn_metadata_layer_names()` returns, i.e. the layer
map every draft step's metadata is keyed by).

`draft_attn_groups` itself is built later: the runner's KV-cache initialization calls
`drafter.initialize_attn_backend(kv_cache_config, draft_kernel_block_sizes)` after the
target's own backend, and only for `use_eagle()` / `uses_draft_model()` drafts. That call
site also forks the block-size argument: DSpark receives a *list* (one kernel block size
per KV cache group, taken as the first element of each target group's size) while every
other draft receives the target's single value, matching DSpark's own per-group group
construction. A draft architecture whose attention layers are indistinguishable from
target layers, or whose layers report no KV-cache spec, leaves the set empty and trips the
`assert len(self.draft_attn_groups) > 0` guard at the top of `build_draft_attn_metadata()`.
DSpark is the exception: it derives the layer names from
`self.model.get_draft_kv_cache_layer_names()`, rebuilds `draft_attn_groups` per
`kv_cache_group_id` so a multi-group draft gets one group per KV cache group, and records
`kv_cache_gid` / per-group kernel block sizes. `AscendStep3p5MTPProposer` overrides
`initialize_attn_backend()` for the same reason — its draft layers may span several KV
cache groups, so it builds a layer→group map and a no-op
`validate_same_kv_cache_group()`. `extract_hidden_states` takes a third route: it builds no
draft groups at all and instead has the runner call
`drafter.validate_same_kv_cache_group(kv_cache_config)`, because it writes into the
*target's* KV cache and therefore has to live in the same group.

Weight reuse is negotiated per method rather than assumed:

| Sharing hook | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `_maybe_share_embeddings` | Only runs when PP is 1 (with PP > 1 the draft and target embeddings can live on different devices). EAGLE/EAGLE3 share when `has_own_embed_tokens` is false **or** the two weight tensors compare equal (compared on CPU); DSpark shares only on the `has_own_embed_tokens == False` signal, with no weight comparison; MTP shares unless `use_compress` |
| `_maybe_share_lm_head` | For `eagle`/`dflash`/`dspark`, `draft_has_own_lm_head` is true when the draft carries `draft_id_to_target_id` or has not set `has_own_lm_head = False` (the `getattr` default is `True`). DFlash and DSpark keep their own head in that case — reduced-vocab d2t mapping and trained distinct heads must not be overwritten, since predicting over the wrong vocabulary makes the verifier reject nearly everything — while EAGLE always installs the target head. DFlash2 clears `has_own_lm_head` first so it inherits the target head. For `mtp` on DeepSeek-MLA targets, each layer's `shared_head.head` is replaced when `has_own_lm_head is False` *or* the weights compare equal, so a checkpoint with no MTP head (which `AscendDeepSeekMTP` marks with `has_own_lm_head = False`) cannot "win" the comparison against allocation-time garbage. A target with no reachable `lm_head` logs a warning and leaves the draft head in place (multimodal wrappers keep the head on the nested language model) |
| `_maybe_share_topk_indices` | MTP binds the draft's modules to the *target's* `topk_indices_buffer` object so DSA top-k indices flow from target to draft without a copy |
| `_maybe_remove_d2t` | Drops the identity `draft_id_to_target_id` map of a full-vocab EAGLE3 draft |

`_maybe_share_topk_indices` is what makes `compact_mtp_topk_indices()` work: at draft
step 0 the shared buffer still holds the target's per-token top-k rows, so step 0 uses
them directly, and for steps 1+ the helper moves the sampled rows into the position the
next step's (one-query-per-request) layout expects.

### The dual-runner call contract: `dummy_run` and `_propose`

The base proposer (and every `_propose`-bearing subclass) exposes two mirrored entry points:

- `dummy_run(...)` — capture-time and profile-time execution, with the Ascend-specific
  signature (`with_prefill`, `in_graph_capturing`, `num_reqs`, `num_tokens_across_dp`,
  `aclgraph_runtime_mode`, `batch_descriptor`, `dummy_compute_logits`, `is_profile`).
  The base implementation calls `runner._sync_metadata_across_dp(..., is_draft_model=
  True)` *first* and wraps the run in `runner.synchronize_input_prep()`, because
  `dummy_run` shares pinned CPU buffers with `execute_model` and must not overwrite them
  while a non-blocking H2D copy is still in flight. Idle DP ranks must issue the same
  collective or the DP `cpu_group` deadlocks. The model-free and medusa proposers override
  `dummy_run()` with an empty or zero-pushing stub, so the runner can call it uniformly.
- `_propose(...)` — the real drafting pass. It takes `num_speculative_tokens` as an
  explicit argument and **sets `self.num_speculative_tokens` from it**, mirroring
  upstream's `propose(num_speculative_tokens=...)`. `K == 0` returns an empty
  `[batch_size, 0]` tensor immediately so downstream code, which keys off
  `draft_token_ids.shape[1]`, stays consistent under dynamic speculation.

`_propose()` in order: (1) for `eagle3`/`dflash`/`dspark`, run the draft's
`combine_hidden_states()` over the concatenated aux hidden states and assert the result
is `hidden_size` wide; (2) `set_inputs_first_pass()` to build the draft query block and
rewrite `common_attn_metadata`; (3) dispatch the CUDA-graph bucket and pad
`query_start_loc`/`block_table`/`seq_lens` for FULL replay; (4) optionally apply
`SlidingWindowAdapter`; (5) `build_draft_attn_metadata()` for step 0 and
`attn_update_stack_num_spec_norm()` for steps 1..K-1; (6) run `self._runnable` inside
