`set_ascend_forward_context(..., is_draft_model=True, draft_attn_metadatas=...)`; (7)
`_update_full_graph_params_if_needed()`.

`_run_merged_draft()` is the default `_runnable`. It performs step 0 as a batched
forward and then loops `num_speculative_tokens - 1` times autoregressively, mutating
`forward_context.attn_metadata` to the next step's pre-built metadata. Two invariants
it maintains: positions are clamped to `max_model_len` (out-of-range drafts are kept in
the batch but will be rejected), and `_last_draft_probs` is only produced when every
step produced probabilities — if any step returns `None`, the whole list is dropped
rather than shipped partially.

Under fine-grained LM-head TP (`lmhead_tp_enable()`) the sample indices are padded to the
target graph bucket before the head runs and the logits/token tensors are trimmed back with
`_align_tensor_and_indices()` afterwards; DSpark takes a separate branch because its real
LM-head input is `batch_size * K` and is only padded to the current target bucket. Getting
this alignment wrong shows up as the `target/draft row mismatch` assertion in the rejection
sampler rather than as a drafting error.

### Draft probability export

Probabilistic drafting is opt-in and interacts badly with vocab remapping. When
`self.model.draft_id_to_target_id` exists, draft probabilities live in draft-vocab
space and cannot be used for target-space rejection sampling, so `compute_draft_token_ids`
falls back to greedy and returns `draft_probs=None`. The same fallback fires for DSpark
with a `warning_once`, and `_enable_probabilistic_draft_probs` is rejected outright at
construction for `use_local_argmax_reduction` and `use_heterogeneous_vocab`. DFlash2
rejects probabilistic sampling in `__init__` because its selector needs the unquantized
target LM head.

## Model-specific proposers

| Proposer | Shape of the draft |
| --- | --- |
| `AscendEagleProposer` | Plain EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP: `pass_hidden_states_to_model=True`, one forward per draft token, hidden states threaded through steps |
| `AscendDraftModelProposer` | Generic external draft LLM: `pass_hidden_states_to_model=False`, plus `_raise_if_vocab_size_mismatch()` / `_raise_if_draft_tp_mismatch()` |
| `AscendDSparkProposer` | Block drafting: target hidden states prepopulate draft K/V, then one anchor-first query block emits all tokens; `num_query_per_req` is `K` when `sample_from_anchor` else `1 + K` |
| `AscendDflashProposer` | Cross-attention block drafting with a context/query split; overrides `set_inputs_first_pass()` to fill context and query slot mappings with one fused Triton kernel |
| `AscendDflash2Proposer` | Same input layout as DFlash, but `compute_draft_token_ids()` walks a top-k selector graph (`greedy_select_path`) from the verified anchor instead of taking an argmax |
| `AscendGemma4Proposer` | Delegates to upstream `Gemma4Proposer` for KV-sharing and constant draft positions; keeps centroid sampling eager and disables MM inputs |
| `AscendStep3p5MTPProposer` | Full `_propose()` override (does not call `super()`), so it re-implements the dynamic-`K` assignment and empty-draft early return itself |
| `AscendNgramProposer` / `AscendNgramProposerNPU` / `AscendSuffixDecodingProposer` | Model-free: no weights to load, so `dummy_run()` is an empty stub (ngram additionally overrides `load_model()` to a no-op) |
| `AscendMedusaProposer` | Reuses upstream medusa heads; `propose()` picks the last accepted hidden state per request before delegating, and `dummy_run()` only pushes zeros through the heads inside `set_ascend_forward_context(..., is_draft_model=True)` |
| `AscendExtractHiddenStatesProposer` | Drafts nothing: it extracts and caches target hidden states for EAGLE training |

Two of these carry non-obvious state. `AscendDSparkProposer` forces
`use_cuda_graph = False` in its `__init__` — the path is not graph-safe — and rebinds
`hidden_size` to the *draft* model's hidden size, replacing the target-sized DFlash
buffers. `AscendDflash2Proposer._maybe_share_lm_head()` raises if a reduced draft
vocabulary is configured, because the selector's top-k needs the full target head.

The inheritance chain is not flat: `AscendDflashProposer` and `AscendStep3p5MTPProposer`
derive from `AscendEagleProposer`, and `AscendDSparkProposer` / `AscendDflash2Proposer`
derive from `AscendDflashProposer`. So `isinstance(drafter, AscendEagleProposer)` holds
for four other proposer classes, which is why runner-side branches that need
DSpark-specific behaviour (the `initialize_attn_backend` per-group block sizes, the
`BreakableACLGraphWrapper` unwrap) test `AscendDSparkProposer` *first*, and why
`_maybe_share_lm_head` keys on `self.method` strings rather than on class identity.

`AscendExtractHiddenStatesProposer` is the only proposer that depends on runner hooks it
does not own: `_determine_batch_execution_and_padding()` calls
`runner._pad_for_sequence_parallelism()` and `runner._sync_metadata_across_dp()`, and
raises `NotImplementedError` with an explicit message when the runner lacks them. The V2
`NPUModelRunner` lacks both, which is consistent with V2 reaching `extract_hidden_states`
through the upstream speculator instead of this proposer. It also refuses upstream's DP
coordination because that posts a differently shaped tensor to the same `cpu_group`, which
would break the gloo collective the main runner uses.

### The MTP draft model's half of the contract

`mtp` is the one method whose draft *model* also participates in the Ascend contract.
`vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_mtp.py` registers `AscendDeepSeekMTP` (a
`@support_torch_compile` subclass of upstream `DeepSeekMTP`) and it does two things the
proposer depends on:

- **It publishes head ownership.** Upstream always constructs `shared_head`, so module
  existence proves nothing. `_maybe_set_own_lm_head()` runs at the end of `load_weights()`
  and sets `has_own_lm_head = False` unless
  `model.layers.<mtp_start_layer_idx>.shared_head.head.weight` was actually in the loaded
  weight set — the case for GLM-5.3-family checkpoints that ship no MTP head and would
  otherwise leave the head at allocation-time garbage. This is precisely the signal
  `_maybe_share_lm_head` reads, which is why the weight-equality fallback is described as
  a safety net rather than the primary mechanism.
- **It applies the optional `rot` rotation.** When `is_rot_weight_used(vllm_config)` is
  true — it reads `quant_config.quant_description["is_rot_used"]`, cached in a module
  global — an extra `nn.Linear` rotates `hidden_states` before
  `spec_step_idx`-indexed forwarding, and `load_weights` remaps the
  `model.layers.<spec_layer>.rot.` prefix back to `rot.` (via `WeightsMapper`) so the
  checkpoint loads cleanly. Without the remap the quantized rotary weights would be
  reported as unexpected.

## The two-runner state machine in `execute_model` / `sample_tokens`

Since vLLM split the decode step, `execute_model` runs the target forward and
`sample_tokens` does sampling *and* drafting. Ascend follows the split, with the draft
work pushed into `sample_tokens` because it needs the sampled tokens.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant EC as EngineCore
    participant W as NPUWorker
    participant R as NPUModelRunner
    participant S as AscendRejectionSampler
    participant D as drafter

    EC->>W: execute_model(scheduler_output)
    W->>R: execute_model(scheduler_output, intermediate_tensors)
    R->>R: guard execute_model_state is None
    R->>R: build inputs, batch desc, attention metadata
    R->>R: target forward plus compute_logits
    R->>R: store ExecuteModelState
    R-->>W: None
    W-->>EC: None
    EC->>W: sample_tokens(grammar_output)
    W->>R: sample_tokens(grammar_output)
    R->>R: unpack and clear ExecuteModelState
    R->>S: rejection_sampler(metadata, draft_probs, logits)
    S-->>R: SamplerOutput with sampled_token_ids
    alt padded drafter batch
        R->>D: propose_draft_token_ids from GPU sampled ids
    else list-returning methods
        R->>R: _bookkeeping_sync builds valid sampled ids
        R->>D: propose_draft_token_ids from CPU token lists
    end
    D-->>R: draft_token_ids tensor or list
    R->>R: _copy_draft_token_ids_to_cpu on side stream
    R-->>EC: ModelRunnerOutput
    EC->>W: take_draft_token_ids()
    W->>R: take_draft_token_ids()
    R-->>EC: DraftTokenIds with per-request drafts
```

The `execute_model` / `sample_tokens` / `take_draft_token_ids` handshake, showing `ExecuteModelState` as the carrier between the two runner calls.

The guard at the top of `execute_model` is the whole reason the pairing is documented as
a state machine:

```python
if self.execute_model_state is not None:
    raise RuntimeError("State error: sample_tokens() must be called after execute_model() returns None.")
```

`ExecuteModelState` is the ephemeral carrier between the two calls — `scheduler_output`,
`logits`, `spec_decode_metadata`, `spec_decode_common_attn_metadata`, `hidden_states`,
`sample_hidden_states`, `aux_hidden_states`, `attn_metadata`, `positions`,
`ec_connector_output`, `cudagraph_stats`, `batch_desc`. Because sampling no longer
happens in `execute_model`, several things that used to be "just in scope" now have to
ride this struct, and `sample_tokens` clears it before doing any work. A worker that
calls `execute_model` twice without `sample_tokens` in between therefore fails loudly
rather than drafting from stale hidden states.

Ordering inside `sample_tokens` matters for latency, not just correctness:

1. `_sample()` dispatches to `self.rejection_sampler` whenever `spec_decode_metadata`
   is not `None`, after `prepare_sampling(max_topk)` when `enable_reduce_sample` is on.
2. `use_padded_batch` is computed as (`use_eagle` or `uses_draft_model` or
   `uses_extract_hidden_states` or `use_ngram_gpu`) and *not*
   `disable_padded_drafter_batch`. Those methods can draft straight from the GPU
   `sampler_output.sampled_token_ids` and are therefore proposed **before**
   `_bookkeeping_sync`; ngram, suffix and medusa need CPU token lists and are proposed
   **after**. The `early_pp_padded_drafter` variant hoists the proposal even earlier
   when PP spec decoding is active without async scheduling.
3. `finalize_kv_connector()` runs only after the draft model has finished, because
   target-model KV-connector finalization is deferred whenever speculative decoding is
   enabled.
4. `_update_states_after_model_execute()` is deferred onto a separate stream gated by
   `sampling_done_event` when mamba layers request accepted-token counts.

## Draft-token bookkeeping between runner and router

Three methods move drafts off the device and out to the scheduler. Their contracts are
easy to conflate, so they are worth stating separately.

**`propose_draft_token_ids(...)`** (the runner method) exists because proposers have
mutually incompatible signatures. It is one large `isinstance` ladder plus a fallback
on `speculative_config` predicates:

| Branch | Proposer call |
| --- | --- |
| `AscendNgramProposer` | `propose(K, valid_sampled_token_ids, num_tokens_no_spec, token_ids_cpu)` |
| `AscendSuffixDecodingProposer` | `propose(num_speculative_tokens=K, sampled_token_ids=...)` |
| `AscendNgramProposerNPU` | `triton_ngram_spec_decode(...)` driven straight from the runner — this proposer's own `propose()` is a stub |
| `AscendMedusaProposer` | `propose(K, ids, sampling_metadata, spec_decode_metadata, sample_hidden_states)` |
| `uses_extract_hidden_states()` | `propose(K, sampled_token_ids, target_hidden_states, common_attn_metadata)`; raises if aux hidden states are missing |
| `use_eagle() or uses_draft_model()` | `prepare_next_token_ids_{cpu,padded}` then `drafter._propose(...)` |

It also resets `self._draft_probs` / `_draft_prob_req_ids` at entry so a step that
produces no fresh probabilities never reuses the previous step's, and re-caches them via
`take_last_draft_probs()` afterwards. Every branch passes
`scheduler_output.num_spec_tokens_to_schedule` (not the configured maximum) as `K`, which
is what makes dynamic speculation work end to end.

The `ngram_gpu` branch is the one that returns more than drafts. `triton_ngram_spec_decode`
also hands back `num_valid_draft_tokens` and `valid_sampled_tokens_count`; the runner
caches the first in `self._num_valid_draft_tokens` (staged to CPU through
`copy_num_valid_draft_tokens` on its own stream and event) so the scheduler can trim, and
feeds the second to `_copy_valid_sampled_token_count`. That extra channel exists because
ngram_gpu decides acceptance on-device, and the scheduler needs the count before the normal
`sampled_token_ids` path has been unpacked.

The eagle/draft-model branch has two runner-side hooks worth knowing, because they let the
*target* model shape the drafter's inputs:

- `get_model().get_mtp_target_hidden_states()` is consulted for `mtp` and, when it returns
  a tensor, replaces the `hidden_states` fed to `_propose()`. DeepSeek-V4 MTP needs the
  pre-`hc_head` residual rather than the post-head hidden state, so the MLP default is
  wrong for it. The hook is optional (`getattr(..., lambda: None)`), so models that do not
  define it are unaffected.
- The padded/eager split is decided by `disable_padded_drafter_batch`:
  `prepare_next_token_ids_cpu()` (list in, list out) versus
  `prepare_next_token_ids_padded()` (GPU tensor, `-1` marks rejected slots), and matching
  `prepare_inputs()` versus `prepare_inputs_padded()`. The two must agree — the runner
  asserts the sampled-token container type on each path.

**`_copy_draft_token_ids_to_cpu(scheduler_output, zeros_only=False)`** stages the drafts
into a pinned CPU buffer on its own stream with an event:

- It records `prev_num_spec_tokens = self._draft_token_ids.shape[1]` *before* any early
  return, so the next step unpacks the previous draft tensor with the right stride even
  when the copy itself is skipped.
- It returns early when `num_spec_tokens` is 0, and under async scheduling it returns
  early unless the batch has structured-output requests, output token ids, or PP > 1.
- It slices the pre-allocated buffer to the *actual* draft width
  (`draft_token_ids.shape[1]`), because under dynamic speculation the produced width can
  be below the configured maximum and an unsliced copy would shape-mismatch.
- Non-tensor drafts (the list-returning ngram/suffix path) are skipped; only tensors are
  copied.

**`take_draft_token_ids()`** is the router-facing getter, delegated unchanged from
`NPUWorker.take_draft_token_ids()` to the runner. It calls `super()` and then applies
*per-request truncation* when `self.drafter` owns a `dynamic_spec` scheduler:
`dynamic_spec.num_verify_tokens` is clamped into `[0, num_spec_tokens]` and each request's
draft list is cut to that length. This is how the DSpark/DFlash verify budget reaches the
scheduler as a shorter `spec_token_ids` list.

Drafts also reach the scheduler through a second channel: `ModelRunnerOutput.spec_token_ids`
is populated in `sample_tokens` **only** when `use_pp_spec_decode`
(`speculative_config is not None and pp.world_size > 1`). There the drafts are converted
to per-request lists and re-ordered into `req_ids_output_copy` order via a
`dict(zip(draft_req_ids, draft_ids_list))` lookup, so requests absent from the draft
batch get `[]`. Outside PP, `spec_token_ids` stays `None` and the engine core takes the
drafts from `take_draft_token_ids()`; the comment at the top of `execute_model` records
that vLLM removed the async-scheduling `deepcopy` in favour of exactly this pair.

### Async scheduling: repairing `optimistic_seq_lens_cpu`

With async scheduling the scheduler has already advanced `num_computed_tokens_cpu` by the
*previous* step's full scheduled width (`prev_drafts + 1`), i.e. it assumed every draft
would be accepted. The host-side seq lengths therefore over-count by the number of rejected
tokens, and anything that builds attention metadata from CPU seq lengths would see them.
`correct_optimistic_seq_lens_cpu()` (in `spec_decode/utils.py`) subtracts
`prev_drafts + 1 - valid_sampled_token_count` per participating request, where a request
participates only if it existed last step (`prev_positions >= 0`) and actually had drafts.
The counts come from `_copy_valid_sampled_token_count()`, which stages them onto a side
stream with an event; the correction synchronizes that event first, but since the copy was
launched a full step earlier it is normally already signalled, so this does not reintroduce
the device-to-host seq-lens sync the design avoids. `update_num_computed_tokens_for_batch_change()`
is the matching CPU-side helper for batch-composition changes.

## The rejection sampler

`AscendRejectionSampler` subclasses upstream `RejectionSampler` and overrides the pieces
that must be NPU-aware. `patch/worker/patch_rejection_sampler.py` additionally rebinds
the module-level `apply_sampling_constraints`, `rejection_sample` and
`expand_batch_to_tokens` in `vllm.v1.sample.rejection_sampler`, so upstream callers that
imported those names use the Ascend implementations — a patch with an explicit TODO to
delete once upstream makes them class methods.

`forward()` asserts `metadata.max_spec_len <= MAX_SPEC_LEN`, samples the **bonus** token
from `bonus_logits_indices` with logprobs mode overridden so logits are returned, then
takes `target_logits` (cast to float32, cloned when raw logprobs are needed) through
`apply_logits_processors()` and `apply_sampling_constraints()`, and finally calls
`rejection_sample()`.

`apply_logits_processors()` is a full replacement of the upstream version, not a hook:
upstream introduced blocking H2D copies; the Ascend version expands request indices to
token indices on device (`expand_batch_to_tokens`) and applies Triton penalties via
`apply_all_penalties` when `HAS_TRITON`, falling back to `Sampler.apply_penalties` with a
`warning_once` otherwise. It also handles `allowed_token_ids_mask`, bad words, `MinTokens`
via `apply_with_spec_decode`, and thinking-budget state.

`rejection_sample()` selects one of four execution paths, all Triton-first with PyTorch
fallbacks:

| Path | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| Greedy | `sampling_metadata.all_greedy`, or per-request `temperature == GREEDY_TEMPERATURE` |
| Random | default non-greedy path |
| Block verify | `max_spec_len >= 3` **and** `rejection_sampler_config.enable_block_verify` |
| Entropy verify | `rejection_sampler_config.enable_entropy_verify`, using `posterior_threshold` / `posterior_alpha` |

Two constraints are enforced rather than documented: `synthetic_mode` combined with
block verify raises `ValueError` (per-token first-rejection acceptance is incompatible
with joint cumulative-product verification), and every output slot is pre-filled with
`PLACEHOLDER_TOKEN_ID` so `RejectionSampler.parse_output()` can derive the valid
per-request prefix later in `_bookkeeping_sync`. Under `enable_reduce_sample` the greedy
path uses the distributed `greedy_sample()` all-gather instead of a local `argmax`, and
constraints use `apply_top_k_top_p(logits, k, p, top_k)` — the top-k/all-gather/top-p
order matters because each rank only holds `vocab_size // tp_size`.

`rejection_sample` also asserts `target_logits.shape[0] == num_tokens` with a message
naming the mismatch, which is the single most common symptom of a drafting path whose
padding disagrees with `spec_decode_metadata`.

## ACL-graph interaction for draft models

The draft model gets its **own** execution path through the graph subsystem; it is not
captured as part of the target graph (except in the merged EAGLE case).

- `load_model()` replaces `self._runnable` with `ACLGraphWrapper(self._run_merged_draft,
  self.vllm_config, runtime_mode=CUDAGraphMode.FULL, use_eagle=..., enable_enpu=...)` when
  the compilation config has full cudagraphs and `use_cuda_graph` is set. `get_model()`
  unwraps it, and any proposer needing the raw module (DSpark's `BreakableACLGraphWrapper`
  case) unwraps explicitly.
- The draft has **three** module-level `GraphParams` registries rather than one: main
  model, draft model, draft prefill (`set_draft_graph_params`,
  `set_draft_graph_prefill_params` in `compilation/acl_graph.py`). Each raises
  `ValueError` if set twice, and each keys entries by *captured* token count — under
  `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` with spec decoding the configured sizes are rounded up to multiples
  of `decode_query_len`, so the runner derives keys with
  `sorted({desc.num_tokens ...})` from the dispatcher's capture descriptors, not from raw
  config sizes. See [Graph Mode, Compilation, and Fusion Passes](graph-mode-and-compilation.md)
  for the capture/replay contract itself.
- `_update_full_graph_params()` delegates to `update_full_graph_params(attn_backend,
  self.update_stream, forward_context, num_tokens, vllm_config, speculative_config,
  draft_attn_metadatas=...)`, which wraps the backend dispatch in
  `set_current_vllm_config()`. It fires on every FULL-mode invocation that is not a
  capture, and `enable_enpu` flips whether it runs before or after `run_draft()`; in
  `dummy_run()` it is additionally suppressed while capture is in progress.
- Upstream's replay barrier is skipped for the merged EAGLE draft path
  (`is_draft_eagle`), and `BreakableACLGraphWrapper` reproduces it, so draft FULL replay
  does not double-synchronize.

`--cudagraph_capture_sizes` must therefore contain multiples of `K + 1` (documented as
`n * (K + 1)`), because the dispatcher buckets the target-side `1 + K` decode query block
and the draft inherits those buckets.

## Pipeline-parallel and aux-hidden-state constraints

Speculative decoding and PP compose only through explicit, registered support:

- The drafter is built and loaded **only on the last PP rank**
  (`load_model()` asserts it). Non-last ranks keep `drafter = None` and therefore fall
  through `propose_draft_token_ids` to `draft_token_ids = None`.
- `_set_up_drafter()` gates the whole drafter construction on `get_pp_group().is_last_rank`.
- For V2, `worker/v2/pp_utils.py` holds `_SPEC_PP_SUPPORT_BY_METHOD`, a per-method
  capability record (`architectures`, `needs_aux_hidden_states`,
  `bypass_upstream_pp_guard`, `unsupported_feature`). Only `mtp`, `eagle3` (MiniMax M3
  sparse only) and `dspark` (`DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`) are registered; anything else
  returns `None` from `resolve_spec_pp_support()` and the upstream spec+PP guard stays in
  force. `bypass_upstream_spec_pp_guard()` temporarily rewrites
  `pipeline_parallel_size = 1` during upstream init and `restore_pp_after_upstream_init()`
  rebuilds the `PPHandler` afterwards.
- Aux hidden states are the PP constraint that bites: `eagle3`, `extract_hidden_states`
  and `dspark` need the target's intermediate hidden states, and under
  `broadcast_pp_output` the runner must `send_tensor_dict`/`broadcast_tensor_dict`
  them explicitly. `need_accepted_tokens` (mamba layers) forces
  `_update_states_after_model_execute()` onto a stream that waits on
  `sampling_done_event`, because accepted-token counts feed mamba state bookkeeping.
  Which target layers contribute is config-driven: `_eagle3_uses_aux_hidden_state()` reads
  `draft_model_config.hf_config.eagle_config["use_aux_hidden_state"]` (default `True`,
  also `True` when the draft config is absent), and
  `_get_eagle3_aux_layers_from_config()` extends the upstream eagle3 layer-id lookup with
  DSpark's `dspark_target_layer_ids` (DeepSeek-V4) or `target_layer_ids` (GQA), adding 1
  because those checkpoints index the *pre*-layer residual.
- On V2, drafts travel inside the *same* PP broadcast slot as the accepted tokens.
  `patch_v2/patch_spec_pp.py:install_spec_pp_token_broadcast()` widens
  `pp_handler.max_sample_len` to `max_sample_len + (max_sample_len - 1)`
  (sampled tokens plus the draft width) and rewraps `broadcast` /
  `get_prev_sampled_outputs`: the sender appends `req_states.draft_tokens` after the
  sampled ids, the receiver slices the tail back out and scatters it into
  `req_states.draft_tokens` via `index_copy_`, and the CPU-side mask filters freed or
  no-longer-selected slots before the copy. The installation is idempotent
  (`_vllm_ascend_spec_pp_broadcast_patched`) and a second pending send raises
  `RuntimeError`, so exactly one sample/broadcast pair is in flight at a time.
- The `dspark` config patch (`patch_speculative_config.py`) has to run its
  `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__` with DCP temporarily forced to 1
  (`_temporarily_disable_dspark_dcp`), because upstream does not yet support
  MLA-DCP + DSpark. It also restores `DSparkDraftModel` after multimodal config
  conversion and fills `ptd_token_id` from either `dspark_noise_token_id` or
  `mask_token_id` depending on the checkpoint family.

## Dynamic speculation: a per-step `K`

`K` is not always the configured maximum. Two mechanisms reduce it per step, and the
runner-side contract is the same for both: `scheduler_output.num_spec_tokens_to_schedule`
is authoritative and every proposer must honour it.

- **Batch-size based.** The scheduler builds `dynamic_sd_lookup` from
  `num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size` and indexes it by the current batch size
  (`core/recompute_scheduler.py`, `core/dyntra_lb_scheduler.py`, and the balance-schedule
  patch). The resulting `K` can be 0, which is exactly why `_propose()` and
  `AscendStep3p5MTPProposer._propose()` both short-circuit on `K == 0`.
- **Confidence based.** `DynamicSpecScheduler` (in `spec_decode/utils.py`) is shared by
  DFlash and DSpark: it converts a per-token acceptance estimate into cumulative survival
  probabilities, spends a shared verify budget on them, and emits per-request verify
  lengths. DFlash derives confidence from `max(softmax(logits))` of the argmax draft token;
  DSpark from `compute_confidence()` — the confidence head's sigmoid over the target hidden
  state concatenated with the Markov embedding of the draft token. The pipeline is
  `cumprod` → `compute_verify_budget` → `allocate_verify_budget`: the budget is recomputed
  only every `budget_update_interval` steps, from the mean number of surviving prefix
  positions above `budget_threshold`, rounded up and nudged to odd (verification widths of
  `K+1` are even, which the kernels pad more efficiently), then clamped to
  `[min_verify_tokens, num_speculative_tokens]`. Allocation gives every request `min_k`
  tokens and hands the remaining global budget to the globally highest survival positions,
  which yields prefix lengths for free because survival is monotonically non-increasing
  within a request. The runner then reads `dynamic_spec.num_verify_tokens` in
  `take_draft_token_ids()` and truncates each request's draft list. It is enabled by
  `additional_config.dynamic_spec_config` (`method` ∈ {`dspark`, `dflash`}) and is
  documented as a model-runner-v1-only, exploratory feature; the proposer's own
  `dynamic_spec` attribute is what `take_draft_token_ids` looks for, so a method string
  that does not match the class leaves the drafts untruncated.

Note the two halves are independent: `num_spec_tokens_to_schedule` bounds how many drafts
are *produced*, while `num_verify_tokens` bounds how many the scheduler is asked to
*verify*. When the second is smaller the excess drafts are simply discarded before the
next forward, which is why truncation happens in `take_draft_token_ids()` rather than in
the proposer.

`prev_num_spec_tokens` and the width-sliced CPU copy are the other half of this contract:
because `K` varies, both the D2H copy and the unpack stride are derived from the tensor
actually produced rather than from config.

## What fails, and how it announces itself

| Symptom | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `RuntimeError: State error: sample_tokens() must be called after execute_model() returns None.` | A previous `execute_model` left `ExecuteModelState` unconsumed |
| `ValueError: Unknown speculative decoding method: ...` | Method not in the dispatch ladder (raised at setup, or defensively during proposal) |
| `NotImplementedError` mentioning `disable_padded_drafter_batch` | `disable_padded_drafter_batch=True` with ACL graph + full cudagraphs |
| `assert len(self.draft_attn_groups) > 0` | No draft attention group was registered — usually the `load_model()` set difference found no draft layers, or the runner's `drafter.initialize_attn_backend(...)` call never ran |
| `rejection_sample: target/draft row mismatch` assertion | Draft padding disagrees with `SpecDecodeMetadata` |
| `ValueError` about synthetic mode and block verify | Incompatible rejection-sampler configs (`enable_block_verify` with `rejection_sample_method="synthetic"`) |
| `ValueError` naming `use_local_argmax_reduction` or `use_heterogeneous_vocab` | Probabilistic drafting (`draft_sample_method="probabilistic"`) combined with either flag |
| ngram requests silently getting no drafts | `num_tokens >= max_model_len` filtering inside `AscendNgramProposer.propose()` |
| DSpark drafts produced but never shortened | `dynamic_spec_config.method` does not match the proposer class, so `self.drafter.dynamic_spec` is `None` and `take_draft_token_ids()` skips truncation |

Debug tooling exists at both boundaries: `_log_propose_draft_token_ids_entry()` logs the
concrete drafter class, method, `K`, request count, and `spec_decode_metadata` state;
`AscendRejectionSampler._log_rejection_sampler_entry/_log_rejection_sampler_exit` log
shape/dtype baselines and an approximate accept rate. Both are gated on
`logger.isEnabledFor(DEBUG)` and record only host scalars.

## Configuration surface

`speculative_config` (vLLM) supplies `method`, `num_speculative_tokens`, `model`,
`draft_tensor_parallel_size` (1 or the target's TP size), `disable_padded_drafter_batch`,
`enforce_eager`, `draft_sample_method`, and
`num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`. `(num_speculative_tokens + 1) <= 16` because
`npu_fused_infer_attention_score` caps decode tokens per round.

Ascend-only knobs live in `additional_config`:

- `rejection_sampler_config` — `enable_block_verify`, `enable_entropy_verify`,
  `posterior_threshold` (default `0.95`, validated in `(0, 1]`), `posterior_alpha`
  (validated `>= 0`).
- `dynamic_spec_config` — `method` (`dspark` or `dflash`, or `None` to disable; validated
  against `SUPPORTED_METHODS`) plus `method_params`, a free-form dict whose keys the
  scheduler reads with fallbacks: `initial_verify_budget_per_req` (default 5, clamped into
  `[min_verify_tokens, num_speculative_tokens]` to seed `budget_k`),
  `budget_update_interval` (default 16), `budget_threshold` (default 0.3) and
  `min_verify_tokens` (default 1). Because `method_params` is not schema-checked, a typo
  silently selects the default rather than failing.
- `draft_window_size` — the sliding-window draft attention cap, read from the validated
  `AscendConfig` singleton and applied through `SlidingWindowAdapter`. It is ignored
  (with a warning) for `mtp` because MTP reuses the target's own layers, and it is *not*
  applied in `_propose()` for `dspark`, which re-applies it later to the per-group block
  table that DSpark's draft FIA actually reads. The adapter's `future_offset` is method
  dependent: `K` for EAGLE3 (its `seq_lens` are context-only, so the K draft positions lie
  beyond it) and `0` for DFlash/DSpark (their `set_inputs_first_pass()` already bakes the
  query stretch into `seq_lens`, so adding `K` again would double-count).

`enable_reduce_sample` is the other cross-cutting switch: it swaps in the distributed
reduce-sample path on both sides of the step (`prepare_sampling(max_topk)` before the
sampler, `greedy_sample()` all-gather inside it), and it is refused at startup when
combined with `finegrained_tp_config.lmhead_tensor_parallel_size` or when the node is a
PD-disaggregated `kv_producer`.

## The V2 landing zone

Model Runner V2 does not use `get_spec_decode_method`. `init_speculator(vllm_config,
device)` returns an Ascend *speculator*. `AscendNPUModelRunner` deletes the upstream
`self.speculator`, sets it to `None`, and re-creates it through `init_speculator()` — gated
on `not self.use_spec_pp or self.is_last_pp_rank`, the V2 echo of the V1 "drafter lives on
the last PP rank" rule — then assigns the runner's shared `update_stream` so the main-model
graph manager and the draft graph manager record and replay on the same stream.

| Method | V2 speculator |
| --- | --- |
| `extract_hidden_states` | Upstream `ExtractHiddenStatesSpeculator`, reused as-is apart from `update_stream`; raises `NotImplementedError` on vLLM 0.28.0 |
| `speculative_config.use_dspark()` | `AscendDSparkSpeculator` |
| `speculative_config.use_dflash()` | `AscendDFlashSpeculator` |
| `mtp` that is neither gemma4 nor step3p5 | `AscendMTPSpeculator` |
| everything `use_eagle()` still accepts (`eagle`, `eagle3`) | `AscendEagleSpeculator` |
| anything else | `NotImplementedError` |

`AscendAutoRegressiveSpeculator` is the V2 analogue of `AscendSpecDecodeBaseProposer`:
it layers the Ascend draft loop over any upstream autoregressive speculator
(`super().__init__()` first, then the upstream `input_buffers` is replaced with
`AscendInputBuffers`, which carries the extra `seq_lens_cpu` the Ascend attention-metadata
builders need, plus per-step `draft_seq_lens_cpus` buffers under FULL decode graphs).
`AscendMTPSpeculator` is a bare subclass of it; `AscendEagleSpeculator` adds only
`_create_draft_vllm_config()` (forcing `pipeline_parallel_size=1`,
`enable_expert_parallel=False`, `enable_eplb=False`, because EAGLE drafts are dense even
when the target is MoE).

V2 does not subclass the rejection sampler at all. It keeps upstream's sampler object and
`patch_v2/patch_triton.py` rebinds `rejection_sampler_utils.rejection_sample` and
`rejection_sampler.rejection_sample` to the NPU Triton implementation in
`worker/v2/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py` (block-level logits stats plus a
probabilistic rejection kernel). Two visible capability gaps there: `use_fp64=True` raises
`NotImplementedError`, and `use_block_verification` is accepted but documented as not yet
implemented on NPU. The sampler is only invoked when `input_batch.num_draft_tokens != 0`,
and it receives `self.speculator.draft_logits` so probabilistic rejection can see the draft
distribution.

The V2 graph substitution is done by patch, not by dispatch:
`vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_v2/patch_eagle_speculator.py` rebinds
`vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.autoregressive.speculator.SpeculatorCudaGraphManager` to
`AutoRegressiveAclGraphManager`, and `patch_v2/patch_dflash_speculator.py` rebinds
`DFlashCudaGraphManager` to `DFlashAclGraphManager` plus `build_attn_metadata` in the
dflash cudagraph module. On 310P the workers re-override the manager *after*
`patch_eagle_speculator` (to `AutoRegressiveAclGraphManager310`, which has no FIA
graph_task), and `patch_spec_decode_310.py` additionally swaps in CPU
`prepare_prefill_inputs` / `prepare_decode_inputs` / `update_draft_inputs` helpers and
routes `mtp` to `AscendMTPSpeculator310` (rebinding both the `init_speculator` module
symbol and the name already imported into `model_runner`).
`tests/ut/spec_decode/test_eagle_aclgraph_source_regression.py` pins this contract by AST:
the manager must derive from `SpeculatorCudaGraphManager`, and the patch must assign the
module symbol, with no `Prefill*`/`Decode*` split.

## Tests worth knowing

- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_llm_base_proposer.py` — the `disable_padded_drafter_batch`
  guard across every `CUDAGraphMode`, `_create_draft_vllm_config` runner-type
  propagation, MTP LM-head lookup, and multimodal image-token resolution per architecture.
- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_eagle_proposer.py` — the largest harness: graph-mode/enforce-eager
  initialisation per method, `load_model()` on PP1/PP>1/multimodal, `dummy_run` variants,
  `_run_merged_draft` per-method input preparation, and both `prepare_inputs` flavours.
- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dflash2_proposer.py` — `get_spec_decode_method("dflash",
  ...)` routing by `architectures`, plus the selector/anchor path.
- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_gemma4_proposer.py` — `mtp` + `use_gemma4_mtp` routing.
- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_mtp.py` — `compact_mtp_topk_indices` across DSA-CP world
  sizes, including the empty-batch case that must skip the collective.
- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd.py` — schedule lookup boundaries, gaps, clamping
  to the runtime maximum, and range-validation errors.
- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_eagle_aclgraph_source_regression.py` and
  `test_step3p5_source_regression.py` — source-level regressions that assert the patch
  and override structure rather than behaviour.
- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_extract_hidden_states_proposer.py` — the runner-hook contract
  (`_pad_for_sequence_parallelism` / `_sync_metadata_across_dp`) and the explicit
  `NotImplementedError` messages when a runner lacks them.
- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_dspark_proposer.py` and `test_dspark_speculator.py` — DSpark
  draft-layout, Markov/confidence-head, and V2 speculator `load_draft_model()` behaviour.
- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_autoregressive_draft_metadata.py` — asserts GQA draft block
  tables match the padded batch (executes the production initializer via AST).
- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_utils.py` — `SlidingWindowAdapter` and the CPU correction
  helpers (`correct_optimistic_seq_lens_cpu`,
  `update_num_computed_tokens_for_batch_change`).
- `tests/ut/sample/test_rejection_sampler.py` — greedy/random/block-verify PyTorch
  reference implementations that the Triton kernels are checked against.
- `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_speculators_vwn_eagle3.py` — the VWN-EAGLE3 draft model
  (`Eagle3VwnLlamaForCausalLM` and its layers) on CPU.

## Related pages

- [Graph Mode, Compilation, and Fusion Passes](graph-mode-and-compilation.md) — the
  `ACLGraphWrapper` capture/replay contract and the three `GraphParams` registries the
  draft path uses.
- [KV Cache and Block Layout](kv-cache-and-block-layout.md) — draft attention groups,
  per-group block tables, and slot mappings.
- [Model Registry and Models](../integrations/model-registry-and-models.md) — where
  `DeepSeekMTPModel` / `DeepseekV32MTPModel` are registered to `AscendDeepSeekMTP`.
- [Request Execution](../workflows/request-execution.md) — how `execute_model` /
  `sample_tokens` / `take_draft_token_ids` fit the engine-core loop.

nodes.title: Distributed Groups, HCCL, and Collective Helpers
nodes.description: How vllm-ascend reshapes the NPU world into its own DP/PP/PCP/TP plus Ascend-only process groups, how the patched GroupCoordinator reuses HCCL process groups and sizes their comm buffers, what the pyhccl ctypes communicator is for, and which patched collectives and custom collective ops run on the hot path.
nodes.body:
# Distributed Groups, HCCL, and Collective Helpers

Ascend inference needs process groups that upstream vLLM never asks for. MoE communication wants an EP-shaped group on every pipeline stage, PD disaggregation wants a prefill-side tensor-parallel group whose all-to-all layout differs from the decode side, fine-grained TP wants four extra groups sharded along the *data-parallel* axis, KV layer parallelism (KVPP) wants a group that never crosses a pipeline stage, and dynamic EPLB wants an isolated communicator that must not be merged with EP. All of that is defined in one place — `init_ascend_model_parallel` — and instantiated through one patched class, `GroupCoordinatorPatch`, which is also where HCCL process-group reuse, comm-buffer sizing, and sleep-mode teardown live.

Three distinct communication layers are easy to confuse, so fix them first:

| Layer | Owner | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `torch.distributed` HCCL process groups | `GroupCoordinatorPatch` / `HcclPgRegistry` | Every model-parallel collective: TP, DP, PCP, EP/MC2, KVPP, EPLB, fine-grained TP. |
| `PyHcclCommunicator` (`pyhccl`) | [`pyhccl.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/device_communicators/pyhccl.py) | Direct `libhccl.so` calls on a group that is **not** HCCL (weight transfer from a trainer, packed broadcasts). |
| Patched `torch.distributed` primitives + `torch.ops.vllm.*` | [`patch_distributed.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_distributed.py), [`register_custom_ops.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/register_custom_ops.py) | 310P tensor-alignment shims and the padded EP all-gather / reduce-scatter pair that MoE runs every forward. |

Related reading: [MoE Execution](../concepts/moe-execution.md) for which of these groups a given forward actually uses, [Platform and Hardware Profiles](../architecture/platform-and-hardware-profiles.md) for the capability that gates the 310P shims, [Patching Architecture](../architecture/patching-architecture.md) for how the monkey patches get installed, and [PD Disaggregation and KV Transfer](../workflows/pd-disaggregation-and-kv-transfer.md) for the `p_tp` consumer side.

## Entry point and rank layout

`NPUWorker._init_worker_distributed_environment` ([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L1223-L1236)) is strictly ordered: `init_distributed_environment(..., "hccl")`, then upstream `ensure_model_parallel_initialized(TP, PP, PCP, DCP)`, then `init_ascend_model_parallel(self.parallel_config)`. So the Ascend groups are built *on top of* an already-live world group, and the HCCL backend string they inherit is read back from it (`torch.distributed.get_backend(get_world_group().device_group)`).

`init_ascend_model_parallel` ([`parallel_state.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/parallel_state.py#L22-L147)) flattens the entire world into one 5-D grid and then re-slices that grid once per group kind:

```python
# The layout of all ranks: ExternalDP * EP
all_ranks = torch.arange(world_size).reshape(
    -1, global_dp_size, global_pp_size, global_pcp_size, global_tp_size,
)
```

The leading `-1` is the ExternalDP axis described in the docstring — data-parallel replicas that are not part of the model (the verl-integration case where each replica generates independently). Every subsequent group is a slice of this same tensor, which is why all of them agree on rank adjacency by construction.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["all_ranks = arange(world).reshape(ExternalDP, DP, PP, PCP, TP)"] --> B["reshape(-1, kvpp_size)"]
    A --> C["transpose(1, 2) then reshape(-1, DP * PCP * TP)"]
    A --> D["flat view split into pd_tp_ratio chunks"]
    A --> E["arange(world).reshape(PP, DP, TP) with DP chunks of fine-grained size"]
    B --> KVPP["KVPP group: within one pipeline stage"]
    C --> MC2["mc2 and dynamic_eplb groups: one per pipeline stage, EP-shaped"]
    D --> PTP["p_tp_N groups: prefill all-to-all peers"]
    E --> FG["otp / lmheadtp / emtp / mlptp groups: sharded along DP"]
```

*One rank tensor, four different re-slicings: each Ascend-only group is a view of the same layout, so their rank arithmetic can never drift apart.*

State is held in module globals (`_MC2`, `_MLP_TP`, `_OTP`, `_LMTP`, `_EMBED_TP`, `_P_TP`, `_DYNAMIC_EPLB`, `_KVPP`), each with a `get_*_group()` accessor that asserts it was initialized. Initialization is idempotent through `model_parallel_initialized()`, which is just `_MC2 is not None` — MC2 is the one group that is always created, so it doubles as the sentinel. The two groups with their own precondition assert that they are not already initialized (`_KVPP`, `_P_TP`), which means re-entering the function after a partial failure raises rather than silently leaking a second communicator.

### What each group covers

| Global | Group name | Rank set | Gated by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `_KVPP` | `kvpp` | Consecutive `kvpp_size` (= TP size) ranks, i.e. one pipeline stage's TP row | `kvpp_config.size > 1` (`additional_config.enable_kvpp`) |
| `_P_TP` | `p_tp_{num}` | Prefill-side all-to-all peers, `pd_tp_ratio` (or head-replica-split) sized | `pd_head_ratio > 1` **and** `kv_transfer_config.is_kv_producer` |
| `_MC2` | `mc2` | All `DP × PCP × TP` ranks of one pipeline stage | Always |
| `_DYNAMIC_EPLB` | `dynamic_eplb` | Same rank set as `mc2` | `eplb_config.dynamic_eplb` |
| `_OTP` | `otp` | Chunks of `oproj_tensor_parallel_size` along DP, per PP stage, per TP index | `oproj_tensor_parallel_size > 0` |
| `_LMTP` | `lmheadtp` | Same construction | `lmhead_tensor_parallel_size > 0` |
| `_EMBED_TP` | `emtp` | Same construction | `embedding_tensor_parallel_size > 0` |
| `_MLP_TP` | `mlptp` | Same construction | `mlp_tensor_parallel_size > 0` |

`destroy_ascend_model_parallel` ([L194-L233](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/parallel_state.py#L194-L233)) mirrors the table: `destroy()` on each live group in a fixed order (KVPP, MC2, MLP, LMTP, EMBED, OTP, P-TP, dynamic EPLB) and rebind to `None`.

**EP-shaped groups.** `all_ranks.transpose(1, 2).reshape(-1, DP * PCP * TP)` produces one group per `(ExternalDP, PP)` pair containing every DP, PCP and TP rank of that pipeline stage. Both `mc2` and `dynamic_eplb` are built from the *same list object*, so they span identical ranks but are deliberately separate HCCL communicators — the EPLB weight-exchange P2P traffic and the MoE dispatch traffic must not share one collective ordering or one comm buffer. `TokenDispatcherWithMC2` caches the mc2 backend's comm name at construction ([`token_dispatcher.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py#L109-L151)), and the EPLB loader issues `isend`/`irecv` against `get_dynamic_eplb_group().device_group` ([`eplb_device_transfer_loader.py`](../../vllm_ascend/eplb/core/eplb_device_transfer_loader.py#L32-L78)).

**KVPP stays inside a stage.** `all_ranks.reshape(-1, kvpp_size)` cuts the *flattened* rank order, and because `kvpp_size` equals the TP size the chunk boundaries land exactly on TP rows. The unit test pins this: for `TP=4, PP=2, world=8` the groups are `[[0,1,2,3],[4,5,6,7]]` ([`test_parallel_state.py`](../../tests/ut/distributed/test_parallel_state.py#L147-L193)). The KVPP transport then broadcasts each layer's cache from its owner rank over that group's `device_group` on a transfer stream, gated by a recorded NPU event so the persistent cache is not overwritten before the copy completes ([`kvpp.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kvpp.py#L9-L36)).

**P-TP exists only on PD prefill nodes.** `pd_tp_ratio` and `pd_head_ratio` are *derived*, not configured: they come from `kv_transfer_config`'s `prefill.tp_size` / `decode.tp_size` divided by each other, then clamped to the model's total KV head count, with `num_head_replica = prefill_tp_size // num_kv_head` ([`ascend_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py#L718-L737)). The derivation is skipped entirely for DeepSeek-MLA models, so MLA deployments keep both ratios at 1 and never build `p_tp`. When `num_head_replica <= 1` the groups are simply flat `pd_tp_ratio` chunks; otherwise the rank tensor is reshaped to `[DP*PP*PCP, num_head, num_head_replica]`, permuted to put replicas adjacent, and then cut into `alltoall_group_size` chunks — the head-replica-aware all-to-all layout. The group is named `p_tp_{num}` where `num` is the index of the group containing the local rank, and it is the only group whose consumers call raw `all_to_all_single` on `device_group` to rearrange KV heads with `pd_tp_ratio` cut-and-transpose ([`kv_transfer/utils/utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/utils/utils.py#L50-L77)).

**Fine-grained TP groups are sharded along DP, not TP.** `_create_or_get_group` ([L115-L131](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/parallel_state.py#L115-L131)) builds its *own* grid `arange(world_size).reshape(PP, DP, TP)`, takes `num_chunks = DP // group_size` chunks along the DP axis, and for each `(pp, chunk, tp_idx)` emits one group. That is the mechanical reason `FinegrainedTPConfig` requires MoE models and `data_parallel_size % size == 0` ([`ascend_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py#L1118-L1135)), and why the config doc says these components are only *effective* at `tensor_parallel_size == 1`. Two consequences worth knowing before adding a fifth component:

- The cache is keyed on `group_size` alone. Configuring `oproj_tensor_parallel_size == mlp_tensor_parallel_size` yields **one** coordinator, and the first-created `group_name` is the one that sticks (and therefore the one `create_hccl_pg_options` sees).
- The grid has no PCP axis, so non-zero fine-grained sizes assume `pcp_size == 1`; with prefill context parallelism on, that `reshape` no longer matches `world_size`.

Consumers pick their group by checking the enable flags and the layer prefix: embeddings and LM head in [`vocab_parallel_embedding.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/vocab_parallel_embedding.py#L64-L73), MLP `down_proj` `reduce_scatter` and `o_proj` `all_to_all_single` + `reduce_scatter` in [`linear_op.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/linear_op.py#L174-L268), and the quant-method `tp_rank` in [`method_adapters.py`](../../vllm_ascend/quantization/method_adapters.py#L208-L223).

### Cross-DP global rank

vLLM exposes no single cross-DP global rank, and the two deployment shapes disagree about what `rank_in_group` means. `get_global_rank` ([L236-L266](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/parallel_state.py#L236-L266)) normalizes both by computing `replica_size = TP * PP * PCP`, taking `rank_in_group % replica_size`, and adding `data_parallel_index * replica_size` — the true DP rank that is never reset, unlike `data_parallel_rank` on dense DP=1 engines. DCP and EP deliberately do not appear in `replica_size` because they overlay existing NPUs. The Mooncake store backend uses it to derive a globally unique rank ([`mooncake_backend.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/backend/mooncake_backend.py#L246)).

## The patched GroupCoordinator and HCCL process-group reuse

`vllm.distributed.parallel_state.GroupCoordinator` is replaced wholesale by `GroupCoordinatorPatch` at import of [`patch/worker/patch_distributed.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_distributed.py#L253-L254) (imported unconditionally from `patch/worker/__init__.py`). Every group in the table above — and every upstream group vLLM creates later — therefore goes through this constructor.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as Worker
    participant GC as GroupCoordinatorPatch
    participant R as HcclPgRegistry
    participant PG as torch.distributed
    W->>GC: init_model_parallel_group(ranks, backend, group_name)
    GC->>GC: create_hccl_pg_options(group_name)
    GC->>R: acquire(ranks, backend, pg_options, reuse_domain)
    alt key already held
        R-->>GC: existing HCCL device group, refcount + 1
    else new key
        R->>PG: new_group(ranks, backend, pg_options)
        PG-->>R: device group handle
        R-->>GC: handle, refcount 1
    end
    GC->>PG: new_group(ranks, gloo)
    GC->>GC: NPUCommunicator if world_size > 1
```

*Coordinator construction: options first, then a deduplicated HCCL group per rank set, then an always-separate Gloo CPU group.*

### Reuse key and reuse domains

`make_hccl_pg_key` ([`_hccl_pg_registry.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/_hccl_pg_registry.py#L65-L91)) returns `None` unless the backend is `hccl` *and* the options are auditable *and* the options' `global_ranks_in_group` (if populated) matches the requested ranks. The key itself is `(backend, ranks tuple, normalized options, reuse_domain)`, where normalization keeps only non-default audited fields — in practice `hccl_config`. Everything else in a `ProcessGroupHCCL.Options` is either runtime-populated and already represented elsewhere (`global_ranks_in_group`, `group_id`, `group_name`) or a known default.

`_resolve_reuse_domain` ([L39-L43](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_distributed.py#L39-L43)) splits the group name on `:` and returns the base name verbatim only for names containing `eplb` or exactly `mc2`; everything else collapses to `shared`. So `ep` and `tp` over the same ranks with the same buffer size share one HCCL communicator, while `eplb`, `dynamic_eplb` and `mc2` never do — even against an EP group with identical ranks and options. The tests in [`test_patch_distributed.py`](../../tests/ut/patch/worker/patch_common/test_patch_distributed.py#L294-L374) pin all three behaviors: one HCCL `new_group` for two shared coordinators, two for `ep` vs `mc2`, two for `ep` vs `eplb`, and sharing for two unremarkable names.

Reuse is **fail-closed by design**. An unrecognized non-default pg-option field logs `Disabling HCCL process-group reuse because pg_options has non-default field '...'` and returns no key ([L183-L216](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/_hccl_pg_registry.py#L183-L216)). The group is still created, but it is tracked in `_unshared_hccl_groups` and destroyed directly by its owner, so a future torch_npu option cannot silently alias two incompatible communicators. The registry docstring also states the ordering contract explicitly: `new_group` is collective, so the registry only deduplicates *within* a process-serial, globally ordered construction sequence — it is not a concurrent group factory.

### Per-coordinator resources and teardown

`_init_device_groups` ([L156-L182](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_distributed.py#L156-L182)) loops over every rank set in `group_ranks` (a coordinator may cover several disjoint rank sets), calling `create_hccl_pg_options` *per set* and creating a `gloo` CPU group for each. Only the rank set containing `self.rank` populates `ranks` / `world_size` / `rank_in_group` / `cpu_group` / `device_group`. Then `_init_device_communicator` attaches an `NPUCommunicator` when `use_device_communicator` and `world_size > 1`, and an optional `MessageQueue` shm broadcaster is created over the CPU group when `use_message_queue_broadcaster` (used by speculative decoding's single-rank draft TP group, [`llm_base_proposer.py`](../../vllm_ascend/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py#L208-L216)).

Failure handling is deliberate: any exception in the constructor body triggers `self.destroy()` before re-raising, and `destroy()` is idempotent — it tolerates callers that call it twice or on a half-built instance. `_release_hccl_resources` releases device communicator → registry keys in **reverse** acquisition order → unshared groups; `destroy()` then destroys the device group directly only when the backend is not `hccl`, and finally the CPU group. Registry refcounting means a shared communicator survives until the last coordinator releases it ([test L481-L509](../../tests/ut/patch/worker/patch_common/test_patch_distributed.py#L481-L509)), and `destroy_distributed_environment` is wrapped so the registry is cleared *after* the upstream teardown succeeds — otherwise a re-initialized engine would reuse stale handles ([L79-L97](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_distributed.py#L79-L97)).

### Sleep mode: `destroy_hccl` / `restore_hccl`

Sleep mode must free the HCCL comm buffers without tearing down the CPU groups. `HcclSleepWakeupManager` walks every live `GroupCoordinator` in vLLM's `_groups` weakref registry and calls `destroy_hccl()` on each ([`sleep_mem_optimized.py`](../../vllm_ascend/device_allocator/sleep_mem_optimized.py#L131-L186)). That drops the device communicator, releases the registry keys, sets `device_group = None`, and returns whether anything was released. `restore_hccl()` then re-runs `_init_device_groups(create_cpu_group=False)` plus `_init_device_communicator()`, so a **new** HCCL communicator is built and the Gloo group is left untouched; calling it a second time returns `False`.

The subtlety that bites: MC2 token dispatchers cache `backend.get_hccl_comm_name(local_rank)` for the fused `npu_moe_distribute_*` operators. After a restore that name is stale, so `refresh_moe_hccl_groups()` re-reads it on every dispatcher that exposes `refresh_hccl_group` ([`token_dispatcher.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py#L146-L151)). Any new group whose communicator name is cached in an operator must add the same hook.

## Group-option plumbing: buffers, names, and when to add a coordinator

`create_hccl_pg_options(group_name)` ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L1025-L1030)) is the single funnel from a name to an HCCL option object:

```python
options = torch_npu._C._distributed_c10d.ProcessGroupHCCL.Options()
hccl_config = get_hccl_config_for_pg_options(group_name) or {}
hccl_config["group_name"] = group_name
options.hccl_config = hccl_config
```

`get_hccl_config_for_pg_options` ([L1033-L1052](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L1033-L1052)) is a three-entry dispatch table plus a default:

| `group_name` | `hccl_config` | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| contains `mc2` | **none** (only `group_name`) | Explicit `FIXME`: MC2 operators partition the comm space from `HCCL_BUFFSIZE`, so passing `pg_options` misaligns memory |
| exactly `dp` | `{"hccl_buffer_size": calculate_dp_buffer_size()}` | Must hold `dp_size + 1` int32 values (one flag per rank plus `with_prefill`) |
| exactly `dynamic_eplb` | `{"hccl_buffer_size": 100}` | Small, fixed P2P weight-exchange buffer |
| anything else | `{"hccl_buffer_size": 200}` | Default (MiB-scale) shared buffer |

`calculate_dp_buffer_size` sizes the DP buffer as `ceil((dp_size + 1) * 4 bytes / 1 MiB)` clamped below by 50, i.e. it is a *correctness floor* rather than a tuning knob — undersizing it truncates the all-reduce payload that carries per-rank token counts ([L1055-L1070](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L1055-L1070), with `_DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE = 200`, `_MIN_DP_BUFFER_SIZE = 50`, `_DYNAMIC_EPLB_BUFFER_SIZE = 100` at [L74-L76](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L74-L76)).

So, concretely, **a new group needs its own coordinator when** any of these holds:

1. **Its rank set differs** from an existing group's — reuse is keyed on the exact rank tuple, not on a name.
2. **It needs a different comm-buffer size**, because `hccl_config` participates in the key; two names that map to the same buffer config will share.
3. **Its collectives must not interleave** with another component's on one communicator. This is the reason `mc2` and `*eplb*` get their own reuse domains even over identical ranks.
4. **Its lifecycle differs** — anything that must be torn down and rebuilt independently of the world group (sleep mode, or an operator that caches the HCCL comm name) needs a `refresh_hccl_group`-style hook.
5. **The name matters downstream.** Names are not decorative: `mc2`, `dp` and `dynamic_eplb` select buffer behavior, and `*eplb*`/`mc2` select reuse isolation. A new name inherits the default 200 buffer and the `shared` domain, which is usually what you want for a plain module-TP group.

One more buffer caveat that is not an HCCL option at all: CANN MegaMoe's symmetric buffer is a separate `torch` allocation, not `HCCL_BUFFSIZE`, and its shape parameters must be derived only from rank-invariant config — otherwise ranks allocate mismatched buffers and HCCL aborts with `SUSPECT REMOTE ERROR 507057` ([`moe_comm_method.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py#L292-L358)).

## `PyHcclCommunicator`: HCCL without a HCCL process group

`pyhccl` is a hand-written `ctypes` binding to `libhccl.so`, exporting six symbols — `HcclGetErrorString`, `HcclGetRootInfo`, `HcclCommInitRootInfo`, `HcclAllReduce`, `HcclBroadcast`, `HcclCommDestroy` — with `hcclUniqueId` modeled as a 4108-byte struct ([`pyhccl_wrapper.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/device_communicators/pyhccl_wrapper.py#L34-L167)). The library is loaded once per path via a class-level cache, and `find_hccl_library` resolves it from `HCCL_SO_PATH` or falls back to `libhccl.so` only when `torch.version.cann` is set, raising `ValueError("HCCL only supports Ascend NPU backends.")` otherwise ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L477-L495)).

`PyHcclCommunicator.__init__` ([`pyhccl.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/device_communicators/pyhccl.py#L37-L128)) enforces the invariant that makes this layer worth having: **it refuses to attach to an HCCL group** (`assert dist.get_backend(group) != dist.Backend.HCCL`). Its purpose is to stand up a data-plane communicator over a *host-side* rendezvous — a Gloo group or a vLLM `StatelessProcessGroup` — which is exactly the trainer↔worker case. Rank 0 calls `hcclGetUniqueId`, then the id bytes are broadcast through the group (plain `dist.broadcast` over the process group, or `broadcast_obj` for a stateless group), then `hcclCommInitRank` runs on the target device and a one-element `all_reduce` warms the communicator up before the stream is synchronized. Two loud failure modes are deliberate:

- `world_size == 1` or an unloadable library leaves the object constructed but `available = False, disabled = True`, and `all_reduce`/`broadcast` become no-ops. This is what makes the class importable and testable off-NPU.
- Every op asserts the tensor is on `self.device`, because an HCCL comm created for one device touching another device's memory produces an illegal memory access rather than an error code.

Concrete consumers: `HCCLWeightTransferEngine.init_transfer_engine` computes a DP-offset global rank, creates a `StatelessProcessGroup` to the trainer and wraps it in a `PyHcclCommunicator` ([`hccl_engine.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/weight_transfer/hccl_engine.py#L141-L167), [L325-L340](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/weight_transfer/hccl_engine.py#L325-L340)); the trainer side is always rank 0. Weight updates then either broadcast tensor-by-tensor on a given stream or use `packed_broadcast_producer/consumer`, which concatenates parameters into ~1 GiB `uint8` buffers on rotating streams with double buffering ([`packed_tensor.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/weight_transfer/packed_tensor.py#L18-L113)).

## Intra-node versus inter-node boundaries

Nothing in the group layout branches on node topology: an HCCL process group spans whatever ranks you give it, intra-node over HCCL's local transports and inter-node over RDMA, and the same `GroupCoordinator` code builds both. Where the code *does* draw the line is in three specific places:

- **CPU rendezvous is per group, not per node.** Every coordinator creates its own `gloo` group over its own ranks, and the optional `MessageQueue` shm broadcaster is that group's CPU-side transport. On the multiprocess executor the whole engine is single-node with a loopback rendezvous (`get_loopback_ip()`), while `node_rank_within_dp * local_world_size` establishes the global rank offsets for the DP-per-node case ([`patch_multiproc_executor.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_multiproc_executor.py#L43-L80), [L141-L158](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_multiproc_executor.py#L141-L158)).
- **Weight transfer picks its transport by locality.** `npu_ipc` shares memory through Ascend IPC handles and therefore only works between processes on the same physical chip: the handle key is `{host_ip}-{physical_chip_id}`, cached for the process lifetime, so co-located trainer and worker derive the same UUID and a non-local one fails the handle lookup ([`npu_ipc_engine.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/weight_transfer/npu_ipc_engine.py#L62-L90)). `hccl` is the choice when the trainer is on another node.
- **EPLB peer ranks live in a different space.** The EPLB transfer planner addresses peers group-locally, but `P2POp.peer` is global. `AscendGlooEplbCommunicator` translates with `dist.get_global_rank(self._cpu_group, peer)` and validates the range, and it disables the upstream profile-time buffer-reservation collective because Gloo needs no HCCL buffer reservation ([`communicator.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/eplb/communicator.py#L9-L56)).

## Patched collectives on the hot path

### 310P tensor-alignment shims

`communication_adaptation_310p` ([`patch/platform/patch_distributed.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_distributed.py#L33-L88)) rewrites two module-level primitives, but only when the profile advertises `HardwareCapability.DISTRIBUTED_COMMUNICATION_ADAPTATION` — today only the 310P profile ([`hardware_profile.py`](../../vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py#L188-L210)):

- `torch.distributed.broadcast` (and the `distributed_c10d` alias) becomes all-gather-then-select: build a `tensor_list`, place the local tensor at its own rank index, `all_gather`, then copy `tensor_list[src]` back into the caller's tensor. `group_src` takes precedence over `src`; CPU tensors are delegated to the original function; `async_op=True` returns a `NullHandle` whose `wait()` is a no-op, because the gather already ran synchronously.
- `torch.distributed.all_reduce` is emulated **only for `int64` tensors** — otherwise it delegates untouched. `SUM` returns `stack(tensor_list).sum(0)`; `MAX` round-trips through `cpu().numpy().max(0)`; anything else raises `RuntimeError(f"not implement op {op}")`.

Both do all-gather-and-reduce because 310P cannot perform those reductions on the problematic layouts/dtypes directly; the patch header records the intent and the future plan to remove it once alignment is handled natively. Note the shape of the contract: the `MAX` branch returns a **new** tensor instead of writing in place, and `SUM` likewise — callers that ignore the return value would silently lose the result.

### The padded EP all-gather / reduce-scatter pair

Two Ascend custom ops are registered on the `PrivateUse1` dispatch key with fake implementations for ACL graph capture ([`register_custom_ops.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/register_custom_ops.py#L181-L195)):

| Op | Collective sequence | Fake shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `torch.ops.vllm.maybe_all_gather_and_maybe_unpad` | optional pad to max local size → `ep_group.all_gather(x, 0)` → trim each rank back to its real size | `sum(local_sizes)`, or `x.shape[0] * ep_group.world_size` with no DP metadata |
| `torch.ops.vllm.maybe_pad_and_reduce` | pad each DP shard to the common length → `ep_group.reduce_scatter(x, 0)` → slice this rank's original token count | `local_sizes[rank_in_group]`, or `x.shape[0] // ep_group.world_size` |

**Why padding is mandatory, not an optimization.** `all_gather` and `reduce_scatter` are equal-length collectives: every rank must contribute a first dimension of identical size. But DP (and SP) ranks hold *different* token counts in the same forward — that is the whole point of data parallelism — and PCP only adds another ragged axis. Two layouts bridge the gap, and the code picks between them at runtime:

- **SP/EP chunk layout.** When the MoE runner installed per-rank chunk sizes, `dp_metadata.get_chunk_sizes_across_dp_rank()` returns a list of length `ep_group.world_size`; the local tensor is zero-padded up to `max(local_sizes)`, gathered, then reshaped to `[num_ranks, max_local_size, ...]` and concatenated back with each rank's real slice ([L32-L72](../../vllm_ascend/ops/register_custom_ops.py#L32-L72)). The reduce direction pads *per rank* into `[num_ranks, max_local_size, ...]` before `reduce_scatter` and returns `reduced[:local_sizes[rank_in_group]]`, with a comment calling out the mismatch between the collective's equal chunks and the next layer's ragged expectation ([L88-L98](../../vllm_ascend/ops/register_custom_ops.py#L88-L98)).
- **Classic DP layout.** With no chunk-size list, the code uses `dp_metadata.num_tokens_across_dp_cpu` and `_EXTRA_CTX.padded_length`, where `padded_length = ceil(max_tokens_across_dp / TP) * TP` is recorded in the forward context ([`ascend_forward_context.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py#L200-L204)) — the same ceil-to-TP-multiple rounding that MC2 uses for `padded_num_tokens`.

The two callers are the MoE prepare/finalize pair: `_prepare_with_ep_group` gathers `hidden_states`, `router_logits` and the per-token scale, then PCP-gathers again truncated to `max_tokens_across_pcp`; `_finalize_with_ep_group` PCP-reduce-scatters then calls `maybe_pad_and_reduce` ([`prepare_finalize.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/prepare_finalize.py#L401-L455), [L539-L555](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/prepare_finalize.py#L539-L555)). The draft-model-plus-VL combination short-circuits to `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` instead, because that path has no DP token distribution to reconcile.

Fake implementations are as load-bearing as the real ones: they must return exactly the shape the real op returns or ACL graph capture will bake in a wrong buffer. `_maybe_pad_and_reduce_fake` therefore reproduces the `local_sizes[rank_in_group]` slice, not a naive division, and the tests assert the ragged cases ([`test_register_custom_ops.py`](../../tests/ut/ops/test_register_custom_ops.py#L44-L80)).

### Device communicator

`NPUCommunicator` ([`npu_communicator.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/device_communicators/npu_communicator.py#L23-L62)) is the class `NPUPlatform.get_device_communicator_cls()` hands back ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L192-L194)), and the MRv2 graph path temporarily swaps it in for `CudaCommunicator` during capture ([`worker/v2/utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/utils.py#L34-L48)). It is a thin `DeviceCommunicatorBase` subclass that pins the current NPU device, leaves `ca_comm` and `fi_pcie_ipc_ar_comm` as `None` (a protocol placeholder for vLLM's CUDA-only FlashInfer PCIe IPC path), and installs `_NpuAll2AllManager` — a no-op with `support_fault_tolerance = False` and CPU zero tensors for the queries, because NPU MoE dispatches through MC2 or all-gather and never registers a real all-to-all manager. Its existence is what satisfies vLLM's fault-tolerance probe for `data_parallel_size > 1` plus MoE without enabling a CUDA-only backend.

## Configuration and operational notes

- `additional_config.finegrained_tp_config` sizes must be `> 0`, `≤ data_parallel_size`, divide it, and require a MoE model; `oproj` additionally requires `tensor_parallel_size == 1` and graph mode, and only on PD decode nodes.
- `additional_config.enable_kvpp` sets the KVPP group size to the TP size and rejects PCP, DCP, KV-transfer connectors, graph mode, hybrid/MLA-only violations, and variable-step MTP in one `KVPPConfig.validate` pass ([`ascend_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py#L59-L92)).
- `pd_tp_ratio` / `pd_head_ratio` / `num_head_replica` are derived and not user-settable; a `prefill.tp_size` that is not a multiple of `decode.tp_size` fails `assert` at config time.
- `HCCL_SO_PATH` overrides the HCCL library used by `pyhccl` only; the torch_npu process groups load their own.
- Batch-invariant mode forces `HCCL_DETERMINISTIC=strict` (plus `LCCL_DETERMINISTIC=1`) and clears `weight_nz_mode` ([`batch_invariant.py`](../../vllm_ascend/batch_invariant.py#L79-L95)); MiniMax-M2 sets `HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV` for ACL graph capture; PD QoS is injected as `ASCEND_GLOBAL_RESOURCE_CONFIG.comm_resource_config.qos`; KV transfer timeouts derive from `HCCL_RDMA_TIMEOUT`/`HCCL_RDMA_RETRY_CNT` when `ASCEND_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT` is unset.
- Mooncake `register_buffer` must merge KV-cache ranges down to at most 256 regions, the HCCL per-process registration limit; exceeding it raises with the fragment count and byte totals rather than failing opaquely inside HCCL ([`kv_transfer/utils/utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/utils/utils.py#L460-L477)). See [Performance Tuning](../operations/performance-tuning.md) for the buffer-size knobs these constants feed.

| [`test_pyhccl.py`](../../tests/ut/distributed/device_communicators/test_pyhccl.py), [`test_pyhccl_wrapper.py`](../../tests/ut/distributed/device_communicators/test_pyhccl_wrapper.py) | Disabled paths for `world_size == 1` and a missing library; stateless-group rank handling; dtype and reduce-op enum mapping; `HCCL_CHECK` error text. |
| [`test_communicator.py`](../../tests/ut/distributed/eplb/test_communicator.py), [`test_sleep_mem_optimized.py`](../../tests/ut/device_allocator/test_sleep_mem_optimized.py) | Group-local to global EPLB peer translation; sleep/wakeup wiring through the HCCL manager. |

# Files

- [Distributed Groups, HCCL, and Collective Helpers](distributed-and-hccl.md) - How vllm-ascend reshapes the NPU world into its own DP/PP/PCP/TP plus Ascend-only process groups, how the patched GroupCoordinator reuses HCCL process groups and sizes their comm buffers, what the pyhccl ctypes communicator is for, and which patched collectives and custom collective ops run on the hot path.
- [LoRA and Adapter Support](lora.md) - How multi-LoRA is served on Ascend — the PunicaWrapperNPU platform hook and its kernel-backend selection, the BGMV/SGMV custom ops with their C++ and Meta registration, the packed and Triton single-slot linear fast paths, MoE-aware LoRA including the quantized-MoE variant, and the worker-level add/remove/pin surface.
- [Model Loading Paths: NetLoader, rfork, and Sharded State](model-loading-and-registration.md)
- [Model Registration and Ascend Model Wrappers](model-registry-and-models.md) - How vllm-ascend registers model architectures into vLLM's ModelRegistry, why some architectures are carried downstream instead of upstream, the shape of an Ascend model wrapper (text backbone, vision preprocessing, indexer, MTP and DSpark draft heads), and the _CONFIG_REGISTRY / MODEL_ARCH_CONFIG_CONVERTORS patches that must exist before any model import.
- [Upstream vLLM Integration Surface and Version Lanes](upstream-vllm-interfaces.md) - The contract between vllm-ascend and an unmodified vLLM — declared plugin entry points, the NPUPlatform subclass hooks, Worker/ModelRunner inheritance, the AttentionBackend and KV cache spec contracts, the KVConnector/Offloading/ModelRegistry registries, the monkey-patch surface, and how one installation supports both the vLLM 0.28.0 release lane and the pinned main lane.
