| `dump_config` materialisation path/content, conflict and type rejection | `tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py` ([`test_ascend_config.py`](../../tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py#L627-L658)) |
| Dump start/finalize semantics, `stop` only for stop-capable debuggers, `dump=False` on dummy runs | `TestNPUModelRunnerDebugger` ([`test_model_runner_v1.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py#L1964-L2092)) |
| `reduce_sum` dispatch vs native fallback, env overrides, AscendC-priority vs Triton-only registration, no-backend no-op, `init_batch_invariance` gating | `tests/ut/test_batch_invariant.py` ([`test_batch_invariant.py`](../../tests/ut/test_batch_invariant.py#L26-L272)) |
| End-to-end bitwise invariance of logprobs between BS=1 and BS=N | `tests/e2e/pull_request/four_card/rlhf/consistency/test_batch_invariant_tp4.py` ([`test_batch_invariant_tp4.py`](../../tests/e2e/pull_request/four_card/rlhf/consistency/test_batch_invariant_tp4.py#L130-L304)) |
| Env-registry contract and the strict `0`/`1` parser | `tests/ut/test_envs.py` ([`test_envs.py`](../../tests/ut/test_envs.py#L22-L79)) |
| Profiling-symbol config generation (the artifact the service profiler consumes) | `tests/ut/test_profiling_config.py` ([`test_profiling_config.py`](../../tests/ut/test_profiling_config.py#L8-L52)) |

The e2e invariance test is worth reading as the executable specification of the mode: it reads
`envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` to decide that custom all-reduce must be considered non-deterministic,
runs 32 prompts individually and then batched, and compares per-step logprobs with `torch.equal`,
failing with a per-prompt, per-token diff
([`test_batch_invariant_tp4.py`](../../tests/e2e/pull_request/four_card/rlhf/consistency/test_batch_invariant_tp4.py#L130-L160),
[`test_batch_invariant_tp4.py`](../../tests/e2e/pull_request/four_card/rlhf/consistency/test_batch_invariant_tp4.py#L236-L304)).

## Related pages

- [Logging, Metrics, and Service Profiling Configuration](observability-and-logging.md) — the logger, the metric provider, and the generated `service_profiling_symbols.<version>.yaml` that MS Service Profiler reads.
- [Performance Tuning](performance-tuning.md) — where to spend the time these tools help you find, and the host knobs (`PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF`, HCCL, CPU binding) that sit next to them.
- [The Configuration System](../architecture/configuration-system.md) — `additional_config` validation, `_NON_USER_INPUT_KEYS`, and the `envs.py` registry rule.
- [Graph Mode and Compilation](../concepts/graph-mode-and-compilation.md) — why `cudagraph_mode` selects a different dump class, and what ACL graph capture hides from eager hooks.
- [Build, Packaging, and Installation](build-and-install.md) — the source-build paths for the `batch_invariant_ops` wheel and for msprobe with `aclgraph_dump`.

nodes.title: vLLM-Ascend Code Wiki: Start Here
nodes.description: Task-routing entry point for the vllm-ascend code wiki — what the plugin is, how the plugin registration, platform, worker, model-runner and attention/MoE layers fit together, and the shortest reading order for changing a platform hook, an attention backend, the MoE path, KV-cache layout, graph capture, a patch, or a test.
nodes.body:
# vLLM-Ascend Code Wiki: Start Here

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../vllm_ascend] file "../vllm_ascend" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
**vllm-ascend is a hardware plugin, not a fork.** It does not add model files to upstream vLLM. It reaches vLLM through four mechanisms only — platform hooks, setuptools entry points, monkey patches, and subclassing — and `AGENTS.md` makes that a review rule, not a preference ([`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md#L206-L226)). Everything Ascend-specific lives in [`vllm_ascend/`](../vllm_ascend): a `Platform` subclass, worker and model-runner subclasses, registered attention backends, registered registries (KV connectors, model loaders, models, quant configs), and a two-tier patch tree.

That single fact explains most of the indirection you will read about here. When a question feels like "where does Ascend code get called from?", the answer is almost always one of: vLLM asked the platform for a dotted path, vLLM loaded a general plugin, a patch replaced an upstream function, or a runtime capability gate consulted the hardware profile.

## The map

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    REG["setup.py entry points: vllm.platform_plugins plus four vllm.general_plugins"] --> PLAT["platform.py: NPUPlatform"]
    PLAT --> PROF["device/hardware_profile.py: HardwareProfile and HardwareCapability"]
    PLAT --> CFG["ascend_config.py: AscendConfig from additional_config"]
    PLAT --> PATCHP["patch/platform: engine-core patch tier"]
    PLAT --> WK["worker/worker.py: NPUWorker"]
    WK --> PATCHW["patch/worker: per-worker patch tier"]
    WK --> MR1["worker/model_runner_v1.py: default v1 runner"]
    WK --> MR2["worker/v2: MRv2 behind VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER"]
    WK --> MR3["_310p: NPUWorker310 and NPUModelRunner310"]
    MR1 --> ATTN["attention/: backends, metadata builders"]
    MR1 --> MOE["ops/fused_moe: router, dispatch, comm methods"]
    MR1 --> KVL["core/kv_cache_interface.py and worker/block_table.py"]
    MR1 --> COMP["compilation/: ACLGraph, compiler, fusion passes"]
    ATTN --> OPS["ops/ and csrc/: torch.ops._C_ascend kernels"]
    MOE --> OPS
```

*Registration flows down through the platform, worker and model runner into the attention, MoE, KV-cache, compilation and op packages; each box names the directory that owns it.*

Two other layers cut across the diagram and are worth knowing before you dive in:

- **The hardware profile is the decision surface.** [`device/hardware_profile.py`](../vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py#L113-L131) holds one frozen `HardwareProfile` per Ascend family — A2, A3, 310P, A5 — carrying enum-valued implementation families, a `default_worker_cls`, and a `frozenset[HardwareCapability]` ([lines 157-251](../vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py#L157-L251)). Code asks `get_current_hardware_profile().supports(HardwareCapability.X)` instead of branching on chip identity.
- **The forward context carries per-step state.** [`ascend_forward_context.py`](../vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py) publishes the MoE comm method, padding lengths, masks and layer index so kernels can read them without argument threading. That is why the same op code serves both runners.

## Pick your lane first

Three execution variants exist, and choosing the wrong one wastes an afternoon. Decide this before reading any runner code.

| Lane | Selected by | Code | State |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **v1 model runner** (default) | `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` unset or `0` | [`worker/model_runner_v1.py`](../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L341) — `NPUModelRunner(GPUModelRunner)`, the full step pipeline | The lane most features and tests target |
| **v2 model runner** | `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` only | [`worker/v2/model_runner.py`](../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py#L79) — overrides `prepare_inputs`, `sample`, `sample_tokens`, `postprocess_sampled` around upstream's step driver | Experimental; [`worker/v2/README.md`](../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/README.md#L1-L8) tracks the remaining gaps |
| **310P compatibility** | Installed wheel built for 310P; `HardwareProfile` selects it automatically | [`_310p/worker_310p.py`](../vllm_ascend/_310p/worker_310p.py#L32-L43), `_310p/model_runner_310p.py`, `_310p/attention/`, `_310p/quantization/` | Separate worker class, compatibility attention and quant families, forced-NZ weight layout |

The v1/v2 switch is a single read in the worker: `init_device` builds the v2 runner when `self.use_v2_model_runner` is true, otherwise the v1 runner ([`worker/worker.py`](../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L496-L511)). And that flag is **environment-only by construction**: `VllmConfig.use_v2_model_runner` is monkey-patched to return `envs.VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER` and default to `False`, precisely so upstream's model-architecture whitelists, Triton checks and feature inspections cannot silently enable MRv2 on Ascend ([`patch/platform/patch_use_v2_model_runner.py`](../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_use_v2_model_runner.py#L18-L30), catalogued at [`patch/__init__.py`](../vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py#L673-L696)).

For 310P, `NPUWorker310` subclasses `NPUWorker` and swaps the runner in `_create_model_runner`, choosing `NPUModelRunner310V2` or `NPUModelRunner310` by the same flag. The compatibility lane also replaces the attention backend family and quant config class at platform level, so a 310P change usually touches `_310p/` **and** a capability gate — never just one.

## Route by task

Each row is "you are about to change X, read this first". Pages are named for the question, not the directory.

### Changing behaviour in code

| You want to change | Start here | Use this when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A platform hook, a device query, or config write-back | [NPUPlatform and Hardware Capability Profiles](architecture/platform-and-hardware-profiles.md) | You are editing `NPUPlatform`, adding a capability, or need to know why a hook returns a dotted path instead of a class |
| The hardware-identity model (A2/A3/310P/A5) | [NPUPlatform and Hardware Capability Profiles](architecture/platform-and-hardware-profiles.md) | You need a new `HardwareCapability`, a new `*Family` enum value, or discover code branching on `is_310p()` and want the sanctioned alternative |
| An attention backend or its metadata builder | [Attention Backend Selection and Implementations](concepts/attention-backends.md) | You are adding an MLA/GQA/sparse/compress backend, or a kernel ignores tensors that its metadata declares |
| The MoE router, dispatcher, or comm method | [MoE Execution: Router, Dispatch, Comm Methods, and EPLB](concepts/moe-execution.md) | You are touching experts, prepare/finalize overlap, ALLGATHER vs ALLTOALL vs MC2 selection, or expert load balancing |
| KV-cache layout, specs, block tables | [KV Cache Specs, Block Layout, and Placement](concepts/kv-cache-and-block-layout.md) | Separate K/V tensors, NZ format, padded pages, hybrid attention+Mamba pooling, or KVPP are involved |
| Graph capture, compilation, fusion passes | [Graph Mode, Compilation, and Fusion Passes](concepts/graph-mode-and-compilation.md) | You are changing ACLGraph capture/replay, batch-descriptor keyed caching, FULL vs PIECEWISE, or a graph fusion pass |
| Quantization behaviour | [Quantization Methods and Schemes](concepts/quantization.md) | A new quant scheme, a `(quant_type, layer_type)` registry entry, KV-cache quant, or the 310P variant |
| Speculative decoding / draft proposers | [Speculative Decoding and Draft Proposers](concepts/speculative-decoding.md) | You are adding an MTP/eagle3/dspark/dflash/ngram proposer or debugging draft-token bookkeeping |
| A monkey patch | [Patching Architecture and Catalog Discipline](architecture/patching-architecture.md) | You are adding a file under `patch/platform/` or `patch/worker/`, or wondering which tier a fix belongs in |
| A custom op or ACLNN/Triton kernel | [Custom Ops, ACLNN Kernels, Triton Ops, and Meta Registration](architecture/custom-ops-and-kernels.md) | You are adding `torch.ops._C_ascend` bindings, meta/fake implementations, or the CMake build for the `.so` |
| A user-facing config knob | [Configuration System: additional_config, Sub-configs, and Env Vars](architecture/configuration-system.md) | Adding an `AscendConfig` sub-config or `VLLM_ASCEND_*` environment variable (all env vars must be registered in `envs.py`) |
| Distributed groups or collectives | [Distributed Groups, HCCL, and Collective Helpers](integrations/distributed-and-hccl.md) | You need a new parallel group (DP/PP/PCP/TP or Ascend-only MC2, MLP-TP, O-TP, LM-TP, embed TP, KVPP), or pyhccl/HCCL options |
| LoRA / adapters | [LoRA and Adapter Support](integrations/lora.md) | You are touching punica on NPU, BGMV/SGMV ops, or MoE-aware LoRA |
| Which models the plugin registers | [Model Registration and Ascend Model Wrappers](integrations/model-registry-and-models.md) | An architecture is missing from `ModelRegistry` or needs an Ascend wrapper/draft head |
| Weight loading (netloader, rfork, sharded state) | [Model Loading Paths: NetLoader, rfork, and Sharded State](integrations/model-loading-and-registration.md) | Startup weight transfer, elastic loading, or 310P sharded save/load is in scope |
| A test | [Test Architecture: Unit Tests, E2E Suites, and CPU Mocking](testing/test-architecture.md) | You are writing a UT (CPU, mocked `torch_npu`) or an e2e case, or need to know why a UT must not touch a device |
| Which tests CI will run | [CI Workflows and Selective Test Execution](testing/ci-and-test-selection.md) | Your change needs the right runner labels, a curated suite, or you are debugging why a test was not selected |

### Understanding a flow end to end

| Question | Start here | Use this when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "How does vLLM even find this plugin?" | [Workflow: Plugin Registration and Startup Sequence](workflows/plugin-bootstrap.md) | You need the authoritative ordering of entry points, `pre_register_and_update`, `check_and_update_config`, engine-core spawn, then per-worker replay |
| "What happens in one engine step?" | [Workflow: One Engine Step Through the Model Runner](workflows/request-execution.md) | A `SchedulerOutput` becomes a forward plus sampled tokens and you need to know where padding, graph dispatch or metadata diverges |
| "How is KV cache sized and captured?" | [Workflow: KV Cache Sizing, Allocation, Reshape, and Capture](workflows/kv-cache-initialization.md) | Memory budgeting, per-spec allocation, block-table publication, profile run and graph warmup are involved |
| "Who builds the architecture layers?" | [System Architecture Overview](architecture/overview.md) | You want the process model (main/engine-core vs worker) and the domain table before opening files |
| "Which vLLM surface does this hook implement?" | [Upstream vLLM Integration Surface and Version Lanes](integrations/upstream-vllm-interfaces.md) | You are checking whether an extension point is supported, what is patched vs subclassed, or how two vLLM revisions are handled |

### Operating and debugging

| Question | Start here | Use this when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build, wheel, container, SOC detection | [Build, Packaging, and Installation](operations/build-and-install.md) | `SOC_VERSION` / `_build_info` generation, the ACLNN extension build, or a hardware-family image is the problem |
| Logs, metrics, service profiling | [Logging, Metrics, and Service Profiling Configuration](operations/observability-and-logging.md) | You need the Ascend logger's prefixes/handlers, the `ms_service_metric` provider, or the generated profiling symbol config |
| Throughput/latency knobs | [Performance Tuning Levers and CPU Affinity](operations/performance-tuning.md) | KV-cache budgeting, cudagraph capture sizes, CPU/IRQ binding, MoE token capacity, or SP/EP tradeoffs are in play |
| Profiling, dump, debug aids | [Profiling, Dump, and Debug Aids](operations/profiling-and-debugging.md) | You need the torch_npu profiler wrapper, msprobe/dump, deterministic or batch-invariant modes, or debug env vars |
| Scheduler choice and DP balance | [Workflow: Scheduler Variants, Selection Rules, and DP Load Balancing](workflows/scheduler-variants.md) | `scheduler_cls` selection, rejected combinations, or DyntraLB/balance/recompute/profiling-chunk scheduling |
| PD disaggregation and KV transfer | [Workflow: Prefill-Decode Disaggregation and KV Transfer Connectors](workflows/pd-disaggregation-and-kv-transfer.md) | Connector registration, handshake metadata, kv_producer vs kv_consumer roles, or load-failure policy |
| KV offloading and tiering | [Workflow: KV Offloading, Tiering, and KV Store](workflows/kv-offload-and-store.md) | CPU offload specs, simple/recompute offload connectors, tiering, Ascend KV store, or sparse KV offload |
| Weight hot reload and sleep mode | [Workflow: Weight Transfer, Hot Reload, and Sleep/Wake](workflows/weight-update-and-sleep-mode.md) | Replacing weights without a restart, HCCL/NPU-IPC transfer engines, or freeing and restoring device memory |

## Shortest reading orders

Four sequences cover most first visits. Each is deliberately short; follow links only when a step raises a question.

- **New contributor, no specific task** — [System Architecture Overview](architecture/overview.md) → [Plugin Registration and Startup Sequence](workflows/plugin-bootstrap.md) → [Patching Architecture](architecture/patching-architecture.md) → [Test Architecture](testing/test-architecture.md). After that, the task tables above.
- **Serving-path performance work** — [request execution](workflows/request-execution.md) → [attention backends](concepts/attention-backends.md) → [MoE execution](concepts/moe-execution.md) → [graph mode](concepts/graph-mode-and-compilation.md) → [performance tuning](operations/performance-tuning.md).
- **Memory / KV-cache work** — [KV cache and block layout](concepts/kv-cache-and-block-layout.md) → [KV cache initialization workflow](workflows/kv-cache-initialization.md) → [KV offload](workflows/kv-offload-and-store.md).
- **Adding a model or a patch** — [model registry](integrations/model-registry-and-models.md) → [upstream interfaces](integrations/upstream-vllm-interfaces.md) → [patching architecture](architecture/patching-architecture.md), then write the catalog entry that `patch/__init__.py` requires.

## Ground rules that change how you read the code

A handful of conventions recur on every page; knowing them prevents most confusion.

1. **Platform hooks return dotted path strings, never classes.** `get_attn_backend_cls`, `get_compile_backend`, `get_pass_manager_cls`, `get_static_graph_wrapper_cls`, `get_device_communicator_cls` and `get_punica_wrapper` all answer vLLM with strings such as `"vllm_ascend.compilation.acl_graph.ACLGraphWrapper"` ([`platform.py`](../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L166-L201), [lines 226-267](../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L226-L267)). This keeps `vllm_ascend.platform` importable during vLLM's own bootstrap.
2. **Two patch tiers, two moments.** `patch/platform/` installs before any worker starts, via `adapt_patch(is_global_patch=True)`; `patch/worker/` installs inside each worker's `__init__`, via `adapt_patch()` ([`patch/__init__.py`](../vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py#L17-L27), [`utils.py`](../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L547-L551), [`worker/worker.py`](../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L144-L148)). Scheduler-visible fixes must be in the platform tier; tensor- and stream-touching fixes must be in the worker tier.
3. **`check_and_update_config` is ordered, and the order matters.** It is ten commented steps — logging, validators, quant auto-detect, incompatible-config repair, `init_ascend_config`, compilation modes, compile backend, worker/scheduler selection, SFA/DCP/KV/SP validation, allocator env ([`platform.py`](../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L442-L497)).
4. **The same `vllm_config` object is corrected once and reinterpreted per process.** The platform writes decisions *back into* `additional_config` and `vllm_config` (worker class, scheduler class, compilation modes, `custom_ops`), and each worker re-initializes `AscendConfig` from it ([`platform.py`](../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L1227-L1242), [`worker/worker.py`](../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L144-L157)).
5. **Every new environment variable goes through `vllm_ascend/envs.py`**, named `VLLM_ASCEND_*`, with a documented default and valid range ([`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md#L40-L73), [`envs.py`](../vllm_ascend/envs.py#L38-L92)).
6. **A new behaviour in `model_runner` is a reviewed decision**, not a default: the guideline is to ask "why can't this be a patch?" ([`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md#L252-L267)).

## Validate your change

New functionality needs tests: unit tests in `tests/ut/`, e2e in `tests/e2e/`, benchmarks in `tests/e2e/nightly/` ([`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md#L78-L107)). The unit tier runs on CPU with `torch_npu` mocked by the conftest boot shim, so a UT that implicitly needs a device fails by construction ([`tests/ut/conftest.py`](../tests/ut/conftest.py#L18-L27)).

```bash
# unit tests — no NPU required
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 pytest -sv tests/ut
pytest -sv tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py::test_prepare_inputs

# NPU-specific e2e (requires Ascend hardware)
pytest -sv tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/aclgraph/test_aclgraph_accuracy.py::test_default_full_and_piecewise_res_consistency

# lint + format gate (required for all file types, including Markdown)
bash format.sh ci
```

CI does not run everything on every PR: selection and runner partitioning are driven by [`test_config.yaml`](../.github/workflows/scripts/test_config.yaml#L1-L38) plus the coverage/AST selector described in [CI Workflows and Selective Test Execution](testing/ci-and-test-selection.md). If a test you need did not run, that page explains why.

## Where this wiki stops

This wiki documents the source tree. Installation prerequisites, the supported-model matrix, feature availability per hardware family, and release policy live in the official documentation indexed by [`docs/source/llms.txt`](../docs/source/llms.txt); the top-level [`README.md`](../README.md) lists the supported hardware families (Atlas A2/A3 series, Atlas 300I Duo as experimental) and the pinned CANN/PyTorch/vLLM versions. Contributor workflow, commit conventions and review checklists are in [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) and [`docs/source/developer_guide/index.md`](../docs/source/developer_guide/index.md).

nodes.title: CI Workflows and Selective Test Execution
nodes.description: How the vllm-ascend CI control plane decides which tests run - the coverage/AST selector that recommends tests, the routing pass that maps them to runner labels and load-balanced partitions, the A3 560T accuracy invariant, and the workflow families that consume the result on PR, nightly, weekly, and scheduled builds.
nodes.body:
# CI Workflows and Selective Test Execution

<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [../../.github/workflows] file "../../.github/workflows" does not exist. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
Everything the project runs on CI lives under [`.github/workflows/`](../../.github/workflows). That directory is not a flat pile of jobs: it is a small control plane with two responsibilities that are easy to confuse.

1. **Selection** — decide *which* test targets a change requires.
2. **Scheduling** — decide *where* each of those targets runs, on which physical machine class, and how the work is split.

Those two jobs are performed by different programs, with different inputs, and the boundary between them is the single most important thing to understand before changing CI. `.github/workflows/scripts/test_selector.py` is the selector; `.github/workflows/scripts/select_tests.py` is the router and is the only producer of the matrix that workflows actually consume. The curated lists, skip lists, accuracy pins, and timing estimates all live in routing configuration next to the router, not in the selector.

## The two-stage model

The selector never emits runner labels, and the router never looks at source diffs. A PR run is a pipeline of two independent decisions with a text file in between.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    LBL["PR label: ready-precise, ready-all, main2main, ready-a5"] --> DEC["select-tests: decide mode"]
    DIFF["PR diff via GitHub API"] --> SEL["test_selector.py: coverage plus AST match"]
    MAP["test_case_map.json and coverage.tar from OBS"] --> SEL
    EXTRA["extra_recommended_tests.yaml from OBS"] --> SEL
    SEL --> REC["recommended_pytest_paths.txt"]
    REC --> DEC
    DEC -->|recommended| ROUTE["select_tests.py --test-list-file --skip-cpu-ut"]
    DEC -->|all| ROUTEALL["select_tests.py --all-tests --skip-cpu-ut"]
    ROUTE --> GROUPS["test_groups JSON, has_tests, csrc_cache_target_ids"]
    ROUTEALL --> GROUPS
    GROUPS --> CACHE["prepare-csrc-cache: _ensure_csrc_cache.yaml"]
    GROUPS --> MATRIX["run-selected-tests: _selected_tests.yaml matrix"]
    MATRIX --> GATE["ci-gate: single required status check"]
```

*Two decisions, one handoff: the selector recommends pytest targets as text, the router turns them into runner-labelled matrix groups.*

**Stage 1 — recommendation.** `test_selector.py` loads a prebuilt `test_case_map.json` (test case → covered files and lines) plus the matching `coverage.tar` package from the OBS bucket `vllm-ascend` under `ci/precision-test/`, fetches the PR diff through the GitHub API, and selects affected tests with a cascading granularity: line-level intersection, then function-level (via AST parsing of the changed file), then file-level. Changed test files are added unconditionally, deleted test files are removed, and a diff that touches `csrc/` collapses the result to the full suite. The output is a plain newline-separated list, `recommended_pytest_paths.txt`. Before routing, `merge_extra_recommended_tests.py` appends entries from an `extra_recommended_tests.yaml` object on OBS — the mechanism by which newly merged test files become recommendable before the next coverage rebuild.

**Stage 2 — routing.** `select_tests.py` accepts exactly one of four mutually exclusive input modes (`--test-list-file`, `--explicit-e2e-tests`, `--all-tests`, `--curated`) and always produces the same output shape: `test_groups` (a JSON array of matrix groups), `has_tests`, `csrc_cache_target_ids`, and `matched_modules`. Each group carries `runner`, `image_tag`, `npu_type`, `num_npus`, `partition_name`, `partition` (like `2-4`), `tests`, and optionally `csrc_cache_target`.

| Stage | Program | Input | Output | Knows about hardware? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Recommend | `test_selector.py` | PR diff, `test_case_map.json`, `coverage.tar` | `recommended_pytest_paths.txt` | No |
| Route | `select_tests.py` | test list / explicit paths / `--all-tests` / curated suite name | `test_groups` matrix JSON | Yes — runner labels and partitions |

The same router is reused verbatim by every caller that needs a matrix: PR selection, the `/e2e` slash command, the full-suite schedules, and the coverage producer. That is why a routing bug is never local to one workflow.

### The routing pass in detail

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    IN["input mode: test-list-file, explicit-e2e-tests, all-tests, curated"] --> COLLECT["collect targets as individual files"]
    COLLECT --> ROUTE["route each file through runner_mapping regex to a logical partition"]
    ROUTE --> DEDUP["dedup: drop nodeids whose bare file is already selected"]
    DEDUP --> SKIP["remove skip_tests entries"]
    SKIP --> PIN["if any accuracy test selected or --all-tests: swap A3 partitions to 560T labels"]
    PIN --> OVR["apply --runner-label-override if given"]
    OVR --> PART["partition: resolve each logical key to an exact runner_label and split groups"]
    PART --> OUT["write test_groups, has_tests, csrc_cache_target_ids, matched_modules"]
```

*Inside `select_tests.py`: collection routes by regex, then dedup, skip filtering, the 560T pin, the optional label override, and finally time-balanced partitioning.*

`runner_mapping` in `test_config.yaml` maps a regex to a logical partition key with a `default` and an optional `310p` variant for files whose basename contains `_310p`; patterns are sorted longest-first so the most specific pattern wins. The `partition` section then binds each logical key to an exact label from `runner_label.json` and a `count` — the number of load-balanced groups to create for that bucket. Loading is validated eagerly: a partition referencing an unknown runner label, or a `runner_mapping` entry pointing at an undefined partition, raises `ValueError` and kills the job rather than producing a matrix that silently schedules nowhere.

`runner_label.json` is the hardware table: `chip` (`a2`/`a3`/`310p`/`a5`/`cpu`), `npu_num`, `image_tag`, and `csrc_cache_target`. Those fields travel into every matrix group, so the label a partition names also decides the container image the job runs in and which CPU-side csrc cache must exist before the job starts.

## Invariant: accuracy tests pin A3 to the dedicated 560T pool

This is the least obvious scheduling rule in the repository, and it is a correctness rule, not a performance one.

The generic A3 labels `linux-aarch64-a3-2`, `-4`, and `-8` are **mixed pools** of 560T and 752T machines: scheduling on them picks a machine class at random per job. Accuracy tests must not land on 752T hardware. So `select_tests.py` keeps a hard-coded mapping and applies it conditionally:

```text
linux-aarch64-a3-2  ->  linux-aarch64-a3-800i-2
linux-aarch64-a3-4  ->  linux-aarch64-a3-800i-4
linux-aarch64-a3-8  ->  linux-aarch64-a3-800i-8
```

The trigger is `_has_accuracy_tests()`: if **any** selected target's file path appears in `accuracy_tests` in `test_config.yaml`, the whole run's partition table is rewritten through `_prefer_560t_partitions()`, keeping each partition's group count (the 800i partitions declare the same counts). The same rewrite happens unconditionally for `--all-tests`, because a full-suite run necessarily contains accuracy tests.

Two consequences matter operationally:

- **Allocation changes with test content.** Adding a file to `accuracy_tests` changes which physical machine class an entire PR run consumes — not just that file's partition. Reviewing an `accuracy_tests` edit is reviewing hardware allocation.
- **752T machines are never started for accuracy coverage.** That is the stated purpose of the rule: an accuracy-bearing run must not boot 752T runners at all, so the reroute happens before partitions resolve to runners rather than as a retry after a failure.

`accuracy_tests` entries must be file paths; nodeid entries are rejected at load time, because the pin is evaluated per selected file.

## Load balancing and `estimated_times.yaml`

Splitting a partition's tests into `count` groups uses `_partition_tests()`: sort targets descending by estimated duration, then greedily assign each to the currently lightest bucket (longest-processing-time first). The per-file estimate comes from `estimated_times.yaml`, looked up at **file** granularity only — any `::nodeid` suffix is stripped, and unlisted files default to 600 s. Nodeid-level entries are not supported and `update_estimated_times.py` actively drops them.

`estimated_times.yaml` is deliberately a separate file from `test_config.yaml`, and the PR paths-filter omits it from the `ci_pipeline` category on purpose: timing values only affect load-balanced partitioning, never which tests are recommended, so a timing-only PR keeps its `ready-precise` status instead of escalating to the full suite.

The file is not hand-maintained in the long run. `schedule_e2e_test.yaml` with `update_est_times` enabled asks `_selected_tests.yaml` to upload `timing-data-*` artifacts, then `update_estimated_times.py` takes the **median** elapsed time per test, applies a 10 % safety buffer, rounds to the nearest 10 s, rewrites the `estimated_times:` section, and opens a PR titled `[CI] Auto-update estimated test times in estimated_times.yaml`.

Practically: when you add or retime an E2E test, add an entry. A new test without an estimate is not broken, but it is scheduled as if it took ten minutes and skews every partition it joins.

## What runs where: workflow families

The workflows split into a handful of families with distinct triggers and distinct artifacts. "Artifact" here means the durable state a family leaves behind, whether a GitHub Actions artifact, an OBS object, or a required status check.

| Family | Entry points | Trigger | Artifact / state |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR gate | `pr_test.yaml` | `pull_request` opened / synchronize / reopened / labeled on `main`, `*-dev`, `releases/v*` | Required check `ci-gate`; `test_groups` between jobs |
| PR runner | `_selected_tests.yaml`, `_selected_tests_upstream.yaml` | called by PR and slash-command workflows | `selected-test-logs-*`, `selected-test-coverage-*`, `timing-data-*` |
| Slash commands | `slash_command_dispatch.yml` + `pr_e2e_command.yml`, `pr_rerun_command.yml`, `pr_cancel_command.yml`, `pr_nightly_command.yml`, `pr_cherry_pick_command.yml`, `pr_revert_command.yml` | `issue_comment` → `repository_dispatch` | Dispatched runs; PR comments with results |
| Nightly per hardware | `schedule_nightly_test_{a2,a3,a3_560t,a5,310p}.yaml` with `_e2e_nightly_single_node.yaml`, `_e2e_nightly_single_node_560t.yaml`, `_e2e_nightly_single_node_models.yaml`, `_e2e_nightly_multi_node.yaml`, `_nightly_wait_for_pods_ready.yaml` | `workflow_dispatch` only (from `/nightly`) | `nightly-test-benchmark-results-*`, merged `nightly-a3.zip`; `good_table.csv` cache |
| Weekly per hardware | `schedule_weekly_test_{a2,a3,a3_560t,310p}.yaml` | cron `0 2 * * 0` (Sundays 10:00 Beijing) | Same benchmark artifacts under the `weekly` good-table namespace |
| main2main | `schedule_main2main.yaml` | cron `0 14 * * *` + dispatch | Adaptation commits/branch, `main2main-workspace` artifact, PR |
| Upstream E2E | `schedule_e2e_upstream_test.yaml`, `_selected_tests_upstream.yaml` | cron Sunday 08:00 for the schedule; call for the PR job | Results of vLLM's own test suite against the built wheel |
| Full suite and coverage | `schedule_e2e_test.yaml`, `schedule_test_coverage.yaml` | `workflow_dispatch` | `coverage.tar` + `test_case_map.json` on OBS; updated `estimated_times.yaml` PR |
| Image builds | `nightly_image_build.yaml`, `_nightly_image_build.yaml`, `schedule_image_build_and_push.yaml`, `schedule_lint_image_build.yaml`, `schedule_release_code_and_wheel.yml` | schedule / tag push / `image-build` label / dispatch | `nightly-ci-<branch>-<chip>` images, lint image, release images and wheel |
| csrc cache | `push_build_csrc_cache.yaml`, `_build_csrc_cache.yaml`, `_ensure_csrc_cache.yaml`, `push_build_precommit_cache.yaml` | push to `main` on csrc inputs, plus `workflow_call` | CPU-built kernel cache keyed by arch + image tag + csrc hash |
| Docs | `schedule_doc_translate.yaml`, `schedule_doc_linkcheck.yaml`, `schedule_doctest.yaml` | cron every 3 days / Sunday / PR path filter + dispatch | Translation PRs, link-check report, doctest jobs |
| Housekeeping | `bot_*.yaml`, `schedule_stale_manage.yaml`, `labeled_download_model_dataset.yaml`, `pr_supplement_new_tests.yaml`, `openwiki-update.yml` | various | Issue/label maintenance, extra-test-list updates, wiki refresh |

Two asymmetries are worth stating explicitly because they trip people up. First, the *nightly* workflows have **no cron trigger** — they are `workflow_dispatch` entry points that `/nightly` fires with `skip_build_image=true`; the only cron cadence in that area belongs to the weekly workflows. Second, the coverage producer (`schedule_test_coverage.yaml`) is manual dispatch only; there is no scheduled coverage rebuild, so the selector's data ages until someone runs it.

### Nightly and weekly mechanics

`schedule_nightly_test_a3.yaml` and its siblings do not hardcode test cases. They read `.github/workflows/configs/nightly_config.yaml` through `resolve_nightly_tests.py --mode=matrix`, extracting per-family lists (`a3.multi_node.test_config`, `a3.double_node.test_config`, `a3.single_node.test_config`, `a3.multi_card.test_config`) into job outputs, then fan out with `_e2e_nightly_single_node.yaml` / `_e2e_nightly_multi_node.yaml`. Adding a nightly case is appending a `- name:` entry under the right `soc`/section; `/nightly <name>` can exercise an unmerged entry because the dispatcher resolves names against the PR's own copy of the config.

Weekly workflows reuse the same reusable workflows and config family, differing in cron trigger and in passing `test_frequency: weekly`, which selects both the `good_table.csv` namespace and the commit-age threshold used by the AOP failure-triage path. On success the single-node workflow appends to that good table, and failures can feed a bisect flow started from a known-good commit.

The upstream family is a different path entirely: `_selected_tests_upstream.yaml` does not consume `test_groups` routing semantics beyond the matrix, and `schedule_e2e_upstream_test.yaml` runs vLLM's *own* `tests/` through `run_suite.py` against suites declared in `upstream_config.yaml` (`e2e-upstream_pr`, `e2e-upstream_singlecard`, `e2e-upstream_a2_*`, `e2e-upstream_online_*`), with the same greedy time-balanced partitioning but its own `estimated_time` values and its own `is_skipped` flags.

## The PR gate: labels, modes, and the `ci-gate` contract

`pr_test.yaml` is the workflow developers interact with, and its job graph encodes the policy:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PC["pre-commit: lint, mypy, gitleaks, secret scan, paths filter"] --> UT["cpu-ut: tests/ut on the CPU runner"]
    UT --> REC["recommend-tests: only under ready-precise"]
    UT --> SEL["select-tests: mode decision + routing + coverage config validation"]
    REC --> SEL
    SEL --> CACHE["prepare-csrc-cache"]
    SEL --> A5["select A5 curated suite"]
    CACHE --> RUN["run-selected-tests: matrix over vLLM versions"]
    CACHE --> UP["run-selected-tests-upstream: ready-precise only"]
    A5 --> RUNA5["run-selected-tests-a5: ready-a5 only"]
    RUN --> GATE["ci-gate"]
    RUNA5 --> GATE
    PC --> GATE
    UT --> GATE
```

*The PR job graph: pre-commit and cpu-ut always run; test execution requires a run-enabling label; `ci-gate` condenses everything into one stable required check.*

Mode selection in the `select-tests` job is a strict precedence, not a fallback chain:

| Condition | Mode | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `main2main` label | `all` | Full suite, executed once per vLLM version in the matrix |
| `ready-all` label | `all` | Full suite |
| `ci_pipeline` paths changed | `all` | Full suite, even if `ready-precise` was set |
| `ready-precise` label | `recommended`, or `none` if the recommendation is empty | Routed recommendation |
| none of the above | job skipped | `ci-gate` decides |

Two behaviors here are deliberate and easy to break. A `ready-precise` run whose recommendation step failed **does not** fall back to the full suite; it fails, because silently running everything would hide a broken selector. And a PR that touches the CI pipeline files listed in the `ci_pipeline` paths-filter is escalated to `all`, because the recommendation produced by a modified selector can no longer be trusted.

`ci-gate` is the piece to wire branch protection to. It asserts pre-commit and cpu-ut succeeded, that `has_tests` and `has_tests_a5` are explicitly `true`/`false` (a missing output is an error, never "no tests"), and that a run whose selection was skipped happened because neither `src` nor `ci_pipeline` paths changed. When something is wrong it prints the remediation — which label to add — rather than just failing.

The `main2main` label additionally widens the vLLM version matrix: `pre-commit` emits `vllm_versions` containing both the commit in `.github/vllm-main-verified.commit` and the tag in `.github/vllm-release-tag.commit`, so the same `test_groups` execute against both.

### Snapshotting the base

`select-tests` resolves the moving base branch to one immutable `base_sha` and passes it to the cache producer and every test job, which rebase onto that exact SHA. This keeps selection, cache keying, and test execution on the same tree when the base branch advances mid-run. The same step refuses to proceed if the CSRC cache workflows or `csrc_cache_targets.json` changed on the base branch since the event was created, telling the author to rebase — because pairing an old workflow graph with new cache helpers can produce incompatible keys.

## Curation, skipping, and the other fixed lists

Four kinds of list live in `test_config.yaml` and adjacent files. They are not interchangeable, and picking the wrong one is a common review finding.

| List | Location | Semantics | Reached by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `curated_tests` | `test_config.yaml` | Named suites (`kvpp`, `a5`) run explicitly by name | `select_tests.py --curated <name>` |
| `skip_tests` | `test_config.yaml` | Whole files removed from **every** selection mode after collection | automatic, all modes |
| `accuracy_tests` | `test_config.yaml` | Files whose selection triggers the 560T reroute | automatic, all modes |
| `runner_mapping` / `partition` | `test_config.yaml` | Routing metadata: regex → logical key → label + group count | automatic, all modes |
| `main2main_tests.json` | `scripts/` | Case list for the main2main agent flow | `schedule_main2main.yaml` |
| nightly / weekly matrices | `configs/` | Per-hardware test case definitions | `resolve_nightly_tests.py` |
| upstream suites | `scripts/upstream_config.yaml` | vLLM-owned test suites | `run_suite.py` |

`skip_tests` exists specifically for tests where every case is unconditionally skipped: the file is registered instead of paying for a runner slot that executes nothing. It is applied *after* directory expansion, so a skipped file is never scheduled in any mode, and the entries carry the reason and the condition for returning the file to rotation. Do not use it to silence a flaky test that still has live cases — that is what markers are for.

`curated_tests` serves a different purpose: suites that are meaningful on specific hardware and useful outside the directory convention. The `a5` suite is scheduled on PRs whose diff touches source paths, routed with `--runner-label-override linux-aarch64-a5-4`, and then only executed when the PR carries `ready-a5`. The `kvpp` suite is a single-file suite with no dedicated label.

`--skip-cpu-ut` is the last routing nuance. On the PR path, `tests/ut` runs in the dedicated `cpu-ut` job (which never goes through `select_tests.py`), so the scheduling path passes `--skip-cpu-ut` to drop UT targets from every mode and avoid reserving a runner twice. The coverage producer deliberately does **not** pass it, because that run must collect CPU UT coverage.

## Validation: the coverage configuration gate

`select-tests` runs `.github/workflows/scripts/coverage.py` before it selects anything when the recommendation path is used. The script is a static audit of the routing configuration and fails the job on:

- paths referenced in `curated_tests`, `skip_tests`, or `accuracy_tests` that do not exist;
- E2E or NPU-routed UT files with no `estimated_times` entry, and CPU UT files that *do* have one;
- invalid or never-matching `runner_mapping` patterns, patterns missing a `default`;
- `partition` keys referenced by routing but undefined, malformed keys, or keys no test routes to;
- `@pytest.mark.e2e_coverage` marker values outside the taxonomy defined in `tests/e2e/coverage_taxonomy.py`.

Unmarked (but existing) E2E tests are reported as a warning during the migration, while an out-of-taxonomy marker value is a hard failure. Because this gate runs inside `select-tests`, a misconfigured list fails the PR that introduced it rather than a later scheduled run.

## Execution and the coverage feedback loop

Once the matrix exists, `_selected_tests.yaml` fans `test_groups` into one job per group, keyed by the group's own `runner` and container `image_tag`. Each job restores or builds the csrc cache, then calls `run_selected_tests.sh`, which runs each target as a separate `pytest` invocation in its own process group (so orphaned `EngineCore`/HCCL workers cannot retain NPU memory or the log pipe), writes a `test_timing_data.json`, and — in coverage mode — gives each target its own `covdata` directory plus a `FAILED` sentinel when the target fails.

That sentinel is what makes the selector's data trustworthy across failures. `assemble_coverage.py` treats a target as available only when `covdata/` exists, is non-empty, and carries no `FAILED` sentinel; missing or failed keys are backfilled from the historical `coverage.tar` on OBS instead of shipping a partial run's data. The rebuilt `test_case_map.json` and new `coverage.tar` are then uploaded back to OBS, closing the loop: coverage produced by a full-suite run is what the next PR's recommendation reads.

Selection also feeds the build cache. The union of `csrc_cache_target` values implied by the chosen runner labels — plus a forced `a2-arm64-ubuntu` — becomes `csrc_cache_target_ids`, which drives `_ensure_csrc_cache.yaml` before any test job starts. Changing a partition's `runner_label` therefore changes which CPU-side kernel caches get produced, not just which machine runs the tests.

## Changing CI safely

Touching this directory is a code change with hardware consequences, and should be reviewed as such:

- **`ci_pipeline` files escalate any PR to `ready-all`.** That list covers `pr_test.yaml`, `_selected_tests.yaml`, `_selected_tests_upstream.yaml`, the csrc cache workflows and their metadata, `select_tests.py`, `test_selector.py`, `run_selected_tests.sh`, `test_config.yaml`, `runner_label.json`, and `coverage.py`. If you change the selector and leave the paths filter stale, the PR will validate the *old* logic — update both together.
- **`runner_label.json` and `partition` are the hardware allocation table.** A wrong label sends tests to the wrong silicon; a wrong `count` changes how many machines a bucket claims; `csrc_cache_target` changes cache production; `image_tag` changes the container.
- **`estimated_times.yaml` keeps PR scheduling stable.** It is intentionally outside `ci_pipeline`, so timing edits do not trigger a full-suite run — which also means nobody will catch an implausible estimate for you. Keep it file-level and roughly accurate; the automation will refine it on the next timed full run.
- **Allocation invariants are silent when broken.** Dropping a file from `accuracy_tests` does not fail anything; it just lets accuracy coverage land on randomly-chosen 752T hardware.
- **Validate before pushing.** `python3 .github/workflows/scripts/coverage.py` from the repository root runs the same audit CI runs, and the router can be exercised locally without any hardware:

```bash
# What would this file route to?
python3 .github/workflows/scripts/select_tests.py \
  --explicit-e2e-tests tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_qwen3_0_6b.py

# Full-suite matrix, i.e. the ready-all / coverage shape
python3 .github/workflows/scripts/select_tests.py --all-tests

# A curated suite
python3 .github/workflows/scripts/select_tests.py --curated a5 \
  --runner-label-override linux-aarch64-a5-4
```

Both commands print a "Selective Test Scope Summary" to stderr listing every partition, its runner, and its per-group partition index, which is usually enough to see an unintended reroute before a full CI run.

## Related

- [NPUPlatform and Hardware Capability Profiles](../architecture/platform-and-hardware-profiles.md) — what the A2/A3/310P/A5 labels actually select.
- [Upstream vLLM Interfaces](../integrations/upstream-vllm-interfaces.md) — the pinned `vllm-main-verified` / release-tag refs that the `main2main` matrix and every test job check out.
- [Build and Install](../operations/build-and-install.md) — the csrc build inputs that key the cache consumed before tests run.
- [Test Architecture](./test-architecture.md) — how the tests the selector chooses are organized and written.

nodes.title: Test Architecture: Unit Tests, E2E Suites, and CPU Mocking
nodes.body:
# Test Architecture: Unit Tests, E2E Suites, and CPU Mocking

The repository splits verification into two tiers with different physics, not just different granularity.

| Tier | Location | Runs on | What it asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit tests (UT) | `tests/ut/` | Any CPU runner, no NPU | Logic, arithmetic, layout, error paths of `vllm_ascend` modules, with every device call stubbed |
| E2E / system tests (ST) | `tests/e2e/` | Real Ascend hardware | End-to-end model serving: outputs, logprobs, precision deltas, distributed topology behavior |

The split is load-bearing: because every UT runs on a CPU-only runner, the unit tier is where type/layout/control-flow bugs are caught cheaply, and the E2E tier is where numerics and multi-card behavior are proven. Which targets run on which machine is a separate concern, covered in [CI Workflows and Selective Test Execution](./ci-and-test-selection.md); this page is about how the tests themselves are built.

## The unit-test contract: CPU-only, mocks by default

`tests/ut/conftest.py` opens with the contract in its own docstring: **NPU vs CPU routing is decided by directory convention, not decorators**, all UTs run on CPU, and 310P-specific tests live in `tests/ut/_310p/` but also run on CPU through mocks. Because the router sends the entire `tests/ut` tree to the CPU partition unconditionally, a UT that implicitly needs a device is a CI failure by construction, not a hardware misconfiguration.

Local invocation is therefore plain pytest:

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 pytest -sv tests/ut
pytest -sv tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py::TestPrepareAndFinalize::test_mc2_prepare_finalize
```

### The bootstrap sequence

`tests/ut/conftest.py` is not a fixture file; it is a boot shim that fabricates an Ascend-shaped Python environment before `vllm_ascend` is imported for the first time.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant PC as pytest conftest import
    participant SM as sys.modules
    participant T as torch
    participant TN as torch_npu
    participant VA as vllm_ascend
    PC->>PC: subprocess npu-smi info as probe only
    alt no NPU detected
        PC->>SM: stub triton.runtime, torch_npu, torch_npu._C, op_plugin.atb, profiler, acl.rt, mooncake.engine
        PC->>T: import torch, rename_privateuse1_backend("npu")
        PC->>T: torch.npu = MagicMock, current_device returns cpu, Stream = _NpuStreamStub
    end
    PC->>SM: setdefault fake vllm_ascend._build_info with __device_type__
    PC->>VA: import utils, call adapt_patch x2 and register_ascend_customop
    PC->>VA: enable_custom_op, install golden npu_copy_and_expand_eagle_inputs stub
    PC->>SM: re-sync torch.npu, seed dozens of NPU op mocks
    PC->>SM: drop stale MagicMock entries under vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer
```

*The conftest builds a fake NPU world in a fixed order, then hands control to the real package.*

Four ordering constraints make this work, and every one of them has a comment explaining why:

- **`torch` must not be imported before the `torch_npu` stubs exist.** The file says so explicitly: importing torch early in a CPU environment produces a circular import.
- **`torch.npu.current_device` returns the string `"cpu"`, not an ordinal.** Returning an int makes `torch.empty(device=...)` treat it as a CUDA/NPU device id and break tensor allocation, so the stub hands back a device string that the CPU build accepts.
- **`torch.npu` is assigned as an attribute *and* registered in `sys.modules`**, because some code paths do `import torch.npu` rather than attribute access.
- **The stub is re-synced after `adapt_patch()` and `enable_custom_op()`**, so `@patch("torch.npu.*")` on a test hits the same object production code resolves through `torch.npu`.

The stubs are not decorative — they reproduce specific third-party surfaces that `vllm_ascend` imports at module scope: `torch_npu.op_plugin.atb._atb_ops._register_atb_extensions` (imported by worker code), `torch_npu.profiler.dynamic_profile` plus seeded enum members (`ExportType.Text`, `ProfilerLevel.Level1`, `AiCMetrics.PipeUtilization`, `ProfilerActivity.CPU/NPU`) so `@patch(..., create=False)` and plain attribute reads both succeed, `acl.rt.memcpy`, `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine`, and `triton.runtime.driver.active.utils.get_device_properties` with a plausible `num_aic`/`num_vectorcore`. Enum-like values are set to *real* strings rather than `MagicMock` so production branches that compare against them take the intended path; numeric dtype ids (`float4_e2m1fn_x2`, `hifloat8`, `float8_e8m0fnu`) are hardcoded to their real values because code compares against them.

Two fakes matter beyond `torch_npu`:

- **`vllm_ascend._build_info`** is normally written by `setup.py`'s `gen_build_info()` from `SOC_VERSION` and contains exactly one fact, `__device_type__`. On CPU there is no build, so the conftest installs a module object with `__device_type__ = "A2"` via `sys.modules.setdefault`. This is what lets `get_device_config()`, the hardware-profile layer, and every capability check import cleanly — and where a test needs a different chip it monkeypatches that attribute directly, as `tests/ut/device/test_device_config.py` does for `A3`, `A2`, and legacy `__soc_version__` fallback.
- **Custom-op registration** runs for real (`register_ascend_customop()`, `adapt_patch()`, `adapt_patch(True)`, `enable_custom_op()`), so the patched upstream and the registered op namespace are the ones tests see. Where a compiled kernel cannot exist, a pure-Python reference is injected into `torch.ops._C_ascend` — `npu_copy_and_expand_eagle_inputs` is installed from `tests/ut/helpers/golden_copy_and_expand.py`, a numpy implementation adapted from the NPU-only nightly op test, giving CPU tests a golden reference instead of a `MagicMock` that returns garbage.

### Autouse fixtures: the mutable global reset layer

Mocked device objects are stateless; production code is not. Three autouse fixtures in the same file protect tests from each other:

| Fixture | Resets | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `_clear_enable_sp_before_test` | `clear_enable_sp()` — the `lru_cache`s behind `enable_dsa_cp`, `enable_dsa_cp_full_o_proj`, `enable_pcp_o_proj_weight_sharding`, `_libc_getenv` | Config-derived cached booleans would otherwise leak a previous test's `parallel_config` into the next one |
| `_reset_stream_globals_before_test` | `utils._CURRENT_STREAM`, `utils._GLOBAL_STREAM`, `_SHARED_EXPERTS_CALCULATION_STREAM`, `moe_utils.COMM_STREAM` — before **and** after yield | `vllm_ascend.utils.current_stream()` memoizes the stream to avoid the expensive `torch.npu.current_stream()` call, so a cached stub from test A stays live in test B |
| `_mock_ascend_store_deps` | Patches `get_attention_compute_start_gate`, `reset_attention_compute_start_gate`, `AttentionComputeStartGate` — **only** when `"distributed/ascend_store/" in request.node.nodeid` | An earlier global `_mock_deps.py` mutation leaked into unrelated tests; narrowing by nodeid restored isolation |

The file also sweeps `sys.modules`: any entry under `vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.*` that is not a real `ModuleType` is deleted, because a helper module in `ascend_store/` used to replace real subpackages with `MagicMock` objects and break later imports. That helper still exists but is now opt-in: `tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/_mock_deps.py` must be imported explicitly at the top of a test file, before any `vllm_ascend`/`vllm` import.

### Base classes

`tests/ut/base.py` offers two bases for the same reason: re-apply the global setup per test. `TestBase` (unittest) calls `adapt_patch(True)`, `adapt_patch()`, `register_ascend_customop()` in `__init__`; `PytestBase` does the same from an autouse `setup` fixture, because pytest-mock and `parametrize` do not compose with `unittest.TestCase`. Choose `TestBase` for `self.assertEqual`-style tests, `PytestBase` when you need fixtures or parametrization.

### Where the representative tests live

Read a few well-chosen files rather than the tree; each is the canonical example for its subsystem.

| Subsystem | Representative tests | What they demonstrate |
|---|---|---|
| Ops / kernels | `tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py`, `tests/ut/ops/test_fused_moe.py`, `tests/ut/ops/test_token_dispatcher.py` | Mocked `FusedMoEConfig`/distributed groups with tensor assertions on padding, masks, and split/combine shapes |
| Attention | `tests/ut/attention/test_mla_v1.py`, `tests/ut/attention/utils.py` (`patch_distributed_groups`) | Building real `VllmConfig` objects and patching CP/DCP group sizes via decorator |
| Scheduler / core | `tests/ut/core/test_kvpp_cache_placement.py`, `tests/ut/core/test_recompute_scheduler.py` | Pure-arithmetic placement planning driven by `tests/ut/kvpp_utils.py` spec factories; ordering invariants |
| Worker / runner | `tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py`, `tests/ut/worker/test_pcp_manager_v2.py`, `tests/ut/_310p/test_model_runner_310p.py` | Heavy runner wiring with device calls mocked; 310P variants live under `_310p/` but run on CPU |
| Distributed | `tests/ut/distributed/test_parallel_state.py`, `tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/test_pool_worker.py` | `ParallelConfig` plus patched `torch.distributed` primitives; per-module mock harness for the KV pool |
| Spec decode | `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_eagle_proposer.py`, `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_mtp.py`, `tests/ut/spec_decode/test_step3p5_source_regression.py` | All-reduce row ownership in `compact_mtp_topk_indices`, plus AST/source-level regression guards |
| KV transfer / offload | `tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/test_kv_transfer_failures.py`, `tests/ut/kv_transfer/test_layerwise_multi_cache_spec.py`, `tests/ut/kv_offload/utils.py` | Failure-code accounting for failed blocks; real `VllmConfig` built against `tests/ut/_fake_weight` with `inspect_model_cls` patched |

`tests/ut/_fake_weight/` is the shared trick for config-level tests: a tiny `facebook/opt-125m`-shaped `config.json` with no weights, used wherever a `ModelConfig` must be constructible without downloading a checkpoint.

Two style notes that show up across the tree: **source-level regression tests** parse a production file with `ast` and assert on structure (used where the invariant is "the patch replaces this symbol", e.g. the Eagle ACL graph manager), and **placeholder tests** exist (`tests/ut/test_cpu_binding.py` is a single `pass`) as named slots for future coverage.

## The E2E harness

`tests/e2e/conftest.py` is the shared runtime for the entire ST tier. It is roughly 2000 lines, and it has three distinct responsibilities: build `LLM` objects in-process, launch `vllm serve`/proxy subprocesses for black-box HTTP tests, and keep NPU memory and process groups from leaking between tests.

At import time it calls `adapt_patch(True)` then `adapt_patch(False)` so both platform-level and worker-level patches are active inside pytest, and it registers one extra CLI option (`--msa-m3-sparse-backend`, `all`/`triton`/`torch_npu`) for the MiniMax M3 sparse-attention test.

Not every E2E test needs hardware. `tests/e2e/vllm_interface/test_vllm_pr_interface_compatibility.py` is a source-only analysis: it parses the checked-out vLLM PR and the installed vllm-ascend revision, resolves direct imports/overrides/calls, and fails only when an *introduced* break is found or the analysis cannot complete — it never imports either project and never touches an NPU.

### In-process runners

`VllmRunner` wraps `LLM` with sane test defaults (`max_model_len=1024`, `block_size=16`, `enable_chunked_prefill=True`, `trust_remote_code=True`) and normalizes every output shape into `(token_ids_including_prompt, text)` so comparisons are one expression. It exposes `generate`, `generate_w_logprobs`, `generate_greedy`, `generate_greedy_logprobs`, `classify`, `embed`, `encode`, `reward`, `score`. Its `__exit__` shuts down `llm_engine.engine_core`, deletes the model, calls `clear_ascend_config()` and `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()` — the order matters, because a live engine holds NPU memory and a stale Ascend config poisons the next `LLM`.

`VllmRunner` **refuses** `data_parallel_size > 1` and points at `DPVllmRunner`, which starts `data_parallel_size` `spawn` processes connected by `multiprocessing.Pipe`, each setting `VLLM_DP_RANK`/`VLLM_DP_SIZE`/`VLLM_DP_MASTER_IP`/`VLLM_DP_MASTER_PORT`, and dispatches a small command protocol (`generate`, `classify`, `embed`, `score`, …) with per-request index routing so shard results can be merged back into one answer.

`ModelCache` sits above `VllmRunner`: it keys a constructed runner by the MD5 of its sorted config dict, checks free NPU memory against `total * gpu_memory_utilization`, evicts and waits before creating a new engine, and is cleared by a session-scoped autouse fixture. The `vllm_runner` fixture is the ergonomic entry point and **requires** a `@pytest.mark.model(...)` marker — without it, it raises.

### Subprocess servers and disaggregation proxies

Black-box tests need real serving processes, so the harness defines a server class per topology. The serving classes descend from `RemoteOpenAIServer`, which starts `vllm serve`, waits for `/health` (default timeout 2800 s), exposes an OpenAI client with a dummy API key and 600 s timeout, and tears the whole process tree down with `psutil` (terminate → 60 s wait → kill, then children). `MooncakeLauncher` is the one exception: it is a plain context manager for a non-vLLM process, not a server subclass.

| Class | Topology | Key mechanics |
|---|---|---|
| `RemoteOpenAIServer` | One `vllm serve` | Auto port via `get_open_port`, injects `--seed`/`--hf-overrides` JSON, forces `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` because the parent may already have initialized NPU |
| `RemotePDServer` | N prefill/decode servers | Requires explicit `--port` per serving arg list; computes each server's device span from `--tensor-parallel-size × --data-parallel-size[-local]` and allocates disjoint `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` ranges; relays each process's stdout/stderr under a `[PD_i]` prefix |
| `DisaggPDProxy` | Load-balancing proxy | Launches `examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py` with `--prefiller-hosts/--prefiller-ports/--decoder-hosts/--decoder-ports`, waits on `/healthcheck` |
| `RemoteEPDServer` | Encoder/prefill/decode | One server per arg list, `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<i>`, `_poll()` always returns `None` so readiness never aborts early; it also carries a `_delete_shm` helper that can remove the `--ec-transfer-config` `shared_storage_path` (defined but not wired into startup in the current code) |
| `DisaggEpdProxy` | EPD proxy | Launches `examples/disaggregated_encoder/disagg_epd_proxy.py`, parses `--port` out of the proxy args |
| `MooncakeLauncher` | KV pool master | Runs `mooncake_master` with eviction watermarks and metrics port after prefixing `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` with the Ascend mooncake path; kills the process group on exit |

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant T as test function
    participant PD as RemotePDServer
    participant PR as DisaggPDProxy
    participant P as vllm serve x N
    participant M as mooncake_master
    T->>M: MooncakeLauncher enter
    T->>PD: start server arg lists
    PD->>P: spawn with disjoint ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES
    PD->>PD: poll /health per port (always_check_nodes)
    T->>PR: DisaggPDProxy enter
    PR->>PR: spawn load_balance_proxy_server_example.py
    PR->>PR: poll /healthcheck
    T->>PR: POST /v1/completions through proxy
    T->>PR: exit, terminate process tree
    T->>PD: exit, terminate each server tree
```

*A disaggregated test drives the proxy, not the workers: the harness owns start ordering, readiness polling, and process-tree teardown.*

Two helpers make tests robust rather than flaky. `wait_until_npu_memory_free(target_free_percentage=0.5, max_wait_seconds=50)` decorates a test and, because polling NPU memory in the parent would initialize the device and break subsequent forks, spawns a **subprocess** that calls `torch.npu.mem_get_info()` until enough is free, raising `TimeoutError` on expiry. `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()` destroys model-parallel and distributed state, suppresses the `destroy_process_group` assertion, optionally shuts down Ray, and only touches the NPU cache when `torch.npu.is_initialized()` — deliberately avoiding device initialization in the main process.

### Assertion vocabulary

E2E assertions are about equivalence to a reference, and the helpers encode the tolerance policy:

- `tests/e2e/model_utils.py::check_outputs_equal` — exact token-id and string equality between two runs.
- `tests/e2e/pull_request/utils.py::compare_logprobs` — the default accuracy check. It runs the model once eager (baseline) and once in the configured compilation mode, generates 3 tokens per prompt, and requires: token 0 identical with logprob within `atol=0.0689`; decode tokens within `decode_atol` (default `2 * atol`), or — if they differ — the baseline token present in the compiled model's top-K with logprob within tolerance.
- `tests/e2e/utils.py::check_embeddings_close` — cosine similarity ≥ `1 - tol` (default `1e-3`) for pooling/embedding parity.
- `tests/e2e/utils.py::fork_new_process_for_each_test` — runs a test in a forked process group and `SIGTERM`s the group afterwards, for cases whose children would otherwise survive pytest (adapted from vLLM's own `tests/utils.py`).

## The `e2e_coverage` marker taxonomy

E2E tests carry a second, structured marker that describes *what the test covers*, not just what model it uses:

```python
@pytest.mark.e2e_coverage(
    arch="moe", feature="kvpp,chunked_prefill,prefix_caching,mtp",
    parallel="TP,EP", deploy="pd_mix", hardware="A3",
    quantization="W8A8", graph_mode="eager",
)
```

`tests/e2e/coverage_taxonomy.py` is the single source of truth: `ALLOWED_VALUES` defines exactly seven dimensions (`arch`, `feature`, `parallel`, `deploy`, `hardware`, `quantization`, `graph_mode`), `DIM_LABELS`/`DIM_ORDER` drive report rendering, `REQUIRED_DIMS` makes all seven keys mandatory (an empty string is allowed when a dimension does not apply, but the key must be present), and `MULTI_VALUE_DIMS` marks `feature` and `parallel` as comma-separated so `feature="lora,mtp"` is legal while each token must itself be in the allowed set. Adding a new value is one edit — append to the relevant set — and everything downstream picks it up.

Three consumers import that module so they cannot drift:

| Consumer | Role | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/e2e/conftest.py::pytest_collection_modifyitems` | Local, fast feedback at collection | Raises `pytest.CollectError` naming the nodeid and the offending values |
| `.github/workflows/scripts/coverage.py` | Static CI audit, invoked by the PR `select-tests` job (`python3 .github/workflows/scripts/coverage.py`) alongside routing checks | Adds marker warnings to `has_errors` and exits non-zero |
| `tests/e2e/generate_coverage_html.py` | AST-scans `tests/e2e/pull_request/**/test_*.py` and renders a self-contained `coverage.html` | Surfaces unmarked tests and taxonomy gaps as a report |

The enforcement asymmetry is deliberate and documented in both places: **an out-of-taxonomy value is a hard failure; a missing marker is only a warning**, because the migration to `e2e_coverage` is still in progress. `validate_coverage_marker` returns human-readable warnings (including a "did you mean" hint from substring matching) rather than raising, so each caller decides the severity.

`INVALID_COMBOS` deserves a note: it is where dimension combinations that are semantically impossible (a chip that cannot run a feature) are recorded. It is hand-maintained and currently holds only commented-out examples, so it affects **reporting only** — the coverage HTML excludes matching combinations from its zero-coverage enumeration — and never influences marker validation. Rules are partial mappings: a rule is skipped unless every dimension it names is present in the combination being tested.

The generator also infers card count from the directory (`one_card` → 1, `two_card` → 2, `four_card` → 4, `eight_card` → 8), which is why the `_card` directory convention is part of the marker story and not just routing. Both markers are registered in `pyproject.toml` (`e2e_model`, `e2e_coverage`).

### Nightly and weekly suites

`tests/e2e/nightly/` and `tests/e2e/weekly/` are shaped differently from `pull_request/`, and the difference is visible in the tests themselves:

- **Single-node ops** (`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/`, `multicard_ops_a3/`) are direct kernel-correctness tests against real NPUs. Their `conftest.py` calls `init_device_properties_triton()` and `enable_custom_op()` at import, and installs a watchdog: after **5** cases in one file each exceed **120 s**, the remaining cases in that file are `pytest.skip`ped, so a slow kernel cannot eat the whole nightly slot.
- **Single-node models** (`tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/models/`) are driven by YAML case configs rather than Python literals: `SingleNodeConfigLoader.from_yaml_cases()` reads the config named by `CONFIG_YAML_PATH`, and `test_single_node.py` picks `RemoteOpenAIServer` or `DisaggEpdProxy` based on that config, then runs completion/chat/vision/benchmark checks and posts results through `tests/e2e/nightly/scripts/result_postprocess.py`.
- **Multi-node** (`tests/e2e/nightly/multi_node/{internal_dp,external_dp}/`) builds cluster state from `NodeInfo` records: `DisaggregatedPrefillCfg` validates that prefiller and decoder indices are in range and disjoint, `DistEnvBuilder` derives `HCCL_IF_IP`/`HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME`/`MASTER_IP` from the node's IP and NIC, and `ProxyLauncher` starts the disaggregation proxy **only on the master node**, expanding `$VAR` placeholders in the server command from that env.

Which cases exist is data, not code: `.github/workflows/configs/nightly_config.yaml` and `weekly_config.yaml` enumerate per-SoC case names, and `resolve_nightly_tests.py` turns them into workflow matrices. Weekly suites reuse the same reusable workflows with a cron trigger (`0 2 * * 0`) and a different good-table namespace; the mechanics live in the [CI page](./ci-and-test-selection.md).

Two smaller families complete the picture. **Accuracy evals** in `tests/e2e/models/` are parameterized over YAML model configs (`--config`, `--config-list-file`, `--tp-size`, `--report-dir` from `tests/e2e/models/conftest.py`) and run `lm_eval`/ASR/reranker scoring, emitting a Markdown report per model from `report_template.md`. **Doctests** in `tests/e2e/doctests/` are shell-driven, not pytest-driven: `run_doctests.sh <quickstart|installation> <device|method>` extracts and executes the marked code blocks from the Quick Start and Installation docs, so the documentation is a tested artifact rather than prose that drifts.

## The benchmark harness

`benchmarks/` is a standalone performance harness, separate from both tiers: it is invoked from a prepared NPU environment (`bash benchmarks/scripts/run-performance-benchmarks.sh`) rather than from a pytest target, and it exists so a PR author can answer "did this regress?"

The methodology is fixed and documented: latency (32-token input, 128-token output, batch 8), throughput (200 ShareGPT prompts, dynamic batching), and serving (same prompts, average QPS of 1/4/16/inf with Poisson arrivals, measuring throughput plus TTFT/ITL/TPOT percentiles) — about 800 s per model on an Atlas 800I A2.

`run-performance-benchmarks.sh` is a thin jq-driven driver over three JSON case files:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    N["check_npus via npu-smi info -l"] --> D["ensure_sharegpt_downloaded"]
    D --> M["main: export VLLM_HOST_IP, VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE"]
    M --> S["run_serving_tests serving-tests.json"]
    M --> L["run_latency_tests latency-tests.json"]
    M --> T["run_throughput_tests throughput-tests.json"]
    S --> J["json2args: keys underscore to dash"]
    J --> Q["spawn api_server, wait_for_server, loop qps_list with vllm bench serve"]
    Q --> K["kill_npu_processes between cases"]
    L --> K
    T --> K
    K --> R["results/*.json"]
```

*One shell entry point, three case families, one JSON-per-case result file.*

Details that matter operationally: `json2args` converts `{"tensor_parallel_size": 1}` into `--tensor-parallel-size 1`, so the JSON keys *are* the CLI; test names must be prefixed `latency_`/`throughput_`/`serving_` or the run aborts; `TEST_SELECTOR` filters cases by regex; a serving case whose server and client `model` differ is skipped with a message; `kill_npu_processes` kills whatever holds port 8000, all `python3` and `VLLM` processes, and wipes `~/.config/vllm` between cases, because leaked workers silently corrupt the next measurement. `convert_json_to_markdown.py` then folds `results/*.json` into `benchmark_results.md` from `perf_result_template.md`, converting latency seconds to milliseconds and deriving `P10…P99`.

Use `"load_format": "dummy"` in the case JSON to build random weights instead of downloading a checkpoint — the README recommends it, and it is what makes the harness usable on a PR-sized time budget.

## What contributors owe the test tree

`AGENTS.md` states the expectation plainly under **Unit and System Tests**: all new functionality requires corresponding tests, unit tests live in `tests/ut/` covering core logic, edge cases, and error conditions, system tests live in `tests/e2e/` verifying end-to-end behavior and integration points, and nightly tests include benchmarks for NPU-specific code paths. The coverage guidelines are specific: new features must cover happy path **and** failure modes, and bug fixes must include a regression test for the bug — the review checklist repeats this as a checkbox for both `tests/ut/` and `tests/e2e/`.

Practically, that maps onto conventions rather than ceremony:

- **Mirror the source path.** `vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py` → `tests/ut/worker/test_worker.py`, prefixed `test_` — the documented convention, and the reason the router can treat the UT tree as a flat CPU partition.
- **Mock at the device boundary, not at your own module boundary.** If a test needs a device, the fix is a stub in `conftest.py` or a `@patch("torch_npu.<op>")`, not an `if npu_available` branch in the test.
- **Use the base classes when you depend on patched state.** `tests/ut/conftest.py` installs patches once per process; `TestBase`/`PytestBase` re-apply them around each test, which matters for tests that mutate patch state or run after a module that did. Plenty of files (`tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py`) are plain `unittest.TestCase` and work because the conftest already ran.
- **Prefer a real config over a mock** when the shape is what you are testing — `tests/ut/kv_offload/utils.py` builds a genuine `VllmConfig` against `tests/ut/_fake_weight` and patches only `ModelRegistry.inspect_model_cls`.
- **Reuse the shared factories** (`tests/ut/kvpp_utils.py`, `tests/ut/attention/utils.py`) instead of re-deriving spec objects per file.
- **New E2E tests get an `e2e_coverage` marker.** It is not enforced yet, but it is the data behind the coverage report, and `.github/workflows/scripts/coverage.py` flags every unmarked test by name.

## Related

- [CI Workflows and Selective Test Execution](./ci-and-test-selection.md) — which tests run on which runner, the selector/router split, and the coverage-configuration gate these markers feed.
- [NPUPlatform and Hardware Capability Profiles](../architecture/platform-and-hardware-profiles.md) — what `hardware="A2"`/`"A3"`/`"310P"`/`"A5"` and the faked `__device_type__` actually select.
- [Profiling and Debugging](../operations/profiling-and-debugging.md) — the profiler surface whose stubs the UT conftest seeds, and how to debug a run outside the harness.
- [Request Execution](../workflows/request-execution.md) — the runtime path an E2E serving test exercises end to end.

# Files

- [Workflow: KV Cache Sizing, Allocation, Reshape, and Graph Capture](kv-cache-initialization.md) - The Ascend KV-cache initialization pipeline - how the worker budgets cache memory, allocates and reshapes per-spec tensors, publishes block tables, runs the profile and dummy runs, and captures NPU graphs, including the failure modes that bite at each stage.
- [Workflow: KV Offloading, Tiering, and KV Store](kv-offload-and-store.md) - The non-network KV retention paths in vllm-ascend - connector-based CPU/tiering offload and preemption preservation, the AscendStore pooled KV reuse path with its coordinator, backends and layerwise transfer, and the model-level sparse KV offload driven by SparseKVOffloadConfig, including the attention start gate and the config gates each family must preserve.
- [Workflow: Prefill-Decode Disaggregation and KV Transfer Connectors](pd-disaggregation-and-kv-transfer.md) - How vllm-ascend pairs a prefill and a decode instance - the connector registry that maps kv_connector names to Ascend implementation classes, the handshake metadata exchanged at startup and per request, the pull/push/layerwise data paths built on the Mooncake transfer engine and MemFabric, and the role-dependent gates (kv_producer versus kv_consumer, preemption stores, kv_load_failure_policy).
- [Workflow: Plugin Registration and Startup Sequence](plugin-bootstrap.md) - The end-to-end Ascend startup path — which entry points vLLM resolves, what register()/register_connector()/register_model_loader()/register_model() do, how NPUPlatform.pre_register_and_update and check_and_update_config mutate configuration, and how each worker re-applies patches, re-initializes AscendConfig, binds the device, loads the model, sizes and allocates KV cache, profiles, warms up, and captures graphs — plus the orderings that break if changed.
- [Workflow: One Engine Step Through the Model Runner](request-execution.md) - How one SchedulerOutput travels through the Ascend worker and model runner - input preparation, batch and padding decisions, attention metadata, the Ascend forward context, model forward, sampling and the async output path - including the sequence-parallel, data-parallel and pipeline-parallel branches that change the flow.
- [Workflow: Scheduler Variants, Selection Rules, and DP Load Balancing](scheduler-variants.md) - How vllm-ascend chooses its Ascend scheduler family at platform-config time, which combinations startup rejects, and how the balance and DyntraLB variants hook the DP engine-core busy loop to share per-rank load.
- [Workflow: Weight Transfer, Hot Reload, and Sleep/Wake](weight-update-and-sleep-mode.md) - How Ascend rollout engines replace weights without a restart - the worker's init/start/update/finish lifecycle and its guards, the HCCL and NPU-IPC transfer engines with the packed-tensor wire format, the CaMemAllocator sleep levels that offload weights and discard KV cache, and the RL configuration surface that makes all of it safe.

nodes.description: The Ascend KV-cache initialization pipeline - how the worker budgets cache memory, allocates and reshapes per-spec tensors, publishes block tables, runs the profile and dummy runs, and captures NPU graphs, including the failure modes that bite at each stage.
nodes.body:
# Workflow: KV Cache Sizing, Allocation, Reshape, and Graph Capture

KV-cache initialization on Ascend is one ordered pipeline with a single hard
constraint driving its shape: **the amount of memory the cache may occupy is only
known after a real forward pass has been profiled, and the shapes the cache must take
are only known after the attention backends for every cache group have been selected.**
Everything else - the five budget adjustments, the descriptor geometries, the block
tables, the graph capture - is downstream of those two facts.

This page follows the pipeline in call order and records what each stage depends on and
how it fails. The data model itself (which specs exist, page layout, block-stride
addressing, KVPP placement) is documented in
[KV Cache Specs, Block Layout, and Placement](../concepts/kv-cache-and-block-layout.md);
what happens to those tensors after capture is in
[Graph Mode, Compilation, and Fusion Passes](../concepts/graph-mode-and-compilation.md),
[KV Offload and Store](./kv-offload-and-store.md), and
[PD Disaggregation and KV Transfer](./pd-disaggregation-and-kv-transfer.md).

## The pipeline in order

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SPEC["runner.get_kv_cache_spec: per-layer specs, no tensors"]
```
