```mermaid
    SPEC --> GROUPS["patched planner: groups, num_blocks, KVCacheConfig"]
    GROUPS --> BUDGET["worker.determine_available_memory: profile_run inside, five budget adjustments"]
    BUDGET --> INIT["worker.initialize_from_config"]
    INIT --> BACKEND["runner.initialize_attn_backend: attn groups, cudagraph mode, capture sizes"]
    BACKEND --> BATCH["may_reinitialize_input_batch: kernel block sizes, MultiGroupBlockTable"]
    BATCH --> ALLOC["_allocate_kv_cache_tensors: raw int8 buffers per descriptor"]
    ALLOC --> RESHAPE["_reshape_kv_cache_tensors: backend views, dtypes, page strides"]
    RESHAPE --> BIND["bind to forward context, register with offload and KV connectors, KVPP runtime"]
    BIND --> WARM["compile_or_warm_up_model: dummy runs plus kernel warmup"]
    WARM --> CAPTURE["capture_model: NPU graph pool"]
```

*The real call order: profiling precedes allocation because the budget depends on it, and block tables are rebuilt between backend selection and allocation.*

Two corrections to a naive reading of the sequence are worth stating explicitly, because
both are load-bearing:

- **`profile_run` runs before allocation, not after.** It is called from inside
  `determine_available_memory`, and it is the only way to measure weights + activation +
  non-torch memory for the current model on the current device
  ([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L594-L632)).
- **`may_reinitialize_input_batch` runs before allocation, not after.** It is the step that
  resolves each group's *kernel* block size from its attention backends, and reshape needs
  that number ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4223-L4251)).

## Stage 1: `get_kv_cache_spec` - what must be cached, but not how much

`NPUWorker.get_kv_cache_spec` is a thin wrapper with two side effects that later stages
depend on: it builds the KVPP allocation plan (`create_kvpp_cache_allocation_plan`, keyed by
this rank's KVPP rank) when `kvpp_config.size > 1`, and it caches the spec dict on the worker
as `self.kv_cache_spec` when sparse KV offload is enabled, because the budget planner needs
the specs before any tensor exists
([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L1106-L1125)).

`NPUModelRunner.get_kv_cache_spec` walks the static forward context and emits one spec per
layer, with four special cases
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5629-L5793)):

| Layer kind | Emitted spec |
| --- | --- |
| `Attention` with `kv_sharing_target_layer_name` | **none** - the layer is recorded in `shared_kv_cache_layers` and reuses its target's tensor |
| `MLAAttention` under sparse attention | `AscendMLAAttentionSpec` with packed SFA-C8 head size and dtype, or combined `kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim` |
| `MLAAttention` (dense, compressed, GLM) | `AscendMLAAttentionSpec`, propagating `model_version`, `indexes_kv_by_block_stride`, and the compression ratio as `compress_ratio` on `0.28.0` / `tokens_per_state` on main |
| `DeepseekV32IndexerCache` | `AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec` - a *separate* spec, so the scheduler still treats it as full-attention-compatible while the runner allocates it independently |
| `CacheOnlyAttentionLayer` | `HiddenStateCacheSpec`, rebuilt fresh (and deliberately **not** downgraded to `MLAAttentionSpec`, which would break hybrid page-size unification) |
| `MambaBase` | collected separately, then appended **after** all attention layers to preserve the ordering the graph-parameter update path expects |

The final Mamba pass is the only cross-layer adjustment: the Mamba page size is captured from the
last Mamba spec, and then every layer recorded in `attn_layer_names` whose
`page_size_bytes` is smaller is padded up to it through
`object.__setattr__(spec, "page_size_padded", mamba_page_size_padded)` - a frozen dataclass field
written around the immutability guard
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5780-L5790)). That single
<!-- openwiki: broken internal link [#stage-5-reshape-where-padded-pages-must-not-cross-block-ids] heading anchor "stage-5-reshape-where-padded-pages-must-not-cross-block-ids" does not exist in /openwiki/workflows/kv-cache-initialization.md. Fix the href or restore the target, then delete this comment. -->
write is what later forces [padded-page handling](#stage-5-reshape-where-padded-pages-must-not-cross-block-ids)
and, in pooled layouts, block-stride addressing.

Group formation and `num_blocks` derivation are **not** in this repo's runner - they are
patched upstream functions (`_ascend_get_kv_cache_config_from_groups`,
`_ascend_pool_bytes_per_block`, `_ascend_max_memory_usage_bytes_from_groups`) that restore the
Ascend/DSV4/GLM-Next planners and keep the rank re-plan divisor consistent
([`patch_kv_cache_utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_utils.py#L535-L637)).
The practical consequence for this workflow: the `KVCacheConfig` handed to allocation already
encodes `num_blocks`, the descriptor list, and the group list, and the runner treats it as
authoritative.

## Stage 2: `determine_available_memory` - five adjustments on top of one measurement

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["maybe_apply_startup_plan"] --> B{"kv_cache_memory_bytes set"}
    B -->|yes| FAST["profile_run only: budget is the user value"]
    B -->|no| PROF["memory_profiling wraps profile_run"]
    PROF --> CALC["budget = requested_memory minus non-KV memory"]
    CALC --> MULTI["_scale_kv_cache_memory_for_multi_group"]
    MULTI --> LAYER["layerwise buffer-reuse factor"]
    FAST --> OFF{"sparse KV offload enabled"}
    LAYER --> OFF
    OFF -->|yes| PLAN["plan_sparse_kv_offload_memory: min of npu, dram, workload"]
    OFF -->|no| KEEP["budget unchanged"]
    PLAN --> KVPP{"KVPP allocation plan present"}
    KEEP --> KVPP
    KVPP -->|yes| ROUND["floor to whole blocks, convert back to bytes"]
    KVPP -->|no| DONE["return bytes to the engine"]
    ROUND --> DONE
```

*The budget is measured once and then monotonically constrained; only the layerwise-reuse step can scale it up.*

### The measurement and the pre-graph peak override

`memory_profiling` wraps `profile_run`, and the interesting detail is what happens *inside*
the context: immediately after `profile_run` returns and **before** the context exits, the
worker samples `torch.npu.memory_stats(...)["allocated_bytes.all.peak"]` and later overwrites
`profile_result.torch_peak_increase` with that pre-capture value
([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L596-L618)). The stated reason is that graph
pool allocations would otherwise inflate the activation peak and shrink the KV budget for a
cost that is not an activation cost. The two categories are then stashed on the worker
(`peak_activation_memory`, `non_torch_memory`) precisely so
`compile_or_warm_up_model` can reuse them
([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L615-L617), [`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L899-L941)).

Two invariants guard the measurement:

- `init_snapshot.free_memory > free_gpu_memory` after profiling, otherwise the worker raises
  `"Error in memory profiling"` - the signature of another process in the same container
  releasing memory mid-startup
  ([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L619-L628)).
- The budget is **not clamped at zero**: `available = requested_memory - non_kv_cache_memory`
  may come out negative, and the worker returns the negative integer so the failure surfaces
  as zero blocks rather than a silently substituted value
  ([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L629-L629),
  [`test_worker_v1.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py#L1269-L1323)).

### The explicit-size fast path

If `cache_config.kv_cache_memory_bytes` is set, the worker still calls `profile_run` - the
model must compile and the activation buffers must materialize - but it skips the arithmetic
and logs that `gpu_memory_utilization` is **not** respected
([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L574-L592)). A startup-plan hit sets exactly
this field, which is why `maybe_apply_startup_plan` is called *before* the branch;
`test_determine_available_memory_applies_startup_plan_before_fast_path` pins that ordering
([`test_worker_v1.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py#L1119-L1153)).

### Adjustment 1: multi-group scaling

vLLM derives `num_blocks` from the *largest* cache group's bytes per block, but Ascend runners
that keep per-layer contiguous buffers pay `num_blocks × sum(all groups' pages)`. The worker
therefore scales the advertised budget by `bytes_per_block / sum_pages` so the derived block
count fits the per-layer representation
([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L663-L750)).

The function returns the budget **unchanged** when there is nothing to scale, and each
exemption has a distinct justification:

1. `kv_cache_spec` is not a dict (nothing to group), or `get_kv_cache_groups` is empty.
2. Any group contains a `model_version == "deepseek_v4"` spec - the restored shared-tuple
   planner already fits all groups into one physical budget.
3. The model is hybrid attention+Mamba, the resolved layout is layer-compact **and**
   block-compact, no KV-transfer connector is active, the runner advertises
   `supports_standardized_shared_kv_backing`, and neither sparse attention nor compression is
   on - the runner consumes one overlayed backing, so shrinking would waste capacity.
4. The `0.28.0` lane (legacy `shared_by` aliasing, one allocation per descriptor).
5. After the scan, the ratio is only applied when `sum_pages > bytes_per_block` and
   `bytes_per_block > 0`; a single group, or equal-sized groups, leaves the budget intact.

Otherwise the sum over all groups' layers is compared to the max per-group total and the ratio
is applied with an info log naming both byte counts. `test_worker_v1.py` pins the truth table:
DeepSeek-V4 keeps `12345`, hybrid attention+Mamba keeps `12345` only when
`supports_standardized_shared_kv_backing`, drops to `6172`, and a two-group pure-attention model
also halves ([`test_worker_v1.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py#L209-L329)).

### Adjustment 2: layerwise buffer reuse

When a layerwise KV-transfer config maps several layers onto fewer physical buffer slots, the
logical budget is scaled **up** by `num_layers / num_buffer_assignments`; the factor is 1.0
when there is no reuse, in which case the multiplicative step is skipped entirely
([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L634-L652)). The worker precomputes the
`(num_layers, num_buffer_assignments, factor)` triple during `get_kv_cache_spec` and falls back
to computing it from `build_layerwise_cache_layout` if absent
([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L1074-L1113)). The reuse layout itself is
applied later, when `apply_layerwise_kv_cache_plan` rewrites the config's tensor descriptors into
shared ones ([`layerwise_cache_layout.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/layerwise_cache_layout.py#L297-L360)).

### Adjustment 3: sparse KV offload decode constraints

With `sparse_kv_offload_config.enabled`, the plain budget is replaced by
`plan_sparse_kv_offload_memory`, which splits the layer specs into host-resident
(`store_on_host`) and device-resident sets and computes three block limits
([`sparse_kv_offload_manager.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/sparse_kv_offload_manager.py#L235-L295)):

- **npu** - available device bytes over the total page size (or the device page size alone when
  `keep_device_kv_cache` is false);
- **dram** - `dram_size_per_dp_GB` minus a per-host-layer 2 MiB alignment reserve, over the host
  page size;
- **workload** - `max_blocks_per_request × max_num_seqs + 1` (the extra block is the null block),
  where the per-request figure comes from `spec.max_memory_usage_bytes`.

The minimum wins, and one `logger.info_once` line reports all three limits, the winning factor
name, and the planner/host/device/alignment-reserve byte counts
([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L535-L551)). A warning fires specifically when
DRAM, not the NPU, is the binding limit, pointing at `dram_size_per_dp_GB`. The split itself is
strict: no host specs, no device specs, or more than one distinct block size across the two sets
is a `ValueError` ([`sparse_kv_offload_manager.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/sparse_kv_offload_manager.py#L213-L232)).

### Adjustment 4: KVPP block quantization

With a KVPP plan present, the byte budget is **not** what the engine sees. `get_num_blocks`
divides by `persistent_bytes + 2 × max_scratch_bytes` (one scratch buffer for the current layer,
one for the prefetch), and the worker multiplies back by `sum(spec.page_size_bytes)` so the
planner derives a consistent `num_blocks`
([`kv_cache_placement.py`](../../vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_placement.py#L33-L44),
[`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L553-L559)). The unquantized value is preserved
on `self.available_kv_cache_memory_bytes` for logging and for the post-capture suggestion. The
observable behaviour is a step function: `1175` bytes yields `952`, `1176` yields `1428`
([`test_worker_v1.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py#L2188-L2213)).

### Adjustment 5: the published number

On the profiled path, `logger.info_once("Available KV cache memory: %.2f GiB", scope="local")`
reports the multi-group- and reuse-scaled value **before** the offload and KVPP adjustments, so the
log line is a pre-constraint figure, not the final budget
([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L654-L661)). The attribute
`self.available_kv_cache_memory_bytes` outlives the call: `_apply_kvpp_memory_budget` reassigns it
to its own incoming argument, so afterwards it holds the offload-constrained but not yet
block-quantized budget, which is what the post-capture suggestion log quotes as
`"Current KV cache memory"` ([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L553-L561),
[`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L930-L936)). The fast path never emits the
`info_once` line at all - it logs the reserved size instead.

On 310P the whole function is replaced: the budget is **halved** for operator workspace, an RC
device reads free memory from `psutil.virtual_memory()` instead of `torch.npu.mem_get_info()`,
and the non-torch term is reduced by the amount `empty_cache` reclaimed
([`worker_310p.py`](../../vllm_ascend/_310p/worker_310p.py#L73-L137)).

## Stage 3: `initialize_kv_cache` - configuration rewrite, then backends, then tensors

`NPUWorker.initialize_from_config` is the engine-facing entry point; it initializes KV transfer
and, in sleep mode, runs the allocation inside the `kv_cache` memory pool
([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L1140-L1151)). Inside the runner,
`initialize_kv_cache` performs a fixed sequence
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4223-L4302)):

1. **Rewrite the config.** `may_add_encoder_only_layers_to_kv_cache_config`,
   `apply_layerwise_kv_cache_plan` (shared buffers), and
   `maybe_add_kv_sharing_layers_to_kv_cache_groups` (cross-layer KV sharing). The config is
   deep-copied first, so the caller's object is never mutated.
2. **`initialize_attn_backend`.** Must happen before anything touches `self.attn_groups`.
3. **`use_hybrid_blocks = len(self.attn_groups) > 1`** - `attn_groups` holds one entry per
   scheduler cache group (each entry possibly containing several `AttentionGroup`s), so this is
   true exactly when more than one cache group exists, i.e. when kernel-block splitting may be
   needed. `need_accepted_tokens` is taken from `kv_cache_config.has_mamba_layers`, because the
   packed K3 layout can hide Mamba specs inside `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`.
4. **`may_reinitialize_input_batch`** - kernel block sizes and block tables.
5. **`initialize_kv_cache_tensors`** - allocate, then reshape, then bind.
6. **Registration.** Sparse-offload manager, then `get_kv_transfer_group().register_kv_caches`,
   then `KVPPRuntime.create_from_kv_cache`.

### Backend selection decides the graph mode, which decides capture sizes

`initialize_attn_backend` maps each scheduler group's layers to backends **grouped by
`(backend class, layer spec, use_mla_rope)`**, so a group can fan out into several attention
groups and metadata builders
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5507-L5596)). Two rules matter
downstream:

- The layer's own `get_attn_backend()` wins; an `AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec` layer whose declared
  backend does not accept the indexer's block size (checked against
  `get_supported_kernel_block_sizes`, including `MultipleOf`) is rerouted to
  `AscendSFAIndexerBackend`.
- The *minimum* `get_cudagraph_support` across all groups feeds
  `resolve_cudagraph_mode_and_sizes`, which re-derives the effective graph mode and the capture
  descriptors; the dispatcher keys are initialized from it, and only afterwards are
  `set_graph_params`/`set_draft_graph_params` called with the sorted capture sizes, because those
  sizes are not known until the dispatcher has computed them
  ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5795-L5877)).

That ordering is the reason graph capture cannot be described independently of the KV config:
the capture-size list - and therefore the number of `NPUGraph`s and their per-shape attention
workspaces - is a function of the cache groups' backends
([`acl_graph.py`](../../vllm_ascend/compilation/acl_graph.py#L341-L360)).

### Block-size contract: `may_reinitialize_input_batch`

```python
self.kernel_block_sizes = []
for group in kv_cache_groups:
    if group spec is AttentionSpec:
        selected = select_common_block_size(group.spec.block_size, [g.backend for g in attn_groups[i]])
        self.kernel_block_sizes.append([selected])
    else:                                   # Mamba / other
        self.kernel_block_sizes.append([0])  # 0 disables slot mapping for the group
```

Each group's `max_num_blocks_per_req` then comes from the spec, not from
`cdiv(max_model_len, block_size)`; the fallback inside `MultiGroupBlockTable` only applies when
no list is supplied
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5429-L5468),
[`block_table.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/block_table.py#L348-L354)).

The `NPUInputBatch` - and with it the `MultiGroupBlockTable` - is rebuilt only when
`block_sizes != [cache_config.block_size]`, or `kernel_block_sizes != [[cache_config.block_size]]`,
or there is more than one cache group; that rebuild asserts
`offload_config.uva.cpu_offload_gb == 0` because CPU weight offloading is incompatible with a
late rebuild ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5470-L5499)).
The initial `NPUInputBatch` created in the runner constructor uses the single default block size
and is explicitly documented as a placeholder for exactly this replacement
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L566-L599)).

The three lists are kept in lockstep by construction: `non_encoder_groups` filters out
`EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec` groups, `block_sizes` and `max_num_blocks` are built from that filtered
list, and `kernel_block_sizes` skips encoder-only groups *without* appending - so all three have
the same length and `MultiGroupBlockTable`'s length check can only fire on a genuine bug
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5422-L5468),
[`block_table.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/block_table.py#L338-L359)).

### What the block table commits to

`BlockTable` is where the block-size contract becomes concrete
([`block_table.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/block_table.py#L21-L120)):

- `physical_block_size` is the scheduler block size. If `kernel_sizes` is `None`/`[0]` there is
  no splitting; otherwise the first advertised size that divides the physical block is selected,
  and if none divides, construction raises
  `"None of the kernel sizes ... can divide physical block size ... evenly"`.
- `blocks_per_phys_block > 1` sets `use_hybrid_blocks`, doubles the logical row width, and makes
  `append_row` expand each physical id into `blocks_per_phys_block` consecutive logical ids
  ([`block_table.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/block_table.py#L286-L301)).
- Rows are duplicated (`1 + num_speculative_tokens`) only under DCP, and `slot_mapping` reserves
  `max(num_speculative_tokens - 1, 0) * max_num_reqs` extra entries for MTP draft positions.
- A Mamba group is flagged `is_mamba_group` and skipped by both slot-mapping paths, because
  recurrent state has no token-level slot ([`block_table.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/block_table.py#L447-L494)).
- When more than one non-Mamba group exists and every one has `dcp_world_size == 1`, slot mapping
  is fused across groups via `compute_slot_mapping_fused_groups`, passing per-group table pointers,
  row strides, block sizes and the minimum block size as one constexpr window
  ([`block_table.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/block_table.py#L398-L425)).

**Hybrid and sparse groups share block ids but never storage.** This is the invariant that makes
the group fan-out safe: `AscendSFAIndexerCacheSpec` is registered with `FullAttentionManager` so the
scheduler can hand it the same ids as the MLA cache, yet the runner allocates it as an independent
`(k, scale)` pair ([`kv_cache_interface.py`](../../vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_interface.py#L165-L191),
[`kv_cache_interface.py`](../../vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_interface.py#L315-L336)).
`AscendIndexerKPoolStateSpec` (a `SlidingWindowManager` group) goes further and reports exactly one
page per request, since it only holds the current incomplete pool
([`kv_cache_interface.py`](../../vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_interface.py#L283-L312)). On the
scheduler side the coordinator allocates one `BlockPool` of `kv_cache_config.num_blocks` blocks and
one single-type manager per group, so ids are drawn from a shared pool while managers decide
validity per group ([`patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py#L125-L156)).

## Stage 4: allocate - pool strategy before any `torch.zeros`

`initialize_kv_cache_tensors` is deliberately thin: allocate, reshape, alias cross-layer
sharing, then bind ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4310-L4354)).
Binding differs by model: DeepSeek-V4 appends caches in `(layer index, name)` order and assigns a
one-element `kv_cache` list, everything else goes through the patched `bind_kv_cache` which fills
`runner_kv_caches` in layer-index order and sets `forward_context[layer].kv_cache`
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4330-L4352),
[`patch_bind_kv_cache.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_bind_kv_cache.py#L14-L58)).

`_allocate_kv_cache_tensors` chooses a **pool strategy** first, then allocates per descriptor
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4491-L4553)):

| Condition | Strategy |
| --- | --- |
| `kvpp_config.size > 1` | `allocate_kvpp_cache` owns the pool; hybrid mode forced off |
| `requires_padded_page_layout(...)` | one backing per GLM-Next descriptor, shared by every listed layer, after validating `offset`, `layer_stride`, `block_stride == page_size_bytes`, `size == num_blocks * block_stride` |
| main lane + any `deepseek_v4` spec | all descriptors must declare the same `size`; one backing allocated once and sliced into contiguous per-layer regions |
| main lane + hybrid attention/Mamba + layer/block-compact layout + compatible connector | one backing, sliced per layer |

`KVPPRuntime` is created from the *allocated* views, and KVPP allocation is where the scratch
aliasing happens: owned layers get a private buffer, non-owned layers alias one of
`KVPP_SCRATCH_BUFFER_COUNT = 2` shared buffers
([`kvpp_cache.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/kvpp_cache.py#L23-L52)).

### Alignment: the PD-transfer contract

Every raw cache tensor is an `int8` buffer. The 2 MiB alignment that prefill/decode
disaggregation requires is applied **only when `kv_transfer_config` is set**:
`_allocate_int8_cache_tensor` allocates `numel + alignment` bytes and trims to an aligned slice,
so a non-transfer deployment pays nothing
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4413-L4434)). Reshape relies
on the same fact - the allocator comment states that K and V are split "to support prefill
disaggregation, as it only support the 0-dim of kv_cache is `num_blocks`"
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4827-L4832)).

The SFA indexer allocation packs K and its scale into **one** aligned int8 tensor so a connector
can register a single range: `scale_offset` is rounded up to the scale dtype size, and three
assertions enforce contiguity, pointer alignment and a whole multiple of the dtype size
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4436-L4489)).

The consumer side re-derives region starts and rounds them **down** to 2 MiB, asserting that the
raw tensor pointer was already aligned
([`pool_worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/pool_worker.py#L766-L783)).

## Stage 5: reshape - where padded pages must not cross block ids

`_reshape_kv_cache_tensors` walks `self._kv_cache_spec_attn_group_iterator()` and picks a branch
per layer spec. Three invariants hold across the branches:

- `num_blocks` is recomputed from the raw allocation (`numel // page_size_bytes`) and asserted
  `>= kv_cache_config.num_blocks` - ranks may over-allocate, and the scheduler uses the minimum
  ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5224-L5235)). The
  page-strided branch is the exception: a page-strided cache has no slack, so it asserts equality
  instead ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5013-L5017)).
- Shapes come from `attn_backend.get_kv_cache_shape(...)`, fed `get_storage_block_size(spec)` rather
  than `spec.block_size` for page-strided caches, so a compressed spec needs no special case
  ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5011-L5024)).
- When `use_hybrid_blocks` is on and the backend advertises supported kernel sizes, the view is
  built as `num_blocks * (spec.block_size // kernel_block_size)` blocks of the *kernel* size
  ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5237-L5253)).

`_adjust_kv_layout` is the primitive for padded pages: it builds each view with
`torch.as_strided` and overrides the outermost stride with `page_size_bytes // dtype_size`
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4948-L4978)). For a
page-strided MLA cache it emits the latent-KV and RoPE halves as two logical tensors over the same
backing, and for a compressed cache with `scale_dim` on capable hardware it adds a third
overlapping full view ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5026-L5082)).

`requires_padded_page_layout` is what decides whether Mamba state views also advance by the padded
page ([`kv_cache_interface.py`](../../vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_interface.py#L51-L72)). It is a
**pool-level** conjunction: at least one `MambaSpec`, at least one state spec carrying
`page_size_padded`, and at least one spec in the pool setting `indexes_kv_by_block_stride`.
Padding alone must not trigger it, because hybrid models pad Mamba pages while keeping the packed
contiguous state layout. When it is true, state views are built through `_adjust_kv_layout`,
otherwise the packed `(kv_padding, conv)` / `(k, ssm)` / `(v, mamba_padding)` cursor walk is used
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5361-L5407)).

Conversely, when the *attention* page was padded up to the Mamba page, the trailing padding is
stripped before the K/V views are created - from the front of a combined raw tensor when K and V
share one allocation, so that both views start at the same page offset
(`should_trim_page_padding`, [`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5254-L5309)).

## Stage 6: profile and dummy runs

`profile_run` is not one forward pass ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4024-L4040)):

1. `eplb_warmup()` if dynamic EPLB is on;
2. `allocate_kv_offload_topk_profile_buffers` for sparse KV offload, using the cached spec - the
   top-k buffers must be reserved before profiling or the measured peak is wrong;
3. an **extra** MC2-capacity dummy run under `disable_compilation` when `max_num_tokens` exceeds
   the MC2 capacity and the selected MoE comm method is MC2/Fused-MC2, so HCCL buffers are reserved
   in proportion;
4. the upstream `profile_run` itself.

`_dummy_run` builds attention metadata with `force_attention` or under `FULL` graphs, and does two
things that matter for KV state: it commits the block table for the *padded* request count so
GDN/Mamba metadata does not read stale rows, and - unless it is itself capturing a graph - it fills
every group's `slot_mapping` with `-1` before the backend derives metadata, so a backend cannot
observe a real request's slots during a dummy pass
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3841-L3852),
[`test_model_runner_v1.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py#L99-L143)).

## Stage 7: capture

`compile_or_warm_up_model` removes the graph capture sizes from the compile-warmup list, warm-ups
the remaining sizes in descending order, runs `kernel_warmup`, and only then calls
`capture_model()` - guarded by `not enforce_eager` - keeping the returned NPU-graph byte count
([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L867-L897)).

`NPUModelRunner.capture_model` is a thin adapter: it enters `_torch_cuda_wrapper` (rebinds
`torch.cuda.Event/Stream/CUDAGraph` to their `torch.npu` counterparts and patches
`breakable_cudagraph` weak-ref helpers), swaps upstream's `graph_capture` and
`EncoderCudaGraphManager` for the Ascend versions, delegates to `GPUModelRunner.capture_model`,
and returns the graph pool size
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5879-L5889),
[`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5955-L6029)).

`ACLGraphWrapper` owns the per-batch-descriptor cache: on a runtime-mode match it captures a
`torch.npu.NPUGraph` into `self.graph_pool`, weak-refs the collected attention workspaces and the
output, and weak-refs the output again so the pool allocation can be released; on replay it
optionally synchronizes the stream first (FULL mode, non-draft) and replays
([`acl_graph.py`](../../vllm_ascend/compilation/acl_graph.py#L150-L292)). In debug mode it asserts
the input addresses are identical between capture and replay - the check that catches a KV cache
tensor being reallocated after capture.

## Failure modes and how they present

| Signature | Cause | Where it is enforced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid kv cache tensor, raw tensor ptr must be align to 2MB` | a raw cache tensor was not 2 MiB-aligned although a connector is registering regions | [`pool_worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/pool_worker.py#L774-L783) |
| Connector sees a shifted region, or `reshape_and_cache` writes to the wrong address | K/V split assumptions broken (a single combined tensor where the tuple path is required), or alignment skipped because `kv_transfer_config` was unset at allocation time and set later | [`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4413-L4434), [`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4827-L4832) |
| KV transfer rejected outright | 310P refuses `kv_transfer_config`, sparse attention, and MLA before allocation | [`model_runner_310p.py`](../../vllm_ascend/_310p/model_runner_310p.py#L689-L720) |
| `Invalid GLM-Next shared-slot KV cache descriptor geometry` | descriptor `offset`/`layer_stride`/`block_stride`/`size` does not match the layer's `page_size_bytes` - the padded page would map a second block id onto the same page | [`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4557-L4577) |
| `DeepSeek-V4 KV cache descriptors must share one backing allocation` / `requires contiguous per-layer pages` | the shared-tuple planner's geometry was perturbed, which would over-commit the device | [`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4585-L4634) |
| State write lands in another block's pages | `page_size_padded` on the state spec without `indexes_kv_by_block_stride` in the pool (packed layout kept) or with the flag but a compact state view | [`kv_cache_interface.py`](../../vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_interface.py#L51-L72), pinned by [`test_glm5next_pooled_cache.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_glm5next_pooled_cache.py#L277-L342) |
| `num_blocks: X should be equal to kv_cache_config.num_blocks: Y` | page-strided cache whose raw allocation does not divide evenly into pages | [`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5013-L5017) |
| `Some layers are not correctly initialized` | a group layer was missed by every allocation branch | [`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4938-L4944) |
| `None of the kernel sizes ... can divide physical block size ... evenly` | backend advertises kernel block sizes that do not divide the scheduler block | [`block_table.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/block_table.py#L59-L70) |
| `Cannot re-initialize the input batch when CPU weight offloading is enabled` | multi-group or non-default block size combined with `cpu_offload_gb > 0` | [`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L5470-L5477) |
| Worker dies during or right after startup with graph-related OOM | automatic profiling sized the cache from pre-capture peak, leaving no headroom for the graph pool; the documented remedy is an explicit, smaller KV budget | [`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L602-L613), [`Dots3-Note.md`](../../docs/source/tutorials/models/Dots3-Note.md#L406-L406) |
| `stream resources are insufficient` / `Insufficient_Stream_Resources` / error `207008` at capture | too many captured graphs for the HDK/CANN stack | re-raised with mitigation guidance in [`acl_graph.py`](../../vllm_ascend/compilation/acl_graph.py#L229-L238) |
| `Alloc sq cq fail` at capture | old HDK/CANN signature | re-raised as an upgrade instruction in [`acl_graph.py`](../../vllm_ascend/compilation/acl_graph.py#L221-L228) |

### The capture-OOM feedback loop

Because the budget deliberately excludes graph pool memory, the worker closes the loop *after*
capture: if the user did not pin `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, it computes
`non_kv_memory = weights + peak_activation + non_torch + npugraph_memory`, subtracts a 150 MiB
safety margin (explicitly because `memory_profiling` may under-count ACL/HCCL/driver allocations),
logs two suggested `--kv-cache-memory` values, and persists the one that fits the requested slice
through `maybe_save_startup_plan` - which the next start consumes via the fast path
([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L899-L941)). The margin, not the arithmetic, is
the reason a value suggested by that log line is expected to survive a restart.

`capture_model` runs before the ATB warm-up and CPU binding so that hot allocations are already
materialized when `migratepages`/`taskset` execute
([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L943-L956)).

## Operations and configuration surface

| Lever | Effect on this workflow |
| --- | --- |
| `--gpu-memory-utilization` | sets `requested_memory` at device init; startup fails if free memory is below it |
| `--kv-cache-memory` (`kv_cache_memory_bytes`) | skips profiling arithmetic; ignores utilization; the correct lever for a reproducible block count |
| `--enforce-eager` | skips `capture_model` entirely, so `npugraph_memory_bytes` stays zero and no capture-OOM risk exists |
| `additional_config.enable_kvpp` | replaces the allocation strategy and quantizes the budget; requires eager, non-hybrid MLA, and rejects PCP/DCP/KV transfer |
| `sparse_kv_offload_config` | swaps the plain budget for the three-limit planner and moves host-resident layers to aligned pinned memory |
| layerwise KV-transfer config | rewrites descriptors into shared buffers and scales the logical budget up |
| `max_num_seqs`, `--max-num-batched-tokens` | enter the workload limit of the sparse-offload planner and the MC2 extra dummy run trigger |
| `--cudagraph-mode`, `max_cudagraph_capture_size` | bounded by the minimum `AttentionCGSupport` across groups, so a weak backend lowers capture cost and OOM risk |

## Focused tests

| Test | What it protects |
| --- | --- |
| [`test_worker_v1.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py#L1024-L1323) | fast path vs profiling path, sparse-offload constraint application, startup-plan precedence, non-torch accounting, the free-memory assertion, and the unclamped negative budget |
| [`test_worker_v1.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py#L209-L329) | multi-group scale truth table: DeepSeek-V4, hybrid via `supports_standardized_shared_kv_backing`, pure-attention two-group |
| [`test_worker_v1.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py#L2188-L2213) | KVPP budget quantization and `available_kv_cache_memory_bytes` publication |
| [`test_worker_multi_instance.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_worker_multi_instance.py#L125-L323) | two instances on one card stay positive, graph memory is not profiled, free-memory regression |
| [`test_model_runner_v1.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py#L485-L514) | KVPP allocate/reshape view construction (packed and unpacked) |
| [`test_model_runner_v1.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py#L877-L1180) | DSV4 single-backing geometry allocated once, draft GQA per-layer sizing, cache-only BHNC axis order, hybrid padding strip |
| [`test_glm5next_pooled_cache.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_glm5next_pooled_cache.py#L182-L342) | contiguous slot backings, per-block-id isolation across permutations, the `requires_padded_page_layout` truth table |
| [`test_block_table.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_block_table.py#L85-L338) | MTP slot reservation, Mamba row capacity under DCP, no logical-id expansion for DSV4, DCP slot mapping at several interleave sizes |
| [`test_kvpp_cache_placement.py`](../../tests/ut/core/test_kvpp_cache_placement.py#L98-L113) | per-rank block cost and budget flooring |
| [`test_multi_instance.py`](../../tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_multi_instance.py#L18-L93) | the end-to-end regression that two instances initialize and generate |

nodes.title: Workflow: KV Offloading, Tiering, and KV Store
nodes.description: The non-network KV retention paths in vllm-ascend - connector-based CPU/tiering offload and preemption preservation, the AscendStore pooled KV reuse path with its coordinator, backends and layerwise transfer, and the model-level sparse KV offload driven by SparseKVOffloadConfig, including the attention start gate and the config gates each family must preserve.
nodes.body:
# Workflow: KV Offloading, Tiering, and KV Store

Three unrelated mechanisms in this repository all answer the question "where does KV live when it does not fit in HBM", and they are easy to confuse because they share the `kv_transfer` package and the same connector interface. They differ in **who owns the decision**:

| Family | Decision owner | Data plane | Configured by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A. Connector offload** | Upstream vLLM block pool / manager | Batched NPU DMA on dedicated streams between HBM and pinned host memory | `kv_connector` = `OffloadingConnector`, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, or `RecomputeCPUOffloadConnector` |
| **B. Store / pool reuse** | An external KV pool keyed by block hash | Backend `get`/`put` (Mooncake, Memcache, Yuanrong) driven by scheduler-side hit masks | `kv_connector` = `AscendStoreConnector` (or legacy `MooncakeConnectorStoreV1`) |
| **C. Sparse KV offload** | The attention layer itself | Per-token-row D2H into a shared host pool plus top-k miss H2D into per-layer resident buffers | `additional_config.sparse_kv_offload_config` plus the `SfaRemoteD2HConnector` |

Family A and B are connectors and therefore see the `KVConnectorBase_V1` scheduler/worker split. Family C is not a connector at all: it changes the KV-cache allocation (`store_on_host`), the SFA attention implementation, and the device memory budget. Family B is also the only one that can composite with P/D transfer connectors through `AscendMultiConnector`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    REG["register_connector: pop upstream names, register Ascend classes"] --> A["Family A: connector offload"]
    REG --> B["Family B: AscendStore pool"]
    REG --> C["Family C: model-level sparse offload"]
    A --> A1["OffloadingConnector plus NPU spec: upstream scheduler, NPU DMA worker"]
    A --> A2["SimpleCPUOffloadConnector: upstream connector, NPU copy backend"]
    A --> A3["RecomputeCPUOffloadConnector: Ascend scheduler and Ascend worker"]
    B --> B1["KVPoolScheduler: keys, hit masks, lookup RPC, delayed free"]
    B --> B2["KVPoolWorker: backend get and put, layerwise threads, start gate"]
    C --> C1["SparseKVOffloadManager: shared host pool, top-k LRU residency"]
    C --> C2["AscendSFAKVOffload: decode-only SFA, optional fused overlap"]
```

*Where each family attaches: only A and B are KV connectors, while C is wired into allocation and the attention backend.*

For the network paths (Mooncake P2P, layerwise P/D pulls, `SfaRemoteD2HConnector`'s MemFabric read path) see [PD Disaggregation and KV Transfer](./pd-disaggregation-and-kv-transfer.md); this page stops at the process boundary. For the block/page vocabulary used throughout see [KV Cache Specs, Block Layout, and Placement](../concepts/kv-cache-and-block-layout.md), and for where in the startup pipeline each piece is initialized see [KV Cache Initialization](./kv-cache-initialization.md).

## Registration: which names are overridden and which are added

Every Ascend KV connector enters the process through one function, called from `vllm_ascend.register_connector()` during plugin load. It does two different things and the difference matters when you are debugging "which implementation is actually running":

- **Override** — the upstream registry entry is *removed* and re-registered pointing at an Ascend module. This covers `CPUOffloadingSpec` → `NPUOffloadingSpec`, `TieringOffloadingSpec` → `NPUTieringOffloadingSpec`, `OffloadingConnector` → `AscendOffloadingConnector`, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` → `AscendSimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, and `MultiConnector` → `AscendMultiConnector`. Users keep writing upstream connector and spec names; the Ascend class is what instantiates ([`kv_transfer/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/__init__.py#L21-L117)).
- **Add** — new names that only exist here: `AscendStoreConnector` (plus the deprecated alias `MooncakeConnectorStoreV1`), `RecomputeCPUOffloadConnector`, `UCMConnector`, `SfaRemoteD2HConnector`, and the `Mooncake*` P2P connectors.

The `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` override is guarded by an import probe of `vllm.v1.simple_kv_offload`, so a vLLM version without that module silently keeps working without the override instead of failing at import.

The stated rationale for the override pattern is worth preserving in any refactor: *"The scheduler-side managers stay upstream; only worker-side transfers use torch.npu streams and the Ascend batched memcpy op"* ([`kv_transfer/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/__init__.py#L22-L24)). The reason is layout: upstream assumes an attention layer's KV is one packed tensor, while Ascend keeps K, V, and quant scales in separate allocations.

## Family A: connector offload with a scheduler/worker split

### A1. Native CPU offload and tiering (`OffloadingConnector`)

This family is a thin Ascend skin over vLLM's own offloading framework. `NPUOffloadingSpec` and `NPUTieringOffloadingSpec` subclass the upstream CPU and tiering specs and replace exactly one behaviour — worker creation ([`native/npu.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/kv_offload/native/npu.py#L41-L97)):

- `NPUOffloadingSpec` keeps the single-tier path on PyTorch's pinned allocator. The comment records why: CANN has no public equivalent of `cudaHostRegister` for an arbitrary mmap buffer, so upstream's shared-region layout stays disabled for this spec and `replicated_layout` remains safely off.
- `NPUTieringOffloadingSpec._uses_shared_region()` returns `True`, telling upstream that every worker and the scheduler-side primary tier really do share one `SharedOffloadRegion`; that is what lets upstream enable its single-copy layout for configurations it has certified as byte-replicated (currently pure MLA under the supported TP topology). The worker computes its mmap slot from `rank % world_size`, or rank 0 when the replicated layout is active.

The layout adaptation lives in `AscendOffloadingConnectorWorker.register_kv_caches`. It first *detects* whether adaptation is needed — an `AttentionSpec` layer whose cache is not a single `torch.Tensor`, or a `MambaSpec` layer whose cache is a list — and calls `super()` unchanged when the layout is already packed. Otherwise it builds canonical two-dimensional `int8` block views per component ([`native/offloading_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/kv_offload/native/offloading_connector.py#L152-L315)):

- `_canonicalize_split_cache` sorts the components by size and accepts a single overlapping full-page view **only if that tensor's storage actually contains every other component's first physical block**. Shape comparison alone was insufficient — it silently dropped V or the scale tail. When no such view exists, it emits one view per component and the caller leaves the page mapping unset rather than applying one page offset to every component.
- Contiguity is enforced: a non-contiguous block payload, overlapping block storage, or a component set that does not sum to one logical page raises `ValueError` instead of producing a wrong copy.
- Mamba layers are canonicalized the same way after checking that the state tensors sum to `page_size_bytes` computed with `page_size_padded=None`.

The transfer worker is where the Ascend-specific performance lives. `NPUOffloadingWorker` owns **two direction-specialized handlers** — store is D2H, load is H2D — and each `SingleDirectionNPUOffloadingHandler` keeps its own stream pool, event pool, and descriptor buffer pool so shutdown of one direction cannot release tensors the other still uses ([`native/cpu_npu.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/kv_offload/native/cpu_npu.py#L104-L272)):

- Copies are issued as one `torch.ops._C_ascend.swap_blocks_batch` call per chunk on a borrowed stream. The op takes three **CPU** `int64` tensors (source pointers, destination pointers, sizes) and a direction code `0=H2D, 1=D2H, 2=D2D`, and routes to `aclrtMemcpyBatchAsync` when the CANN build provides it ([`csrc/torch_binding.cpp`](../../csrc/torch_binding.cpp#L147-L200)).
- A D2H chunk first does `stream.wait_stream(torch.npu.current_stream())` because KV writes happen on the model stream and the copy must not observe a partially written block. Each handler also chains its own transfers in order so one chunk cannot overwrite a buffer still being read by the previous chunk.
- Completion is polled, not synchronized: `get_finished()` drains transfers whose `end_event.query()` is true, computes `transfer_time` from the timing events, and returns the stream/events/descriptors to their pools. `wait(job_ids)` exists for the blocking case.

### A2. Simple CPU offload (`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`)

This is a second, independent upstream offload implementation, and the Ascend version replaces even less: `AscendSimpleCPUOffloadConnector` calls the upstream constructor — which only initializes Python state and parses config — and then swaps `worker_handler` for `SimpleCPUOffloadNPUWorker` on the `WORKER` role, but **only when upstream created a handler**. Upstream deliberately leaves the worker unset when prefix caching is disabled, so the connector is a no-op in that case and the Ascend subclass preserves that ([`simple/simple_cpu_offload_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/kv_offload/simple/simple_cpu_offload_connector.py#L26-L54)).

The NPU worker keeps every upstream step-time behaviour (event lists, high-water cursors, pending sets, completed-store map) and overrides only three platform realities, documented at the top of [`simple/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/kv_offload/simple/worker.py#L1-L23):

1. the copy backend is swapped for `NPUDmaCopyBackend`;
2. block views are rebuilt from tensor shape/stride rather than `storage.nbytes()`, because the runner over-allocates each tensor for 2 MiB alignment and K/V are separate allocations;
3. CPU mirrors are plain pinned `torch.zeros`, because `cudaHostRegister` is CUDA-only, and transfer streams drop the lowest-priority hint that `torch.npu.Stream` does not expose.

`NPUDmaCopyBackend` caches exactly two prebuilt `BatchMemcpyParams` — one H2D for loads and one D2H for stores — and dispatches submitted jobs in FIFO order to a single worker thread; each job issues its copies on a dedicated NPU stream and records an `Event` the main thread polls without device synchronization ([`simple/copy_backend.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/kv_offload/simple/copy_backend.py#L24-L60)).

**Choosing between A1 and A2.** A1 is the tiered path (CPU primary tier plus optional filesystem/3FS secondary tiers) and is the one with the multi-tier tuning knobs; A2 is the minimal single-tier path that reuses vLLM's prefix-caching-driven offload scheduler. Both share the same `swap_blocks_batch` primitive, so their DMA behaviour is the same; only the eviction policy and tier stack differ.

### A3. Recompute CPU offload (`RecomputeCPUOffloadConnector`)

This family exists for one scenario: a **Decode node in a P/D disaggregated deployment whose `RecomputeScheduler` preempts a running request**. Without it, the request is sent back through prompt recompute; with it, the already-computed blocks are copied to CPU DRAM before their HBM blocks are reused and copied back on reschedule. Unlike A1/A2, both halves are Ascend code ([`recompute_cpu_offload_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/recompute_cpu_offload/recompute_cpu_offload_connector.py#L39-L96)):

- Budget is **per rank**: `cpu_bytes_to_use` defaults to 8 GiB and is divided by `world_size`; `cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank` overrides it, and a mismatch only logs a warning rather than failing startup.
- The role decides which half exists: `SCHEDULER` builds `RecomputeCPUOffloadScheduler`, `WORKER` builds `RecomputeCPUOffloadWorker`.
- `enable_offload_prefix_caching` (default `false`) decides whether full hashed blocks may share a CPU block; the scheduler's docstring states the invariant directly — *"When offload prefix caching is enabled, full hashed blocks share CPU blocks. Otherwise every offloaded block is private to its request"* ([`manager.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/recompute_cpu_offload/manager.py#L57-L80)).

The scheduler half derives a CPU `KVCacheConfig` sized to the capacity, then tracks one `PreemptedRequestState` per preserved request (CPU block ids, `num_computed_tokens`, store/load transfer metadata, store and load event ids, readiness). Its three connector hooks are the state machine:

- `update_state_before_preempt` snapshots the request's block ids before HBM reuse. Mamba groups are special-cased: only the trailing `1 + num_spec_tokens` blocks are preserved, because that is what the recurrent state needs ([`manager.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/recompute_cpu_offload/manager.py#L265-L292)).
- `has_preempted_request` + `get_num_new_matched_tokens` answer for a returning request. Crucially, while the store has not completed the manager returns `(None, False)` — *not* `0` — which is the vLLM convention for "no decision yet"; returning `0` here would make the scheduler fall through to the next connector in a `MultiConnector` and lose the preserved state ([`manager.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/recompute_cpu_offload/manager.py#L205-L229)).
- `update_state_after_alloc` prepares the H2D restore and **raises** `RuntimeError` if preparation fails, rather than silently letting the request run with an incomplete prefix.

The worker half issues plain per-block `copy_` calls on dedicated store and load NPU streams and records an event per job, with `TODO`s marking where a dedicated NPU copy kernel should replace the torch copy. Loads are appended to `_load_events` and polled in `get_finished`, which reports `finished_recving` for every request whose event index is at or below the polled high-water mark ([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/recompute_cpu_offload/worker.py#L201-L305)).

Because the connector is opt-in and correctness-first, the fallback path is part of the contract: if the connector is not configured, the recompute scheduler is off, or CPU capacity is insufficient, behavior reverts to plain recompute.

## Family B: the AscendStore pooled KV reuse path

`AscendStoreConnector` is the largest single component in this area, and it is a different animal from family A: it does not move evicted blocks, it *publishes and reloads* KV under content keys so that a request can start with a longer prefix than local prefix caching provides. Both the scheduler and the worker sides are Ascend-owned objects (`KVPoolScheduler`, `KVPoolWorker`) created per role ([`ascend_store_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/ascend_store_connector.py#L92-L143)).

Three construction-time facts are enforced before any transfer happens:

- `use_layerwise` forces **PIECEWISE** CUDA graph mode; `requires_piecewise_for_cudagraph` reports it to the engine so graph capture matches the per-layer connector protocol.
- `backend` selects mooncake (default), memcache, or yuanrong. Selecting the deprecated `MooncakeConnectorStoreV1` name logs a migration warning.
- `validate_mooncake_layerwise_topology` rejects PP/PCP/DCP greater than 1 for Mooncake block-key layerwise, because those coordinates are not present in the block key ([`metadata.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/metadata.py#L43-L71)).

### Key identity

The pool is content-addressed but not *only* content-addressed. A key is a model name plus every coordinate that changes the bytes ([`metadata.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/metadata.py#L128-L193)):

```
{model}@pcp:{pcp_rank}@dcp:{dcp_rank}@head_or_tp_rank:{head_or_tp_rank}@pp_rank:{pp_rank}
@group:{kv_cache_group_id}@cache_role:{cache_role}@cache_family:{cache_family}@{chunk_hash}
```

`cache_role` separates KV from recurrent state that shares a chunk hash; `cache_family` distinguishes compressed hybrid layouts. `PoolKey.split_layers` turns one chunk key into per-layer `LayerPoolKey`s, which is how layerwise transfer addresses a single layer of a chunk. Two independent ranking decisions hide inside `head_or_tp_rank`: when the model has fewer KV heads than TP ranks (`num_kv_head < tp_size`), several ranks share one key slot and only every `tp_size // num_kv_head`-th rank saves.

Mooncake layerwise uses a different, one-object-per-block-and-saving-rank key (`make_layerwise_block_key`), and `is_block_key_layerwise` is true **only** for `use_layerwise and backend == "mooncake"`. Keeping that flag backend-specific is deliberate: Memcache also stores one object per block, but its layerwise path goes through the backend protocol registry and uses GVA allocation, so mixing the two data planes must not be possible.

### Scheduler side: hit masks, not a hit length

A pool hit is only useful if *every* cache group can actually reach the bytes, so the scheduler does not compute a single hit length. `AscendStoreCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit` returns **per-group boolean masks plus a hit length**, and the masks are derived from a `BlockPool`-duck-typed `ExternalCachedBlockPool` that answers existence per `(group_id, hash)` ([`coordinator.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/coordinator.py#L34-L210)):

- Groups with identical effective specs are merged into one `attention_groups` entry; full-attention groups sort first.
- `_reachable_masks` consults the per-spec block manager (`SlidingWindowManager` and friends) to ask *which* blocks of a chunk are reachable at all, honouring a `retention_interval` for store masks. A group whose cache family has no reachability limits gets `None`, meaning "all blocks apply".
- `lookup_mask` is the mask used to ask the store which blocks exist; `store_mask` decides which of them are worth writing; `load_mask` decides which of a known hit are worth loading.

`KVPoolScheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens` then applies the scheduler's own correction rules on top of the raw hit ([`pool_scheduler.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/pool_scheduler.py#L627-L740)): it floors the prompt to the transfer granularity when partial chunks are discarded, trims the hit back by one LCM block when Eagle/MTP would rewrite the generation point, never lets the hit cover the entire request (leaving one token to compute), and — in layerwise mode — sets `can_load` even when vLLM already has local cached tokens, because layerwise transfer loads data that is *not* in HBM.

The lookup itself has two modes. Non-layerwise schedulers ask a worker-side server over ZMQ IPC: `LookupKeyClient.lookup` sends `(token_len, group_ids, hbm_hit_tokens, hashes)` to a socket path derived from `lookup_rpc_port` (legacy `mooncake_rpc_port` is accepted with a warning) plus the DP rank, and `LookupKeyServer` in worker rank 0 answers with a single 4-byte hit-token count ([`pool_scheduler.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/pool_scheduler.py#L1215-L1268), [`ascend_store_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/ascend_store_connector.py#L378-L424)). Layerwise and block-key layerwise schedulers instead resolve hits through the coordinator, which is why the coordinator owns the mask logic rather than the worker.

### Backends: a registry with an opt-in protocol

Backends are looked up in a plain dict — `mooncake`, `memcache`, `yuanrong` — mapping to a class name and module path, so adding a backend is a registry entry plus a `Backend` subclass ([`backend/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/backend/__init__.py#L22-L57)). The interesting part is that **the layerwise protocol lives in the backend module itself**: a backend opts in by carrying a `layerwise_protocol` marker and exposing module-level `make_full_key`, `make_partial_key`, `make_hit_check_keys`, and `extract_layout_config`. Generic layers resolve the module through `get_layerwise_protocol()` and never import a backend by name — which is also why Mooncake, whose module pulls heavy top-level imports, is never imported on that path.

`Backend` declares the extension surface every backend must satisfy: `register_buffer(ptrs, lengths)`, `exists(keys)`, and an optional ladder of batch primitives (`batch_alloc`, `batch_add_lease`, `batch_put_start`, `batch_copy_put`, `batch_commit`, `batch_revoke`, `batch_get_start`, `batch_copy_get`, `batch_get_key_info`, `batch_write_finish`, `validate_layerwise_support`). Unimplemented primitives raise `NotImplementedError`, which is what makes a backend work for one transfer mode and fail loudly for another instead of silently degrading ([`backend/base.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/backend/base.py#L73-L140)). `requires_exists_before_put` is a per-backend hint that the connector must filter existing keys before writing.

### Worker side: layerwise buffer planning and the two thread classes

Layerwise transfer maps many logical cache-bearing layers onto fewer physical HBM buffers. `build_layerwise_cache_layout` turns three extra-config knobs into a concrete assignment ([`layerwise_cache_layout.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/layerwise_cache_layout.py#L128-L192)):

| Knob | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `layerwise_num_shared_buffers` | number of layers | Omitted ⇒ no reuse at all; setting it below the layer count creates shared buffers. |
| `layerwise_prefetch_layers` | `min(shared_buffers, 8)` | How many layer loads may be in flight. |
| `layerwise_independent_layers` | `[0]` | Layers that keep a dedicated buffer; `"all"` disables reuse entirely. |

The planner emits `storage_indices` (buffer → member layers, round-robin over the reused layers) and `prefetch_layer_map` (`layer N` reuses the buffer of `layer N - num_shared_buffers`), and validates that the requested shared count is at least 1 and that independent indices are in range. `has_layer_reuse` is the flag that decides whether the reuse gate machinery is needed at all.

At runtime the worker starts up to three thread classes, chosen by role and protocol ([`pool_worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/pool_worker.py#L524-L600)):

- `KVCacheStoreLayerSendingThread` for the GVA-based layerwise save path (Memcache protocol),
- `KVCacheStoreKeyLayerSendingThread` for the key-major layerwise save path,
- `KVCacheStoreLayerRecvingThread` for layerwise loads, shared by both save styles.

Sending threads only start when `is_kv_save_role(kv_role, consumer_is_to_put)` is true, i.e. for `kv_producer`, `kv_both`, or a consumer configured to put. A load-only consumer therefore has no send thread at all, which is also why `request_finished` can free blocks immediately in that configuration.

### The attention start gate: why layerwise transfer cannot start when the Python call site is reached

Layerwise loads must be in HBM before the layer's attention reads them, but issuing the H2D *too early* is equally wrong: the destination buffer's previous contents may still be read by a save or by a P/D peer. The repository solves this with a per-layer gate rather than with an unconditional stream dependency, because the dependency is on *where the compute stream actually is*, not on whether a CPU thread has reached a function call.

`AttentionComputeStartGate` is a condition variable plus one `torch.npu.Event` ([`attention_fence.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/attention_fence.py#L27-L91)):

- The attention path calls `record_attention_compute_start()` immediately before submitting the attention op. The gate records an event on the current compute stream, and only the **first** record wins (later records are dropped), so one gate corresponds to one layer boundary.
- A transfer thread calls `wait(timeout=10.0)`, which blocks until an event exists and then `event.synchronize()`s. Because the event was recorded *before* the attention op, the wait returns when the compute stream has reached the attention boundary.
- `reset_attention_compute_start_gate()` publishes a fresh gate and returns it, so each layer gets its own gate and a stale event can never satisfy a later layer.

The wiring on both sides is small and specific:

- `KVPoolWorker.wait_for_layer_load` resets the gate on every layer, then submits ready loads; `_submit_ready_layer_loads` attaches the current gate to a `LayerLoadTask` **only for layers other than the current one** — the current layer's load must be synchronous, so gating it would deadlock ([`pool_worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/pool_worker.py#L2145-L2208)).
- The receive thread honours the gate before issuing `m_store.get`, and also before the key-major range path ([`kv_transfer.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/kv_transfer.py#L1969-L1974)).
- On the compute side, `record_attention_compute_start()` is called from every attention implementation that participates — MLA, DSA, SFA, the CP variants, and the GDN op — which is what makes the gate work for non-SFA models too ([`mla_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/mla_v1.py#L1350), [`sfa_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py#L1728-L1737)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as KVPoolWorker
    participant RECV as RecvThread
    participant SEND as SendThread
    participant ATTN as Attention layer
    participant STORE as Backend
    W->>RECV: reset gate, submit loads for layer N and prefetches
    RECV->>STORE: load layer N, synchronous
    W->>ATTN: wait_for_layer_load N returns, run layer N
    ATTN->>SEND: on_kv_cache_written, queue layer N save
    SEND->>STORE: put layer N
    ATTN->>ATTN: record_attention_compute_start before the attention op
    RECV->>RECV: layer N plus 1 task wakes on the gate
    RECV->>STORE: load layer N plus 1 into the freed shared buffer
```

*The gate orders a prefetch load to start at the compute stream's attention boundary of the layer that just recorded it, not at the Python call site.*

Note the split of responsibilities in that diagram: `wait_for_layer_load` blocks the *current* layer, while the gate only ever gates *future* layers. Both mechanisms are needed; collapsing them into one wait either deadlocks the current layer or lets a prefetch race the save of the buffer it targets.

### Lifecycle, delayed free, and observability

Because a save is asynchronous, the scheduler cannot free a finished request's HBM blocks as soon as the request ends. `KVPoolScheduler.request_finished` returns `(True, None)` and records the blocks in a delayed-free set, which is only released when `update_finished_sending` reports the save completed ([`pool_scheduler.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/pool_scheduler.py#L1134-L1212)). Two cases deliberately free immediately:

- a `kv_consumer` without `consumer_is_to_put` never saves anything;
- **layerwise mode records no sending event**, so delaying the free would leak blocks outright. The comment in `request_finished_all_groups` says exactly this.

The hybrid-group counterpart, `request_finished_all_groups`, additionally clips sliding-window groups to their trailing `cdiv(sliding_window, block_size) + 1` blocks before counting, because those are the only blocks the pool can ever usefully hold.

Observability has three surfaces: `AscendStoreKVConnectorStats` records non-layerwise `get` durations and key counts plus the delayed-release gauges, exposed as `vllm:ascend_store_load_get_duration_seconds`, `vllm:ascend_store_load_get_keys_total`, `vllm:ascend_store_delayed_release_requests`, and `vllm:ascend_store_delayed_release_blocks` ([`metrics.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/metrics.py#L36-L140)); KV cache events are aggregated so only events common to **all** workers survive, which prevents a partially written chunk from being advertised ([`ascend_store_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/ascend_store_connector.py#L58-L89)); and load failures surface through `get_block_ids_with_load_errors`, which upstream turns into the configured `kv_load_failure_policy` (recompute or fail). See [Observability and Logging](../operations/observability-and-logging.md) for the profiling side.

### Composing with P/D: `AscendMultiConnector`

The store path is usually one of several connectors. `AscendMultiConnector` adds three behaviours to upstream `MultiConnector` that exist because the Ascend layerwise protocol has a *shared physical slot* ([`ascend_multi_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/ascend_multi_connector.py#L18-L199)):

1. **Slot-release providers run first, always.** A connector is a provider when it is a producer, has a worker, declares `supports_layerwise_buffer_reuse`, and exposes `wait_for_layer_reuse`. `save_kv_layer`, `on_kv_cache_written`, and the load path all iterate providers before siblings, so the ordering does not depend on the order the user listed connectors.
2. **One sink owns the wait.** If any connector accepts `set_external_slot_release_waiter`, the composite waiter is handed to it — `AscendStoreConnector` does accept it and consults it at layer entry — and provider `wait_for_layer_load` calls are then skipped as redundant. Without a sink, the providers keep their own layer-entry wait so shared slots are still protected.
3. **Preempted-request state wins.** `get_num_new_matched_tokens` walks the connectors looking for `has_preempted_request`, because recompute offload may hold an unhashed partial block that a prefix-cache connector cannot restore; that request is bound to the recompute connector regardless of configuration order. `update_state_after_alloc` then forwards real blocks only to the chosen connector and to any connector that opts in with `requires_full_blocks_on_update_after_alloc`; everyone else gets `blocks.new_empty()`.

`request_finished_all_groups` also enforces a global invariant: **at most one connector may produce KV transfer params**, and extra async saves are tracked per request. The slot-release ordering above is pinned by [`test_ascend_multi_connector.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/test_ascend_multi_connector.py#L69-L106), which asserts the exact call order `store-load, pd-save, store-save, pd-written, store-written`.

## Family C: model-level sparse KV offload

Sparse offload is the only family that changes what "KV cache" means. It applies to sparse-attention SFA/MLA models in the **Decode** stage of a P/D deployment, where per-token compute is too small to hide a full-layer transfer. The design instead keeps the entire main KV history in a pinned host pool and loads only the entries the indexer selects. `AscendSFAKVOffload`'s module docstring states the resulting data plane precisely ([`attention/sfa_kv_offload.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_kv_offload.py#L1-L20)):

- **decode**: no NPU main K/V cache at all (only the indexer K cache). The current token's K/V is produced compute-only and committed D2H; top-k misses are loaded H2D into the resident top-k buffer and a single resident SFA attention runs.
- **prefill/mixed**: only reachable with `keep_device_kv_cache=True`, i.e. the debug PD-colocate path; `exec_kv` writes the NPU paged cache as usual and then commits the written rows D2H.
- **fused overlap** (`use_fused_overlap`): replaces resident onload + SFA with `npu_fused_sparse_attention_overlap`, reading full KV from the shared CPU pool while keeping a selection buffer on NPU.

### Configuration gates are the contract

`SparseKVOffloadConfig` is small — `enabled`, `topk_buffer_size` (4096), `dram_size_per_dp_GB` (128), `keep_device_kv_cache` (false), `use_fused_overlap` (false), plus a derived `topk` — but its `_validate_preconditions` is where every assumption is enforced before any memory is allocated ([`ascend_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py#L1376-L1442)). A change that relaxes any of these without relaxing the corresponding data path will produce silent corruption, not a crash:

| Gate | Rejection | Why the data path depends on it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `compress_ratios` present on `hf_text_config` | "don't support compress now" | Compressed MLA holds fewer physical rows than logical tokens, and the offload pool is addressed by logical slots. |
| no `index_topk` on `hf_text_config` | "only support sparse attention model" | Without an indexer there is no top-k selection, so there is nothing to load sparsely. |
| `pcp_size * dcp_size > 1` | "don't support context parallel now" | CP splits a sequence across ranks, so one rank does not own the whole host pool it addresses. |
| `pipeline_parallel_size > 1` | "don't support pipeline parallel now" | Layer-local host ranges are computed per rank from the full layer count. |
| not a PD consumer and `keep_device_kv_cache` false | `AssertionError` | A Decode node never stages prefill KV; the debug colocate path is the only exception. |
| `use_v2_model_runner` | "doesn't support model_runner_v2 now" | The offload metadata hooks live in Model Runner V1's prepare-inputs path. |
| `topk_buffer_size < topk` | must be `>= topk` | The resident buffer must be able to hold one row's top-k selection. |
| `enable_sparse_sfa_c8` | `NotImplementedError` | The main cache must be BF16; C8 is only supported for the device-resident indexer cache (`enable_sparse_li_c8`). |

Two more gates are checked at runtime rather than at config parse, and both are equally load-bearing: `init_sparse_kv_offload_manager` raises unless the device is **A3** ([`sparse_kv_offload_manager.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/sparse_kv_offload_manager.py#L1642-L1664)), and the manager asserts a single KV cache group — hybrid layouts are not supported — and a BF16 main cache, then requires `topk_buffer_size % block_size == 0` ([`sparse_kv_offload_manager.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/sparse_kv_offload_manager.py#L727-L768)). `SfaRemoteD2HConnector` adds the cross-process half of the same contract: the producer (P) must run with the feature **off** and the consumer (D) with it **on**, because the two sides have asymmetric cache layouts ([`sfa_pd_rd2h/connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/sfa_pd_rd2h/connector.py#L73-L86)).

### Memory: three limits, one plan

Sparse offload enlarges the memory the scheduler can see, which means the block count is no longer a simple `free_memory // page_size`. `plan_sparse_kv_offload_memory` computes three independent bounds and takes the minimum ([`sparse_kv_offload_manager.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/sparse_kv_offload_manager.py#L200-L295)):

- **npu** — `available_device_memory // npu_page_size`, where `npu_page_size` is the device-resident part of a block (the whole block only when `keep_device_kv_cache` keeps the main cache on device).
- **dram** — `(dram_size_per_dp_GB - alignment_reserve) // host_page_size`. The reserve is `3 × 2 MiB` per host layer: one alignment round-up for the raw buffer base and one tail pad for each of the two aligned tensors.
- **workload** — `max_blocks_per_request * max_num_seqs + 1`, the null block included. This is the active-demand bound: it is what stops a large `dram_size_per_dp_GB` from letting the pool grow past what the scheduler could ever assign.

The winner is reported as `limiting_factor` and logged with all three numbers by `NPUWorker._apply_kv_offload_decode_memory_constraints`, which replaces the ordinary budget with `final_planner_bytes` ([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L517-L551)); see [Performance Tuning](../operations/performance-tuning.md) for how this slots into the rest of the budget pipeline. A DRAM bound below the NPU bound logs a targeted warning suggesting a larger `dram_size_per_dp_GB` ([`tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/test_sparse_kv_offload_manager.py`](../../tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/test_sparse_kv_offload_manager.py#L68-L114) pins all three cases, including the warning text).

`SparseKVOffloadManager.__init__` then cross-checks the plan against the real allocation: if the aligned CPU pool exceeds `dram_size_per_dp_GB` it raises instead of clamping silently, and it initializes the external `offload` allocator with `reserve_size` for every rank and `alloc_size` only on TP 0, followed by a TP-group barrier. A per-layer K/V cache tuple of exactly six tensors is then registered: NPU K, NPU V, CPU K, CPU V, top-k buffer K, top-k buffer V. Layers whose name contains `indexer` are excluded and stay device-resident, which is why LIC8 indexer quantization remains compatible ([`sparse_kv_offload_manager.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/sparse_kv_offload_manager.py#L36-L48), [`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4867-L4895)).

### The decode loop

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    KV["compute current-token K and V only"] --> D2H["TP0 writes rows D2H into the shared host pool at slot_mapping"]
    D2H --> BC["TP broadcast: other ranks wait for TP0 D2H"]
    BC --> IDX["indexer selects top-k logical positions"]
    IDX --> LRU["LRU residency: mark hits, assign miss slots, pick evictions"]
    LRU --> H2D["sparse_copy issues H2D for miss rows only"]
    H2D --> REMAP["remap logical top-k to physical resident slots"]
    REMAP --> SFA["resident SFA attention"]
```

*One decode step: transfer volume tracks top-k misses, not sequence length.*

Mechanically, in [`sfa_kv_offload.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_kv_offload.py#L346-L394) the decode branch calls `manager.offload_new_kv` with `k`/`v` only and never touches a paged NPU cache; the prefill branch is guarded by `_check_device_kv_cache_exist()`, which raises if a prefill/mixed batch arrives without `keep_device_kv_cache`, because a real Decode node never sees one. `offload_new_kv` writes on the current stream by default and only uses the dedicated save stream when a graph is being captured with `use_fused_overlap` ([`sparse_kv_offload_manager.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/sparse_kv_offload_manager.py#L1077-L1200)). `_offload_new_kv_on_current_stream` enforces the TP discipline: **only TP 0 writes new decode rows**, because decode-produced K/V is replicated across TP ranks; other ranks' contributions arrive through the P/D pull path into disjoint parts of the same shared pool.

`onload_topk_kv` is where the LRU and the copy are fused into one descriptor submission ([`sparse_kv_offload_manager.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/sparse_kv_offload_manager.py#L1215-L1336)):

- Layer 0 (and the MTP layer, whose metadata can differ) copies the per-request metadata to host: block table, `adler32` request id hashes, stable prefix lengths, and — under speculative decoding — an expanded block table indexed by token-to-request. Interior layers reuse the previous layer's result via `skip_topk`, applying a single base-address delta; the code asserts the K/V gvas and address deltas are identical, which is why the allocator places the two tensors together.
- The LRU residency op produces miss counts/tokens/slots plus `gvas_buffer`, `addr_buffer`, `size_buffer`, and `num_tokens_buffer`; then a **TP broadcast of an empty int8 tensor** serializes "TP0 has finished its D2H" before every rank issues `offload.sparse_copy`. The comment records why a barrier cannot be used: it cannot be captured in a graph.
- `current_slots_npu` is then updated so the attention kernel reads the resident buffer, and residency metadata is retained for the next step.

Under graph capture the host-side LRU runs through `torch_npu.npu._launch_host_func` after subscribing the compute stream, so the same code path serves eager and captured execution ([`sparse_kv_offload_manager.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/sparse_kv_offload_manager.py#L1307-L1321)).

With `use_fused_overlap` the planner can also be run *externally*: `prepare_fused_overlap_external_plan`, `allocate_fused_overlap_membership_map`, `get_fused_overlap_cpu_kv_inputs`, `inject_current_kv_into_selection`, and `wait_for_current_kv_writeback` form a small protocol for running the LRU on a side stream and feeding a fused attention kernel that reads full KV from the CPU pool.
