Those entry points validate input shapes and plan ownership aggressively (`_validate_fused_overlap_external_plan_inputs`) because a mismatched plan silently corrupts attention rather than failing. [`tests/ut/kv_offload/test_sparse_kv_offload_external_plan.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/test_sparse_kv_offload_external_plan.py) is the reference for that protocol.

## Invariants a change must preserve

| Invariant | Consequence of breaking it | Where it is enforced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ascend split K/V must be canonicalized before any offload copy | V or the scale tail is silently omitted, or a page offset is applied per component | `_canonicalize_split_cache` + `AscendOffloadingConnectorWorker` |
| A D2H copy must wait for the model stream | A partially written block is offloaded | `SingleDirectionNPUOffloadingHandler.transfer_async` |
| Only future layers may be gated on the attention start gate | Current-layer deadlock or a prefetch racing a save | `_submit_ready_layer_loads`, `wait_for_layer_load` |
| Exactly one connector may emit KV transfer params | The engine applies the wrong transfer state | `AscendMultiConnector.request_finished_all_groups` |
| Providers must close the slot gate before siblings publish | Prefill overwrites a buffer a decoder is still reading | `save_kv_layer` / `on_kv_cache_written` ordering |
| A user "no decision yet" must be `None`, not `0` | Recompute-preserved state is dropped for a pooled hit | `RecomputeCPUOffloadScheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens` |
| Layerwise mode must free HBM blocks immediately | Delayed-free entries leak, because no sending event is ever recorded | `request_finished_all_groups` |
| Sparse offload config gates must hold before allocation | Wrong block count, wrong page geometry, or an unsupported cache layout | `SparseKVOffloadConfig._validate_preconditions`, runtime asserts in `SparseKVOffloadManager` |
| Sparse prefill D2H requires `keep_device_kv_cache` | A Decode node would need an NPU paged main cache it never allocates | `_check_device_kv_cache_exist`, `_offload_new_kv_on_current_stream` |

## Tests worth reading before changing any of this

- [`tests/ut/kv_offload/test_native_cpu_offload.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/test_native_cpu_offload.py) — spec registration through the upstream factory, split K/V and aligned Mamba canonicalization, and the two failure cases (non-contiguous payload, extra physical blocks hiding a separate value cache).
- [`tests/ut/kv_offload/test_npu_offload_spec.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/test_npu_offload_spec.py) — direction routing of store/load, handler-shutdown-before-mmap ordering, and both shared-region view APIs.
- [`tests/ut/kv_offload/test_recompute_cpu_offload.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/test_recompute_cpu_offload.py) — metadata aggregation, scheduler forwarding, and the preempt store/load event protocol.
- [`tests/ut/kv_offload/test_ascend_multi_connector.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/test_ascend_multi_connector.py) — slot-release ordering and allocation fan-out.
- [`tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/`](../../tests/ut/distributed/ascend_store/) — coordinator masks, pool scheduler hit rules, layerwise layout, backends, metrics, and pool worker (including the `external_slot_release_waiter` fallback in `wait_for_layer_load`).
- [`tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/test_sparse_kv_offload_manager.py`](../../tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/sparse_kv_offload/test_sparse_kv_offload_manager.py) — the A3 rejection and the three memory-plan limits.
- [`tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py`](../../tests/ut/test_ascend_config.py#L716-L757) — `SparseKVOffloadConfig` type coercion, unknown-key rejection, and the disabled-path early return.

nodes.title: Workflow: Prefill-Decode Disaggregation and KV Transfer Connectors
nodes.description: How vllm-ascend pairs a prefill and a decode instance - the connector registry that maps kv_connector names to Ascend implementation classes, the handshake metadata exchanged at startup and per request, the pull/push/layerwise data paths built on the Mooncake transfer engine and MemFabric, and the role-dependent gates (kv_producer versus kv_consumer, preemption stores, kv_load_failure_policy).
nodes.body:
# Workflow: Prefill-Decode Disaggregation and KV Transfer Connectors

Prefill/decode disaggregation splits one logical engine into two fleets: a **producer** (`kv_role: kv_producer`, the prefiller) that runs the prompt and keeps the resulting KV, and a **consumer** (`kv_role: kv_consumer`, the decoder) that pulls that KV and generates. Everything that makes this work on Ascend lives in `vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer`, and the split of responsibilities is deliberate:

- **The request lifecycle stays upstream.** Block allocation, `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`, delayed free, prefix-cache bookkeeping, and the `get_num_new_matched_tokens` / `update_state_after_alloc` / `build_connector_meta` / `request_finished` scheduler protocol are vLLM's. Ascend connectors implement those hooks; they do not replace the scheduler.
- **Only the transfer is Ascend-specific.** Worker-side data movement goes through the Mooncake `TransferEngine` (initialized as `ascend` / `P2PHANDSHAKE`) or MemFabric, over per-rank ZMQ control sockets and 2 MiB-aligned NPU allocations.

This page covers the P/D paths. For CPU/tiering offload, pooled KV store reuse, and model-level sparse offload see [KV Offloading, Tiering, and KV Store](./kv-offload-and-store.md); for the block/page vocabulary see [KV Cache Specs, Block Layout, and Placement](../concepts/kv-cache-and-block-layout.md); for where these allocations are created see [KV Cache Sizing, Allocation, Reshape, and Graph Capture](./kv-cache-initialization.md).

## The connector registry is the authoritative map

There is exactly one entry point. The `ascend_kv_connector` plugin entry point resolves to `vllm_ascend.register_connector()`, which applies the global patch and then delegates to `vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer.register_connector()` ([`vllm_ascend/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/__init__.py#L74-L81)). That function edits `KVConnectorFactory` and `OffloadingSpecFactory` directly, so the table below — not the docs, not the example scripts — is what a `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector": ...}'` value actually resolves to ([`kv_transfer/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/__init__.py#L21-L129)).

| `kv_connector` name | Module | Class | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MooncakeConnectorV1` | `kv_p2p.mooncake_connector` | `MooncakeConnector` | added |
| `MooncakeConnectorV2` | `kv_p2p.mooncake.connector` | `MooncakeConnector` (= `MooncakePullConnector`) | added |
| `MooncakePullConnector` | `kv_p2p.mooncake.connector` | `MooncakePullConnector` | added |
| `MooncakeHybridConnector` | `kv_p2p.mooncake_hybrid_connector` | `MooncakeConnector` | added |
| `MooncakeLayerwiseConnector` | `kv_p2p.mooncake_layerwise_connector` | `MooncakeLayerwiseConnector` | added |
| `SfaRemoteD2HConnector` | `kv_p2p.sfa_pd_rd2h.connector` | `SfaRemoteD2HConnector` | added |
| `MultiConnector` | `ascend_multi_connector` | `AscendMultiConnector` | **replaced** |
| `AscendStoreConnector` / `MooncakeConnectorStoreV1` | `kv_pool.ascend_store.ascend_store_connector` | `AscendStoreConnector` | added |
| `UCMConnector` | `kv_pool.ucm_connector.connector` | `UCMConnectorV1` | added |
| `OffloadingConnector`, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, `RecomputeCPUOffloadConnector` | `kv_pool.*` | `Ascend*` variants | replaced / added |
| `CPUOffloadingSpec`, `TieringOffloadingSpec` | `kv_pool.kv_offload.native.npu` | `NPUOffloadingSpec`, `NPUTieringOffloadingSpec` | **replaced** |

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ENTRY["vllm_ascend.register_connector"] --> PATCH["_ensure_global_patch"]
    PATCH --> REG["kv_transfer.register_connector"]
    REG --> REPLACE["pop upstream name, register Ascend class"]
    REG --> ADD["register Ascend-only names"]
    REPLACE --> MULTI["MultiConnector becomes AscendMultiConnector"]
    REPLACE --> SPEC["CPU and Tiering offloading specs become NPU specs"]
    REPLACE --> OFFLOAD["OffloadingConnector and SimpleCPUOffloadConnector"]
    ADD --> V1["MooncakeConnectorV1: block-granular push-pull"]
    ADD --> V2["MooncakeConnectorV2 and MooncakePullConnector: scheduler-mediated pull"]
    ADD --> HYB["MooncakeHybridConnector: attention plus Mamba"]
    ADD --> LW["MooncakeLayerwiseConnector: per-layer push"]
    ADD --> SFA["SfaRemoteD2HConnector: decode-offload pull"]
    ADD --> STORE["AscendStoreConnector and UCMConnector"]
```

*One registration function produces two kinds of edit: names that are rebound to Ascend classes and names that only exist here.*

### Why some upstream names are popped first

Two different justifications are recorded in the source, and conflating them hides real constraints.

**Layout: Ascend keeps K/V as separate tensors.** `OffloadingConnector` is replaced because *"vLLM's native offloading worker assumes attention KV caches are packed into one Tensor. Ascend keeps K/V as separate tensors, so replace only the connector's worker-side canonicalization boundary while reusing the upstream scheduler, manager, metrics, and transfer lifecycle"* ([`kv_transfer/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/__init__.py#L91-L101)). The same reasoning drives the offloading *spec* overrides, whose comment states the invariant for the whole package: *"The scheduler-side managers stay upstream; only worker-side transfers use torch.npu streams and the Ascend batched memcpy op"* ([`kv_transfer/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/__init__.py#L21-L36)). Details of that canonicalization are on [KV Offloading, Tiering, and KV Store](./kv-offload-and-store.md).

**Composition: P/D connectors share a physical KV slot.** `MultiConnector` is replaced because the layerwise P/D connectors expose per-layer buffer reuse: a producer must finish reading a slot before a sibling connector writes it, at most one child may emit KV transfer params, and a child that needs real block ids (rather than `new_empty()`) must say so. Those behaviours cannot be expressed by delegating to upstream's fan-out, so `AscendMultiConnector` overrides them ([`ascend_multi_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/ascend_multi_connector.py#L41-L67), [`#L175-L199`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/ascend_multi_connector.py#L175-L199)).

The P/D transfer connectors themselves are all *net-new names*. There is no upstream Mooncake path to canonicalize, which is why their worker side can hold per-tensor metadata (base address, block stride, block length, block shape, block-size scale) instead of a packed-buffer view.

`MooncakePushConnector` exists as a declared-but-unimplemented class in the V2 package, and its constructor raises `NotImplementedError`. `MooncakeConnector` is a plain alias for the pull connector, pinned by test ([`mooncake/connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/connector.py#L243-L256), [`test_connector.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/test_connector.py#L26-L28)).

## The handshake: what P and D must agree on before any byte moves

Every connector splits into a scheduler half and a worker half, created by role in the connector constructor ([`mooncake_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L1608-L1624), [`mooncake/connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/connector.py#L224-L241)). The scheduler half decides *which* requests transfer; the worker half owns the transfer engine, the registered buffers, and the background threads. The two exchange structured metadata in two stages.

**Stage 1 — startup handshake (engine-mediated).** Each worker publishes its cache geometry via `get_handshake_metadata()`; vLLM carries that out of band to the peer's scheduler, which installs it via `set_xfer_handshake_metadata()` (and the PP-aware variant, `set_xfer_handshake_metadata_pp_aware()`). What travels is not a block list but an address table:

| Connector | Metadata type | What it carries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MooncakeConnectorV1` | `MooncakeAgentMetadata` | `engine_id`, `te_rpc_port`, `kv_group2layeridx`, `block_size`, `num_blocks`, per-layer `kv_caches_base_addr`, `block_lens`, `block_strides`, `block_size_scale`, `local_ip`, `handshake_port` |
| `MooncakeConnectorV2` / `MooncakePullConnector` | `MooncakeTransferMetadata` → merged into `MooncakePPTransferMetadata` / `MooncakeTransferMetadataGroups` | the same fields plus `layer_names`, `layer_block_sizes`, `group_indices`, `block_shapes`, and a per-TP-rank `MooncakeTPTransferMetadata` holding `layer_indices`, addresses, `te_rpc_port`, `handshake_port` |
| `MooncakeLayerwiseConnector` | `MooncakeAgentMetadata` (`layer_metadata: dict[str, LayerMetadata]`) | per-layer `tensor_group_idx`, base addresses, `block_len`, `block_size_scale` |
| `SfaRemoteD2HConnector` | MemFabric HBM/GVA registration | main MLA KV GVA plus indexer KV, split per TP rank |

`MooncakeTransferMetadata.__post_init__` validates itself: every per-layer field must have one entry per layer name, and every nested per-tensor field must have one entry per address in that layer. A mismatch raises instead of producing a wrong address table ([`mooncake/metadata.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/metadata.py#L16-L71)).

**Stage 2 — per-request handshake (in the HTTP response).** The scheduler's `request_finished` returns `(delay_free_blocks, kv_transfer_params)`; upstream forwards that dict to the client, and the P/D proxy attaches it to the decode request. In V1 and V2 that dict contains `remote_block_ids`, `remote_engine_id`, `remote_request_id`, `remote_host`, `remote_port` and the remote `pcp`/`dcp`/`tp` sizes ([`mooncake_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L2042-L2057), [`pull_scheduler.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/pull_scheduler.py#L634-L644)). The reference proxy is the canonical example of this split: the prefiller is called with `do_remote_decode=True` and `max_tokens: 1`, and the returned `kv_transfer_params` are copied verbatim onto the decoder request ([`load_balance_proxy_server_example.py`](../../examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py#L818-L834), [`#L963-L966`](../../examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py#L963-L966)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Proxy as P/D proxy
    participant PS as P scheduler
    participant PW as P worker
    participant DW as D worker
    participant DS as D scheduler
    Proxy->>PS: prompt with do_remote_decode true, max_tokens 1
    PS->>PW: prefill step, publish KV
    PS-->>Proxy: response with kv_transfer_params
    Proxy->>DS: same prompt plus kv_transfer_params
    DS->>DW: start_load_kv with local and remote block ids
    DW->>PS: get_meta_msg on the producer control port
    PS-->>DW: merged TP and PP transfer metadata
    DW->>PW: batch_transfer_sync_read per block range
    DW-->>DS: get_finished reports finished_recving
    DS->>PS: done_recving_msg
    PS-->>DS: ACK, producer blocks may be freed
```

*The Mooncake V2 pull path: metadata comes from the producer scheduler's control port, the reads are issued by the decode worker, and release is acknowledged scheduler to scheduler.*

### Where each control port lives

Ports are derived, not configured per rank, and the two generations place the scheduler socket differently — a difference worth understanding before changing `kv_port`.

- **V1 workers** listen at `kv_port + dp_rank * tp_size * pp_size * pcp_size + device_index`, where `device_index = (pp_rank * pcp_size + pcp_rank) * tp_size + tp_rank`. The `KVCacheSendingThread` binds a ZMQ `ROUTER` at that port and serves `GET_META_MSG` / `DONE_RECVING_MSG` ([`mooncake_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L2172-L2182), [`#L302-L331`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L302-L331)).
- **V2** gives the *scheduler* one control port per DP rank placed **after** the entire worker handshake range: `kv_port + max_device_id + dp_rank`. The comment states the invariant — the worker range is `[kv_port, kv_port + dp_size * pp_size * pcp_size * tp_size)`, so the scheduler port must sit outside it ([`mooncake/base_scheduler.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/base_scheduler.py#L76-L82)). `MooncakeSchedulerSendingThread` then serves the merged metadata and collects `DONE_RECVING_MSG`; `MooncakeSchedulerRecvingThread` sends the completion and requires the `ACK` ([`pull_scheduler.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/pull_scheduler.py#L303-L339), [`#L404-L419`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/pull_scheduler.py#L404-L419)).
- **Layerwise** derives `kv_port + dp_rank * tp_size` for the scheduler and `+ tp_rank` for the worker socket ([`mooncake_layerwise_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_layerwise_connector.py#L870-L874), [`#L1226-L1231`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_layerwise_connector.py#L1226-L1231)).

Operationally the base port must clear the range that AscendDirectTransport allocates randomly: `[20000, 20000 + npu_per_node * 1000)`. The deployment guide therefore recommends `kv_port >= 28000` for 8-NPU nodes and `>= 36000` for 16-NPU nodes, and names the symptom of getting it wrong — intermittent `zmq.error.ZMQError: Address already in use` at startup ([`pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.md`](../../docs/source/tutorials/features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.md#L277-L288)).

## The three data planes

### Block-granular push and pull (`MooncakeConnectorV1`)

`MooncakeConnectorV1` is the largest and most feature-complete connector. Its worker owns two thread classes: `KVCacheSendingThread` on the producer, which answers metadata requests and — after the decoder reports `DONE_RECVING_MSG` — accounts the request complete so its blocks can be freed, and `KVCacheRecvingThread` on the consumer, which fetches the remote address table once per `(host, handshake_port)`, maps local block ids to remote block ids, and issues `batch_transfer_sync_read` on the shared transfer engine ([`mooncake_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L1466-L1500), [`#L370-L397`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L370-L397)).

The topology rules are enforced at construction, and they are the most common source of startup failures:

- **Prefill TP ≥ decode TP**, and the prefill TP must be an integer multiple of the decode TP ([`mooncake_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L2109-L2115), [`ascend_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py#L718-L737)). When they are unequal, `tp_num_need_pulls = num_decode_block_heads // num_prefill_block_heads` tells the decoder how many producer ranks jointly hold one of its head shards ([`#L2201-L2206`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L2201-L2206)).
- **PCP is producer-only.** A consumer with `prefill_context_parallel_size > 1` raises with an explicit message ([`#L2141-L2145`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L2141-L2145)); PP and PCP cannot both exceed 1.
- **Decode PP must be 1**; prefill PP is supported, with `pp_layer_partition` mapping global layer indices per stage ([`#L2210-L2230`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L2210-L2230)).

Two mechanisms exist only because P and D may shard heads differently. On the producer side, `kv_alltoall_and_rearrange` regroups K and V across the prefill-tensor-parallel group so the layout matches what the decoder expects; the all-to-all runs on `_P_TP`, a group that exists only when `pd_head_ratio > 1` and the engine is a producer ([`parallel_state.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/parallel_state.py#L58-L86), [`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/utils/utils.py#L50-L77)). On the consumer side the inverse reshape is done inline with `torch_npu.npu_scatter_pa_kv_cache` after transposing the head dimension ([`mooncake_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L1421-L1444)).

Hybrid attention+Mamba models need prompt truncation rather than plain block copying, because the decoder recomputes the last token and must start from `h(N-1)`: the producer drops the final prompt token and sets `max_tokens = 1`, guarded by `_p_side_truncated` so a preempted-and-rescheduled request is not truncated twice ([`mooncake_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L1866-L1897)). `MooncakeHybridConnector` is the same architecture specialized for attention+Mamba pairs (`ssm_sizes` in its metadata) ([`mooncake_hybrid_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_hybrid_connector.py#L83-L107)).

### Scheduler-mediated pull (`MooncakeConnectorV2` / `MooncakePullConnector`)

V2 is the same pull idea with the control plane hoisted into the scheduler, which buys PP and layer-split correctness:

- `MooncakeBaseConnectorScheduler` refuses to construct unless exactly one of `is_kv_producer` / `is_kv_consumer` is true, and currently asserts `pcp_size == 1` ([`mooncake/base_scheduler.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/base_scheduler.py#L44-L74)).
- `MooncakeSchedulerSendingThread._merge_metadata_by_pp_rank` merges every TP worker's metadata into one PP-wide layer table. It validates that all PP and TP ranks are present, that `block_size` and `num_blocks` agree across TP ranks, and that duplicate layer names carry identical structural signatures. When TP ranks own *different* layer sets (layer split), it records `use_kv_pp = True`, pads each rank's address table to the PP-union layer order, and rejects layer split combined with DCP ([`pull_scheduler.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/pull_scheduler.py#L113-L284)).
- The decoder fetches that blob once per remote engine from the producer scheduler port, caches it in a `SizedDict`, derives the remote TP candidate groups, and only then issues `batch_transfer_sync_read` per remote PP/TP bucket ([`pull_worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/pull_worker.py#L1319-L1357), [`#L1239-L1284`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/pull_worker.py#L1239-L1284)).
- `MooncakeBaseConnector.get_required_kvcache_layout()` returns `"HND"` for non-MLA models specifically to avoid a reformat before D2D transfer, and `None` under MLA where the head dimension does not exist ([`mooncake/connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/connector.py#L83-L98)).

`MooncakeConnectorV2` and `MooncakePullConnector` are the only P/D connectors in the shared-backing allowlist of the KV-cache allocator, which is what lets them reuse the standardized attention/Mamba backing allocation while retaining per-layer transfer metadata ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4532-L4549)).

### Per-layer push (`MooncakeLayerwiseConnector`)

Layerwise transfer starts the copy for layer *N* as soon as layer *N*'s KV has been scattered, instead of waiting for the request to finish. It is the connector with the most cross-cutting requirements:

- **Scheduler side** binds a metaserver client and, on the decode side of the handshake, POSTs the request's transfer parameters to `metaserver` (with up to three retries) unless `do_virtual` is set. That is how a layerwise decoder learns the prefiller's per-layer metadata before the prefiller has finished the request ([`mooncake_layerwise_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_layerwise_connector.py#L1015-L1044), [`#L1151-L1162`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_layerwise_connector.py#L1151-L1162)).
- **`request_finished` returns `(False, None)` on both sides.** The comment says why: layerwise push needs no delayed free, because the send thread's per-layer reuse gate — not an end-of-request event — is what protects the source buffers ([`#L1164-L1186`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_layerwise_connector.py#L1164-L1186)).
- **The reuse gate** maps each layer to the physical storage slots it touches and keeps one `threading.Event` per slot, initially set. `_mark_layer_reuse_pending` clears them, `_complete_layer_reuse` sets them (recording any error), and `wait_for_layer_reuse` blocks with a periodic log until the slot is released — raising if the send thread died or the transfer reported an error ([`#L1284-L1336`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_layerwise_connector.py#L1284-L1336)). This gate is what `AscendMultiConnector` composes through `supports_layerwise_buffer_reuse`.
- **Resharding and quantization** are handled on a dedicated `torch.npu.Stream`: `pd_head_ratio > 1`, `enable_kv_quant`, or `enable_c8_quant` cause the layer's group to be marked for resharding, with a staging `k_buffer`/`v_buffer` aligned to 2 MiB ([`#L1252-L1262`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_layerwise_connector.py#L1252-L1262), [`#L1338-L1360`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_layerwise_connector.py#L1338-L1360)).
- **Unsupported layouts fail loudly.** A sparse-SFA-C8 packed main cache raises `NotImplementedError`, as does a group whose components have differing block-size scales (which covers DCP-replicated indexer caches) ([`#L1398-L1433`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_layerwise_connector.py#L1398-L1433)).

Hybrid attention+Mamba is handled differently from V1: instead of truncating the prompt token, `_trim_hybrid_remote_block_ids` drops the trailing block when `prompt_len % block_size == 1`, and `_truncate_request_for_hybrid_prefill` is guarded by `need_truncate` — computed from the *actual* cache groups rather than a config flag ([`#L881-L950`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_layerwise_connector.py#L881-L950)).

### Decode-offload pull (`SfaRemoteD2HConnector`)

This connector is asymmetric by design: the consumer is a Sparse-SFA decode node whose main MLA KV lives in a pinned host pool owned by `SparseKVOffloadManager`, so there is no NPU paged main cache to pull into. The constructor encodes that contract as assertions — the producer must run with `sparse_kv_offload_config.enabled == false` and the consumer with `true` ([`sfa_pd_rd2h/connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/sfa_pd_rd2h/connector.py#L71-L86)).

The data plane is a *pull notification* protocol, not an RDMA push: the producer registers HBM KV with MemFabric and whose send thread advertises `READ_READY_BATCH` per layer; the consumer's read thread pulls the main MLA KV into the CPU pool and the indexer KV into rank-local HBM, then answers `READ_DONE` or `READ_FAILED` ([`sfa_pd_rd2h/protocol.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/sfa_pd_rd2h/protocol.py#L13-L46), [`sfa_pd_rd2h/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/sfa_pd_rd2h/worker.py#L1-L13)). Layer ownership is split: `main_group_id` and `indexer_group_id` are inferred from layer names rather than assumed, because SFA layouts may put the indexer in its own group or in the main group.

Two invariants make this safe. `wait_for_layer_load` is a no-op on the consumer but on the producer blocks until the decoder has finished reading every storage slot the layer will overwrite ([`sfa_pd_rd2h/connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/sfa_pd_rd2h/connector.py#L168-L186)). And for unequal TP the producer maps its rank onto the decode rank that consumes it, adjusts `remote_port` by that rank, and records `tp_ratio`/`group_member_idx` so a single decode rank waits for every contributing producer rank ([`sfa_pd_rd2h/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/sfa_pd_rd2h/worker.py#L508-L558)). The sparse-offload half of this contract is documented in [KV Offloading, Tiering, and KV Store](./kv-offload-and-store.md).

## Lifecycle: waiting states, delayed free, and deadlines

The engine's request state machine does the sequencing; the connector only reports facts. On the consumer, `get_num_new_matched_tokens` returns the number of prompt tokens that will arrive from the peer plus `load_async = True`, and upstream parks the request in `RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` until `finished_recving` appears in `KVConnectorOutput` ([`test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py#L37-L126)). That test also pins a subtle invariant: blocks allocated for a pending remote prefill must stay unhashed, so they can never be returned as a spurious prefix-cache hit.

On the producer, blocks cannot be freed when the request ends, because the decoder has not read them yet:

- `request_finished` computes the block ids the decoder needs (attention groups clipped to the prompt block count, sliding-window groups clipped to their trailing window, Mamba groups trimmed of speculative tail blocks) and returns `delay_free_blocks = True` when any remain ([`mooncake_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L2030-L2057), [`base_scheduler.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/base_scheduler.py#L113-L139)).
- The request becomes releasable when the decoder's completion signal arrives; if it never does, `KVCacheTaskTracker._retrieve_expired_requests` force-frees it after `VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT` and logs an error naming the timeout ([`mooncake_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L177-L253)). V2 has the equivalent logic in `MooncakeSchedulerSendingThread`, including an `early_finished_requests` set for completions that arrive *before* the request finished.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Allocated: request admitted on the producer
    Allocated --> Published: request_finished returns kv_transfer_params
    Published --> DelayedFree: blocks are still needed
    DelayedFree --> Released: done_recving_msg arrives
    DelayedFree --> Released: abort timeout expires
    Published --> Released: no blocks to transfer
    Released --> [*]
```

*Producer-side block release: the only two ways out of the delayed-free state are an acknowledgement or the timeout.*

A rejected remote-prefill request is a real case, not a corner: if a prompt plus `max_tokens` exceeds `max_model_len`, `update_state_after_alloc` never runs, so `request_finished` enqueues an **empty** receive anyway. The worker skips the data movement but still sends the completion signal, which is what releases the stranded producer blocks ([`mooncake_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_connector.py#L2013-L2028)).

## Role gates a configuration must satisfy

Almost every validation in this area is a role check, because the same binary and the same config file run on both fleets. They fall into three groups.

**P/D topology validation.** `check_kv_extra_config` compares `kv_connector_extra_config.prefill.{tp_size,dp_size}` against the producer's actual parallel config and `decode.{tp_size,dp_size}` against the consumer's, raising on mismatch — so a wrong `extra_config` fails at startup rather than by hanging a transfer ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L1301-L1325)). `AscendConfig` then derives `pd_tp_ratio`, `pd_head_ratio`, and `num_head_replica` from the same fields, and additionally resets `kv_buffer_size` to `1e9`, forces `enable_permute_local_kv = False`, and makes `engine_id` unique per process so two nodes or two restarts can never collide ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L702-L728)).

**Scheduler features that only make sense on one side.** These are enforced in `_check_ascend_config` ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L909-L1028)):

| Feature | Allowed where | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enable_balance_scheduling` | PD-mixed only (`kv_role: kv_both` or no transfer config) | raises in P/D-disaggregated mode |
| `short_request_first_config.enabled` | prefill or PD-mixed | raises on `kv_consumer` |
| `dyntra_lb_config.enabled` | decoder only, `data_parallel_size > 1`, single node | raises otherwise |
| `recompute_scheduler_enable` | decoder only | **warns and writes `False` back** into `additional_config` on a producer, so worker processes observe it disabled |
| `enable_kv_nz` | MLA, decoder only | `RuntimeError`/`NotImplementedError` on producer or non-MLA |

**Cache-layout gates.** `enable_kv_nz` requires DeepSeek-MLA without sparse SFA ([`ascend_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py#L739-L751)), and `SfaRemoteD2HConnector` requires the two sides' sparse-offload flags to be opposite. `MooncakeLayerwiseConnector` rejects a consumer with PCP > 1 at scheduler construction ([`mooncake_layerwise_connector.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_layerwise_connector.py#L864-L868)).

### Load-failure policy

`kv_load_failure_policy` is a top-level `KVTransferConfig` field, not connector-specific. Every connector surfaces failed blocks through `get_block_ids_with_load_errors()`, and upstream applies the policy. On Ascend the policy is validated once: `recompute` is rejected for hybrid models, because a partially loaded hybrid cache cannot be recomputed consistently ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L1031-L1037)). V2 narrows the report further — `MooncakePullRecvingThread` only attributes invalid block ids to the request when the engine has a single KV cache group (`can_report_invalid_block_ids`), so hybrid layouts degrade to reporting the request rather than guessing a block ([`pull_worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/pull_worker.py#L118-L140)).

### Local communication resources (A5 only)

On hardware whose profile declares `LOCAL_KV_COMM_RESOURCE` — currently the A5 profile — the worker loads a per-device endpoint descriptor before it takes its memory snapshot: `setup_ascend_local_comm_res(local_rank, kv_transfer_config)` reads `ub_endpoint_npu_<device>.json` from `kv_connector_extra_config.ascend_local_comm_res_path` and exports it as `ASCEND_LOCAL_COMM_RES` ([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L455-L456), [`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L554-L590), [`hardware_profile.py`](../../vllm_ascend/device/hardware_profile.py#L211-L249)). It is skipped entirely when there is no `kv_transfer_config` or no path, and it fails with an actionable message on a missing file, unparseable JSON, or a `local_rank` outside the visible device list.

## Allocation, registration, and QoS

Three worker-side steps happen before the first transfer and each has a hard failure mode.

**2 MiB alignment.** When `kv_transfer_config` is set, `_allocate_kv_cache_tensors` allocates every int8 raw cache with `alignment = 2 * 1024 * 1024` and returns a sliced, aligned view. The same path also merges the sparse-C8 indexer K and its scale into one raw allocation so that `register_buffer` can merge their ranges ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4491-L4513), [`#L4436-L4489`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4436-L4489)). Without KV transfer the alignment is skipped, so a change that starts using transfer metadata on a non-transfer path will read an unaligned base address.

**Region-count cap.** `register_kv_caches` builds the register regions, validates them, and only then calls `global_te.register_buffer`. Ranges are merged by underlying storage with `REGISTER_MERGE_GAP_BYTES = 4096`, and `MAX_HCCL_REGISTER_REGIONS = 256` is a hard per-process limit: exceeding it raises with the region count, registered bytes, and the advice to merge k/v/dsa/scale allocations further ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/utils/utils.py#L421-L477), [`mooncake/base_worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake/base_worker.py#L205-L320)). `GlobalTE` is a lazily-initialized singleton that initializes the engine as `ascend` / `P2PHANDSHAKE` exactly once and registers buffers exactly once ([`mooncake_transfer_engine.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/utils/mooncake_transfer_engine.py#L4-L43)).

**QoS.** `inject_qos` runs in the worker constructor *before* the transfer engine is created, merging `kv_connector_extra_config.qos_priority` (default `1`, integer in `[0, 4]`) into the literal top-level key `"comm_resource_config.qos"` of `ASCEND_GLOBAL_RESOURCE_CONFIG` while preserving every other field. Booleans are rejected, and malformed existing JSON fails before the environment is mutated ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/utils/utils.py#L23-L47)). Because HIXL takes channel QoS from the connection initiator, the effective value for a pull is the **decoder's** and for a push the **prefiller's**; configuring only the passive side does not change the channel. The `Injected comm_resource_config.qos=...` log line proves the local environment write, not that the channel used it ([`pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.md`](../../docs/source/tutorials/features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.md#L219-L275)).

## How the attention layer participates

P/D transfer is invisible to the model code except for two hooks in `vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py`, both called unconditionally and both no-ops for connectors that do not opt in:

- `save_kv_layer` / `wait_for_layer_load` are invoked around each layer's attention when the connector has metadata for the current step, which is how layerwise push and layerwise pull start work early ([`attention/utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py#L503-L531)).
- `notify_kv_cache_written(layer_name)` fires immediately after `reshape_and_cache` (and after the NZ/C8 scatter path), letting a producer record a compute-stream event or publish a PD-pull notification at scatter time. AscendStore and SFA-PD implement it; others omit the hook ([`attention/utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py#L534-L551), [`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L1651-L1672), [`#L2229-L2254`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L2229-L2254)).

The one behaviour that changes with role is `is_kv_producer`: for a KV-sharing target layer the attention layer records the reshape event but writes nothing, because writing its dummy K/V would overwrite slots the sharing layer owns. That is why the role flag is read in the attention implementation rather than only in the connector.

## Composing with offload through `AscendMultiConnector`

A production deployment often wants P/D transfer *and* a pooled store, or P/D *and* preemption offload. That is exactly the `MultiConnector` path, and the Ascend subclass adds three orderings that exist because layerwise transfer shares physical slots:

1. **Slot-release providers run first.** A connector is a provider when it is a producer, has a worker, declares `supports_layerwise_buffer_reuse`, and exposes `wait_for_layer_reuse`. `save_kv_layer`, `on_kv_cache_written`, and the load path all iterate providers before siblings, independent of the order the user listed connectors.
2. **One sink owns the wait.** If a connector accepts `set_external_slot_release_waiter`, it receives the composite waiter and provider layer-entry waits are then skipped as redundant.
3. **Only one connector may emit KV transfer params.** `request_finished_all_groups` raises `RuntimeError("Only one connector can produce KV transfer params")` if two do, and tracks extra async saves per request. `update_state_after_alloc` forwards real blocks only to the chosen connector and to any connector setting `requires_full_blocks_on_update_after_alloc` (which `MooncakeLayerwiseConnector` and the SFA producer side do); everyone else gets `blocks.new_empty()`.

Mamba state copying is also sequenced here: if any child sets `requires_mamba_state_copy_after_layer_load`, the composite prepares the copy, runs it inside `wait_for_layer_load`, and finishes it after all loads. The ordering is pinned by [`test_ascend_multi_connector.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/test_ascend_multi_connector.py#L69-L106).

## Invariants a change must preserve

| Invariant | Consequence of breaking it | Where it is enforced |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A connector instance has exactly one KV role | Transfers are silently attributed to the wrong side | `MooncakeBaseConnectorScheduler.__init__`, `MooncakeBaseConnectorWorker.__init__` |
| Prefill TP ≥ decode TP and is an integer multiple | Head shards cannot be mapped; requests hang or corrupt | `MooncakeConnectorWorker.__init__`, `AscendConfig` `pd_tp_ratio` |
| PCP is producer-only in P/D | The decoder would address blocks it never allocated | `MooncakeConnectorWorker.__init__`, layerwise scheduler assert |
| Scheduler control port must sit outside the worker handshake range | Metadata requests land on a KV socket | `MooncakeBaseConnectorScheduler.__init__` |
| Producer blocks are freed only on acknowledgement or timeout | HBM leak, or a decoder reading reused blocks | `KVCacheTaskTracker`, `MooncakeSchedulerSendingThread` |
| A pending remote prefill's blocks must stay unhashed | A later request reuses blocks whose KV has not arrived | upstream scheduler + `finished_recving` handling |
| Sparse-offload flags are opposite on the two sides of `SfaRemoteD2HConnector` | Producer and consumer disagree on where main KV lives | connector constructor asserts |
| Registered regions ≤ 256 per process | `register_buffer` fails at startup | `validate_register_region_count` |
| QoS is taken from the initiator side | The channel silently runs at the passive side's value | `inject_qos` + HIXL channel semantics |

## Where to read the tests before changing this

- [`tests/ut/kv_offload/test_mooncake_connector.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/test_mooncake_connector.py) — the V1 handshake loop (`GET_META_MSG`, `DONE_RECVING_MSG`, retries), block-id trimming for MTP and sliding window, unequal-P/D-TP split metadata, Mamba normalization, and the expired-request path.
- [`tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/mooncake_v2/) — `test_metadata.py` (per-layer length validation), `test_pull_scheduler.py` (PP/TP merge and port placement), `test_pull_worker.py` (metadata fetch, candidate groups, `batch_transfer_sync_read`), `test_connector.py` (HND layout, role dispatch, unimplemented push).
- [`tests/ut/kv_offload/test_mooncake_layerwise_connector.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/test_mooncake_layerwise_connector.py) — reuse-gate completion and error propagation, metaserver retry, hybrid prompt truncation, and the register-time rejections (sparse-SFA-C8 main cache, DCP-replicated indexer scale).
- [`tests/ut/kv_offload/test_sfa_pd_rd2h_connector.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/test_sfa_pd_rd2h_connector.py) — main/indexer group inference, disjoint TP-range splitting, per-layer read gates, and the all-contributors-then-complete accounting for unequal TP.
- [`tests/ut/kv_offload/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py) and [`test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py`](../../tests/ut/kv_offload/test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py) — the `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` lifecycle and the no-spurious-prefix-hit invariant.
- [`tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/test_utils.py`](../../tests/ut/distributed/kv_transfer/test_utils.py) — `inject_qos` defaults, preservation of other resource fields, idempotence, and the leave-environment-unchanged-on-error guarantee.

For deployment walkthroughs see [Prefill-Decode Disaggregation (DeepSeek)](../../docs/source/tutorials/features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_multi_node.md) and [single-node Mooncake P/D](../../docs/source/tutorials/features/pd_disaggregation_mooncake_single_node.md); for the proxy that drives the two-phase request see [`examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1`](../../examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py).

nodes.description: The end-to-end Ascend startup path — which entry points vLLM resolves, what register()/register_connector()/register_model_loader()/register_model() do, how NPUPlatform.pre_register_and_update and check_and_update_config mutate configuration, and how each worker re-applies patches, re-initializes AscendConfig, binds the device, loads the model, sizes and allocates KV cache, profiles, warms up, and captures graphs — plus the orderings that break if changed.
nodes.body:
# Workflow: Plugin Registration and Startup Sequence

vllm-ascend has no `main()`. It is discovered, called, and re-entered by an unmodified vLLM at several distinct moments in process startup, and the single most useful thing to hold onto while reading this page is that **the work is not done once**: platform-level work happens once per engine-core process, while worker-level work happens again in every worker process, which re-applies the worker patch tier, re-registers custom ops, and re-initializes `AscendConfig` from the same `vllm_config` object it received.

Everything below is grounded in the call sites, not in the documentation. For the *rationale* behind the patch split see [Patching Architecture and Catalog Discipline](../architecture/patching-architecture.md); for the hook inventory see [Upstream vLLM Integration Surface](../integrations/upstream-vllm-interfaces.md); for the process model map see [System Architecture Overview](../architecture/overview.md).

## What the package declares to vLLM

Discovery is entirely declarative. [`setup()`](../../setup.py#L518-L529) publishes three entry-point groups:

| Group | Name | Target | Resolved when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vllm.platform_plugins` | `ascend` | `vllm_ascend:register` | Platform discovery, before any `VllmConfig` exists |
| `vllm.general_plugins` | `ascend_kv_connector` | `vllm_ascend:register_connector` | General-plugin load, inside engine-core |
| | `ascend_model_loader` | `vllm_ascend:register_model_loader` | Same |
| | `ascend_service_profiling` | `vllm_ascend:register_service_profiling` | Same |
| | `ascend_model` | `vllm_ascend:register_model` | Same |
| `ms_service_metric.providers` | `vllm-ascend` | `vllm_ascend.observability:get_metric_provider` | Metric-provider lookup in the monitoring stack |

The same `setup.py` fixes hardware identity at install time: `gen_build_info()` writes `vllm_ascend/_build_info.py` containing `__device_type__`, derived from `SOC_VERSION` or from `npu-smi` output ([`setup.py`](../../setup.py#L157-L165)). That single generated string later decides the `HardwareProfile` — and therefore the default worker class, the attention backend family, the quantization family, and every capability gate in the patch tree.

`vllm_ascend/__init__.py` stays import-light on purpose. Before defining anything it installs stub modules for `triton.experimental.gluon*` and a `_aggregate` shim on `triton.language.core` so a newer vLLM can import against `triton-ascend` 3.2.x, and it imports `vllm_ascend.logger` at the very end ([`vllm_ascend/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/__init__.py#L22-L46), [line 108](../../vllm_ascend/__init__.py#L108)).

## The sequence, in order

The numbered list below is the authoritative order. Each step names the exact function and file. Steps 1–9 run once in the main/engine-core process; steps 10–20 run once per worker process.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant VLLM as vLLM main process
    participant PLUG as vllm_ascend package
    participant PLAT as NPUPlatform
    participant CFG as VllmConfig
    participant EC as EngineCore process
    participant WK as NPUWorker
    participant MR as NPUModelRunner

    VLLM->>PLUG: platform_plugins ascend calls register()
    PLUG-->>VLLM: returns "vllm_ascend.platform.NPUPlatform"
    VLLM->>PLAT: pre_register_and_update(parser)
    PLAT->>PLAT: adapt_patch(is_global_patch=True)
    PLAT->>PLAT: register DeepSeek-V4 vision config convertor
    PLAT->>PLAT: append ascend to quantization choices
    PLAT->>PLAT: import quantization configs for hardware family
    VLLM->>PLAT: check_and_update_config(vllm_config)
    PLAT->>CFG: logging, validators, quantization auto-detect
    PLAT->>PLAT: init_ascend_config(vllm_config)
    PLAT->>CFG: worker_cls, scheduler_cls, compilation modes, custom_ops
    PLAT->>PLAT: _set_pytorch_npu_alloc_env
    VLLM->>EC: spawn engine core
    EC->>PLUG: general_plugins load
    PLUG->>PLUG: _ensure_global_patch then register into vLLM factories
    EC->>WK: WorkerWrapperBase.init_worker
    WK->>WK: adapt_patch() worker tier
    WK->>WK: ops import, dummy fusion op, ATB, customop, init_ascend_config, device check
    WK->>WK: WorkerBase.__init__
    WK->>WK: init_device, set_device, hccl, model parallel
    WK->>MR: construct NPUModelRunner
    WK->>WK: load_model
    WK->>MR: profile_run inside determine_available_memory
    WK->>MR: initialize_from_config allocates KV cache
    WK->>MR: compile_or_warm_up_model, kernel warmup, capture_model
```

*One discovery path, then a per-worker replay: the same `vllm_config` is corrected once and rebuilt into `AscendConfig` in every worker.*

1. **Entry-point resolution — `register()`** ([`vllm_ascend/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/__init__.py#L68-L71)). Returns the *string* `"vllm_ascend.platform.NPUPlatform"`. The string, not the class, is the contract: it keeps `vllm_ascend.platform` — and therefore `vllm.config` — unimported while vLLM is still bootstrapping its own package.

2. **Platform pre-registration — `NPUPlatform.pre_register_and_update(parser)`** ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L285-L320)). Four things, in this order:
   1. `adapt_patch(is_global_patch=True)` installs the platform patch tier.
   2. `register_deepseek_v4_vision_config_convertor()` registers the DeepSeek-V4 config convertor into `MODEL_ARCH_CONFIG_CONVERTORS`.
   3. When a parser is present, `"ascend"` is appended to the `--quantization` action's `choices` so `vllm serve --quantization ascend` parses.
   4. The quantization config classes for the active `QuantizationBackendFamily` are imported (four standard classes, or `AscendModelSlimConfig310`) purely for their registration side effects.

3. **Config construction and correction — `NPUPlatform.check_and_update_config(vllm_config)`** ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L442-L497)). Ten commented steps: (1) `configure_ascend_file_logging` + `configure_ascend_logging`; (2) early exit on device-type mismatch or missing `model_config`, then `_validate_indexer_pp_config`, `_validate_draft_decode_context_parallel_config`, `_validate_parallel_config`; (3) `maybe_auto_detect_quantization`; (4) `_fix_incompatible_config`; (5) `init_ascend_config(vllm_config)` then `_check_ascend_config`; (6) `_update_compilation_modes`; (7) `_setup_compile_backend`; (8) `_setup_worker_and_scheduler`; (9) `_validate_sfa_dcp_kv_sp`; (10) `_set_pytorch_npu_alloc_env`.

4. **Ascend config singleton — `init_ascend_config(vllm_config)`** ([`ascend_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py#L1466-L1582)). Builds `AscendConfig` from `vllm_config.additional_config`, pre-constructing `SchedulerConfig`, `SparseKVOffloadConfig`, `KVPPConfig` and the dump path, then runs `derive_and_validate`, `rl_config.apply`, and the fine-grained-TP / Xlite precondition checks. The result is cached in the module globals `_ASCEND_CONFIG` and `_INIT_VLLM_CONFIG`; a second call returns the cached object only if the flag was not set to refresh *and* the identity of `vllm_config` is unchanged. `get_ascend_config()` raises until this has run ([`ascend_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py#L1594-L1598)).

5. **Worker and scheduler class selection — `_setup_worker_and_scheduler`** ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L1227-L1272)). When `parallel_config.worker_cls == "auto"`, writes either `"vllm_ascend.xlite.xlite_worker.XliteWorker"` (Xlite enabled *and* `STANDARD_WORKER_PATCHES` supported) or `hardware_profile.default_worker_cls` — `"vllm_ascend.worker.worker.NPUWorker"` for standard families, `"vllm_ascend._310p.worker_310p.NPUWorker310"` for 310P. Then `refresh_block_size(vllm_config)`, forces `compilation_config.custom_ops = ["all"]` when `AUTO_ENABLE_CUSTOM_OPS` is supported, and finally selects `scheduler_cls` for DyntraLB, profiling-chunk, or batch-job-aware scheduling.

6. **Allocator environment — `_set_pytorch_npu_alloc_env`** ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L1310-L1329)). Appends `expandable_segments:True` to `PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF` unless sleep mode is on (expandable segments conflict with the CaMem allocator's sleep path).

7. **Engine-core process spawn.** The executor spawns the engine core with the corrected `vllm_config`.

8. **Idempotent platform-patch install — `_ensure_global_patch()`** ([`vllm_ascend/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/__init__.py#L51-L65)). The *first* thing each general plugin does. Behind `_GLOBAL_PATCH_APPLIED`, calls `adapt_patch(is_global_patch=True)`. This is the only reason scheduler- and engine-level patches exist in an engine-core subprocess, where no CLI parse and no test conftest ever ran.

9. **General-plugin registration inside the engine core — `register_connector`, `register_model_loader`, `register_service_profiling`, `register_model`** ([`vllm_ascend/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/__init__.py#L74-L105)). The first three call `_ensure_global_patch()` first; `register_model()` does not, because it only touches `ModelRegistry`. They register KV connectors / offloading specs / weight-transfer engines ([`distributed/kv_transfer/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/__init__.py#L21-L129)), the `netloader`/`rfork` model loaders ([`model_loader/netloader/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/model_loader/netloader/__init__.py#L18-L20)), the service-profiling config file ([`profiling_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/profiling_config.py#L538-L559)), and Ascend-maintained architectures ([`models/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/models/__init__.py#L4-L83)).

10. **Worker construction — `NPUWorker.__init__`** ([`worker/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L127-L169)). In fixed order: warn if `COMPILE_CUSTOM_KERNELS` is off; `adapt_patch()` (worker tier); `from vllm_ascend import ops` + `ops.register_dummy_fusion_op()`; conditionally `_register_atb_extensions()`; `register_ascend_customop(vllm_config)`; `init_ascend_config(vllm_config)`; `configure_ascend_file_logging()`; `check_ascend_device_type()`; then `super().__init__(...)`.

11. **Ascend `CustomOp` table — `register_ascend_customop`** ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L715-L847)). Builds `REGISTERED_ASCEND_OPS` (activations, norms, linear layers, rotary embeddings, attention wrappers, MoE runner/routed experts/gate linear), overwrites individual entries with `*310` classes when `COMPATIBILITY_OP_IMPLEMENTATIONS` is supported, then calls `CustomOp.register_oot(...)` for each and only afterwards sets `_ASCEND_CUSTOMOP_IS_REIGISTERED`.

12. **Runtime-identity assertion — `check_ascend_device_type()`** ([`device/device_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/device/device_config.py#L65-L77)). Compares the install-time `_device_type` against `device_type_from_runtime_soc(torch_npu.npu.get_soc_version())` and raises `RuntimeError` on mismatch — a wrong wheel fails here rather than miscompiling later.

13. **Device binding — `NPUWorker.init_device` → `_init_device`** ([`worker/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L392-L515)). Shifts `local_rank` by `dp_local_rank * tp_pp_world_size` (skipped when `assigned_physical_gpu_ids` is set), publishes the logical-to-physical mapping, converts to a visible device id, calls `torch.npu.set_device`, imports `torch_npu._inductor` *after* `set_device`, takes the `MemorySnapshot`, fails fast if free memory is below `gpu_memory_utilization`, then `_init_worker_distributed_environment()` (`init_batch_invariance`, `init_distributed_environment(..., "hccl")`, `ensure_model_parallel_initialized`, `init_ascend_model_parallel`, `ensure_ec_transfer_initialized`), `set_random_seed`, and `init_device_properties_triton()`.

14. **Model-runner construction — `init_device` continuation** ([`worker/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L496-L515)). `init_workspace_manager(device, num_ubatches=1)` first, then `NPUModelRunnerV2` when `use_v2_model_runner` else `NPUModelRunner`; `report_usage_stats` on rank 0. Subclasses override this step and nothing else: `NPUWorker310.init_device` and `XliteWorker.init_device` both call `self._init_device()` and then build their own runner.

15. **Custom-op environment bootstrap — `NPUPlatform.import_kernels()`** ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L269-L283)). Prepends `<package>/_cann_ops_custom/vendors/custom_transformer` to `ASCEND_CUSTOM_OPP_PATH` via `bootstrap_custom_op_env()` and sets `_CUSTOM_OP_REGISTERED`. It deliberately does **not** import `vllm_ascend_C`: that import is deferred to `enable_custom_op()` ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L415-L474)), which imports the extension and `vllm_ascend.meta_registration`, with an `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` fallback only when the import itself proves `libcust_opapi.so` is missing.

16. **Weight load — `NPUWorker.load_model` → `NPUModelRunner.load_model`** ([`worker/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L842-L865), [`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4061-L4139)). The worker wraps the runner call in `CaMemAllocator.get_instance().use_memory_pool(tag="weights")` when sleep mode is enabled and in `set_current_vllm_config(...)` always; the runner calls `get_model(vllm_config=...)`, records `model_memory_usage`, loads any drafter, and configures Eagle3/DSpark aux hidden-state layers. The weight-transfer engine is created *after* the model exists.

17. **Profile run — `NPUWorker.determine_available_memory`** ([`worker/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L561-L661)). `maybe_apply_startup_plan` first; if `kv_cache_memory_bytes` is set, only `model_runner.profile_run()` runs and the user value is the budget; otherwise `profile_run()` runs inside `memory_profiling`, and the ascending sequence of constraints is then applied (`_scale_kv_cache_memory_for_multi_group`, layerwise-reuse factor, `_apply_kv_offload_decode_memory_constraints`, `_apply_kvpp_memory_budget`). `NPUModelRunner.profile_run` itself does EPLB warmup, sparse-offload top-k buffer reservation, and an extra MC2-capacity dummy run before delegating upstream ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4024-L4048)).

18. **KV-cache allocation — `NPUWorker.initialize_from_config`** ([`worker/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L1140-L1171)). `ensure_kv_transfer_initialized(vllm_config, kv_cache_config)` first, then `model_runner.initialize_kv_cache(kv_cache_config)` inside the `tag="kv_cache"` CaMem pool when sleep mode is on, then the KV-zeroer bookkeeping decided from `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` and the Eagle3/Mamba condition. The full pipeline is in [KV Cache Sizing, Allocation, Reshape, and Graph Capture](./kv-cache-initialization.md).

19. **Warmup — `NPUWorker.compile_or_warm_up_model`** ([`worker/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L867-L970)). Compile sizes are separated from cudagraph capture sizes, remaining sizes are dummy-run in descending order, then `kernel_warmup(worker)` runs the rejection-sampler, penalties and RMS Triton warmups ([`kernel_warmup.py`](../../vllm_ascend/model_executor/warmup/kernel_warmup.py#L36-L49)).

20. **Graph capture and post-capture work** (same function). `capture_model()` under `not enforce_eager`, then the suggested `--kv-cache-memory` computation and `maybe_save_startup_plan`, then `_warm_up_atb()` when `ATB_WARMUP` is supported, then `bind_cpus` when `enable_cpu_binding` is set, then `set_random_seed` again so model init and profiling cannot perturb the RNG state.

## How the two halves stay in sync

The asymmetry is not incidental — it follows from `vllm_config` being the only thing that crosses the process boundary.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph MAIN["Main / engine-core process"]
        R["register returns dotted path"] --> PRE["pre_register_and_update"]
        PRE --> PATCHP["patch/platform tier"]
        PRE --> QC["quantization configs imported"]
        PRE --> CU["check_and_update_config"]
        CU --> AC["init_ascend_config"]
        CU --> WB["write back into vllm_config and additional_config"]
        EC["general plugins"] --> GPL["_ensure_global_patch"]
    end
    subgraph WORKER["Each worker process"]
        WI["NPUWorker.__init__"] --> PATCHW["patch/worker tier"]
        WI --> CO["register_ascend_customop"]
        WI --> ACW["init_ascend_config from the received vllm_config"]
        WI --> DEV["init_device then NPUModelRunner"]
    end
    WB -->|"pickled vllm_config"| WI
    GPL -.->|"platform tier re-imported in the child"| PATCHW
```

*Configuration flows across the process boundary as pickled state; patches and custom-op registrations do not, so each worker rebuilds them.*

| Concern | Main / engine-core | Worker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Patch tier | `patch/platform/` via `adapt_patch(is_global_patch=True)` | `patch/worker/` via `adapt_patch()` |
| `AscendConfig` | `init_ascend_config` inside `check_and_update_config` | re-built in `NPUWorker.__init__` from the received `vllm_config` |
| Registries | KV connectors, offloading specs, weight-transfer engines, model loaders, `ModelRegistry` | `CustomOp.register_oot` table, `torch.ops` via `direct_register_custom_op` |
| Backend selection | dotted paths returned by `NPUPlatform` hooks | the classes those paths name, imported and instantiated |
| Device work | none | `set_device`, HCCL groups, memory snapshot, profiling, graph capture |

Both tiers funnel through one function, [`adapt_patch`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L547-L551), which does nothing but import the chosen package. The contract is stated verbatim in the header of [`patch/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py#L17-L27).

## Orderings that break if reordered

| Ordering | Enforced at | What breaks if violated |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Patch before the quantization config import.** `adapt_patch(is_global_patch=True)` runs before the DeepSeek-V4 convertor registration and before the quantization config classes are imported | [`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L287-L318) | The convertor registration imports `vllm.transformers_utils.model_arch_config_convertor`; doing it first means the platform tier patches arrive after the symbols those modules captured by name. The in-code comment also cites multiprocessing-spawn safety |
| **Patch before any model import.** The `FusedMoEFactory` rebind has to precede models, because models do `from ... import FusedMoEFactory` and capture a local binding | catalog item 7 in [`patch/__init__.py`](../../vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py#L153-L172) | The factory rebind is invisible to already-imported model modules; the patch appears applied but the upstream MoE factory is still used |
| **`init_ascend_config` before `WorkerBase.__init__`.** Same for `register_ascend_customop` and `check_ascend_device_type` | [`worker/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L155-L169) | The base constructor resolves conventions that read the Ascend config and registered ops; `get_ascend_config()` raises `RuntimeError` if it has not run ([`ascend_config.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py#L1594-L1598)) |
| **`torch.npu.set_device` before the custom-op extension import.** `import_kernels` only bootstraps the environment; `enable_custom_op()` performs the actual `import vllm_ascend.vllm_ascend_C` | [`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L269-L283), [`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L415-L474) | Importing the extension early instantiates CANN's RTS component, which freezes device visibility so `ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES` can no longer be changed (the RL-module bug documented in the code comment) |
| **`torch.npu.set_device` before `torch_npu._inductor`** | [`worker/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L441-L450) | The lazy import exists precisely to avoid repeated `set_device` in extra processes |
| **Distributed environment before the model runner** | [`worker/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L487-L511) | The runner reads EP/DP/PCP groups during `__init__` |
| **`profile_run` before allocation** | `determine_available_memory` precedes `initialize_from_config` | The KV budget *is* the measurement; allocating first leaves no budget basis |
| **`kernel_warmup` before `capture_model`** | [`worker/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L891-L897) | Triton kernels compile inside capture otherwise, poisoning the captured graphs |
| **`capture_model` before CPU binding** | [`worker/worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L943-L956) | `migratepages`/`taskset` would run before hot allocations exist |
| **Platform write-back before spawn** | `_setup_worker_and_scheduler`, `_update_compilation_modes`, `_setup_compile_backend` | Workers rebuild from `vllm_config` and `additional_config`; a selection not written back simply does not reach them |

## Failure modes worth recognising

| Symptom at startup | Likely cause |
| --- | --- |
| `RuntimeError: Current device type: X does not match the installed version's device type: Y` | Wheel built for a different SoC than the runtime one — `check_ascend_device_type()` from step 12 |
| `RuntimeError: Ascend config is not initialized` | `get_ascend_config()` called before `init_ascend_config`, i.e. a code path that runs before step 4 or step 10 |
| A kernel-, scheduler-, or config-level patch is effective in the main process but not in the engine core | The patch lives in `patch/worker/`, or a general-plugin entry point was added that skips `_ensure_global_patch()` |
| `ImportError` about `libcust_opapi.so` handled by warning and all custom ops silently disabled | `enable_custom_op()` fell through both import attempts ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L448-L473)); `COMPILE_CUSTOM_KERNELS=0` also triggers this |
| Behaviour differs between a `vllm serve` run and a pytest run | Pytest has no plugin entry point: `tests/e2e/conftest.py` and `tests/ut/conftest.py` call `adapt_patch(True)` and `adapt_patch()` by hand ([`tests/e2e/conftest.py`](../../tests/e2e/conftest.py#L67-L73), [`tests/ut/conftest.py`](../../tests/ut/conftest.py#L239-L243)) |
| `ValueError: Free memory on device ... is less than desired GPU memory utilization` | `_init_device`'s fast fail at step 13 — before any profiling has run |

## Configuration levers that touch this sequence

| Lever | Effect on startup |
| --- | --- |
| `additional_config.refresh` / `rl_config.enabled` | Forces `init_ascend_config` to rebuild instead of returning the cached singleton |
| `additional_config.xlite_graph_config.enabled` | Swaps `worker_cls` to `XliteWorker` at step 5 |
| `additional_config.enable_cpu_binding` | Runs `bind_cpus` during step 20 |
| `additional_config.scheduler_config.profiling_chunk_config.enabled` | Selects `ProfilingChunkScheduler` *and* imports `patch_profiling_chunk` at step 5 |
| `--enforce-eager` | Skips `capture_model`, so no NPU graph pool and no capture-OOM risk |
| `--kv-cache-memory` (`kv_cache_memory_bytes`) | Switches step 17 to the fast path that skips the arithmetic |
| `enable_sleep_mode` | Changes steps 16 and 18 to allocate weights and KV cache in separate CaMem pools, and suppresses `expandable_segments` at step 6 |
| `COMPILE_CUSTOM_KERNELS` | `0` skips the ACLNN and CMake build at install time and produces a warning at step 10 |

## Tests that pin this sequence

- [`tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py`](../../tests/ut/worker/test_worker_v1.py#L331-L376) constructs `NPUWorker` with everything patched and asserts that `adapt_patch` is called exactly once, and that `register_dummy_fusion_op`, `_register_atb_extensions`, `register_ascend_customop`, `init_ascend_config(vllm_config)` and `check_ascend_device_type` each fire — the executable form of step 10's order.
- [`tests/ut/test_platform.py`](../../tests/ut/test_platform.py#L327-L370) asserts `pre_register_and_update` calls `adapt_patch(is_global_patch=True)` exactly once with and without a parser, with no `--quantization` action, and with `ascend` already present (so the choice list is not duplicated).
- [`tests/ut/test_platform.py`](../../tests/ut/test_platform.py#L1683-L1739) pins `worker_cls` selection (`NPUWorker` by default, `XliteWorker` when Xlite is on) and that 310P leaves `custom_ops` empty because `AUTO_ENABLE_CUSTOM_OPS` is unsupported there.
- [`tests/ut/device/test_device_config.py`](../../tests/ut/device/test_device_config.py#L83-L93) covers `check_ascend_device_type` raising on a build/runtime mismatch.

## Where to go next

- [Patching Architecture and Catalog Discipline](../architecture/patching-architecture.md) — why the two tiers exist and how the imports are ordered inside each.
- [Upstream vLLM Integration Surface and Version Lanes](../integrations/upstream-vllm-interfaces.md) — the hook inventory these entry points call into.
- [KV Cache Sizing, Allocation, Reshape, and Graph Capture](./kv-cache-initialization.md) — steps 17–20 in depth.
- [Configuration System](../architecture/configuration-system.md) — what `init_ascend_config` actually builds.

nodes.description: How one SchedulerOutput travels through the Ascend worker and model runner - input preparation, batch and padding decisions, attention metadata, the Ascend forward context, model forward, sampling and the async output path - including the sequence-parallel, data-parallel and pipeline-parallel branches that change the flow.
