# Workflow: One Engine Step Through the Model Runner

One decode or prefill step is a single `SchedulerOutput` handed to a worker, forwarded to a
model runner, and turned into (a) a model forward whose output is almost entirely discarded and
(b) a set of sampled token ids handed back to the engine core. What makes the Ascend version
interesting is not the ordering of those two halves — vLLM's v1 runner already splits a step into
`execute_model` + `sample_tokens` — but the *quantity of state that must be agreed between ranks
before the forward is legal*: a padded token count, a graph mode, a MoE communication method, an
EP/DP padding length, and a per-layer attention metadata dict whose tensors are read by kernels
that never receive them as arguments.

This page walks the step in call order and names the data structures that carry state between the
stages. The backends that consume the metadata are documented in
[Attention Backend Selection](../concepts/attention-backends.md); the MoE communication choice is in
[MoE Execution](../concepts/moe-execution.md); draft-model and rejection sampling are in
[Speculative Decoding](../concepts/speculative-decoding.md).

## The step pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["SchedulerOutput arrives at NPUWorker.execute_model"] --> B["PP recv on non-first ranks, profiler step, memory logging"]
    B --> D["_update_states inside synchronize_input_prep: persistent batch, block tables, PP sampled-token fixup, encoder cache"]
    D --> E{"EC transfer active and this rank is not the consumer"}
    E -->|yes| E1["_execute_mm_encoder then empty encoder runner output"]
    E -->|no| C{"total_num_scheduled_tokens == 0"}
    C -->|yes| C1["_dummy_run for external-launcher DP, then EMPTY_MODEL_RUNNER_OUTPUT or kv_connector_no_forward"]
    C -->|no| F["_prepare_inputs: positions, input_ids, attn_state, logits_indices, spec metadata"]
    F --> G["_determine_batch_execution_and_padding: SP rounding, graph dispatch, DP sync"]
    G --> H["_pad_query_start_loc_for_fia when FULL graph or SP"]
    H --> I["_build_attention_metadata: AscendCommonAttentionMetadata per KV cache group"]
    I --> I1["_sanitize_placeholder_input_ids, then _preprocess and update_cos_sin"]
    I1 --> J["set_ascend_forward_context: MoE comm method, padded lengths, mc2 mask"]
    J --> K["_model_forward inside the ACL graph wrapper"]
    K --> L{"is_last_pp_rank"}
    L -->|no| L1["return IntermediateTensors, worker isends them"]
    L -->|yes| M["compute_logits, store ExecuteModelState, return None"]
    M --> N["sample_tokens: grammar bitmask, _sample, _bookkeeping_sync, draft tokens"]
    N --> Q{"use_async_scheduling"}
    Q -->|no| Q1["ModelRunnerOutput"]
    Q -->|yes| Q2["AsyncGPUModelRunnerOutput plus set_async_sampled_token_ids"]
```

*One step: the runner returns `None` from `execute_model` so that sampling can be issued separately, and the async branch defers the device-to-host copy to a side stream.*

Two runners implement this workflow. `vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py` (`NPUModelRunner`
extending vLLM's `GPUModelRunner`) is the default; `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py` is the
Model Runner V2 variant that *does not* implement the pipeline itself but overrides
`prepare_inputs`, `sample`, `sample_tokens`, `postprocess_sampled` and `_pad_query_start_loc_for_fia`
around upstream's step driver. `NPUWorker` picks between them at `init_device` and warns that V2 is
still in development ([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L496-L511)). The V2 deltas are
collected in [The V2 runner](#the-v2-runner-deltas) below; everything before that section describes
the v1 flow, which the V2 overrides shadow in the same places.

## Entry: the worker, and the three ways a step ends early

`NPUWorker.execute_model` is deliberately thin ([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L764-L840)):

1. it waits on the previous step's pipeline-parallel send handles (`self._pp_send_work`);
2. if a forward will happen and this is not the first PP rank, it issues
   `get_pp_group().irecv_tensor_dict(...)` and wraps the result in `AsyncIntermediateTensors`, so the
   receive of the upstream pipeline stage overlaps local work;
3. it steps the profiler and delegates to `self.model_runner.execute_model(...)`.

The return value decides the rest of the step. A `ModelRunnerOutput` / `AsyncModelRunnerOutput` /
`None` is returned straight through. `IntermediateTensors` means this rank is a non-last pipeline
stage: the worker `isend`s `output.tensors` and returns. For V2 it returns `None` immediately, because
Model Runner V2 has no `kv_connector_output` to propagate from a non-last rank; for v1 the worker keeps
going and re-emits `EMPTY_MODEL_RUNNER_OUTPUT` carrying the connector's `finished_sending` /
`finished_recving` flags. `sample_tokens` on the worker only delegates and attaches profiling-chunk
timing ([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L832-L840)); `take_draft_token_ids` delegates
to the runner ([`worker.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py#L1244-L1245)).

The runner's `execute_model` starts with a hard ordering invariant: if `self.execute_model_state` is
still populated it raises `RuntimeError("State error: sample_tokens() must be called after
execute_model() returns None.")` ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2155-L2156)).
Keeping the two halves separate is what allows the scheduler to overlap the forward of step *N* with the
host-side work of step *N-1*: the sampled token ids leave the worker either synchronously or through an
`AsyncModelRunnerOutput` whose copy is still in flight when `execute_model` returns.

Three early exits avoid a forward entirely. All three sit *after* `_update_states`, and the encoder exit is
tested before the empty-batch exit, so a rank that only runs the multimodal encoder still reconciles its
persistent batch first:

| Condition | Action | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EC transfer initialized and this rank is *not* the consumer | `_update_states`, `_execute_mm_encoder`, `make_empty_encoder_model_runner_output` | [`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2222-L2230) |
| `total_num_scheduled_tokens == 0` | `_dummy_run(1, skip_gdn_state_update=True)` when `distributed_executor_backend == "external_launcher"` and DP > 1 (to keep `coordinate_batch_across_dp` in lock-step); then `EMPTY_MODEL_RUNNER_OUTPUT`, or `kv_connector_no_forward` if a KV transfer group exists | [`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2232-L2247) |
| non-zero total but every per-request count is zero | same empty/`kv_connector_no_forward` return | [`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2255-L2262) |

The DP dummy run in the second row is the subtle one: with both `external_launcher` and DP enabled,
`has_unfinished_requests` can be true while this rank has nothing to do, so skipping the dummy run
would drop this rank out of the DP collective and hang the busy ranks.
`tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py::test_execute_model_skips_dump_start_for_dp_dummy_run` pins
that call.

Four adjustments mutate step state before anything downstream reads it:

- **ngram GPU speculation** replaces (not deep-copies) `num_scheduled_tokens` and
  `scheduled_spec_decode_tokens` on the `SchedulerOutput` before anything reads it
  ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2158-L2173)).
- **non-last PP ranks** deep-copy the output and blank `scheduled_cached_reqs.new_token_ids` when the
  scheduler echoed no tokens, so `_update_states` does not try to consume them
  ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2181-L2186)).
- **KV transfer preemption** must run before `_update_states` zeroes newly allocated blocks, otherwise
  the preemption store can target physical KV ids that were just recycled
  ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2188-L2193)).
- **dropped-request repair** happens *inside* `synchronize_input_prep()`, just before `_update_states`:
  under async scheduling with speculation, a request that the previous `sample_tokens` left out of
  `prev_req_id_to_index` has its `prev_num_draft_len` reset to 0, because upstream's batch reconciliation
  would otherwise raise a `KeyError` for it
  ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2196-L2220)).
  `synchronize_input_prep()` is also the fence that keeps a still-in-flight H2D from having its pinned CPU
  source overwritten.

## State update: `_update_states` and `input_batch`

`_update_states` is upstream's persistent-batch reconciliation wrapped with three Ascend additions
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L889-L907)):

- a rewind guard that clears `prev_num_draft_len` when the scheduler reports fewer computed tokens than
  the runner remembers (a KV-load-failure recompute path);
- `_apply_pp_sampled_tokens_from_scheduler_output`, described under
  [CP, DP and PP special cases](#cp-dp-and-pp-special-cases);
- `_track_tmp_encoder_cache_refs`, which keeps encoder-cache copies alive while any request still
  references the multimodal hash.

The owner of per-step batch state is `NPUInputBatch`
([`npu_input_batch.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/npu_input_batch.py#L38-L258)), an `InputBatch`
subclass that allocates the *host* mirrors of everything the runner needs during input preparation:

| Field group | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `token_ids_cpu_tensor` / `token_ids_cpu`, `is_token_ids` | the token table; `_prepare_inputs` gathers each scheduled token out of it |
| `num_tokens`, `num_tokens_no_spec`, `num_prompt_tokens`, `num_computed_tokens_cpu(_tensor)` | request-level counters; the `_tensor`/`_cpu` pairs exist so numpy and torch views share storage and no copy is needed |
| `block_table: MultiGroupBlockTable` | one `BlockTable` per KV cache group, with fused slot-mapping fast paths ([`block_table.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/block_table.py#L321-L455)) |
| `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, penalties, `generators`, `allowed_token_ids_mask` | sampling state, mirrored CPU-pinned where the sampler needs host values |
| `prev_sampled_token_ids`, `prev_req_id_to_index`, `sampled_token_ids_cpu`, `async_copy_ready_event` | the async-scheduling handoff from the previous step |
| `thinking_budget_state_holder`, `req_prompt_embeds`, `spec_token_ids`, `batch_update_builder` | reasoning budgets, prompt embeddings, last drafted tokens, per-step logits-processor batch diff |

Every tensor in the lower rows is `pin_memory=True` when the runner has pinned memory: the H2D copies
in `_prepare_inputs` are `non_blocking=True`, and the runner fences buffer reuse with upstream's
`synchronize_input_prep()` context so a still-in-flight copy never has its source overwritten
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2196-L2197)).

## `_prepare_inputs`: turning the batch into tensors

`_prepare_inputs(scheduler_output, num_scheduled_tokens) -> (logits_indices, spec_decode_metadata,
total_num_scheduled_tokens)` ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L1191-L1609))
is the longest CPU-side stage and is entirely numpy-plus-`index_select`; the algorithm (positions,
token indices, block-table indices, slot mapping) is written up in the repository's own
[Prepare inputs design document](../../docs/source/developer_guide/Design_Documents/ModelRunner_prepare_inputs.md).
The order matters for overlap:

1. `block_table.commit_block_table(num_reqs)` is issued **first**, before any CPU arithmetic, so the
   block-table H2D copy overlaps the following numpy work.
2. `req_indices = np.repeat(arange[:num_reqs], num_scheduled_tokens)` — one entry per scheduled token.
3. `attn_state = self._build_attn_state(num_reqs, num_scheduled_tokens, num_valid_tokens)`; the state
   is one of `PrefillNoCache`, `PrefillCacheHit`, `DecodeOnly`, `ChunkedPrefill`, `SpecDecoding`
   ([`attention_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/attention_v1.py#L152-L157)), derived from whether
   any computed tokens exist, whether all queries are length 1, whether all *valid* queries are length
   1, and whether chunked prefill is on. `self.with_prefill` and the *displayed* `self.attn_state` are
   set from it; non-MTP speculation deliberately reports `ChunkedPrefill`.
4. `positions = num_computed_tokens_cpu[req_indices] + query_pos`, where `query_pos` is the per-token
   offset inside its request; `query_start_loc` is the exclusive prefix sum of the scheduled counts.
5. `input_ids` is a `torch.index_select` out of the flattened token table into a pinned CPU buffer
   ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L1285-L1300)); the same gather is
   repeated for `is_token_ids` when prompt embeddings are enabled, and prompt embeddings are copied
   request-by-request into `inputs_embeds.cpu`.
6. `optimistic_seq_lens_cpu = num_computed_tokens_cpu[:num_reqs] + num_scheduled_tokens` — the CPU
   upper bound on each sequence length, assuming every draft token from the previous step was accepted.
   It is what attention metadata later uses as `seq_lens`, which is why no device copy is needed to
   build metadata. A separate `discard_request_mask` marks requests whose optimistic length is below
   their real token count (chunked prefill tails) so their sampled tokens are cleared later.
7. `num_accepted_tokens` is either re-synced from the previous step's event or filled with 1, and
   `num_computed_tokens` is copied to the device — or, under async speculation, corrected *on device*
   by `update_num_computed_tokens_for_batch_change` using the previous step's valid-sampled-token
   counts, so the CPU never blocks.
8. `positions`, `seq_lens`, `query_start_loc`, `req_indices`, `query_pos`, `num_scheduled_tokens` are
   copied to the NPU; `block_table.compute_slot_mapping(...)` derives each token's KV slot; M-RoPE and
   XD-RoPE position tensors are computed only for the models that use them.
9. `logits_indices` — the rows of `hidden_states` that will be projected to logits — is
   `query_start_loc[1:num_reqs+1] - 1` without speculation, or `spec_decode_metadata.logits_indices`
   with it; under lm-head TP it is padded to `max_num_reqs * uniform_decode_query_len` so every rank
   feeds the same number of rows to the collective.

Speculative bookkeeping is confined to the tail: `num_draft_tokens` / `num_decode_draft_tokens` are
built per request (`-1` masks a request that is still mid-prefill, so guided decoding can roll back),
`_calc_spec_decode_metadata` produces the `SpecDecodeMetadata`, and the speculative-token H2D copies
are retained in a deque until their event completes
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L1669-L1684)).

## Batch execution and padding

`_determine_batch_execution_and_padding` returns
`(cudagraph_mode, batch_descriptor, should_ubatch, num_tokens_across_dp, cudagraph_stats)`
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3131-L3233)). It is where Ascend
diverges most from the GPU runner, because two constraints — sequence parallelism and data parallelism
— each impose their own padding on top of the graph dispatcher's.

<!-- openwiki: mermaid parse failed and this diagram was converted to a text fence so it does not break rendering. Fix the diagram source and restore the mermaid fence. Parser error: Heuristic: an unescaped angle bracket inside a label breaks rendering; rephrase the label. -->
```text
flowchart TD
    A["num_tokens_unpadded, num_reqs, num_scheduled_tokens_np"] --> B["_pad_for_sequence_parallelism: round up to TP size when enable_sp or enable_dsa_cp"]
    B --> C["uniform_decode = has_initial_state and max_query_len == uniform_decode_query_len and num_tokens == max_query_len * num_reqs"]
    C --> D["cudagraph_dispatcher.dispatch: FULL invalidated for cascade attention or encoder output"]
    D --> E{"data_parallel_size > 1"}
    E -->|no| F["should_ubatch False, num_tokens_across_dp None"]
    E -->|yes| G["_sync_metadata_across_dp: all_reduce num_tokens and graph mode on the DP CPU group"]
    G --> H["num_tokens_padded = num_tokens_across_dp[dp_rank], re-dispatch with the synced mode"]
    H --> I["assert batch_descriptor.num_tokens == num_tokens_padded"]
    F --> J["batch_descriptor and cudagraph_stats returned"]
    I --> J
```

*SP rounds the token count up first; DP then overwrites it with the group-agreed value and re-dispatches, so the graph shape is identical on every DP rank.*

Load-bearing details:

- **Sequence-parallel padding** rounds `num_tokens` up to a multiple of `tensor_parallel_size` when
  `enable_sp(vllm_config)` (i.e. `use_sequence_parallel_moe`) or `enable_dsa_cp()`, and then *asserts*
  the final descriptor keeps that multiple
  ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3078-L3086)). Shards must be
  equal-length or the fused collectives disagree on shape.
- **`uniform_decode`** is the gate for decode-shaped graphs. Note it requires
  `has_initial_state = all(num_computed_tokens_cpu > 0)`, tightened under DCP to "the whole prompt has
  been computed"; a partially-prefilled request with a length-1 query is *still* dispatched as a decode
  graph, which `tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py::test_partial_prompt_with_state_dispatches_speculative_decode_graph`
  asserts.
- **`CUDAGraphMode.FULL` is invalidated** when cascade attention is actually in use — which requires
  `cascade_attn_enabled` *and* DBO disabled, since `execute_model` skips the prefix-length computation
  under DBO — and for encoder-decoder steps carrying encoder inputs.
- **Ubatching is disabled**: `should_ubatch` is always `False`; the runner's `_dummy_run` says outright
  that vllm-ascend does not support ubatch
  ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3762-L3763)).
- **`num_tokens_across_dp`** is a *CPU* `int32` tensor of length `dp_size`. `_sync_metadata_across_dp`
  packs `(num_tokens, cudagraph_mode.value)` into a `2 x dp_size` CPU tensor, `dist.all_reduce`s it on
  `get_dp_group().cpu_group`, takes the max token count, and takes the **minimum** graph mode so that a
  single `NONE` rank forces eager everywhere
  ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L775-L813)). Keeping this exchange
  on the CPU group is what makes the subsequent `.item()` free of a device synchronisation.
- **DP padding can be skipped.** `should_skip_allreduce_across_dp_group` returns `True` for dense
  models (nothing is actually exchanged) and for the MC2 decode path on KV-consumer ranks, and `False`
  whenever that would break an operator contract — `mc2_comm_alg == "hierarchy"` or CANN MegaMoE
  require uniform token counts across ranks
  ([`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/utils.py#L1160-L1200)).
- **`_pad_query_start_loc_for_fia`** then reconciles `query_start_loc` with the padded token count,
  because TND-layout attention requires the first dimension of `hidden_states` to equal the last element
  of `actual_seq_lengths_q` ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L972-L1019)).
  In the uniform case it extends the tail with `uniform_decode_query_len`-sized slots; in the mixed case
  it asserts `num_reqs == num_reqs_padded` and appends **one dummy request** rather than rewriting the
  last offset. `execute_model` only calls it when the dispatched mode is `FULL`, or when SP is on for a
  non-MLA model with DCP size 1
  ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2382-L2397)).

## Attention metadata construction

`_build_attention_metadata` returns `(attn_metadata, spec_decode_common_attn_metadata)` where
`attn_metadata` is a `PerLayerAttnMetadata` — a dict keyed by layer name — and the second value is the
`AscendCommonAttentionMetadata` the drafter will build its own per-step metadata from
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3235-L3644)). The shape of the
stage:

1. **Nothing to build** for attention-free models: if `kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups` is empty it
   returns `({}, None)`.
2. **`max_seq_len`** is `optimistic_seq_lens_cpu.numpy()[:num_reqs].max().item()` — the `.numpy()` view
   makes the reduction (and the `.item()`) host-side, deliberately, so metadata construction never
   synchronises on the device
   ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3285-L3286)).
3. **`cm_base`** is one `AscendCommonAttentionMetadata` carrying the CPU *and* device views of
   `query_start_loc`, `seq_lens`, `_seq_lens_cpu`, `num_computed_tokens_cpu`, `is_prefilling`,
   `block_table_tensor`/`slot_mapping` for group 0, `max_query_len`, `max_seq_len`, `num_actual_tokens`
   vs `num_input_tokens` (padded), `attn_state`, `decode_token_per_req`, the DCP
   `context_parallel_metadata`, the sparse-KV-offload `req_ids_tensor`/`token_to_req`, and
   `mm_req_doc_ranges` for multimodal prefix attention
   ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3412-L3456),
   [`utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py#L279-L356)).
4. **Per KV cache group** the builder shallow-copies `cm_base`, replaces `encoder_seq_lens`, and (for
   groups above 0) the block table and slot mapping. The first group is the one whose slot mapping was
   already snapshotted for routed-expert capture, so a pending D2H cannot be torn by the next step.
   Encoder-only groups get zeroed tables instead of real ones
   ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3313-L3346)).
5. **Padding holes are marked** with `slot_mapping[num_tokens:num_tokens_padded].fill_(-1)` and
   `blk_table_tensor[num_reqs:num_reqs_padded].fill_(0)`; `-1` matches the mamba `PAD_SLOT_ID` so a fully
   captured graph writes nothing. This is the invariant
   `tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py::TestDummyRunSlotInvalidation` checks: slots must already be
   invalidated *before* a metadata builder reads them.
6. **Each attention group** calls `builder.build(common_prefix_len=..., common_attn_metadata=...)` (or
   `build_for_cudagraph_capture` during capture) and the result is written under every layer name in
   that group, so layers sharing a group share one metadata object
   ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3462-L3563)). Backend-specific
   extras are injected here: GDN gets `num_accepted_tokens` and `num_decode_draft_tokens_cpu`; the DSA
   builders get `num_actual_reqs`, the shared-ratio map and a `full_graph_mode` flag.
7. **`spec_decode_common_attn_metadata`** is the copy handed to the draft proposer, and it is
   `unpadded(num_tokens, num_reqs)` whenever padding was applied, because the drafter builds its own
   piecewise metadata and must not see fake requests.
8. **Device metadata tasks** collected from builders that can run their work on a side stream are
   submitted through `DeviceMetadataExecutor.submit(...)`, with an external-event frontier per batch
   descriptor in full-graph mode. `_prepare_device_metadata_for_forward` later refuses to attach such an
   executor to a `FULL` graph unless it uses external events
   ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3068-L3076),
   [`device_metadata.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/device_metadata.py#L45-L120)).

Finally `_sanitize_placeholder_input_ids_for_forward` rewrites speculative placeholder ids to 0 **in the
forward copy only**, after metadata has been built, so the backends that inspect those ids keep seeing
them ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L1652-L1667)).

## The forward context: `set_ascend_forward_context` and `_EXTRA_CTX`

Everything the metadata stage computes has to reach operators that are nested several modules below the
runner — MoE prepare/finalize, HCCL collectives, RoPE, quantized linears — with no plumbing available in
their signatures. Ascend solves this with a forward-context *side channel*.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as NPUModelRunner
    participant FC as set_ascend_forward_context
    participant Ctx as vLLM ForwardContext
    participant X as _EXTRA_CTX proxy
    participant Op as MoE or collective op
    R->>FC: attn_metadata, num_tokens_padded, num_tokens_across_dp, graph mode, batch descriptor
    FC->>Ctx: set_current_vllm_config and set_forward_context
    FC->>Ctx: moe_comm_type, moe_comm_method, padded_length, padded_num_tokens, mc2_mask, capturing, layer_idx
    R->>Op: model forward reaches the operator
    Op->>X: read padded_length or mc2_mask or is_draft_model
    X->>Ctx: resolve the attribute on the current context
    X-->>Op: per-step value
```

*The context is written once per forward by the runner and read many times per forward by operators that never see a runner argument.*

`set_ascend_forward_context` ([`ascend_forward_context.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py#L100-L222))
wraps upstream's `set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config)` **and** `set_forward_context(...)`, then writes
the Ascend extras onto the context object:

| Extra written | Why it is per-step |
| --- | --- |
| `moe_comm_type` / `moe_comm_method` | `select_moe_comm_method(max_tokens_across_dp, config)` depends on the batch size: MC2 up to `_mc2_tokens_capacity`, MegaMoE/FUSED_MC2 when the hardware policy allows, otherwise ALLTOALL/ALLGATHER |
| `padded_length`, `padded_num_tokens` | both are `ceil(max_tokens_across_dp / tp) * tp`, the length MC2 requires every rank to reach. On the V2 hook `padded_length` is only filled when DP metadata is present, so `padded_num_tokens` is the field to read when it must never be `None` |
| `mc2_mask` | a reserved bool buffer sliced to `padded_num_tokens`, set `True` for real tokens and `False` for padding, refreshed every step |
| `max_tokens_across_dp`, `max_tokens_across_pcp` | read by MoE prepare/finalize to pad a local shard up to the DP-agreed (or PCP-agreed) length before its all-gather; PCP is V2-only, so the v1 value stays `0` |
| `is_decode_only_node`, `use_mega_moe` | recomputed from config plus `KVTransferConfig` on every forward (`_is_decode_only_node`, `use_cann_megamoe`); they select whole operator paths, so operators read them rather than re-deriving them. Written by the v1 context manager only |
| `mmrs_fusion` | `tp_world_size <= 8` on the v1 path, because the fused mm+reduce-scatter op does not support wider TP; the V2 platform hook instead disables it outright for MoE models |
| `capturing`, `layer_idx`, `in_profile_run`, `sinks`, `is_draft_model`, `is_draft_model_prefill` | flags that no operator argument carries. `layer_idx`, `model_instance` and the `prefetch_mlp_*` flags are written only by the v1 context manager |
| `num_tokens` | the padded token count as the runner computed it, distinct from `padded_num_tokens` which is derived from the DP-agreed maximum |

The two writer paths do not produce an identical field set: the V2 hook additionally publishes
`dynamic_mx_quant_scale_alg` and omits `is_decode_only_node`, `use_mega_moe`, `layer_idx`, `model_instance`,
`is_first_layer` and the `prefetch_mlp_*` flags, which is called out in the platform hook's own comment. It
also hardcodes `is_draft_model = False` (marked temporary) and `sinks = False`, while the v1 manager takes
both from the runner. Anything an operator needs on both paths must be in the shared subset, and
`_EXTRA_CTX` returns `None` for an allow-listed name the current writer never published.

The reason `set_current_vllm_config` is pinned *here* rather than around `load_model` is stated inline:
custom ops (RMSNorm, rotary, Linear, MoE) call `get_current_vllm_config()` from `__init__` when they are
first created during eager prefill, and the context manager restores `None` on exit
([`ascend_forward_context.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py#L119-L139)).
`tests/ut/test_ascend_forward_context.py::test_set_ascend_forward_context_pins_current_vllm_config`
pins that behaviour.

`_EXTRA_CTX` is the reader side, and it is an **allow-list proxy**, not a dict
([`ascend_forward_context.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py#L385-L444)). A name not in
`extra_attrs` raises an explicit `AttributeError` telling the caller to use vLLM's context directly; a
name in the list resolves to `ctx.additional_kwargs[name]` under Model Runner V2 and to a plain
attribute on the v1 context otherwise. Two consumers illustrate the pattern:

- [`register_custom_ops.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/register_custom_ops.py#L43-L110) reshapes gathered
  expert inputs as `(dp_size, _EXTRA_CTX.padded_length, ...)` to pad before an EP all-gather and to unpad
  after a reduce-scatter, and short-circuits to a plain all-reduce for a VL draft model
  (`_EXTRA_CTX.is_draft_model`).
- [`prepare_finalize.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/prepare_finalize.py#L273-L343) reads
  `_EXTRA_CTX.mc2_mask` and `_EXTRA_CTX.padded_num_tokens` to pad/split the MoE input, and
  `_EXTRA_CTX.max_tokens_across_dp` / `max_tokens_across_pcp` for the CP variants.

Other readers include RoPE (`is_draft_model` gates an MTP+SP all-gather of positions,
[`rotary_embedding.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/rotary_embedding.py#L259-L266)), the graph wrappers
(`capturing`, so an operator can tell capture from replay — set to `True` inside the v1 `ACLGraphWrapper`
capture block and recomputed from `torch.npu.is_current_stream_capturing()` by V2's `ModelWithContext`,
[`acl_graph.py`](../../vllm_ascend/compilation/acl_graph.py#L196-L206),
[`aclgraph_utils.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/aclgraph_utils.py#L256-L269)), and the MoE comm method
selection itself ([`moe_comm_method.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/moe_comm_method.py#L132-L477)).

**Model Runner V2 builds its context inside upstream vLLM**, so the runner never calls
`set_ascend_forward_context`; instead the platform hook
`NPUPlatform.set_additional_forward_context` returns the same fields, which upstream places into
`additional_kwargs` ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L499-L623)). This is exactly the v1/v2
asymmetry `_EXTRA_CTX` exists to hide. Because the platform hook cannot know whether the current
forward is V2's *extra* MC2 profile dummy run, the runner marks that with a `ContextVar`
(`override_mrv2_in_profile_run`) that `set_additional_forward_context` reads back
([`ascend_forward_context.py`](../../vllm_ascend/ascend_forward_context.py#L33-L84),
[`v2/model_runner.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py#L299-L316)).

## The forward

`_model_forward` is small by design ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3036-L3066)):
it assembles `model_inputs` (`input_ids`, `positions`, `intermediate_tensors`, `inputs_embeds`, plus
extra `model_kwargs`), binds them with `functools.partial`, and calls the model inside the context that is
already active. Two details:

- when the graph mode is `FULL`, the runner is *not* capturing, and the model uses neither sparse nor
  compressed KV, `update_full_graph_params(...)` refreshes the attention graph parameters on the
  dedicated update stream; with `enable_enpu` it is issued **before** the call (after an explicit stream
  synchronise), otherwise after
  ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3014-L3034));
- the graph dispatch itself happens inside the `ACLGraphWrapper` that wraps each compiled region, keyed
  by the `BatchDescriptor` from the padding stage
  ([`acl_graph.py`](../../vllm_ascend/compilation/acl_graph.py#L151-L270)).

Surrounding the forward call, `execute_model` brackets the per-step side facilities: `kvpp.prepare_forward(bool(any(num_computed_tokens_cpu > 0)))`
and `kvpp.complete_forward()` for KV-pool placement, `eplb_updator.forward_before()` for dynamic EPLB
heat collection, and `maybe_get_kv_connector_output(...)` with `defer_finalize` when speculation is on
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2436-L2513)). Mamba state copies run
*after* the KV transfer load inside that block, so a layerwise connector can overlap the copy with the
remaining layers' loads.

`skip_compiled=has_encoder_input` keeps encoder-decoder and raw-token multimodal steps (DeepSeek-V4's
vision router needs the raw sentinel ids during image prefill) out of the compiled path for that step
only.

Between metadata construction and the forward, `execute_model` runs `_preprocess` (upstream's helper,
which resolves `input_ids` vs `inputs_embeds`, `positions`, `model_kwargs` and the EC connector output
for the padded batch) and then `update_cos_sin(positions)` to refresh the process-global cos/sin cache
that the RoPE and MLA kernels read
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2415-L2434)).

After the forward, the rank's role decides the shape of the output:

| Rank / model | Result |
| --- | --- |
| non-last PP rank | `hidden_states` asserted to be `IntermediateTensors`, `kv_connector_output` attached, returned to the worker for `isend` |
| last PP rank, pooling model | `self._pool(...)` output returned directly from `execute_model` |
| last PP rank, generative | `sample_hidden_states = hidden_states[logits_indices]`, `logits = model.compute_logits(...)`, packed into `ExecuteModelState`, `execute_model` returns `None` |
| `broadcast_pp_output` | every rank computes `sample_hidden_states`, non-last ranks `send_tensor_dict(hidden_states.tensors)`, the last rank `broadcast_tensor_dict({"logits": ...}, src=last)` so all ranks hold logits |

`ExecuteModelState` is a `NamedTuple` of exactly the ephemeral values the sampling half needs —
`scheduler_output`, `logits`, `spec_decode_metadata`, `spec_decode_common_attn_metadata`,
`hidden_states`, `sample_hidden_states`, `aux_hidden_states`, `attn_metadata`, `positions`,
`ec_connector_output`, `cudagraph_stats`, `batch_desc`
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L323-L338)). `sample_tokens` unpacks
and immediately clears it.

## `sample_tokens`: sampling, bookkeeping, and the async exit

`sample_tokens(grammar_output)` ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2585-L2814))
does, in order:

1. **Grammar bitmask.** Upstream's `apply_grammar_bitmask` is `torch.compile`d and Ascend does not
   support that, so the logits take a CPU round trip: `.to("cpu").float()` → mask → `.to(device)` with
   the original dtype. This is a per-step host transfer confined to structured-output requests.
2. **`_sample`** ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2817-L2844)).
   `input_batch.update_async_output_token_ids()` runs *first* so penalty operators see the previous
   step's newly sampled ids (pinned by
   `tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py::test_sample_updates_output_token_ids_before_sampler`); then
   `AscendSampler` (or the rejection sampler for speculative batches) is called, with optional
   `prepare_sampling(max_topk)` when `enable_reduce_sample` is on. `AscendSampler` replaces
   `torch.multinomial` with an exponential-race `argmax` to avoid a CPU-NPU synchronisation, and offers a
   TP-all-gather greedy/top-k path under `enable_reduce_sample`
   ([`sampler.py`](../../vllm_ascend/sample/sampler.py#L21-L160)).
3. **`_bookkeeping_sync`** ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2862-L3012))
   converts the sampler output into host lists, appends the sampled ids into `input_batch.token_ids_cpu`
   and `req_state.output_token_ids`, and computes prompt logprobs. Requests marked by `discard_request_mask`
   get their sampled ids cleared and, if they own a `torch.Generator`, have its offset rewound by 4 — the
   number of random draws the sampler consumed for a token that is thrown away
   ([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2890-L2895)).
4. **Draft proposal**, when speculation is on: `propose_draft_token_ids(...)` runs either before
   bookkeeping (EAGLE-style padded-drafter batches, which can start from device sampled ids) or after
   (ngram and CPU-dependent methods), and `_copy_draft_token_ids_to_cpu` stages the result for
   `take_draft_token_ids`.
5. **Output assembly** into `ModelRunnerOutput`, plus routed-expert capture and dynamic-EPLB closeout.

The async path is the reason the two-phase split pays off:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["_bookkeeping_sync in async mode"] --> B["keep NaN counts on device, do not build token lists"]
    B --> C["cache prev_sampled_token_ids on the NPU and prev_req_id_to_index"]
    C --> D["AsyncGPUModelRunnerOutput with async_output_copy_stream"]
    D --> E["input_batch.set_async_sampled_token_ids: cpu tensor plus ready event"]
    E --> F["_update_states_after_model_execute on the global stream after wait_event(sampling_done_event)"]
    F --> G["next _prepare_inputs reads prev_sampled_token_ids on device, no host read"]
    G --> H["next _sample calls update_async_output_token_ids, which resolves the host event"]
```

*In async mode neither the forward nor the input preparation blocks on the sampled ids; the host-side event is resolved at the start of the next step's sampling, before penalties run.*

The `_update_states_after_model_execute` leg is conditional: it only runs when
`self.need_accepted_tokens` is set, which the runner derives from
`kv_cache_config.has_mamba_layers`. Hybrid mamba models need accepted-token counts committed on the
default stream before the next step's mamba state copy, and the `sampling_done_event` wait is what makes
that ordering safe without stalling the copy stream
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2637-L2644),
[`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2757-L2764),
[`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L4242)).

The division of labour is what makes this work: `_prepare_inputs` needs the previous step's sampled
tokens only as a *device* tensor — it consults `input_batch.prev_sampled_token_ids` and
`prev_req_id_to_index` to decide whether previous positions must be staged to the device — so no
synchronisation is required there
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L1255-L1265)). The host-side values
are consumed one step later: `set_async_sampled_token_ids` registers the pinned
`sampled_token_ids_cpu` buffer together with `async_copy_ready_event` on `NPUInputBatch`
([`npu_input_batch.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/npu_input_batch.py#L250-L258),
[`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2800-L2813)), and
`update_async_output_token_ids()` — the first call in `_sample` — is what turns that buffer into
`sampling_metadata.output_token_ids` before penalties see it.

Two buffer-ownership rules make that safe, both documented in the code: the routed-expert capture buffer
is `clear_buffer()`-ed at the start of the next step on the default stream, and
`routed_experts_slot_mapping_device` is overwritten by the next `_prepare_inputs` — so both are `clone()`d
into the snapshot the copy stream will read
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2778-L2813)). Similarly the
speculative-metadata H2D keeps its CPU sources in a deque until the copy event completes.

## CP, DP and PP special cases

These are the paths that change the flow rather than merely its cost.

**Sequence-parallel (SP) padding.** With `use_sequence_parallel_moe` or DSA-CP on, the token count is
rounded up to a multiple of TP before graph dispatch, and the invariant is asserted afterwards. The
consequence cascades: `query_start_loc` is padded, slot mappings for the padding are `-1`, and the MoE
`prepare_finalize` path reads `_EXTRA_CTX.padded_num_tokens // tp_size` to decide how much to pad its
local shard. `sync_and_slice_intermediate_tensors` slices PP intermediate tensors to
`ceil(num_tokens / tp)` under SP so the pipeline stage does not effectively all-gather
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L3088-L3118)).

**Data-parallel token agreement.** `num_tokens_across_dp` is produced by the CPU-group all-reduce
described above, consumed three ways: as the padded token count for this rank, as the input to
`select_moe_comm_method`, and as the parameter for the EP pad/unpad inside `register_custom_ops`. If the
all-reduce is skipped (dense model, or MC2 decode on a KV consumer) the tensor is instead a uniform
replica of this rank's own count, and MC2 operators are expected to use a non-zero `global_bs` and no
`mc2_mask`.

**PP sampled-token handoff.** Pipeline stages do not exchange sampled tokens directly, so the scheduler
echoes them back in the next `SchedulerOutput`. `_apply_pp_sampled_tokens_from_scheduler_output`
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L824-L887)) reconstructs
`input_batch.prev_sampled_token_ids` (a `(num_reqs, 1)` device tensor) and `prev_req_id_to_index` from
`scheduled_cached_reqs.new_token_ids` for async-scheduling, non-last, non-PD-prefill ranks, appending a
`PLACEHOLDER_TOKEN_ID` into the request's `output_token_ids` for each token it materialises. Requests
discarded in the previous sampling half are excluded from the mapping so a request cannot inherit another
request's token. `execute_model` also blanks echoed `new_token_ids` on non-last ranks (see the early-exit
section), and `execute_model_state` is `None` on those ranks so `sample_tokens` short-circuits — except
when `kv_connector_output` must still be passed through.

**Encoder cache branch.** With the score encoder cache enabled, `_update_states` → `_track_tmp_encoder_cache_refs`
records, per multimodal hash, the set of requests that reference it
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L1021-L1031)); the mirror
`_on_request_state_removed` discards the request from that set and deletes the `tmp_encoder_cache` entry only
when the last referencing request goes away
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L1033-L1052)).
`_process_encoder_cache_scheduler_output` then applies the scheduler's NPU/CPU tier decisions —
`npu_freed`, `cpu_freed`, `promoting_mm_hashes`, `cpu_get_encoder_mm_hashes` — with non-blocking H2D copies
fenced by an event deque, and `_get_encoder_output_from_cache` falls back to a synchronous copy so a stale
worker entry cannot turn a scheduler CPU hit into a fatal cache miss
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L1054-L1148)). The forward step never
runs on the encoder rank: when an EC transfer exists and this rank is not the consumer, `execute_model`
runs `_execute_mm_encoder` and returns `make_empty_encoder_model_runner_output` immediately
([`model_runner_v1.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py#L2222-L2230)).

**No tokens scheduled.** The empty-batch return is not merely an optimisation: on the DP path it must be
preceded by a dummy run so the rank still participates in `coordinate_batch_across_dp`.

## Invariants and failure modes

| Invariant | Failure if violated |
| --- | --- |
| `sample_tokens` follows every `execute_model` that returned `None` | `RuntimeError("State error: sample_tokens() must be called after execute_model() returns None.")` |
| `num_tokens_padded` is a multiple of TP under SP | assertion in `_determine_batch_execution_and_padding` |
| `batch_descriptor.num_tokens == num_tokens_padded` after the DP re-dispatch | assertion; otherwise `num_tokens_across_dp` no longer describes the batch |
| mixed-batch FIA padding requires `num_reqs == num_reqs_padded` | assertion — the dummy-request insertion keeps this true |
| padding slots are `-1` before any metadata builder reads them | wrong mamba/KV writes inside captured graphs |
| device metadata on a `FULL` graph requires external events | `RuntimeError("Full-graph device metadata requires external events")` |
| no `tensor.item()` on device tensors in the step | this synchronisation blocks `AsyncScheduler` and shows up as a decode stall |

That last row is a project rule, not just a performance hint: [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md#L164-L193)
states that `item()` on a device tensor forces a synchronous NPU→CPU transfer and can severely degrade
hot paths, and requires profiling plus a documented justification for each new occurrence. Inside
`model_runner_v1.py` the surviving `.item()` calls all operate on CPU-side tensors — the DP exchange
tensor and `optimistic_seq_lens_cpu` — which is precisely why the DP all-reduce is done on the CPU
group.

The same file also carries a review gate for this page's subject matter: **all new behaviours added to a
model runner require architectural review**, with reviewers asked to justify why the behaviour cannot
live in a patch, and to assess NPU performance, compatibility with existing models, and long-term
maintainability ([`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md#L252-L267)). Practically that means a change to
`_prepare_inputs` or `_build_attention_metadata` is a reviewable architectural change even if it is a few
lines.

## Where a change goes

The step has a small number of well-defined seams, which is what makes it reviewable:

| If you need to … | Touch | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| produce or reshape per-step attention tensors | the group's metadata builder, invoked from `_build_attention_metadata` | never edit `cm_base` in place — it is shared by shallow copy across groups |
| make a per-step value visible to an operator | `_EXTRA_CTX.extra_attrs` **plus** both writers (`set_ascend_forward_context` and `NPUPlatform.set_additional_forward_context`) | publishing from only one writer makes the value silently `None` on the other runner |
| change the padded token count or graph mode | `_determine_batch_execution_and_padding` | the SP multiple-of-TP assertion and the DP re-dispatch assertion both live here |
| change what the sampler sees | `_sample` / `AscendSampler`, and `NPUInputBatch` for the host mirrors | keep the `update_async_output_token_ids()`-before-penalties ordering |
| add an override for upstream Model Runner V2 | `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py` | V2 already owns the step loop upstream; do not duplicate it |

Before any of these land, [`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md#L252-L267) requires an explicit answer to *why the
behaviour cannot live in a patch*.

## The V2 runner deltas

`vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py` does not own the step loop; it overrides the seams where Ascend
needs different data ([`v2/model_runner.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py#L261-L546)):

| Override | Ascend-specific reason |
| --- | --- |
| `prepare_inputs` | NPU attention backends need CPU sequence lengths, so it computes `seq_lens_np` and `attn_state` and returns an `AscendInputBatch`; `AscendInputBuffers.query_start_loc` carries one extra slot for FIA padding ([`v2/input_batch.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/input_batch.py#L29-L107)) |
| `_pad_query_start_loc_for_fia` | same TND constraint, restated in numpy because V2 builds `query_start_loc` on the host. It decides uniform-vs-mixed from the *query lengths* rather than from `num_tokens_padded` alone, and in the mixed case always inserts the dummy request |
| `prepare_inputs` (tail) | `maybe_partition_pcp_batch(self.pcp_manager, ...)` splits the batch for prefill context parallelism; the pre-partition batch is retained as `global_batch` ([`pcp_manager.py`](../../vllm_ascend/worker/v2/pcp_manager.py#L36-L101)) |
| `sample` | under lm-head TP, hidden states are padded to the group-agreed `max_num_reqs * decode_query_len` capacity and logits trimmed back, because an uneven row count desyncs the LM-head collectives |
| `sample_tokens` | restores PCP/replicated-draft hidden states and, on the `0.28.0` lane with spec PP, broadcasts draft tokens |
| `postprocess_sampled` | copies `num_computed_tokens` back to the CPU on a side stream so NPU backends can read `seq_lens_cpu` on the next step |
| `execute_model` | brackets the upstream step with profiling timing and `kvpp` run-state, and forwards `dummy_run` / `is_profile` / `context_len` |
| `profile_run` | runs an *extra* MC2-sized dummy run so the HCCL/symmetric buffers are reserved before upstream's profile run, under `override_mrv2_in_profile_run(True)` |

PCP is V2-only: `_validate_parallel_config` rejects `prefill_context_parallel_size > 1` outright for the v1
runner ([`platform.py`](../../vllm_ascend/platform.py#L1483-L1490)), and `max_tokens_across_pcp` is
informational (0) on the v1 forward context.

  the "global batch only on non-last PP rank" rule in `sample_tokens`.
